# Apple Silicon M4 / A18 Pro / M5 Audio Subsystem — Hardware Reference

A clean-room hardware specification of the audio subsystem of the M4-class,
A18 Pro-class and M5-class Apple Silicon SoCs and the machines built around
them, written to support independent driver development alongside hardware
tracing and probing.

## What this document is

This is a description of **hardware**. It documents SoC blocks, discrete
codec and amplifier parts, their register interfaces, the buses and control
lines that connect them, and the sequences the hardware requires. It is
written as a delta: for every block, the closest previously documented
equivalent is named, and only what is new, changed or absent is documented in
detail.

The baseline is the M1–M3 implementation as documented in upstream Linux and
by the Asahi Linux project, together with the public counterpart parts of the
third-party chips (Texas Instruments TAS2764 and TAS2770, Analog Devices
SSM3515, Cirrus Logic CS42L42, and the Maxim/ADI MAX98357A/MAX98360A family).
Where this document says a block is unchanged, it means unchanged with respect
to that published baseline, and the reader should work from the published
baseline directly.

## The headline architectural change

On M1 through M3 the audio subsystem is host-owned end to end: a multi-cluster
serial audio controller, a numerically controlled oscillator generating the bit
and frame clocks, and an audio DMA controller behind an IOMMU, all programmed
by the host over MMIO, driving discrete amplifiers and codecs over I2S and I2C.

**Starting with the M4 generation, the control path moved to the coprocessor.** On every SoC
covered here the platform hardware description no longer exposes a
host-addressable serial audio controller or clock generator. In their place the
platform describes a set of per-stream endpoints belonging to a service on the
always-on coprocessor. The **data** path remains host-owned: the audio DMA
controller is still directly addressable over MMIO, now instantiated several
times across a "base" domain and a "low-power audio processor" domain, each
split into secure and non-secure halves.

The practical consequence for a driver author is that bringing up audio on these
SoCs is a two-part problem: direct MMIO programming of the DMA controller and
the IOMMU, and a message-based protocol with a coprocessor for everything to do
with serialisation, routing and clocking. Sections 4 and 11 respectively are the
two halves of that problem; Section 3 records what is known about the serial
audio controller hardware that now sits behind the coprocessor, and Section 18
specifies the firmware ABI that now programs it — the property and call
vocabulary, the stream-configuration message, the clocking and slot-geometry
models, and the register interfaces on the far side.

**The coprocessor half is specified, not a blank.** Section 11 gives the mailbox
register map and its 96-bit message format, the version handshake and endpoint
map, the shared-memory ring protocol every endpoint runs, the framed call layer
with its correlation tags, the way a named service resolves to an
(endpoint, channel) pair, and the audio service's own request framing, device
identifiers, call types and property payloads — ending in a step-by-step
configure-and-start sequence for a stream. A driver can be written against it.
Two qualifications matter and are stated wherever they bear:

- The **register map** the stack sits on is **[Probable]** for the SoCs covered
  here, not Confirmed. It is the published map for the mailbox block revision
  every one of them declares, and it has not been read on an M4-, A18-Pro- or
  M5-class part. Confirming it is one boot with the aperture trapped, and it is
  the first item in Section 11's open questions. Everything layered above the
  register map is **[Confirmed]**.
- The **capture path and the playback path are now both specified.** Section 18
  gives the playback property vocabulary that Section 11 and Section 15's S7
  previously named as the residual gap: the property keys a serial-audio stream
  endpoint accepts, the single 109-byte message that carries slot geometry,
  frame geometry and clocking, the clock model and its invariant, and the
  ordered start sequence. The key **numbers** are **[Confirmed]** on t604x,
  t8140 and t605x and **[Probable]** on t8132 and t8142; two call types remain
  **[Unknown]**. What is left between this document and speaker output is
  confirmation work, not discovery.

wherever that is true.

## Confidence annotations

Every non-trivial claim carries one of:

- **[Confirmed]** — corroborated by more than one independent line of evidence.
- **[Probable]** — consistent with prior-generation behaviour or a public
  counterpart part, single line of evidence.
- **[Inferred]** — deduced, not directly observed.
- **[Unknown]** — identified as needed, not determined.

**[Unknown]** items are not omissions. Each section ends with an
`Open questions` list collecting them, phrased as concrete experiments. Those
lists are a deliverable in their own right: they are the work plan for the
tracing and probing that follows.

## Three hazards to read before driving speakers

All three are established in this document and all three are easy to miss in
20,000 lines.

**1. There is no thermal protection of the voice coil in hardware.** The
per-machine amplifier configuration supplied by platform firmware leaves thermal
foldback **disabled on every machine in scope**, and the supply-tracking limiter
disabled with it (`LIM_EN` = 0 at reset, and no platform-supplied configuration
sets it — **[Probable]**, not yet read back from a live part; §7 §7.7). Overcurrent, brownout prevention and the hard
over-temperature shutdown remain active, but nothing in the amplifier reduces gain
as the voice coil heats. Thermal protection exists only if the host implements it from
the sense return — and two machine families have no sense return at all: the
A18 Pro machine, whose amplifiers have no sense capability, and the iMac, whose
sense-capable amplifiers have the sense path disabled. On those two, no
closed-loop speaker protection is possible. See Sections 7, 8 and 9.

**2. The mapping of slot records to physical transducers is not certain on the
MacBook Pro chassis.** The slot record structure is established: each record
gives a playback slot, an output level and a current/voltage sense slot pair.
Which amplifier — and therefore which physical driver — each record describes
rests on a reading that the published upstream maps contradict on the MacBook
Pro chassis specifically. A wrong binding sends woofer content to a tweeter and
misattributes its sense data, which is destructive and is not detectable from
the platform description alone. Before driving speakers on a MacBook Pro chassis
machine, read the amplifier receive-slot and transmit-slot registers back from a
running system. See §8 §8.2.3, and §1 §1.4.2 and §7 §7.5.1.

**3. The slot map in this document and the channel labels in existing published
speaker-protection configurations come from different stacks and must not be
mixed.** Adopt one stack's register programming together with **that** stack's
channel labels, or swap the labels to match. Mixing them exchanges voltage and
current: a **power**-based protection model will not detect it, and an
**excursion**- or **impedance**-based model will be inverted. This is not a
defect in either stack — each is internally consistent on its own hardware,
because the sense-slot assignment is a host-side choice written explicitly on
every boot, not a property discovered from the part. The defect appears only at
the join, and this document makes that join easy to reach because it publishes
one stack's slot map while the existing published protection configurations were
written for the other. Nothing in the hardware will complain: the amplifier is
symmetric under the exchange, and the coprocessor never distinguishes the two
sense channels at all. Which register carries which quantity is **[Probable]**,
not Confirmed, and it can only be settled on the bench — drive one amplifier
into two different known load resistances and see which received channel
changes. See §8 §8.2.1, §7 §7.5.1, §9 open question 5 and §18 §18.5.5.

Sections 7, 8 and 9 are safety-critical. A driver that gets the amplifier gain
mapping, the sense scaling, or the protection limits wrong can destroy speakers.
Confidence annotations in those sections are deliberately conservative, and
where a safe default exists it is stated.

## A fourth hazard, of a different class — read it before the first bring-up

The three above are hazards on the **output** path and they destroy transducers.
This one is on the **control** path and it destroys a week: it is the only
failure in this document that **succeeds visibly and then corrupts everything
afterwards, with no error anywhere**. It is set out here rather than among the
three because the ☠ marker means physical destruction and this is not that — but
silent corruption is the class of failure that most deserves a warning, and it is
the first thing a new driver will hit.

**A wrong firmware boot-argument alignment value boots the coprocessor
successfully and then mis-parses every ring.** The `alig` boot argument
(§11 §11.5.4) sets the stride the coprocessor uses when it lays out the
shared-memory rings. It is applied after the core is released, nothing validates
it, and every plausible value is structurally acceptable. A wrong one leaves the
core release and the management handshake working perfectly — they run over the
mailbox, not the rings — and then has host and coprocessor addressing the same
buffer with different strides. Every symptom afterwards points at the transport:
the wrong endpoint answering, message bodies that decode as nonsense, a service
that resolves and returns garbage. None of them points at the boot argument.

**The correct in-scope value is [Unknown]** — no board description in scope
supplies it — which is why §17 puts it first in phase 1, ahead of the register-map
confirmation it used to sit behind.

It reaches the output path by one route, and a driver should know it: the rings
carry **configuration**, and configuration includes the slot map and the
amplifier level. A corrupted configuration exchange can therefore produce a
running link programmed from values nobody chose. §15's S8 and S10a preconditions
— read the amplifier slot registers back, and check per-channel impedance before
the first unmute — are what stand between that and a damaged transducer, and they
must not be skipped on a bring-up boot on the grounds that the machine is "just
being tested".

## The safety marker

**☠** marks a statement where getting it wrong **destroys hardware or injures the
user** — a transducer driven beyond its limits, a full-scale output into headphones, a
protection loop that silently watches nothing. It is not a marker for "important"; it is
a marker for physically destructive. It is used in Sections 7, 8, 9, 14 and 18, and in
Section 15 where a sequencing step exists only to prevent such an outcome. Where it
appears on an open question, that question must be resolved before speakers are driven
on the affected machine.

# 1. Topology inventory

## Baseline

The measured-against baseline is the M1–M3 machine topology as it is publicly
documented: a host-owned multi-cluster serial audio controller whose clusters and
ports are named directly in the platform hardware description
(`/arm-io/mca0/mca0a/...`, `/arm-io/mca2/mca2b/...`, `/arm-io/alc0/...`,
`/arm-io/alc4/...`), a host-owned numerically controlled oscillator (`/arm-io/nco`),
a port router (`/arm-io/mca-switch`), and discrete I²C parts on the board: a
TAS2764-family mono Class-D speaker amplifier per driver (Apple part variant
`sn012776`) and a CS42L84 headset codec. Published Asahi Linux device trees give the
per-machine TDM slot maps for several of those machines and the published TAS2764
support in upstream Linux gives the register semantics of the amplifier fields that
the platform description carries as opaque blobs.

Everything below is stated as a delta against that baseline. Where a fact is
identical to the baseline it is stated once and not re-documented.

## Summary of differences

| Aspect | M1–M3 baseline | t8132 (M4) | t604x (M4 Pro/Max) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 (M5) | t6050/t605x (M5 Pro/Max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Serial-audio cluster named per stream | Yes (`mcaN/mcaNx`, `alcN`) | **Absent** | **Absent** | **Absent** | **Absent** | **Absent** |
| Stream endpoint container | cluster node children | `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` | same | same | same | same |
| DMA binding expressed as | implicit (cluster) | 128-byte `dma-channels` blob | 128-byte `dma-channels` blob | `dma-provider-tx/rx` **strings** | `dma-provider-tx/rx` strings | `dma-provider-tx/rx` strings |
| Speaker amplifier family | `sn012776` (TAS2764 class) | unchanged | unchanged | **`max98360`, no control bus** | unchanged | unchanged |
| Jack codec | `cs42l84` (M1: `cs42l83`) | `cs42l84` | `cs42l84` | **`cs42l83`** | `cs42l84` | `cs42l84` |
| Speaker path DMA domain | host "SIO" audio DMA | base non-secure | base non-secure | **low-power audio processor (non-secure)** | base non-secure | base non-secure |
| Built-in mic capture domain | always-on cluster, non-secure | low-power non-secure | low-power non-secure | **low-power secure** | **low-power secure** | **low-power secure** |
| Playback tap endpoint | absent | absent | absent | present | present | present |
| Low-power mic injection endpoint | absent | absent | absent | present | present | present |

| Speaker slot **geometry** and transmit idle masks | reference | **unchanged** (byte-identical to M1 Pro) | **unchanged** | n/a — no control bus | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |

| Serial audio clusters enumerated in power manager | `MCA0…MCA3` + `AOP_MCA0…3` | `AUDIO_MCA0_M…AUDIO_MCA5_M` + `AUDIO_LEAP_MCA` | same | same | same | same |

## 1.1 Encoding conventions used throughout this section

These are properties of the platform hardware description format, restated here so
every table below can be read without cross-reference.

| Construct | Layout | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FourCC-valued property | 4 bytes, stored byte-reversed with respect to the readable form | a property whose raw bytes are `rkps` reads **`spkr`**; `niam` reads **`main`**; `pael` reads **`leap`** |
| `function-<name>` | `u32 provider phandle │ 4-byte tag (byte-reversed) │ u32 arg0 │ u32 arg1 …` | tag `GPIO` ⇒ arg0 = pin number on the named controller, arg1 = flag word |
| I²C child `reg` | `u32 7-bit address │ u32 SCL period (ns) │ u32 0 │ u32 0` | see §1.6 |
| Interrupt on an I²C child | `interrupt-parent` = a GPIO controller phandle, `interrupts` = `u32 pin │ u32 type` | type `1` on every audio node in scope |

**GPIO flag word** (arg1 of a `GPIO`-tagged function), values observed on audio
nodes:

| Flags | Meaning | Where used |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00000001` | driven output | jack-codec reset |
| `0x00010001` | driven output, plus one further attribute bit (bit 16) | speaker-amplifier shutdown/reset; the same bit 16 appears on SPI chip-select lines elsewhere in the same description, so it is an output-parking/deassert attribute rather than an audio-specific one — exact meaning **[Unknown]** |
| `0x00000100` | input (read-only strap) | speaker-identification pins |

**[Confirmed]** — the three values partition exactly along output/strap lines on
every board in scope.

"Speaker protection" is the `speaker-protection` property on the amplifier node with
`speaker-config` (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled). "Built-in mics" is the receive channel
count of the low-power microphone capture endpoint, which agrees with
`/product/audio`'s `supportedChannels`/`enabledChannels`/`historyChannels` mask on
every board (`0x7` = 3 channels, `0x3` = 2 channels). **[Confirmed]**

### 1.2.1 How a driver reads the board code

Every per-machine table in this document — here, in §1.6, §1.7, and in Sections 7, 8,
9 and 16 — is keyed by **board code**. The board code is carried by platform firmware on
the **root node** of the hardware description, in four properties:

| Root-node property | Form | Example (14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro) |
|---|---|---|
| `target-type` | board code, mixed case, no suffix | `J714s` |
| `target-sub-type` | board code + 2-character board-revision class suffix | `J714sAP` |
| `compatible` | string list; the **first** entry equals `target-sub-type` | `J714sAP`, then the model identifier |
| `model` | model identifier | `Mac17,9` |

`target-type` is the shortest reliable key and is the one this document's tables use,
lower-cased. `model` is an equally usable key and is the one printed alongside the board
code in Section 16's headings. Neither is on any bus: both are read out of the
firmware-supplied hardware description at probe time, before any audio block is touched.
**[Confirmed]** — both properties are present, non-empty and mutually consistent on all
56 board descriptions examined, baseline and in scope, and the board-code-to-model
mapping they carry agrees with Section 16 board for board.

Complete mapping for the boards in scope:

| `target-type` | `target-sub-type` | `model` | Board code used in this document |
|---|---|---|---|
| `J604` | `J604AP` | `Mac16,1` | j604 |
| `J623` | `J623AP` | `Mac16,2` | j623 |
| `J624` | `J624AP` | `Mac16,3` | j624 |
| `J713` | `J713AP` | `Mac16,12` | j713 |
| `J715` | `J715AP` | `Mac16,13` | j715 |

| `J616s` | `J616sAP` | `Mac16,7` | j616s |
| `J616c` | `J616cAP` | `Mac16,5` | j616c |

**This is a different mechanism from the speaker-identification straps of §1.10.** The
board code selects the machine; the straps select a **speaker-module variant within one
board** and are read from GPIO pins after the board code is already known. A driver needs
both, in that order: board code first to pick the per-machine table, straps second to pick
the calibration variant within it (Section 15 §15.3).

## 1.3 Speaker driver complement and slot map

> **⚠ Safety rule. Never infer a transducer role from a slot group number.** Slot
> group 2 is a *tweeter* on the MacBook Air chassis and the iMac, and — per the
> platform hardware description — a *second woofer* on the MacBook Pro 14/16-inch
> chassis. Woofer excursion and thermal limits applied to a tweeter can destroy it;
> on the 15-inch Air the tweeters have roughly three times the thermal resistance of
> the woofers, so the error is not marginal. The role must come from a per-chassis
> table.

The amplifier array is described by a set of `audio-control,sn012776` nodes on one or
two I²C buses. Node names are functional and state the transducer each part feeds
directly (`audio-speaker-left-tweeter`, `audio-speaker-right-woofer-2`, …); the node
that also carries `speaker-config`, `bop-config` and the shared GPIO bindings is
named plainly `audio-speaker` and is the left woofer (the first woofer of the left
side where there are two) on every multi-amplifier board in scope.

**The binding from slot group to amplifier is the `speaker1…speakerN` phandle chain
on that node, read together with the node names.** The node carrying `speaker-config`
is slot group 0 and `speakerK` is slot group K.

### 1.3.1 What is universal, and what is not

`speaker-config` and `amp-tx-zd-config` are byte-identical across all 30
six-amplifier boards from the M1 Pro generation onward. On four-amplifier
`sn012776` boards `speaker-config` is byte-identical from the M2 generation onward,
but `amp-tx-zd-config` is byte-identical only from the **M3** generation onward: the
M2 four-amplifier boards store `F0 F0 FF FF` / `0F 0F FF FF` where M3 and later
store `F0 F0 F0 FF` / `0F 0F 0F FF` (§1.8.3). Both crop to the same 16-bit mask, so
the effective idle mask is unchanged, but the stored bytes are not. That fixes the slot
**geometry** — slot count, slot widths, sense slot numbers, idle masks — across the
generation boundary. It does **not** fix which transducer sits in which slot.
**[Confirmed]**

**Universal — slot group to I²C address.** Identical on every board, M1 through M5,
on both chassis families:

| Slot group | Playback slot | I-sense slot | V-sense slot | Address (6-amp) | Address (4-amp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0x38 | 0x38 |
| 1 | 1 | 4 | 6 | 0x3b | 0x3b |
| 2 | 2 | 8 | 10 | 0x39 | 0x39 |
| 3 | 3 | 12 | 14 | 0x3c | 0x3c |
| 4 | 4 | 16 | 18 | 0x3a | — |
| 5 | 5 | 20 | 22 | 0x3d | — |

On M1 the amplifier was a **different part family at different addresses** — 0x31,
0x32, 0x34 and 0x35 in the published tree for that chassis, with the jack codec at
0x48. The 0x38–0x3D block arrived with the present part family at the M2 generation and
is unchanged through M5, so an address map carried forward from an M1 machine will not
match anything in scope. **[Confirmed]** (§6 §6.2.)

**Not universal — the transducer at a given address.** This is a per-chassis
property:

| Address | MacBook Pro 14/16-inch | MacBook Air 15-inch | MacBook Air 13-inch / iMac 24-inch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x38 | Left woofer 1 | Left woofer 1 | Left woofer |
| 0x39 | **Left woofer 2** | **Left tweeter** | **Left tweeter** |
| 0x3a | **Left tweeter** | **Left woofer 2** | — |
| 0x3b | Right woofer 1 | Right woofer 1 | Right woofer |
| 0x3c | **Right woofer 2** | **Right tweeter** | **Right tweeter** |
| 0x3d | **Right tweeter** | **Right woofer 2** | — |

**[Confirmed]** on two independent sources — the amplifier node names in the platform
hardware description, and the published device trees for the predecessor of each
chassis, which agree with them address for address on both chassis families.

### 1.3.2 The tweeter slot group on the MacBook Pro chassis is contested

The two sources agree completely on the 15-inch Air chassis and on every
four-amplifier machine. On the MacBook Pro 14/16-inch chassis they disagree, and only
about which slot group each of two addresses occupies:

| Source | 0x39 (left woofer 2) | 0x3a (left tweeter) | 0x3c (right woofer 2) | 0x3d (right tweeter) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform hardware description | group 2, sense 8/10 | group 4, sense 16/18 | group 3, sense 12/14 | group 5, sense 20/22 |
| Published trees for the M1 Pro/Max, M3 and M3 Pro/Max boards of this chassis | group 4, sense 16/18 | group 2, sense 8/10 | group 5, sense 20/22 | group 3, sense 12/14 |

So the platform description puts the **tweeters in slot groups 4 and 5** on this
chassis, while the published trees put them in **groups 2 and 3**. The published
trees are hardware-tested; the platform description is primary and is internally
uniform (it uses the same slot-group-to-address assignment on every board of every
chassis, whereas the published trees use one assignment on the Air and the opposite
on the MacBook Pro). Neither consideration is decisive on its own.

**This document follows the platform hardware description**, i.e. tweeters at groups
4 and 5 on the MacBook Pro chassis. That choice is recorded as **[Probable]** — the
platform-description reading is adopted; see §8 §8.2.4 for the role-order reading
that would reconcile every source, and for the `TDM_CFG6` / `TDM_CFG3` readback that
settles it — not [Confirmed], and it is Open question 1. A driver must not apply
per-transducer excursion or thermal limits on the MacBook Pro chassis, and must not
drive the speakers on that chassis at all, until the binding has been settled on
hardware by reading the amplifier receive-slot and transmit-slot registers back
(§1.4.2).

**A third possibility reconciles everything.** If the record index is a canonical
**role** order — woofer 1 left/right, tweeter left/right, woofer 2 left/right — rather
than the phandle-chain position, then the platform description and the published trees
agree on **every** chassis and no conflict exists anywhere. Nothing in the platform
description states such an order, so it is not provable and it is not the reading this
document adopts; but it is the parsimonious explanation and it is the one that would
dissolve the disagreement rather than decide it. See §8 §8.2.4, which sets the two
readings side by side, and §1.4.2 for the readback that settles the binding on
hardware.

Note that the left/right link split of §1.4.7 is **unaffected** by this question: the
two contested addresses are on the same side of the machine either way, so link A
remains the left-hand amplifiers and link B the right-hand ones under both readings.

### 1.3.3 Six-driver machines

| Chassis | Boards in scope | Group 0 | Group 1 | Group 2 | Group 3 | Group 4 | Group 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MacBook Pro 14/16-inch | j604, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j704, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c | L woofer 1, 0x38 | R woofer 1, 0x3b | **L woofer 2, 0x39** | **R woofer 2, 0x3c** | **L tweeter, 0x3a** | **R tweeter, 0x3d** |
| MacBook Air 15-inch | j715, j815 | L woofer 1, 0x38 | R woofer 1, 0x3b | **L tweeter, 0x39** | **R tweeter, 0x3c** | **L woofer 2, 0x3a** | **R woofer 2, 0x3d** |

The MacBook Pro row is subject to §1.3.2: on that chassis the record-to-transducer
binding is **[Probable]** and must be confirmed by amplifier register readback before
the speakers are driven (§1.4.2). The 15-inch Air row is **[Confirmed]** on both
sources.

Bus placement: on the base dies (t8132, t8142) all six parts are on `i2c3`; on the
Pro/Max dies (t604x, t605x) the three left-hand parts (0x38, 0x39, 0x3a) are on
`i2c1` and the three right-hand parts (0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d) on `i2c3`.

Two woofers per side in a force-cancelling pair plus one tweeter per side.
**[Confirmed]**

### 1.3.4 Four-driver machines

Boards: **j713, j813** (MacBook Air 13-inch), **j623, j624** (iMac 24-inch)

| Slot group | Driver | I²C address | Bus | Playback slot | I-sense slot | V-sense slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Left woofer | 0x38 | i2c3 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| 1 | Right woofer | 0x3b | i2c3 | 1 | 4 | 6 |
| 2 | Left tweeter | 0x39 | i2c3 | 2 | 8 | 10 |
| 3 | Right tweeter | 0x3c | i2c3 | 3 | 12 | 14 |

**[Confirmed]** — identical to the published, hardware-tested M2/M3 13-inch Air map,
address for address and slot for slot, and byte-identical in `speaker-config` to it.

On the two iMac boards the amplifier node names carry no `-1`/`-2` suffix (a single
woofer per side), the amplifier output level differs (§1.4.3), and the sense return
is **not** captured (§1.4.5).

### 1.3.5 Single-driver machines

Boards: **j773g** (Mac mini M4), **j773s** (Mac mini M4 Pro), **j575c** (Mac Studio)

| Slot group | Driver | I²C address | Bus | Playback slot | I-sense slot | V-sense slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Single full-range driver | 0x38 | i2c3 (j773g) / i2c1 (j773s, j575c) | 0 | 0 | 2 |

`speaker-config` has exactly one record; `speaker1…N` and `amp-tx-zd-config` are
absent; `speaker-protection` is 0; the speaker stream declares one transmit channel
and no receive channel. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.3.6 j700 (A18 Pro, MacBook Neo) — structurally different

There is **no** amplifier node on any I²C bus. The amplifier is described by a node
named `audio-speaker` that is a direct child of `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` with
`compatible = "audio-control,max98360"`, `device_type = "audio-control"` and:

| Property | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `num-channels` | 2 | two amplifier channels on one serial link |
| `function-reset` | GPIO controller `/arm-io/gpio0`, pin 105, flags `0x00010001` | single shutdown/mode line for both channels |
| `samplerate-subset` | `48000, 0` (u64 list, zero-terminated) | 48 kHz only |
| `mute-ramp-sleep-ms` | 20 | mute ramp settling time, 20 ms |
| `enable-iop-ramp-down` | empty (boolean) | ramp-down performed by the always-on coprocessor |
| `iboot-audio-volume` | empty (boolean) | boot-time volume handover, as on the other boards |

There is no `speaker-config`, no `bop-config`, no `amp-dcblocker-config`, no
`amp-tx-zd-config`, no sense slots, no per-amplifier interrupt and no speaker-ID
strap, because the part family has no control bus at all. Channel assignment
(left/right) must therefore be by pin strap on the board; the platform description
carries nothing about it — **[Unknown]**. Two mono parts sharing one shutdown line
and one two-slot I²S link is the only reading consistent with `num-channels = 2`, a
single `function-reset` and a stereo 32-bit transmit stream — **[Inferred]**.

## 1.4 `speaker-config` — definitive decode

### 1.4.1 Record layout

`speaker-config` is an array of **4-byte records, one per amplifier**, in amplifier
index order:

| Byte | Field | Units |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Amplifier index **and** that amplifier's receive (playback) TDM slot number — structural, see §1.4.2 for the binding caveat | slot index, 32-bit slots |
| 1 | Amplifier analogue output level code | see §1.4.3 |
| 2 | Sense transmit slot **A** — the lower slot (`4n`), written to amplifier register `0x0E` | 8-bit slot units |
| 3 | Sense transmit slot **B** — the upper slot (`4n+2`), written to amplifier register `0x0F` | 8-bit slot units |

**[Confirmed]** for the record structure and for the destination of each byte.

☠ **Which of A and B carries voltage and which carries current is [Probable],
not Confirmed.** The naming-independent statement is the [Confirmed] one: this
platform writes `4n` into amplifier register `0x0E` and `4n+2` into `0x0F`,
while the published upstream trees write the two **exchanged** into the same two
registers. The identification of `0x0E` as the voltage-sense slot rests on the
mainline driver headers for the counterpart part and its sibling — one family of
sources sharing one convention, not two independent lines — and the coprocessor
cannot distinguish the two channels at all, so the controller side cannot
arbitrate. §8 §8.2.1 gives both readings and the two-load bench test that
resolves it; §00 carries the hazard of mixing the two conventions.

Byte 0 is a genuine index field and not merely the record's position: on one
baseline board (the M1 13-inch MacBook Pro) the four records appear in the positional
order 0, 2, 1, 3. On **every** board in scope the records are in ascending positional
order, so for the machines documented here position and index coincide.
**[Confirmed]**

### 1.4.2 Which byte is the playback slot

The playback slot is **byte 0**, the index byte — there is no separate playback-slot
byte. Bytes 2 and 3 are both transmit (sense-return) slots. That is a statement about
the record's **structure**; what it does not settle is which physical transducer each
record describes, which is the subject of the second half of this subsection.

The mapping "group k → playback slot k" and "group k → sense slot A at 4k, sense
slot B at 4k+2" reproduces the published, hardware-tested slot maps exactly in **both**
directions for every published machine, four- and six-amplifier alike. On the M1
machines — whose amplifier variant's public counterpart has no current/voltage sense
at all — both slot bytes of every record are `00 00`, and they are populated from the
M2 generation onward, which is the behaviour of a sense-slot field and not of anything
to do with playback. The arithmetic closes: 4k and 4k+2 on an 8-bit grid with 16-bit
words exactly fills the same 32-bit region of the frame that playback slot k occupies,
for every k, with no gaps and no overlap. **[Confirmed]** for the record structure.

**The structure is [Confirmed]; the record-to-transducer binding is not.** Which
physical transducer a given record describes rests on the phandle-chain reading
adopted in §1.3.2, which the published upstream maps contradict on the MacBook Pro
14/16-inch chassis. The binding is therefore **[Probable]** on the MacBook Pro
chassis and **[Confirmed]** on every other machine in scope, and that uncertainty
applies **equally** to the playback slot and to the sense slots, because both come
from the same record.

A wrong binding is not a labelling error. In the playback direction it delivers
woofer content to a tweeter — full-band low-frequency energy into a driver whose safe
continuous dissipation is of the order of 1 W — and it does so **upstream of every
protection mechanism**: the sense channels faithfully report the power delivered,
merely attributed to the wrong driver, so the thermal model sees nothing wrong. In
the capture direction it misattributes sense. **Before driving the speakers on a
MacBook Pro chassis machine, read the receive-slot register (`TDM_CFG3`, page 0,
0x0C) and the sense transmit-slot registers (`TDM_CFG5`, 0x0E; `TDM_CFG6`, 0x0F) back
from every amplifier on a running system and confirm the binding.** A wrong binding
is destructive and is not detectable from the platform description alone. See §8
§8.2.3, §8 §8.2.4 and Open question 1.

### 1.4.3 Byte 1 — the constant byte selects the amplifier analogue output level

Byte 1 is not a slot. It is the amplifier's analogue full-scale output level code, in
the encoding of the public counterpart part's amplifier-level field (page 0,
register 0x03, bits 5:1 on the TAS2764; the same field with a different bit position
on the TAS2770). The published scale is 11.0 dBV at code 0, 0.5 dB per step, maximum
code 0x14.

| Code | Level (dBV) | Full-scale output (V rms) | Machines |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0f (15) | 18.5 | 8.41 | j604, j713, j715, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j704, j813, j815, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c, **and j773g, j773s** |
| 0x12 (18) | 20.0 | 10.00 | j623, j624 |
| 0x14 (20) | 21.0 | 11.22 | j575c |
| 0x0a (10) | 16.0 | 6.31 | *(baseline machines only: M1 13-inch Air, M2 Ultra Mac Pro)* |

**Per-machine change in scope — the M4 Mac mini output level dropped.** j773g and
j773s carry code 0x0f = 18.5 dBV where every earlier Mac mini board, and every Mac
Studio board including the in-scope j575c, carries code 0x14 = 21.0 dBV. That is a
2.5 dB reduction in full-scale output, 11.22 V rms → 8.41 V rms, and it is the only
change to an amplifier electrical setting anywhere in this scope. A driver that
carries a level value forward from an earlier Mac mini will over-drive these
machines. The 24-inch iMac boards j623 and j624 are by contrast **unchanged** from
the M3 iMac at 20.0 dBV. **[Confirmed]**

**[Confirmed]** — four distinct values across the board population, all inside the
published field range 0…0x14, and correlating with machine class (portable, all-in-one,
desktop) rather than with amplifier count or slot layout.

The field is per-record, so the format permits a different level per amplifier; no
board in scope uses that freedom — every record on a given board carries the same
code. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.4.4 Slot geometry

| Quantity | Value | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Playback slot width | 32 bits | **[Confirmed]** (carried explicitly in the stream descriptor, §11 §11.7.3) |
| Playback sample width | 24 bits, left-justified in the 32-bit slot | **[Confirmed]** |
| Sense slot grid | 8 bits | **[Confirmed]** |
| Sense word width | 16 bits = two 8-bit slots | **[Confirmed]** |
| Sense quantities per amplifier | 2 (slot **A** then slot **B**) = 4 slot positions = 32 bits | **[Confirmed]** for the count and the slot positions; which is voltage and which current is **[Probable]** — see below |
| Playback slots per frame | N (N = amplifier count) | **[Confirmed]** |
| Sense slot positions per frame | 4N on the 8-bit grid | **[Confirmed]** |
| Data bits per direction | 32 × N | **[Confirmed]** |
| **Frame length** | **250 bit clocks** on every `sn012776` machine in scope, whatever N; **256** on j700 | **[Confirmed]** |
| **Bit clock** | **12.000 MHz** on every `sn012776` machine in scope; **12.288 MHz** on j700 | **[Confirmed]** |

☠ **The sense row names slot positions, not quantities.** Slot **A** is the
lower slot (`4n`, amplifier register `0x0E`) and slot **B** the upper (`4n+2`,
register `0x0F`); the two slots, their order and their widths are
**[Confirmed]**. **Which of the two carries the voltage sense and which the
current sense is [Probable], not Confirmed**: under the mainline naming A is
voltage and B is current, under the exchanged naming A is current and B is
voltage. The two candidate sources share one convention and neither the host nor
the coprocessor can distinguish the two quantities, so the controller side
cannot arbitrate. §1.4.1 and §8 §8.2.1 give both readings and the two-load bench
test that resolves it; §1.4.5, §7 §7.5.1, §9 open question 5, §16 and §18
§18.5.5 all name the slots by position and carry the attribution no higher than
[Probable].

Each amplifier therefore owns exactly one 32-bit region of the frame in **both**
directions: a 24-in-32 playback sample on the receive line, and its two 16-bit
sense words on the transmit line.

**The frame length does not track the amplifier count.** It is fixed at 250 bit
clocks and the surplus is idle:

| Amplifiers | Data bits per direction | Frame length | Idle bit clocks | Bit clock @ 48 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32 | 250 | 218 | 12.000 MHz |
| 4 | 128 | 250 | 122 | 12.000 MHz |
| 6 | 192 | 250 | 58 | 12.000 MHz |

**[Confirmed]** — 12 000 000 ÷ 250 = 48 000 Hz exactly; the link descriptor in
the platform hardware description carries both figures directly (§11 §11.7.3),
and the amplifier's own bit-clock-to-frame-rate register has a code for 250
(§18 §18.4.4). An earlier version of this table derived the bit clock from the
data-bit count and gave 1.536 / 6.144 / 9.216 MHz; those figures are withdrawn.

### 1.4.5 Sense capture channel order

The sense-return stream presents 2N channels of 16-bit PCM. Channel 2k carries
amplifier k's sense slot **A** (the lower slot) and channel 2k+1 its slot **B**,
following the slot order. **[Confirmed]** for the channel order — the receive
channel mask in the stream descriptor is exactly `(1 << 2N) - 1`, and the
ordering follows from the slot numbers. **[Probable]** for which of A and B is
voltage; see §1.4.1 and §8 §8.2.1.

Sense capture is **absent** on j623, j624, j773g, j773s and j575c: those boards
declare `speaker-protection = 0` and their speaker stream endpoint has no receive
channel at all, even though `speaker-config` still carries nominal sense slot numbers.
A driver must take the endpoint's receive channel mask, not `speaker-config`, as the
authority on whether sense data exists. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.4.6 Cross-check against the published slot maps

| Chassis | Published tree for a predecessor board | Agreement with the platform description |
|---|---|---|
| MacBook Air 13-inch, 4 amplifiers | M2 and M3 13-inch Air | **exact** — address for address, slot for slot, in both directions |
| MacBook Air 15-inch, 6 amplifiers | M2 15-inch Air | **exact** — address for address, slot for slot |
| iMac 24-inch, 4 amplifiers | M3 iMac | `speaker-config` differs only in the level byte, which is the same on both (0x12) |
| MacBook Pro 14/16-inch, 6 amplifiers | M1 Pro/Max, M3, M3 Pro/Max 14/16-inch | agree on which part is which transducer; **disagree on which slot group the parts at 0x39/0x3a and 0x3c/0x3d occupy** — see §1.3.2 and Open question 1 |

Two further observations about the published trees, for anyone consulting them
directly. The published tree for the M3 15-inch Air describes only four amplifiers,
whereas the platform description for that board and for both in-scope 15-inch Air
boards lists six; the six-amplifier map is the correct one for that chassis. And the
published four-amplifier trees assign the two transmit idle masks to the opposite
links from the six-amplifier trees and from the platform description (§1.8.3).

### 1.4.7 Link split — which amplifiers share a serial link

`amp-tx-zd-config` (§1.8.3) pins this down. The amplifier in slot group 0 is told to
drive zeros in the byte groups belonging to the **odd**-numbered slot groups, and the
amplifier in slot group 1 is told to drive zeros in the byte groups belonging to the
**even**-numbered ones. That is only meaningful if the even-numbered groups sit on one
serial link and the odd-numbered ones on a second, each link's bus-keeper filling the
slots its own link does not use.

| Link | Slot groups | Drivers | Side | Bus-keeper (zero-fill) amplifier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0, 2, 4 (6-amp) / 0, 2 (4-amp) | left woofer 1, left tweeter, left woofer 2 | left | slot group 0 |
| B | 1, 3, 5 (6-amp) / 1, 3 (4-amp) | right woofer 1, right tweeter, right woofer 2 | right | slot group 1 |

Both links carry the **full-width** frame (32 × N bits), with each link using only its
own amplifiers' slots. **[Confirmed]** — the byte masks in the platform description
are the exact complement of the occupied slot groups on every board, and the same two
masks appear, on the same two links, as the published transmit-slot idle masks for the
equivalent M1 Pro/Max machines.

On single-amplifier boards `amp-tx-zd-config` is absent: one link, one amplifier, no
zero-fill duty. **[Confirmed]**

## 1.5 Serial audio cluster association

### 1.5.1 What the baseline said

On M1–M3 the platform description named the cluster and the port for every stream by
node path:

| Stream | Baseline node path | Cluster / port |
|---|---|---|
| Speaker array | `/arm-io/mca0/mca0a/audio-speaker` | base cluster 0, port a |
| Base-domain loopback | `/arm-io/mca1/mca1a/audio-loopback` | base cluster 1, port a |
| Jack codec playback | `/arm-io/mca2/mca2a/audio-codec-output` | base cluster 2, port a |
| Jack codec capture | `/arm-io/mca2/mca2b/audio-codec-input` | base cluster 2, port b |
| Built-in microphone array | `/arm-io/alc0/audio-leap-mic` | always-on cluster 0 |
| Low-power internal loopback | `/arm-io/alc4/audio-leap-internal-loopback` | always-on cluster 4 |

### 1.5.2 What the platform description says now

**Nothing about clusters.** On every board in scope the cluster nodes, the port
router node and the oscillator node are gone (on t8140 an oscillator node exists with
a `compatible` value and no `reg`). Stream endpoints are flat children of
`/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` (`compatible = "iop-audio,controller"`,
no `reg`).

What *is* expressed, and is all a driver has:

| Association available | Property | Values seen | What it distinguishes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serialiser family | `compatible` on the endpoint | `iop-adma-stream,mca`, `iop-adma-stream,leap` | base serial-audio domain vs low-power audio processor domain |
| Security domain | `device_type` on the endpoint | `iop-audio-ns`, `iop-audio-s` | non-secure vs secure stream |
| DMA controller instance | `dma-parent` (M4) or the `dma-provider-tx`/`dma-provider-rx` string prefix (A18 Pro, M5) | `admac-base-ns`, `admac-leap-ns`, `admac-leap-s` | which of the four audio DMA instances |
| DMA channel identity | `dma-channels` blob (M4) or channel name (A18 Pro, M5) | see §1.11 | which channel |
| Clock domain | `clock-domain` | `main` — **only** on the playback-tap endpoint, and only on A18 Pro / M5 boards | that the tap runs in the base ("main") clock domain |
| Stream identity | `identifier` (FourCC) | `spkr`, `cout`, `cin `, `lpbk`, `lilb`, `sllb`, `hpai`, `tap `, `lpij`, `lpai`, `adpx`, `lai ` | a stable per-stream tag |
| Power/clock gate | `function-admac_powerswitch` (M4 only), tag `aPSC`, provider = the DMA controller node | — | the DMA instance's power switch |

**Which serial audio cluster drives which group of amplifiers is not stated anywhere
in the platform description. [Unknown]**

### 1.5.3 What the power manager device list adds

The power-domain list in the same platform description is the only place where the
serial audio clusters are still enumerated. Decoded from the device list (48-byte
entries; name at bytes 32…47; device index at bytes 26…27, cross-checked by
resolving every `clock-gates` value elsewhere in the same description against it —
120 of 120 resolve on t8132, 148 of 148 on t604x, 162 of 164 on t6050; parent domain
index at bytes 4…7), the audio power-domain tree is **identical on all five SoCs in
scope**:

```
AUDIO_A                                   aggregate audio domain
└── AUDIO_FR
    ├── AUDIO_P                           base audio domain
    │   ├── AUDIO_BASE_S_A                base DMA, secure
    │   ├── AUDIO_BASE_NS_A               base DMA, non-secure
    │   ├── AUDIO_LEAP_MCA                low-power serial audio cluster
    │   └── AUDIO_MCA0_M … AUDIO_MCA5_M   six base serial audio cluster master clocks
    ├── AUDIO_LEAP_A
    │   └── AUDIO_LEAP_C                  low-power audio processor core domain
    │       ├── AUDIO_LEAP_S_A            low-power DMA, secure
    │       ├── AUDIO_LEAP_NS_A           low-power DMA, non-secure
    │       ├── AUDIO_LEAP_RX0 … RX4      five low-power receive stream domains
    │       └── AUDIO_LEAP_TX0            one low-power transmit stream domain
    └── AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC                  PDM converter — see the note below

PDM0_AUDIO_REF, PDM1_AUDIO_REF            PDM reference clocks, no parent
```

**[Confirmed]** — the same 25 domains, in the same parent relationship, on t8132,
t604x, t8140, t8142 and t6050/t605x.

Two structural points follow. First, `AUDIO_LEAP_MCA` — the low-power audio
processor's own serial audio cluster — is parented to `AUDIO_P`, the **base** audio
domain, not to `AUDIO_LEAP_A`; so the low-power serialiser's clock cannot be gated
independently of the base audio domain. Second, the five low-power receive stream
domains and the single low-power transmit stream domain are siblings of the two
low-power DMA domains under `AUDIO_LEAP_C`, which matches the baseline's five
always-on cluster nodes `alc0`…`alc4` exactly.

The baseline M3 list enumerated `MCA0`…`MCA3`, `SIO_ADMA`, `AOP_LEAP`,
`AOP_AUDIO_SHIM`, `AOP_AUDIO_ADMA0`, `AOP_MCA0`…`AOP_MCA3`, `AOP_PDMC0` and
`AOP_PDM0_REF`/`AOP_PDM1_REF`. So: the base cluster count went **4 → 6**; the four
always-on clusters collapsed to **one** cluster plus six explicit stream domains; and
the single audio DMA domain became **four** (base/low-power × secure/non-secure).
**[Confirmed]**

`AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC` is **not** a speaker-sense converter despite the name: it is a
one-for-one rename of the baseline generation's **microphone** PDM converter domain,
it is present identically on machines whose amplifiers have no sense capability at
all, and every speaker endpoint in scope returns its current/voltage sense as 16-bit
PCM in TDM slots. Do not infer a PDM sense path from the domain name.
**[Confirmed]**

The two amplifier links of §1.4.7 therefore occupy two of the six base clusters, and
the jack codec a third, but the mapping of link → cluster number is **[Unknown]** and
is a probing task. Gating `AUDIO_MCA0_M` … `AUDIO_MCA5_M` one at a time while a
stream runs is the direct experiment, and the domain tree above says it is safe to do
so without disturbing the DMA domains, which are siblings rather than children.

## 1.6 I²C buses and device addresses

### 1.6.1 Second word of an I²C child `reg`

The second u32 of an I²C child's `reg` is the **SCL clock period in nanoseconds**.
Exactly three values occur on any board of any generation:

| Value | Period | Bus frequency | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2500 | 2.5 µs | 400 kHz fast-mode nominal; **375 kHz achieved** (§6 §6.1.4) | **every audio device on every board**, plus most other fast-mode peripherals |
| 10000 | 10 µs | 100 kHz (standard mode) | power-delivery controllers, card readers, retimers |
| 2816 | 2.816 µs | ≈355 kHz | a small number of retimer nodes on some boards |

The third and fourth u32 are zero on every audio node. **[Confirmed]** — two of the
three values are exactly the two standard I²C bus rates, and no audio device deviates.

### 1.6.2 Per-machine bus and address map

Every amplifier and codec in scope requests a 2500 ns SCL period, i.e. **400 kHz**
fast-mode nominal. That is the requested ceiling, not the achieved rate: the
controller's divider yields **375 kHz** actual on every audio bus in scope
(§6 §6.1.4).

| Board | Amplifier bus(es) | Amplifier addresses | Jack codec bus | Jack codec address |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| j604 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j623 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3b, 0x3c | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j624 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3b, 0x3c | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j713 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3b, 0x3c | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j715 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j773g | i2c3 | 0x38 | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j614s / j614c / j616s / j616c | i2c1 (0x38, 0x39, 0x3a) + i2c3 (0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d) | as shown | i2c2 | 0x4b |
| j773s | i2c1 | 0x38 | i2c2 | 0x4b |
| j575c | i2c1 | 0x38 | i2c2 | 0x4b |
| **j700** | **none** | **none — no control bus** | **i2c0** | **0x48** |
| j704 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j813 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3b, 0x3c | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j815 | i2c3 | 0x38, 0x39, 0x3a, 0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d | i2c1 | 0x4b |
| j714s / j714c / j716s / j716c | i2c1 (0x38, 0x39, 0x3a) + i2c3 (0x3b, 0x3c, 0x3d) | as shown | i2c2 | 0x4b |

Structural rule: on the **base-die** boards (t8132, t8142) all amplifiers hang off a
single bus; on the **Pro/Max-die** boards (t604x, t605x) the left-side amplifiers are
on one bus and the right-side amplifiers on another, mirroring the two serial links
of §1.4.7. **[Confirmed]** — unchanged from the M1–M3 Pro/Max baseline.

All I²C controllers carry `compatible = "i2c,t8101"` on every SoC in scope — the
controller itself is unchanged from the baseline. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.7.3 Sharing

| Line | Shared or dedicated |
|---|---|
| Amplifier shutdown/reset | **Shared by all amplifiers on the machine** — declared once, on amplifier index 0 only; no other amplifier node carries `function-reset`. **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier interrupt | **Shared by all amplifiers on the machine** — declared once, on amplifier index 0 only. Level-type (`type = 1`). **[Confirmed]** |
| Speaker-ID strap 0 / 1 | Dedicated to the speaker-identification mechanism; inputs only. **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec interrupt | Dedicated to the jack codec. **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec reset | Dedicated to the jack codec. On t8132/t8142/t604x it is on the always-on "nub" controller; **on t6050/t605x it moved to the main controller** and on t8140 it is likewise on the main controller. **[Confirmed]** |

Note the consequence: with one shutdown line and one interrupt line for the whole
array, a driver cannot reset or mask a single amplifier through GPIO, and every
amplifier interrupt source must be polled over I²C on each edge.

### 1.7.4 Every `function-*` property on an audio node

| Property | Node | Tag | Arguments | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `function-reset` | amplifier index 0 (all boards with a control bus); `audio-speaker` control node on j700 | `GPIO` | pin, flags `0x00010001` | amplifier shutdown / mode line, shared |
| `function-speaker-id0` | amplifier index 0 | `GPIO` | pin, flags `0x100` | speaker module identification strap, bit 0 |
| `function-speaker-id1` | amplifier index 0 | `GPIO` | pin, flags `0x100` | speaker module identification strap, bit 1 |
| `function-reset` | jack codec | `GPIO` | pin, flags `0x1` | codec reset |
| `function-codecinput_master` | jack codec | `AUD1` | phandle → the `audio-codec-input` stream data node; one FourCC argument reading `ap2c` | binds the codec's clock-master role to the capture stream endpoint of the same link. On M1–M3 the phandle pointed at `/arm-io/mca2/mca2b/audio-codec-input`; on M4 and later at `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller/audio-codec-input/audio-codec-input`. **[Confirmed]** |
| `function-codecinput_active` | jack codec, **M1–M3 only** | `i2sR` | phandle → the port router node; FourCC argument reading `pin2` | selected the router pin for the codec capture link. **Absent on every board in scope** — the function has moved behind the always-on coprocessor. **[Confirmed]** |
| `function-admac_powerswitch` | every stream endpoint, **M4 only** (t8132, t604x) | `aPSC` | no arguments; phandle → the endpoint's audio DMA controller node | power switch for the DMA instance. Absent on t8140/t8142/t605x, where the DMA binding is by name instead. **[Confirmed]** |
| `function-input_power_enable` | microphone capture data node, **j700 only** | `pKW8` | phandle → the system power controller's power-management node; three u32 arguments, the first reading as a FourCC | microphone supply enable through the system power controller rather than a GPIO. **[Probable]** |
| `function-iommu_handler` | DMA proxy nodes (A18 Pro, M5) | `sdpr` | phandle → the shared address-translation proxy node | address-translation handler binding for the secure stream proxy |

## 1.8 Amplifier part variant and per-machine configuration tables

### 1.8.1 Part variant

| Boards | `compatible` (control) | `compatible` (data) | Public counterpart |
|---|---|---|---|
| all except j700 | `audio-control,sn012776` | `audio-data,sn012776` | TAS2764 (mono Class-D with I/V sense) |
| j700 | `audio-control,max98360` | `audio-data,max98360` | MAX98360A (mono Class-D, pin-strapped, no control bus) |

No board in scope carries an SSM3515 — **refuted** for this scope. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.8.2 `bop-config` — brown-out prevention register block

24 bytes, written to 24 consecutive amplifier registers starting at the brown-out
configuration register (page 0, register 0x1D on the public counterpart). The value
is **byte-identical on every board from M1 through M5**, and identical to the
brown-out preset published for this part variant in the upstream Linux support for
the public counterpart. **[Confirmed]**

| Register (page 0) | Value | Register | Value | Register | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x1D | 0x01 | 0x25 | 0x06 | 0x2D | 0x30 |
| 0x1E | 0x32 | 0x26 | 0x32 | 0x2E | 0x02 |
| 0x1F | 0x02 | 0x27 | 0x46 | 0x2F | 0x06 |
| 0x20 | 0x22 | 0x28 | 0x30 | 0x30 | 0x3E |
| 0x21 | 0x83 | 0x29 | 0x02 | 0x31 | 0x37 |
| 0x22 | 0x2D | 0x2A | 0x06 | 0x32 | 0x30 |
| 0x23 | 0x80 | 0x2B | 0x38 | 0x33 | 0xFF |
| 0x24 | 0x02 | 0x2C | 0x40 | 0x34 | 0xE6 |

Because the block is invariant it carries no per-machine information; the per-machine
content of this area is the brown-out *source* selection bit in the power-control
register, which the platform description does not carry. **[Unknown]**

### 1.8.3 `amp-tx-zd-config` — transmit zero-drive (bus-keeper) table

8 bytes per amplifier, in amplifier index order:

| Offset | Field | Units |
|---|---|---|
| 0…3 | transmit zero-drive byte mask, LSB = byte 0 of the frame; padding bytes beyond the frame are 0xFF | one bit per 8 bit clocks of the frame |
| 4…7 | zero on every board; a second mask field, purpose **[Unknown]** | not determined |

Only indices 0 and 1 are non-zero on every board; indices 2…5 are all-zero, i.e. only
the two bus-keeper amplifiers drive idle slots.

| Board class | Index 0 mask (frame-cropped) | Index 1 mask (frame-cropped) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6-amplifier (j604, j715, j614s/c, j616s/c, j704, j815, j714s/c, j716s/c) | `0xF0F0F0` (24 bits) | `0x0F0F0F` (24 bits) | left link fills the right amplifiers' byte groups and vice versa |
| 4-amplifier (j713, j813) | `0xF0F0` (16 bits) | `0x0F0F` (16 bits) | as above |
| 4-amplifier iMac (j623, j624) | property absent | property absent | no sense return, no zero-drive |
| 1-amplifier (j773g, j773s, j575c) | property absent | property absent | one amplifier per link |

Raw stored form is `F0 F0 F0 FF 00 00 00 00` / `0F 0F 0F FF 00 00 00 00` on every
board in scope, byte-identical to the M1 Pro generation. The M2-generation
four-amplifier boards store `F0 F0 FF FF` / `0F 0F FF FF`, which crops to the same
16-bit mask; that padding change happened at the M3 generation and is a baseline-era
change, not an M4 delta. The mask must be cropped to *frame length in bytes* before
use, exactly as the public counterpart's published driver does. **[Confirmed]** —
the two mask values are also exactly the transmit-slot idle masks published for the
equivalent M1 Pro/Max machines, on the same two links, which independently confirms
both the property's meaning and the left/right link split of §1.4.7.

Target registers on the public counterpart: the four SDOUT high-impedance mask
registers (page 1, registers 0x3D…0x40), plus the force-zero enable bit in the
adjacent control register (page 1, register 0x45, bit 7).
**[Probable]** — register identification is from the public counterpart; the mask
values and their per-index placement are **[Confirmed]** from the platform description.

### 1.8.4 `amp-dcblocker-config` — amplifier analogue/sense configuration word

4 bytes: `01 <value> 00 00`. Byte 0 is an enable/count field (always 1); byte 1 is the
configuration word programmed into the amplifier; bytes 2–3 are zero.

| Value | Boards |
|---|---|
| `0x41` | j604, j713, j715, j773g, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j773s, j575c, j704, j813, j815, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c |
| `0x71` | **j623, j624** |
| (absent) | j700 |

The word carries four settings: the sense-path high-pass corner, spread-spectrum
modulation of the Class-D switching, the supply-measurement ADC filter, and thermal
foldback. On **every** machine in scope it decodes to a **2 Hz sense high-pass,
spread spectrum off, supply-ADC filter off, and thermal foldback off**.

The consequence is important enough to state plainly, and it belongs to the topology
because it determines what the host is responsible for: **the amplifier does not
autonomously reduce its gain as the die heats.** Overcurrent, brownout prevention
and the hard over-temperature shutdown remain active; the supply-tracking limiter
does **not** — it is left at its reset state with `LIM_EN` = 0 and registers 0x0B,
0x1B and 0x1C are not written by any platform-supplied configuration
(**[Probable]**, counterpart datasheet reset value,
not yet read back — §7 §7.7). Voice-coil thermal protection exists only in the
host. Any driver that relies on the part protecting itself thermally is wrong.
**[Confirmed]**

The two 24-inch iMac boards differ from every other board in scope in bits 5 and 4 of
the word (`0x71` versus `0x41`); bit 6 and the low three bits are common to both.
Thermal foldback is off on those boards too, so the difference lies in one or both of
the remaining two settings; which is **[Unknown]**, and it is the residual part of
Open question 5.

### 1.8.5 Other amplifier-node properties

| Property | Value | Boards | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speaker-protection` | 1 | j604, j713, j715, j614s/c, j616s/c, j704, j813, j815, j714s/c, j716s/c | I/V-sense based protection in use |
| `speaker-protection` | 0 | j623, j624, j773g, j773s, j575c | protection not used; no sense capture stream |
| `iboot-audio-volume` | empty (boolean) | all boards with an amplifier node | boot firmware leaves a volume setting in place to be honoured at handover |
| `private` | `"1"` | all audio control nodes | — |
| `external-power-provider` | phandle | **M1–M3 only** | absent on every board in scope |

### 1.9.1 Presence, part and bus

| Boards | Part | Public counterpart | Bus | Address | Interrupt | Reset |

| j700 | **`cs42l83`** | CS42L42 / CS42L83 | i2c0 | **0x48** | gpio0 pin 104, level | gpio0 pin 103 |

A jack codec is present on **every** board in scope, including the Mac mini and Mac
Studio boards. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.9.2 Configuration properties on the jack codec node — complete decode

| Property | Size | Value | Boards | Decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reg` | 16 B | address, 2500, 0, 0 | all | 7-bit address; 2500 ns SCL period = 400 kHz nominal, 375 kHz achieved (§6 §6.1.4) |
| `interrupt-parent` / `interrupts` | 4 B / 8 B | GPIO controller phandle; pin, type 1 | all | level-sensitive jack interrupt |
| `function-reset` | 16 B | GPIO, pin, flags `0x1` | all | dedicated reset output |
| `function-codecinput_master` | 12 B | tag `AUD1`, phandle → capture stream data node, FourCC `ap2c` | all | **master/slave role**: the codec is bound as the clock master of the capture direction of its link |
| `function-codecinput_active` | 12 B | tag `i2sR`, phandle → port router, FourCC `pin2` | **M1–M3 only** | port-router pin select; **absent in scope** |
| `internal-mclk-src` | 4 B | 1 | all | the codec runs from its **internal** master-clock source; no MCLK is supplied over the link. Corroborated by the stream descriptor, which declares reference clock 0 and a bit-clock ratio of 64 for this link on every board except j700 |
| `mic-config` | 8 B | `01 00 FF FF FF FF FF FF` | all except j700-absent? (present on j700 too) | **microphone bias / input selection**: byte 0 = 1 (microphone input enabled), byte 1 = 0 (input index 0), bytes 2…7 = 0xFF (six unused entries). Invariant across every board and both part variants. Byte-level reading **[Probable]**; invariance **[Confirmed]** |
| `enable-ringsense` | 4 B | 1 | all | RING-sense detection enabled |
| `ringsense-inverted` | 4 B | 1 | all | **ring-sense polarity inverted** on every board in scope |
| `enable-dcid` | 4 B | 1 | all | DC-based headset type identification enabled |
| `bits-per-sample-subset` | 4 B | 24 | all | **bit depth**: 24-bit samples |
| `samplerate-default` | 8 B | `00 00 00 00 80 BB 00 00` | all | **default sample rate**, encoded as a **32.32 fixed-point value in Hz** — 0x0000BB80_00000000 = 48000.0 Hz. **[Confirmed]**: the integer part lands in the upper 32 bits on every board, and the same encoding renders the j700 subset list correctly |
| `samplerate-subset` | 16 B | `48000.0, 0` (32.32 fixed point, zero-terminated list) | **j700 only** | the A18 Pro jack link supports 48 kHz only; every other board's capture stream advertises 48000, 44100, 88200 and 96000 |
| `PowerOffAtSleep` | 4 B | 1 | all | codec is powered off across sleep |
| `private` | 2 B | `"1"` | all | — |
| `external-power-provider` | 4 B | phandle | **M1–M3 only** | absent in scope |

Everything in that table is byte-identical across all 19 `cs42l84` boards in scope;
only `compatible`, `reg`, the GPIO bindings and `samplerate-subset` differ on j700.
**[Confirmed]**

## 1.10 Speaker module identification mechanism

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Enable flag | `find-speaker-id` = 1 on the amplifier index-0 node |
| Number of pins | **2** (`function-speaker-id0`, `function-speaker-id1`), both inputs (flags `0x100`) |
| Encoding | 2-bit code, bit 0 from `…-id0`, bit 1 from `…-id1` |
| Valid values | `valid-speaker-ids` = two u32 words: **0 and 3** |
| Boards with the mechanism | j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j704, j815, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c |
| Boards **without** it | j773g, j773s, j575c (single amplifier), **j813** (four amplifiers — the mechanism was dropped on the M5 13-inch Air, although the M4 13-inch Air has it), j700 (no control bus) |

`valid-speaker-ids` is invariant — `{0, 3}` — on every board from M1 through M5 that
has the mechanism. Only the two codes with both straps at the same level are valid;
codes 1 and 2 are not, which gives an unambiguous strap read and detects a broken
strap. **[Confirmed]**

Two valid codes means **two speaker module variants per machine**. Because the code
is read at the amplifier array level (one pair of pins for the whole array, on the
index-0 node), it selects a variant for the whole module, not per driver.

**Flag for the calibration section:** a speaker module variant implies a different
set of driver parameters — different voice-coil and magnet thermal resistances and
time constants, different nominal impedance, different temperature limits, and
possibly different sense scaling. Any per-machine calibration table must therefore be
indexed by `{board, speaker-id ∈ {0, 3}}`, not by board alone. The per-unit trim data
pointed at by `/product/audio` (§1.11.5) is orthogonal to this: the ID selects the
*model*, the per-unit store supplies the *trim*. **[Inferred]** — the platform
description states the mechanism and the valid values but not what the code selects.

## 1.11 Stream endpoint inventory

### 1.11.1 The container

```
/arm-io/iop-audio-controller
    compatible  = "iop-audio,controller"
    device_type = "iop-audio-controller"
    iop-audio-service-name = <name of a service on the always-on coprocessor>
    (no reg)
```

On t8140, t8142 and t605x the node additionally carries
`external-named-power-provider`, naming a power provider outside the audio tree.
Each child is one **stream endpoint**; each endpoint has exactly one child, the
**stream data node**, which carries the 36-byte `reg` descriptor whose values are
inventoried in §1.12 and whose field layout is §11 §11.7.3.

A second, parallel container `/arm-io/iop-voicetrigger-controller`
(`compatible = "iop-audio,controller"`,
`device_type = "iop-voicetrigger-controller"`) exists on every board with built-in
microphones; see §1.14.

### 1.11.2 Endpoint catalogue

| Endpoint node | `identifier` | Serialiser family | Direction(s) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-speaker` | `spkr` | `mca` (`leap` on j700) | TX (+ RX where sense exists) | speaker array playback and I/V sense return |
| `audio-speaker` (second node, j700 only) | `spkr` | — (`audio-control,max98360`) | — | the amplifier control node itself |
| `audio-speaker-tap` | `tap ` | `mca` | RX | post-mix tap of the speaker playback stream |
| `audio-codec-output` | `cout` | `mca` | TX | jack codec playback |
| `audio-codec-input` | `cin ` | `mca` | RX | **headset microphone** capture, through the jack codec |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | `lpbk` | `mca` | TX + RX | base-domain serial loopback |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback` | `lilb` | `leap` | TX + RX | low-power-domain internal loopback |
| `audio-secure-leap-loopback` | `sllb` | `leap` | TX + RX | **secure** low-power loopback (t6050/t605x only) |
| `audio-hp` (M4) / `audio-hp-mic` (A18 Pro, M5) | `hpai` | `leap` | RX | **built-in digital microphone array** capture — *not* the headset microphone, despite the node name |
| `lp-mic-injection-device` | `lpij` | `mca` | TX | low-power microphone injection (test/insertion path) |
| `lp-mic-device` | `lpai` | — | — | low-power microphone logical device |
| `lp-mic-io-buffer-device` | `adpx` | — | — | shared buffer for the low-power microphone path |
| `siri-listening-device` | `lai ` | — | — | always-listening client manager device |

### 1.11.3 DMA channel bindings — M4 generation (t8132, t604x)

M4 boards bind DMA by a 128-byte `dma-channels` blob, not by name. Layout:

| Record | Offset | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0x00 | transmit channel record |
| 1 | 0x20 | receive channel record |
| 2 | 0x40 | duplicate of record 0 with field 1 = 0x22 instead of 0x21 |
| 3 | 0x60 | duplicate of record 1 with field 1 = 0x22 instead of 0x21 |

Each 32-byte record:

| Word | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | channel number, or `0xFFFFFFFF` = direction not present | see below |
| 1 | `0x21` in records 0–1, `0x22` in records 2–3 | selector distinguishing the two otherwise identical copies; meaning **[Unknown]** |
| 2 | 0 | — |
| 3 | buffer size, bytes | |
| 4 | second size, bytes — equals half word 3 for every endpoint except the low-power loopback | threshold/watermark **[Probable]** |
| 5–7 | 0 | — |

The channel number is a **flat index in which transmit channels are even and receive
channels odd**: flat index = 2 × channel + (0 for TX, 1 for RX). This maps exactly
onto the named channels used by the later generations. **[Confirmed]** — the mapping
reproduces every A18 Pro / M5 channel name for every endpoint that exists on both.

| Endpoint | TX flat index → named channel | RX flat index → named channel | Buffer / threshold (bytes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-speaker` (6 amps) | 0 → `base-ns-adma-tx-0` | 1 → `base-ns-adma-rx-0` | 0x480 / 0x240 |
| `audio-speaker` (4 amps, sense) | 0 → `base-ns-adma-tx-0` | 1 → `base-ns-adma-rx-0` | 0x300 / 0x180 |
| `audio-speaker` (4 amps, iMac) | 0 → `base-ns-adma-tx-0` | none | 0x300 / 0x180 |
| `audio-speaker` (1 amp) | 0 → `base-ns-adma-tx-0` | none | 0xC0 / 0x60 |
| `audio-codec-output` | 4 → `base-ns-adma-tx-2` | none | 0x300 / 0x180 |
| `audio-codec-input` | none | 5 → `base-ns-adma-rx-2` | 0x180 / 0xC0 |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | 6 → `base-ns-adma-tx-3` | 7 → `base-ns-adma-rx-3` | 0xC0 / 0x60 |
| `audio-hp` | none | 1 → `leap-ns-adma-rx-0` | 0x240 / 0x120 |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback` | 8 → `leap-ns-adma-tx-4` | 9 → `leap-ns-adma-rx-4` | 0x300 / 0xC0 and 0x3C0 / 0x180 |

`dma-parent` is `/arm-io/admac-base-ns` for the `mca`-family endpoints and
`/arm-io/admac-leap-ns` for the `leap`-family ones; `external-power-provider` points
at the same node, and `function-admac_powerswitch` (tag `aPSC`) at it again.
Only two audio DMA controller nodes are instantiated on M4 boards
(`admac-base-ns`, `admac-leap-ns`), although the address-translation node declares
mappers for all four (`mapper-admac-base-ns`, `-base-s`, `-leap-ns`, `-leap-s`).
**[Confirmed]**

### 1.11.4 DMA channel bindings — A18 Pro and M5 generations

t8140, t8142, t6050 and t605x bind DMA by **string**: `dma-provider-tx` and
`dma-provider-rx` name a child node of the relevant audio DMA controller.

| Endpoint | j700 (t8140) | j704 / j813 / j815 (t8142) | j714s/c, j716s/c (t6050/t605x) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-speaker` | TX `leap-ns-adma-tx-0` (low-power domain!) | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-0`, RX `base-ns-adma-rx-0` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-0`, RX `base-ns-adma-rx-0` |
| `audio-speaker-tap` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-1` |
| `audio-codec-output` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-2` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-2` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-2` |
| `audio-codec-input` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-2` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-2` | RX `base-ns-adma-rx-2` |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-3`, RX `base-ns-adma-rx-3` | same | same |
| `lp-mic-injection-device` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-5` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-5` | TX `base-ns-adma-tx-5` |
| `audio-hp-mic` | RX `leap-s-adma-rx-0` (**secure**) | RX `leap-s-adma-rx-0` (**secure**) | RX `leap-s-adma-rx-0` (**secure**) |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback` | TX `leap-ns-adma-tx-4`, RX `leap-ns-adma-rx-4` | same | same |
| `audio-secure-leap-loopback` | — | — | TX `leap-ns-adma-tx-5`, RX `leap-s-adma-rx-5` (**secure**) |

DMA controller instances and their declared channel sets:

| Board class | `admac-base-ns` children | `admac-leap-ns` children | `admac-leap-s` children |
|---|---|---|---|
| j700 | tx-2, rx-2, rx-1, tx-3, rx-3, tx-5 | tx-0, tx-4, rx-4 | rx-0 |
| j704, j813, j815 | tx-0, rx-0, rx-1, tx-2, rx-2, tx-3, rx-3, tx-5 | rx-0, tx-4, rx-4 | rx-0 |
| j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c | tx-0, rx-0, rx-1, tx-2, rx-2, tx-3, rx-3, tx-5 | tx-4, rx-4, tx-5 | rx-0, rx-5 |

Per-channel nodes carry `compatible = "audio-dma-channel,v4p0"`,
`device_type = "adma-ch"`, `dma-stream-type` = FourCC `ISOC`, and explicit limits:

| Channel | `max-channel-count` | `max-bit-depth-bits` | `max-sample-rate-hz` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base-ns-adma-tx-2` / `rx-2` (jack codec) | 2 / 1 | 32 | 48000 |
| `base-ns-adma-tx-3` / `rx-3` (base loopback) | 2 | **16** | 48000 |
| `base-ns-adma-tx-5` (low-power mic injection) | 2 | 32 | **16000** |
| `leap-*-adma-*` | 2 | 32 | 48000 |

The DMA controller nodes carry `role` as a byte-reversed FourCC: `BANS` (base
non-secure), `LENS` (low-power non-secure), `LESS` (low-power secure). Their
`irq-destinations` list reads `AIC `, `ACPU`, `GTN `, `UNSD` with
`irq-destination-index = 0`. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.11.5 Secure-stream proxies (A18 Pro and M5 only)

| Node | Boards | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `/arm-io/admac-leap-s-rx-0-proxy` | j700, j704, j813, j815 | proxy for the secure microphone capture DMA channel; `use-case` = FourCC `hpai` |
| `/arm-io/admac-hp-mic-ec-proxy` | j714s/c, j716s/c | same role, renamed; `use-case` = FourCC `hpai`, `dma-channel` = 0 |
| `/arm-io/admac-sllb-ec-proxy` | j714s/c, j716s/c | proxy for the secure low-power loopback DMA channel; `use-case` = FourCC `sllb`, `dma-channel` = 5 |
| `/arm-io/audio-hp-mic-proxy` | all A18 Pro and M5 | `compatible = "iisaudio,isolated-stream-proxy"`, `device_type = "iis-ec-proxy"`, `identifier` = FourCC `hpai` |
| `/arm-io/audio-sllb-proxy` | j714s/c, j716s/c | same, `identifier` = FourCC `sllb` |
| `/arm-io/audio-shared-dart-proxy` | all A18 Pro and M5 | shared address-translation proxy; `usecase-dart-map` pairs the use-case FourCCs with mapper indices |

`physical-descriptions` on the stream proxies is a u32 array
`[size, sample rate, format FourCC, X, bytes per frame]`:

| Node | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `audio-hp-mic-proxy`, j700 | 15840, 48000, `lpcm`, 9, 8 | 48 kHz linear PCM, 8 bytes/frame = **2 channels** × 4 bytes |
| `audio-hp-mic-proxy`, j704/j813/j815/j714*/j716* | 15840, 48000, `lpcm`, 9, 12 | 12 bytes/frame = **3 channels** × 4 bytes |
| `audio-sllb-proxy`, j714*/j716* | 15840, 48000, `lpcm`, 9, 8 | stereo |

The bytes-per-frame field agrees with the microphone count on every board.
**[Confirmed]**; field 4 (the constant 9) is **[Unknown]**.

## 1.12 The stream data node `reg` blob — per-endpoint values

Every stream data node carries `reg` as 36 bytes.

> **The field layout is specified once, in §11 §11.7.3, and that subsection is
> the sole authority for it.** The decode this section previously carried is
> superseded and has been removed; it read byte `0x05` as a port-group tag,
> bytes `0x08`–`0x0b` as a reference clock and bytes `0x20`–`0x21` as
> undecoded flag bytes, and a driver built on it loses the data-delay and
> direction-mask fields that a key-`701` stream-configuration record requires
> (§18 §18.3.1). What remains here is the **per-endpoint value inventory**,
> relabelled against the authoritative field names. The one field the superseded
> decode named that §11.7.3's table does not resolve — the board-independent
> `0x0f` at byte `0x04` on the base-domain loopback endpoint — is preserved
> below and is **[Unknown]**.

### 1.12.1 Interface-class byte (`0x01`)

The same four values §11 §11.7.3 tabulates, listed here by endpoint:

| Code | Meaning | Endpoints |
|---|---|---|
| `0x02` | base-domain stream, no master clock owned | `audio-speaker` (all boards with `sn012776`), `audio-speaker-tap`, `lp-mic-injection-device` |
| `0x12` | base-domain stream, configuration immutable | `audio-mca-loopback` |
| `0x13` | master-clock-owning stream | `audio-codec-output`, `audio-codec-input`; **also the A18 Pro `audio-speaker` and `audio-speaker-tap`** |
| `0x42` | low-power-domain stream | `audio-hp`/`audio-hp-mic`, `audio-leap-internal-loopback`, `audio-secure-leap-loopback` |

That the A18 Pro speaker endpoint reads `0x13` (a master-clock-owning stereo
link) rather than `0x02` (base-domain, no master clock owned) is a direct
consequence of the amplifier change. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.12.2 Link channel count (`0x04`) and frame-wide slot width (`0x05`)

| Endpoint | `0x04` link channel count | `0x05` frame-wide slot width |
|---|---|---|
| `audio-speaker`, 6 amps with sense | `0x0c` = 12 (the sense direction) | `0x10` = 16 bits |
| `audio-speaker`, 4 amps with sense | `0x08` = 8 (the sense direction) | `0x10` = 16 bits |
| `audio-speaker`, 4 amps no sense (iMac) | `0x04` = 4 = amplifiers | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `audio-speaker`, 1 amp | `0x01` | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `audio-speaker`, j700 | `0x02` | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `audio-speaker-tap` | `0x06` / `0x04` / `0x02` = amplifier count | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `audio-codec-output` / `-input` | `0x02` | `0x20` = 32 bits (j700: `0x00`) |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | `0x0f` = 15 on **every** board — **does not equal either direction's channel count (both 2)**. **[Unknown]** | `0x10` = 16 bits |
| `audio-hp` / `audio-hp-mic` | microphone count (3; j700: 2) | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback`, `audio-secure-leap-loopback` | `0x02` | `0x00` = per-direction |
| `lp-mic-injection-device` | microphone count (3; j700: 2) | `0x00` = per-direction |

`0x04` is the channel count of the **wider** direction on every endpoint except
the base-domain loopback, whose `0x0f` is a board-independent constant that
matches neither direction. **A driver must not derive a channel count from
`0x04`** — take the per-direction counts at `0x1c`/`0x1d` and the masks at
`0x14`/`0x18` (§11 §11.7.3). The `0x0f` constant is **[Unknown]** and is §11
open question 40. The apparent correlation of `0x05` with link family — `0x10`
on the speaker and base-domain-loopback endpoints, `0x20` on the jack-codec
endpoints of the M4/M5 boards, `0x00` on j700 — is a consequence of those
families using 16-bit and 32-bit slots, not a port-group tag. **[Confirmed]**

### 1.12.3 Worked examples

Read against the layout of §11 §11.7.3.

| Board / endpoint | Raw `reg` (hex) | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| j604 `audio-speaker` | `0102 0000 0c10 0100 001b b700 fa00 0100 3000 0100 3f00 0000 ff0f 0000 060c 1810 0000 2010` | 12 link channels of 16-bit slots, data delay 1 bit clock, master clock 12 MHz, frame 250 bit clocks, frame-sync pulse 1 bit clock, 48 × 1000 ÷ 1 = 48 kHz, TX mask 0x3F (6 ch), RX mask 0xFFF (12 ch), 6 TX ch of 24 bits in 32-bit slots, 12 RX ch of 16 bits in 16-bit slots |
| j713 `audio-speaker` | `… 3f→0f, fff→ff, 0408 1810 …` | 4 TX ch, 8 RX ch, same widths |
| j623 `audio-speaker` | `… 0f00 0000 0000 0000 0400 1800 0000 2000` | 4 TX ch 24-in-32, **no RX** |
| j773g `audio-speaker` | `… 0100 0000 0000 0000 0100 1800 0000 2000` | 1 TX ch 24-in-32, no RX |
| j700 `audio-speaker` | `0113 0000 0200 0100 0080 bb00 0001 0100 3000 0100 0300 0000 0000 0000 0200 2000 0200 2000` | master-clock-owning link, master clock 12.288 MHz, frame 256 bit clocks, 48 kHz, 2 TX ch of 32 bits in 32-bit slots, no RX; **direction mask `0x02` = transmit only** |
| j604 `audio-codec-output` | `0113 0000 0220 0100 0000 0000 4000 0100 0000 0000 0300 0000 0000 0000 0200 2020 0000 0000` | 32-bit slots, no master clock stated, frame 64 bit clocks, rate fields 0 = rate-agile, 2 TX ch of 32 bits |
| j604 `audio-hp-mic` | `0142 0000 0300 0100 001b b700 fa00 0100 3000 0100 0000 0000 0700 0000 0003 0020 0100 0000` | low-power stream, master clock 12 MHz, frame 250 bit clocks ⇒ 48 kHz, RX mask 0x7 (3 ch) of 32 bits; **direction mask `0x01` = receive only** |
| j704 `audio-speaker-tap` | `0102 0000 0600 0100 001b b700 fa00 0100 3000 0100 0000 0000 3f00 0000 0006 0018 0100 0020` | RX mask 0x3F (6 ch) of 24 bits in 32-bit slots; direction mask `0x01` = receive only, **receive data delay 0** |
| j714s `audio-speaker-tap` | `0102 0000 0600 0100 001b b700 fa00 0100 3000 0100 0000 0000 3f00 0000 0006 0018 0101 0020` | as j704 but **receive data delay 1** — see §2 §2.3.2 |
| j704 `lp-mic-injection-device` | `0102 0000 0300 0100 0000 0000 c000 0100 1000 0100 0700 0000 0000 0000 0300 1800 0000 2000` | no master clock stated, frame 192 bit clocks, **16 kHz**, 3 TX ch of 24 bits in 32-bit slots |
