## 7.1 Part identification and probing

### 7.1.1 The TI-family part (`sn012776`)

| Register | Address | Access | Reset | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REV_ID` | page 0, 0x7D | RO | **0x30** | `[7:4] REV_ID`, `[3:0] PG_ID` | Silicon revision / process-generation identifier |
| `I2C_CKSUM` | page 0, 0x7E | RW | 0x00 | `[7:0]` | Running checksum over every register write on all books and pages; writing it presets the accumulator |
| `BOOK` | page 0, 0x7F | RW | 0x00 | `[7:0]` | Book select; only book 0 is populated |

- **The host can read back a revision.** `REV_ID` at page 0 offset 0x7D returns
  **0x3x**: `REV_ID[7:4] = 3h`, `PG_ID[3:0]` unconstrained. Presence detection on
  these machines consists of reading 0x7D from each amplifier address in the
  group and requiring the **upper nibble to be 3h** (a device returning an upper
  nibble of 0h is also treated as present; any other value means "not this
  part"). [**Confirmed** — the acceptance rule applies on the in-scope
  machines and the value 0x30 is independently the published TAS2764 `REV_ID`
  reset value.]
- **Consequence for probing: `REV_ID` does not distinguish the Apple variant
  from a stock TAS2764.** Both read 0x3x. There is no chip-ID register anywhere
  in the map that identifies the variant. Selection of the variant-specific
  register writes of 7.6 must come from the platform `compatible` string, never
  from probing. [Confirmed]
- A read of 0x7D is nevertheless the correct liveness/presence test: it is
  cheap, non-destructive, and is performed **before any configuration** on every
  amplifier in the group. If any amplifier fails it, the group must not be
  brought up. [Probable]
- The device does **not** distinguish itself by I²C address either: the address
  is strapped, and the same six addresses (0x38–0x3D) are used on every machine.
  The address is re-sampled from the strap pin every time the shutdown pin is
  released. [Confirmed — datasheet]
- Those addresses are not the M1 ones. On M1 the amplifier was a **different part
  family at 0x31, 0x32, 0x34 and 0x35**, with the jack codec at 0x48; the
  0x38–0x3D block arrived with this part family at the M2 generation and is
  unchanged through M5. A driver carrying an address map forward from an M1
  machine will not find these parts. [Confirmed] (§6 §6.2.)

### 7.1.2 The control-less part (`max98360`, t8140 only)

**There is no device ID, no revision, and no register map, because there is no
control bus.** [Confirmed] A driver cannot probe for this part at all: its
presence, its channel assignment, its gain and its enable pin are facts about
the board and must come entirely from the platform description. Presence
detection on this machine is unconditional — the part is assumed present if the
node exists. See 7.9.

---

## 7.2 Precise differences from the public counterpart

**Unchanged from the public TAS2764 in one line:** the entire documented page-0,
page-1 and page-4 register map — addresses, field positions, reset values,
encodings, the I²C protocol, the paging model, the sense path, the limiter,
brown-out, clock and interrupt blocks — is that of the public TAS2764 as
published in the TAS2764 datasheet (SLOS998A), and every field position agrees
with it on the in-scope machines.

Everything below is a difference.

### 7.2.1 Deviations already published for the M1–M3 variant — all still present

Every one of the nine deviations published for the Apple variant of this part is
applied on t8132, t604x, t8142 and t605x, including the two that the
published quirk set defines but leaves **disabled by default**:

| Published deviation | Present on in-scope machines? | Note |
|---|---|---|
| G.2.1 brown-out source select + 24-byte preset at 0x1D | **yes** | 7.5.2; `BOP_SRC = 1` is set in `MODE_CTRL`, and the 24 bytes come from `bop-config` |
| G.2.2 noise-gate disable, page 0 / 0x35 = 0xB0 | **yes** | 7.3 |
| G.2.3 page 0 / 0x6B = 0x41 | **yes** | this is `NG_CFG2`, bit 6 `CONV_VBAT_PVDD_MODE` |
| G.2.4 page 0 / 0x76 = 0x00 | **yes** | this is `DAC_MOD_RST`, bit 1 `DIS_DMOD_RST` |
| G.2.5 page 1 / 0x33 = 0x80 and page 1 / 0x37 = 0x3A | **yes** | semantics still [Unknown] |
| G.2.6 twelve writes on page 6 | **yes** | this block is the **over-power protection** configuration, 7.3 |
| G.2.7 hidden sub-page behind page 0xFD offset 0x0D | **yes** | 7.3, and see 7.6 |
| G.2.8 page 1 / 0x47 = 0x02 (thermal threshold 1 disable) | **yes** | applied, not optional — see 7.7 |
| G.2.9 immediate-shutdown mode plus the hidden-page shutdown sequence | **yes** | applied, with an added delay — see 7.6.4 |

[**Confirmed** — the first seven are corroborated by the published quirk set and
by the in-scope machines independently; the last two are corroborated by the
published quirk definitions (which carry the same addresses and values) and by
their presence in the in-scope configuration.]

### 7.2.2 Further deviations *not* in the published set

These are additional facts about the part or its required configuration that the
published Apple-variant description does not contain. None of them is new to the
in-scope generations — they are present identically on M1 Pro through M5 Max —
but they are new information.

| # | Register | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | page 0 / 0x08 `TDM_CFG0` | **0x48** | `CLASSD_SYNC = 1` — Class-D switching **synchronised to the audio clock**, not free-running. Combined with #2 this resolves the published open item "switch from spread spectrum to class-D switching". [Probable] |
| 2 | page 0 / 0x04 `DC_BLK0` | **0x01** | `AMP_SS = 0` — **spread-spectrum modulation disabled** (reset value enables it); `SAR_FLT = 00` — supply-measurement ADC filter disabled, minimum brown-out latency; `IRQZ_PU = 0` — **internal interrupt pull-up not used**, so an external pull-up to IOVDD is required on the shared line; `VBAT1S_MODE = 0` — VBAT1S supplied externally. [Confirmed — value also carried in `amp-dcblocker-config`] |
| 3 | page 0 / 0x07 `MISC_CFG2` | **0x68** | `SDZ_MODE = 01` (immediate hardware shutdown, as published) **plus `DVC_RAMP_RATE = 10` = 0.5 dB per 8 samples**. This resolves the published open item "DVC ramp rate" and fixes the mute-ramp time (7.4, 7.6.3). [Probable] |
| 4 | page 1 / 0x19 `LSR` | **0x40** | `EN_LLSR = 1`, linear-LSR modulation. This equals the reset value; programming it changes nothing on a part that has just been reset. [Probable] |
| 5 | page 0 / 0x60 `CLOCK_CFG` | ratio-dependent | The `SAMP_RATIO[3:0]` field is at **bits [5:2]**, and the manual ratio is programmed to match the actual bit-clock-to-frame-clock ratio even though automatic rate detection is left enabled. [Confirmed — the code ladder 16/24/32/48/64/96/128/192/256/384/512/125/250/500 → value = code × 4 is exactly the published code table shifted by two] |
| 6 | page 0 / 0x0A `TDM_CFG2` | `RX_SCFG = 01` | Receive source is **mono-left**, i.e. each amplifier takes exactly one receive slot and the "right" slot field is unused. [Probable] |
| 7 | page 0 / 0x03 `CHNL_0` | `CDS_MODE = 00` | **Y-bridge, high power on VBAT1S**. [Probable] |
| 8 | page 0 / 0x05 `DC_BLK1` | `TFB_EN = 0` | **On-chip thermal foldback is disabled on every machine.** Safety-relevant: the graduated thermal-foldback engine is not in use; only the hard over-temperature shutdown and the host-side model protect the driver. [Confirmed — value carried in `amp-dcblocker-config` on every board] |
| 9 | page 0 / 0x06 `MISC_CFG1` | **not configured** | No platform-supplied configuration writes this register; `OCE_RETRY` and `OTE_RETRY` stay at their reset value 0 — **no automatic retry after an over-current or over-temperature event**. Note that this differs from the published Asahi machine configuration, which selects "retry". [Probable] |
| 10 | page 0 / 0x1A `DVC` | **not configured** | No platform-supplied configuration writes this register; digital volume stays at 0 dB; all volume control happens upstream of the amplifier. [Probable] |
| 11 | page 0 / 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x0B (limiter) | **not configured** | No platform-supplied configuration writes these registers; the supply-tracking limiter is left at its reset state, in which `LIM_EN = 0` — **the limiter is disabled**. [Probable] |
| 12 | page 0 / 0x3B–0x41 (interrupt masks) | **not configured** | No platform-supplied configuration writes these registers; the interrupt masks stay at their reset values: over-temperature and over-current unmasked, brown-out and limiter events unmasked, TDM clock error and the four graduated thermal flags masked. See 7.7. [Probable] |
| 13 | page 0 / 0x01 `SW_RESET` | **not configured** | No platform-supplied configuration writes this register; the part is reset only by the shared hardware shutdown pin. [Probable] |
| 14 | page 0xFD / 0x64 | 0x04 / 0x00 | The hidden-page register used around a shutdown transition is at offset **0x64** behind sub-page selector 0x0D — as published — and the transition carries a **1 ms** settling delay (7.6.4). [Confirmed for the address and values; the delay is **[Probable]**] |

### 7.2.3 The amplifier-level field: which counterpart applies

The amplifier full-scale level field sits at **different bit positions** on the
two public counterparts, and their reset values differ (TAS2770: `PB_CFG0[4:0]`,
reset 0x10 = 19.0 dBV; TAS2764: `CHNL_0[5:1]`, reset 0x14 = 21.0 dBV).

**The TAS2764 layout applies.** On the in-scope machines the level code taken
from platform firmware is masked to five bits and **shifted left by one** before
being written to page 0 register 0x03, with bits [7:6] left at 00. That is
`CHNL_0[5:1] AMP_LEVEL`, the TAS2764 position. The reset value is likewise the
TAS2764 one: the part comes up at **0x14 = 21.0 dBV, its maximum**, and the
level must be lowered before the part is unmuted. The dBV mapping
`level_dBV = 11.0 + 0.5 × code` is common to both counterparts and is confirmed
against the datasheet's own table (00h = 11 dBV … 14h = 21 dBV).
[**Confirmed** — the field position and the one-bit shift apply on the in-scope
machines, and the resulting dBV values reproduce the independently published
per-machine amplifier-gain indices for nine different machines (7.5.1).]

## 7.3 Complete register map

**Relationship to the published counterpart map: unchanged except where marked.**
Offsets, field positions and reset values below are those of the public counterpart
part and are **not** a finding of this document; they are reproduced because a driver
must know the layout of every register it programs *and* of every register it
deliberately leaves alone. Read the table as a baseline/delta split:

- A row whose **In scope** cell carries a value is a **delta** — the value programmed
  on every in-scope machine carrying this part, established here.
- A row whose **In scope** cell is blank or `—` is **unchanged from the published
  counterpart**: the register is not written on any in-scope machine and keeps its
  published reset value. That the register is left at reset is itself established here;
  the layout beside it is not.
- Rows marked "not in the public map" (page 0x01 offsets 0x33 and 0x37, all of page
  0x06, and the hidden paging mechanism of §7.3.5) are established here in full.

Book 0 only; no other book is populated. Register model: 8-bit address, 8-bit
data, `PAGE` at offset 0x00 of every page, `BOOK` at offset 0x7F.

### 7.3.1 Page 0x00 — main

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | In scope | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | `PAGE` | RW | 0x00 | per-sequence | `[7:0] PAGE` | Page select |
| 0x01 | `SW_RESET` | RW, self-clearing | 0x00 | — | `[0] SW_RESET` | 1 = restore all registers to defaults |
| 0x02 | `MODE_CTRL` | RW | 0x1A | 0x80/0x81/0x82 (+0x18 if sense unused) | `[7] BOP_SRC`, `[4] ISNS_PD`, `[3] VSNS_PD`, `[2:0] MODE` | Power state. `MODE`: 000 active, 001 active-with-mute, 010 software shutdown, 011/100 load diagnostics, 101 diagnostic generator. `BOP_SRC` 1 = brown-out measures PVDD **and PVDD UVLO is enabled** |
| 0x03 | `CHNL_0` | RW | 0x28 | `level << 1` | `[7:6] CDS_MODE`, `[5:1] AMP_LEVEL` | Class-D supply mode and analogue full-scale level (7.4) |
| 0x04 | `DC_BLK0` | RW | 0x21 | **0x01** | `[7] VBAT1S_MODE`, `[6] IRQZ_PU`, `[5] AMP_SS`, `[4:3] SAR_FLT`, `[2:0] HPF_FREQ_PB` | Playback DC blocker, supply-ADC filter, spread spectrum, interrupt pull-up |
| 0x05 | `DC_BLK1` | RW | 0x41 | **0x41 or 0x71** | `[6] ERC_EN`, `[5:4] EDGE_RATE`, `[3] TFB_EN`, `[2:0] HPF_FREQ_REC` | Sense-path DC blocker, output edge-rate control, thermal foldback enable |
| 0x06 | `MISC_CFG1` | RW | 0x00 | — | `[5] OCE_RETRY`, `[4] OTE_RETRY`, `[3] PFFB_EN`, `[2] SMODE_EN` | Fault retry enables (both off), post-filter feedback, +18 dB-attenuation safe mode |
| 0x07 | `MISC_CFG2` | RW | 0x20 | **0x68** | `[7:6] SDZ_MODE`, `[5:4] SDZ_TIMEOUT`, `[3:2] DVC_RAMP_RATE`, `[1] I2C_GBL_EN`, `[0] I2C_AD_DET` | Hardware-shutdown behaviour, digital-volume ramp rate, global I²C address |
| 0x08 | `TDM_CFG0` | RW | 0x09 | **0x48** | `[7] AMP_INV`, `[6] CLASSD_SYNC`, `[5] RAMP_RATE`, `[4] AUTO_RATE`, `[3:1] SAMP_RATE`, `[0] FRAME_START` | `SAMP_RATE` 100b = 44.1/48 kHz, 101b = 88.2/96 kHz. `AUTO_RATE` 0 = auto-detect enabled |
| 0x09 | `TDM_CFG1` | RW | 0x02 | **0x02** | `[6] RX_JUSTIFY`, `[5:1] RX_OFFSET`, `[0] RX_EDGE` | Receive offset 1 bit clock, capture on rising edge |
| 0x0A | `TDM_CFG2` | RW | 0x0A | `0x10 \| wlen \| slen` | `[7:6] IVMON_LEN`, `[5:4] RX_SCFG`, `[3:2] RX_WLEN`, `[1:0] RX_SLEN` | Sense word width (00 = 16 bit), receive source (01 = mono left), receive word/slot length |
| 0x0B | `LIM_MAX_ATTN` | RW | 0x80 | — | `[7:4] LIM_MAX_ATTN` | Limiter maximum attenuation, 0h = 1 dB … 0Eh = 15 dB |
| 0x0C | `TDM_CFG3` | RW | 0x10 | `0x10 \| index` | `[7:4] RX_SLOT_R`, `[3:0] RX_SLOT_L` | **Receive (playback) slot indices**, in slot-length units |
| 0x0D | `TDM_CFG4` | RW | 0x13 | **0x13** | `[7] TX_KEEPCY`, `[6] TX_KEEPLN`, `[5] TX_KEEPEN`, `[4] TX_FILL`, `[3:1] TX_OFFSET`, `[0] TX_EDGE` | Transmit-pin driver and bus keeper (7.5.4) |
| 0x0E | `TDM_CFG5` | RW | 0x42 | `0x40 \| slot` | `[6]` sense transmit enable, `[5:0]` byte slot | Sense transmit **A**. The mainline naming calls this the *voltage*-sense slot (`VSNS_TX` / `VSNS_SLOT`); **[Probable]**, see §8 §8.2.1 |

### 7.3.2 Page 0x01

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | In scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x19 | `LSR` | RW | 0x40 | 0x40 | `[6] EN_LLSR`: 0 = LSR, 1 = linear LSR modulation. Written, but to its reset value |
| 0x33 | *(undocumented)* | RW | — | **0x80** | Not in the public map; semantics **[Unknown]** |
| 0x37 | *(undocumented)* | RW | — | **0x3A** | Not in the public map; semantics **[Unknown]** |
| 0x3D–0x44 | `SDOUT_HIZ_1`…`SDOUT_HIZ_8` | RW | 0x00 | per amplifier | 64-bit per-slot bitmap, bit *n* = byte slot *n*. **A set bit means "drive 0 in this slot"** when force-0 is enabled; a clear bit means Hi-Z (7.5.4). Only `SDOUT_HIZ_1`…`SDOUT_HIZ_6` (slots 0–47) are written |
| 0x45 | `SDOUT_HIZ_9` | RW | 0x00 | **0x80** | `[7] SDOUT_FORCE_0_CNT_EN`: 0 = all unused slots Hi-Z, 1 = unused slots driven 0 per the bitmap |
| 0x47 | `TG_EN` | RW | 0xAB | **0x02** | `[1] TG_TH2`, `[0] TG_TH1` — the two over-power thermal detectors. In scope: **threshold 1 disabled, threshold 2 enabled**, reserved bits cleared |

### 7.3.3 Page 0x04 — 32-bit coefficients

Unchanged from the public TAS2764 register map: limiter thresholds, slope,
thermal-foldback coefficients and load-diagnostic thresholds, each a 32-bit
quantity MSB-first over four consecutive addresses. **No page-4 register is
written on any in-scope machine**, so every coefficient stays at its reset
value; since thermal foldback is disabled (`TFB_EN = 0`) and the limiter is
disabled (`LIM_EN = 0`), none of them is in effect. [Probable]

### 7.3.4 Page 0x06 — over-power protection (not in the public map)

Twelve writes, order-sensitive — offset 0x16 is written **twice with different
values** and offset 0x1A is skipped:

| Order | Offset | Value | Order | Offset | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0x14 | 0x00 | 7 | 0x16 | **0xAA** *(second write)* |
| 2 | 0x15 | 0x13 | 8 | 0x1B | 0x00 |
| 3 | 0x16 | 0x52 | 9 | 0x1C | 0x12 |
| 4 | 0x17 | 0x00 | 10 | 0x1D | 0xA0 |
| 5 | 0x18 | 0xE4 | 11 | 0x1E | 0xD8 |
| 6 | 0x19 | 0x0C | 12 | 0x1F | 0x00 |

This block, together with the page-1 `TG_EN` write, constitutes the
**over-power protection** configuration: the part separately monitors the
temperature of the internal power FETs against two thresholds, TH1 (typically
116 °C above the bandgap-measured die temperature, floor 250 °C) which triggers
thermal foldback, and TH2 (40 °C above TH1) which triggers thermal shutdown.
[**Confirmed** for the byte sequence — it is byte-identical to the published
quirk sequence; the functional attribution is [Probable], and the meaning of the
individual page-6 registers remains **[Unknown]**.]

### 7.3.5 Pages 0xF0–0xFF — the hidden second-level paging mechanism

**The hidden second-level paging behaviour applies unchanged on every in-scope
generation.** [Confirmed]

- Pages 0xF0–0xFF are absent from the public register map and must be treated as
  entirely volatile.
- Page **0xFD** contains a **second-level page selector at offset 0x0D**.
  Writing 0x0D there opens the hidden sub-page; writing 0x00 closes it. All
  accesses to the hidden registers must be bracketed by that pair, and the
  normal `PAGE` register must be restored to 0x00 afterwards.
- Three hidden registers are used:

| Sub-page offset | Value | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 0x6C | 0x02 | part of the mandatory one-off initialisation |
| 0x6D | 0x0F | part of the mandatory one-off initialisation |
| **0x64** | 0x04 then 0x00 | set before, and cleared after, **every** transition into software shutdown (7.6.4) |

Semantics of all three are **[Unknown]**. Omitting them is not safe (7.8).

## 7.4 Units and scaling

**Baseline/delta split.** The code tables, formulae and threshold values in this
subsection are the public counterpart part's and are **unchanged**; they are given so
that every physical quantity a driver programs has its units and scaling in one place,
not because any of them is a finding here. What **is** established here, and
what a reader should look for, is only the in-scope configuration on top of them:

| § | Established here |
|---|---|
| 7.4.1 | `SMODE_EN` (−18 dB) is not used on any in-scope machine |
| 7.4.2 | Digital-volume ramp rate is `10b` on every in-scope machine → 33.33 ms full-range ramp, the number behind the mute timing of §7.6.3 |
| 7.4.3 | **Both** high-pass corners are code 1 = 2 Hz on every in-scope machine and every amplifier including tweeters — which differs from the published community machine configuration |
| 7.4.4 | Edge rate is code 0 (1 V/ns) everywhere except the iMac boards, which use code 3 (0.25 V/ns); `ERC_EN = 1` everywhere |
| 7.4.5 | — (encodings only; the per-machine values programmed through them are in §7.5) |
| 7.4.6 | The die-temperature register initialises to 0 rather than to the documented equivalent, so 0 must be read as "no data" |
| 7.4.7 | `IVMON_LEN` is left at 00b = 16 bit on every in-scope machine |
| 7.4.8 | Which detectors are enabled and which disabled in scope |

### 7.4.1 Analogue full-scale output level — `CHNL_0[5:1] AMP_LEVEL`

```
level_dBV = 11.0 + 0.5 × code           code 0x00…0x14, others reserved
V_peak    = √2 × 10^(level_dBV / 20)    reference 1 V RMS
```

| Code | dBV | V peak | Code | dBV | V peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0A | 16.0 | 8.92 | 0x12 | 20.0 | 14.14 |
| 0x0F | 18.5 | 11.90 | 0x14 | **21.0 (reset)** | 15.87 |

Step **0.5 dB**. The part powers up at the **maximum**, 0x14 = 21.0 dBV.
`MISC_CFG1[2] SMODE_EN` would add a further **−18 dB**; it is not used.
[Confirmed]

### 7.4.2 Digital volume — `DVC[7:0]`

```
attenuation_dB = −0.5 × code            code 0x00…0xC8  ( 0 dB … −100 dB )
code 0xC9…0xFF                          = mute
```

Step **0.5 dB**; reset 0x00 = 0 dB; **mute code 0xC9 and above**. The ramp rate
is `MISC_CFG2[3:2] DVC_RAMP_RATE`, which on every in-scope machine is
**10b = 0.5 dB per 8 samples**:

```
full-range ramp = 200 steps × 8 samples / 48 000 Hz = 33.33 ms
```

This is the number that fixes the mute timing of 7.6.3. [Confirmed — the ramp
rate and the observed mute delay agree to within one millisecond.]

### 7.4.3 DC blockers / high-pass corners

Two independent first-order filters, identical code tables:

| Code | Corner (48 / 96 kHz family) | Code | Corner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | bypass | 4 | 200 Hz |
| **1** | **2 Hz** | 5 | 400 Hz |
| 2 | 50 Hz | 6 | 800 Hz |
| 3 | 100 Hz | 7 | reserved |

For the 44.1 / 88.2 kHz family divide by **1.0884** (e.g. the "800 Hz" setting
is 735 Hz at 44.1 kHz).

- `DC_BLK0[2:0] HPF_FREQ_PB` — forward (playback) path.
- `DC_BLK1[2:0] HPF_FREQ_REC` — **record path, i.e. the I/V sense output**;
  it is in the signal path of the voltage and current a host protection model
  integrates.

**On every in-scope machine both are set to code 1 = 2 Hz, for every amplifier
including tweeters.** [Confirmed — `amp-dcblocker-config` carries the value on
every board, and the same value is programmed on each amplifier.] The published
community machine configuration instead selects 800 Hz for tweeters; that is a
protective choice made by that implementation, not the platform's own setting, so a
driver following the platform value must not assume a tweeter is protected by a high
corner.

### 7.4.4 Output edge rate — `DC_BLK1[5:4] EDGE_RATE`

| Code | Slew rate | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 V/ns | all portables and desktops except the iMac |
| 1 | 0.5 V/ns | — |
| 2 | 0.35 V/ns | — |
| **3** | **0.25 V/ns** | **iMac j623/j624 (and M3 iMac j433/j434)** |

`DC_BLK1[6] ERC_EN = 1` (closed-loop edge-rate control enabled) everywhere.
[Confirmed]

### 7.4.5 Brown-out prevention — encodings

| Field | Encoding |
|---|---|
| `BOP_THx[7:0]` | **0.05 V per code**. With `BOP_SRC = 1` (PVDD): 00h = **5.50 V**, D2h = 16.00 V. With `BOP_SRC = 0` (VBAT1S): 00h = 2.70 V, 38h = 5.50 V (higher codes invalid) |
| `BOP_ATK_STx[3:0]` | 0h = −0.0625 dB, 1h = −0.5 dB, then ≈−0.396 dB per further code to Fh = −6 dB |
| `BOP_ATK_RTx[2:0]` | 2.5 / 5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 250 / 500 µs |
| `BOP_RLS_STx[3:0]` | same magnitudes as attack, positive |
| `BOP_RLS_RTx[2:0]` | 5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 250 / 500 / 1000 ms |
| `BOP_MAX_ATTNx[4:0]` | 1 dB per code, 00h = 0 dB … 1Fh = −31 dB |
| `BOP_DTx[2:0]` (dwell) | 0 / 100 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 / 4000 / 8000 µs |
| `BOP_HTx[2:0]` (hold) | 0 / 10 / 100 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 ms, 7h = infinite (exit via `BOP_HLD_CLR`) |
| `BOP_DISx` | 1 = that level disabled |
| `DEV_MAX_ATTEN[6:0]` | 1 dB per code, documented 00h = 0 dB … 2Eh = −46 dB |
| `LIM_DHR[4:0]` | limiter maximum headroom as % of PVDD: 00h = −20 %, 2.5 % per code, 10h = +20 % |

Brown-out latency to first attack: **15 µs** (measured at an 8.25 V threshold).

### 7.4.6 Supply and temperature readback

```
VBAT1S_volts = VBAT1S_CNV[11:0] / 128        LSB ≈ 7.8125 mV
PVDD_volts   = PVDD_CNV[11:0]   / 128        LSB ≈ 7.8125 mV
T_degC       = TMP_CNV[7:0] − 93             LSB = 1 °C
```

The temperature register in practice initialises to 0, not to the documented
2.6 °C equivalent; treat a reading of 0 as "no data". The supply/temperature ADC
is powered down in software shutdown, so the register holds the last sample
taken before shutdown. [Confirmed]

### 7.4.7 Sense-path scaling

Unchanged: 16-bit words, full scale **3.75 A peak** (current) and **14 V peak**
(voltage), independent of `AMP_LEVEL`; slot indices are in **8-bit units** so a
16-bit sense word occupies two consecutive slot numbers. `IVMON_LEN` is left at
00b = 16 bit on every in-scope machine. See §8 for the sense path proper and for
the scaling derivation.

### 7.4.8 Fault thresholds in real units

Every value in this table is from the public counterpart's datasheet, a single
source that cannot be checked against the Apple variant by probing (§7.2):
**[Probable]** throughout. The "in scope" enabled/disabled notes are
**[Confirmed]** — they follow from configuration words applied on every in-scope
board.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Thermal shutdown temperature | **135 / 145 / 155 °C** (min / typ / max) |
| Graduated thermal detector flags | 105 / 115 / 125 / 135 °C (all masked at reset) |
| Over-power detector TH1 (thermal foldback) | die temperature + 116 °C, floor 250 °C — **disabled in scope** |
| Over-power detector TH2 (thermal shutdown) | TH1 + 40 °C — **enabled in scope** |
| Output over-current limit, PVDD path | **5.9 A** (output-to-output, output-to-GND, output-to-PVDD) |
| Output over-current limit, VBAT1S path | **2.5 A** (output-to-output, output-to-GND) |
| VBAT1S UVLO | assert 2.0 V, de-assert 2.3 V |
| AVDD UVLO | assert 1.4 V, de-assert 1.6 V |
| IOVDD UVLO | assert 0.7 V, de-assert 1.1 V |
| PVDD UVLO | programmable, **left at 2.2 V**; enabled because `BOP_SRC = 1` |
| Voltage-to-current sense phase error | ≤ 300 ns |

## 7.5 The per-machine configuration tables carried by platform firmware

Four properties on the amplifier-group node (the node named plainly
`audio-speaker`, which is amplifier index 0) carry the whole per-machine
amplifier configuration. All four are byte-identical between the in-scope
machines and their M1 Pro/M2/M3 predecessors.

### 7.5.1 `speaker-config` — level and slot map

An array of **4-byte records, one per amplifier**, in amplifier-index order.
The first record belongs to the node that carries the property; records 1…N−1
correspond to the `speaker1`…`speakerN` phandles on the same node.

| Byte | Meaning | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **amplifier index = playback receive slot** | `TDM_CFG3[3:0] RX_SLOT_L` (with `RX_SLOT_R` = 1 and `RX_SCFG` = mono-left, so only the left index is used) |
| 1 | **analogue full-scale level code** | `CHNL_0[5:1] AMP_LEVEL`, i.e. written as `(byte & 0x1F) << 1` |
| 2 | first sense byte-slot (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20) | one of `TDM_CFG5`/`TDM_CFG6` |
| 3 | second sense byte-slot (2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22) | the other of `TDM_CFG5`/`TDM_CFG6` |

**The record structure is definitive**: byte 0 is the *playback* slot index,
counted in 32-bit receive slots, and bytes 2 and 3 are the two *sense transmit*
byte-slots. Sense occupies **two byte-slots per quantity** (a 16-bit word), so
each amplifier consumes four consecutive byte slots of the transmit frame.
[**Confirmed** — byte 0 goes to the receive-slot register, bytes 2 and 3 go to
the two sense-transmit registers with their enable bits set, and the resulting
frame layout matches the published channel map.]

**What the structure does not settle is which amplifier each record describes.**
The record-to-transducer binding rests on the phandle-chain reading of the
platform description, which the published hardware-tested maps contradict on the
MacBook Pro 14/16-inch chassis: the binding is **[Probable]** on that chassis and
**[Confirmed]** on every other machine in scope. The uncertainty applies
**equally** to the playback slot and to the sense slots, because both come out of
the same record. A wrong binding delivers woofer content to a tweeter — full-band
low-frequency energy into a driver whose safe continuous dissipation is of the
order of 1 W — **upstream of every protection mechanism**, with the sense channels
reporting the delivered power faithfully but against the wrong driver.
**On a MacBook Pro chassis machine, read `TDM_CFG3` (receive slot) and
`TDM_CFG5`/`TDM_CFG6` (sense transmit slots) back from every amplifier on a running
system and confirm the binding before any speaker is driven.** ☠ A wrong binding is
destructive and is not detectable from the platform description alone. See §8
§8.2.3 and §8 §8.2.4.

☠ **Which of bytes 2/3 is current and which is voltage — NOT settled.** What is
[**Confirmed**] is naming-independent: **byte 2 (the lower slot, `4n` — 0, 4, 8,
12, 16, 20) is written into amplifier register `0x0E`, and byte 3 (the upper
slot, `4n+2` — 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22) into register `0x0F`**, with bit 6 set in
each to enable transmission. The published upstream trees write the two
**exchanged** into the same two registers. Which register carries voltage is
**[Probable]** only: the identification of `0x0E` as the voltage-sense slot
rests on the mainline driver headers for the counterpart part and its sibling,
which are one family of sources sharing one convention rather than two
independent lines, and the coprocessor never distinguishes the two channels at
all (§18 §18.5.5), so the controller side cannot arbitrate. A power-based
protection model is **invariant** under the exchange and cannot detect it; an
impedance- or excursion-based model is inverted by it. §8 §8.2.1 gives both
readings and the two-load bench test that resolves it, and §00 carries the
mixing hazard. Open question 6.

**The second byte is not a constant.** It is the per-machine amplifier output
level:

| Code | Level | dBV → V peak | Machines (in scope in bold) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0A | 16.0 dBV | 8.92 V | j313 (M1 Air), j180d (Mac Pro) |
| 0x0F | 18.5 dBV | 11.90 V | every four- and six-amplifier portable, M1 Pro → M5 Max: **j604, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j713, j715, j704, j813, j815, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c** — and **the M4 Mac mini j773g and j773s** |
| 0x12 | 20.0 dBV | 14.14 V | iMac: j433, j434 (M3) and **j623, j624 (M4)** |
| 0x14 | 21.0 dBV | 15.87 V | M1/M2/M3 desktops (j274, j375c/d, j473, j474s, j475c/d, j575d) and **j575c (Mac Studio, in scope)** |

[**Confirmed** — the codes map onto the TAS2764 `AMP_LEVEL` encoding exactly and
reproduce nine independently published per-machine gain indices.]

Two per-machine deltas follow, and the first is safety-relevant:

- **The M4 Mac mini drops from 21.0 dBV to 18.5 dBV** relative to the M2/M3 Mac
  mini — a 2.5 dB reduction in analogue full scale. A driver that carries the
  older Mac mini value forward to j773g/j773s would drive its speaker 2.5 dB
  hotter than the platform intends.
- **The M4 iMac is unchanged from the M3 iMac** at 20.0 dBV.

**Recommendation.** Take the level from `speaker-config` byte 1 of the machine
in front of you; never hard-code one. If the property cannot be read, the
conservative fallback is the lowest observed code, 0x0A = 16.0 dBV — **not** the
part's reset value, which is the maximum.

### 7.5.2 `bop-config` — the brown-out-prevention table

24 bytes, written as a **block starting at page 0 register 0x1D**, i.e. one byte
per register 0x1D…0x34. Byte-identical on every board from M1 Pro to M5 Max:

```
01 32 02 22 83 2D 80  02 06 32 46 30  02 06 38 40 30  02 06 3E 37 30  FF E6
```

Decoded against the register map (7.3.1), with `BOP_SRC = 1` so the monitored
rail is **PVDD** and the threshold scale is `5.50 V + 0.05 V × code`:

| Register | Value | Reset | Field decode | Physical meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x1D `BOP_CFG0` | **0x01** | 0x40 | `LIM_DHR` = 0, `BOP_SHDN` = 0, `BOP_EN` = **1** | Brown-out prevention **enabled**; on reaching level 0 the part **attenuates, it does not mute or shut down**; limiter maximum headroom −20 % of PVDD |
| 0x1E `BOP_CFG1` | 0x32 | 0x32 | `DEV_MAX_ATTEN` = 0x32 | Combined limiter+brown-out device maximum attenuation, nominally −50 dB (see note) |
| 0x1F `BOP_CFG2` | 0x02 | 0x02 | `BOP_DT3` = 0, `BOP_ATK_ST3` = 1 | Level 3: dwell **0 µs**, attack step **−0.5 dB** |
| 0x20 `BOP_CFG3` | **0x22** | 0x06 | `BOP_ATK_RT3` = 1, `BOP_RLS_ST3` = 1 | Level 3: attack every **5 µs**, release step **+0.5 dB** |
| 0x21 `BOP_CFG4` | **0x83** | 0x2C | `BOP_RLS_RT3` = 4, `BOP_MAX_ATTN3` = 3 | Level 3: release every **100 ms**, maximum attenuation **−3 dB** |
| 0x22 `BOP_CFG5` | **0x2D** | 0x4C | `BOP_TH3` = 45 | Level 3 threshold **7.75 V** on PVDD (reset would be 9.30 V) |
| 0x23 `BOP_CFG6` | **0x80** | 0x20 | `BOP_HT3` = 4, `BOP_DIS3` = **0** | Level 3: hold **500 ms**, level **enabled** |
| 0x24–0x27 | 02 06 32 46 | same | level-2 fields at reset | dwell 0 µs, step −0.5 dB, attack 2.5 µs, release step +1.2916 dB every 10 ms, max attenuation −18 dB, threshold **9.00 V** |
| 0x28 `BOP_CFG11` | **0x30** | 0x20 | `BOP_HT2` = 1, `BOP_DIS2` = **1** | **Level 2 disabled** |
| 0x29–0x2C | 02 06 38 40 | same | level-1 fields at reset | max attenuation −24 dB, threshold **8.70 V** |
| 0x2D `BOP_CFG17` | **0x30** | 0x20 | `BOP_HT1` = 1, `BOP_DIS1` = **1** | **Level 1 disabled** |
| 0x2E–0x31 | 02 06 3E 37 | same | level-0 fields at reset | max attenuation −30 dB, threshold **8.25 V** |
| 0x32 `BOP_CFG22` | **0x30** | 0x20 | `BOP_HT0` = 1, `BOP_DIS0` = **1** | **Level 0 disabled** |
| 0x33 `BOP_CFG23` | 0xFF | 0xFF | read-only status | no effect |
| 0x34 `BOP_CFG24` | 0xE6 | 0xE6 | mostly read-only status; `LVS_FTH_LOW` = 3 | no change from reset |

**Resulting physical configuration, every in-scope machine with this part:**

> Brown-out prevention enabled, monitoring **PVDD** (which also enables the PVDD
> under-voltage lockout). **One active level only** — level 3 — engaging when
> PVDD falls below **7.75 V**, attenuating in **0.5 dB steps every 5 µs** with
> **no dwell**, to a maximum of **−3 dB**, holding for **500 ms**, then
> releasing in **0.5 dB steps every 100 ms**. Levels 2, 1 and 0 are disabled, so
> the part never applies the much deeper −18/−24/−30 dB reductions and **never
> mutes or shuts down** on a brown-out. Latency to first attack ≈ 15 µs.

[**Confirmed** for the byte sequence and its destination registers — platform
firmware and the published upstream byte array agree byte-for-byte, and the
block is written as 24 consecutive bytes from 0x1D. **Probable** for the field
decode: the register addresses, bit positions and encodings are taken from the
public counterpart's register descriptions, and the three disabled-level bits
and the level-3 threshold are the only deviations from the published reset
values, which is a coherent and self-consistent reading.]

Two caveats worth recording:

- The counterpart's documentation states that levels should be disabled "in the
  order 3 to 1", i.e. that level 0 is the one always kept. This configuration
  does the opposite — it keeps level 3 and disables 0, 1 and 2 — and the
  level-3 threshold (7.75 V) is set below what would be the level-0 threshold
  (8.25 V), which would violate the documented ordering constraint if the other
  levels were active. The configuration has shipped unchanged on five hardware
  generations, so it evidently works; but the exact behaviour of the level
  ordering with levels disabled out of documented order is **[Unknown]**.
- The documented range of `DEV_MAX_ATTEN` ends at 0x2E = −46 dB while its own
  reset value is 0x32 = −50 dB. This is an inconsistency in the public
  documentation, carried over unchanged here.

**Recommendation: replay the 24 bytes verbatim.** They are identical on every
machine and every generation; there is no reason for a driver to synthesise
them, and doing so risks getting the level-disable bits wrong.

### 7.5.3 `amp-dcblocker-config` — the DC-blocker configuration word

Four bytes, of which **only the first two are used**: byte 0 → page 0 register
**0x04 `DC_BLK0`**, byte 1 → page 0 register **0x05 `DC_BLK1`**. If the property
is absent the defaults are `DC_BLK0 = 0x01` and `DC_BLK1 = 0x00`.
[Confirmed — the property is exactly two meaningful bytes wide and its two
values land in those two registers.]

| Machines | Value | `DC_BLK0` | `DC_BLK1` | Physical configuration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **j604, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j713, j715, j773g, j773s, j575c, j704, j813, j815, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c** (and all M2/M3 predecessors) | `01 41 00 00` | 0x01 | 0x41 | Playback DC blocker **2 Hz**; sense-path DC blocker **2 Hz**; spread spectrum **off**; supply-ADC filter **off**; internal interrupt pull-up **off**; VBAT1S external; closed-loop edge-rate control **on** at **1 V/ns**; thermal foldback **off** |
| **j623, j624** (and M3 iMac j433, j434) | `01 71 00 00` | 0x01 | 0x71 | identical **except** output edge rate **0.25 V/ns** (slowest) |

The only machine-to-machine difference in the whole word is the edge rate, and
the only in-scope machines that differ are the two iMacs.

### 7.5.4 `amp-tx-zd-config` — the transmit-pin drive / keeper table

An array of **8-byte records, one per amplifier**, in the same amplifier-index
order as `speaker-config`; the property is absent on machines with no sense
capture. Bytes 0…5 of each record are written to page 1 registers
**0x3D…0x42** (`SDOUT_HIZ_1`…`SDOUT_HIZ_6`, covering byte slots 0…47); bytes 6
and 7 are padding. Page 1 register **0x45 is then set to 0x80**
(`SDOUT_FORCE_0_CNT_EN = 1`) on **every** amplifier in the group, including
those whose record is all zeroes. [Confirmed — the property length tracks the
amplifier count exactly (32 bytes on four-amplifier machines, 48 on
six-amplifier machines) and the six bytes land in those six registers.]

**Semantics, definitively:** with force-0 enabled, a **set** bit means *this
device actively drives 0 in that byte slot*; a **clear** bit means *Hi-Z*.
A device always transmits its own assigned sense words regardless of the mask.

Values, identical on every in-scope machine and on their M1 Pro/M2/M3
predecessors:

| Machines | Record 0 (amplifier index 0) | Record 1 (amplifier index 1) | Records 2…N−1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Six-amplifier (48 bytes) | `f0 f0 f0 ff 00 00 00 00` | `0f 0f 0f ff 00 00 00 00` | all zero |
| Four-amplifier (32 bytes) | `f0 f0 f0 ff 00 00 00 00` | `0f 0f 0f ff 00 00 00 00` | all zero |

Decoded, on a six-amplifier machine (24 eight-bit slots in use — 192 data bit
clocks of the 250-bit-clock frame, §7.6.2):

| Amplifier | Own sense slots | Drives 0 in slots | Hi-Z elsewhere |
|---|---|---|---|
| index 0 | 0–3 | 4–7, 12–15, 20–23 (and 24–31, outside the frame) | yes |
| index 1 | 4–7 | 0–3, 8–11, 16–19 (and 24–31) | yes |
| indices 2–5 | 8–11, 12–15, 16–19, 20–23 | none | yes |

The two links therefore each have exactly one designated filler device, and
every byte slot of each link's frame is driven by exactly one device: no slot is
left floating and no two devices drive the same bit period. **This is the
safety-critical property of this table** — the same wire carries the I/V sense
data the protection model depends on, so a contention or a floating slot
corrupts a safety measurement rather than merely producing a glitch.

Two further notes:

- The bus keeper itself (`TDM_CFG4[5] TX_KEEPEN`) is **not** used: register 0x0D
  is set to 0x13 on every amplifier, i.e. keeper disabled, unused bits Hi-Z,
  transmit offset 1 bit clock, launch on the falling bit-clock edge. Slot
  ownership is handled entirely by the force-0 bitmap. [Probable]
- The top byte of each mask (`0xff`, byte slots 24–31) lies outside the frame on
  every machine; it is harmless and is cropped by the frame length in practice.
  On the four-amplifier machines this byte is the one historical change in the
  whole amplifier configuration: M1/M2 machines carry `f0 f0 ff ff` /
  `0f 0f ff ff` and M3 onward carry `f0 f0 f0 ff` / `0f 0f 0f ff`. That change
  happened at the M3 generation, not at M4, and affects only slots outside the
  frame. [Confirmed]

The published upstream masks for the equivalent M1 Pro/M2 machines — 0xF0F0F0
for the first amplifier of one link and 0x0F0F0F for the first of the other —
match these values exactly, which independently confirms both the property's
meaning and the even/odd link split. Note that the published device
descriptions for some **M3** machines assign the two masks to the opposite pair
of amplifiers; platform firmware is uniform across all five generations, and a
driver should follow the firmware value. Recorded as open question 7.

All pin numbers are on the application-processor GPIO controller; see §6 for the
controller apertures and the `function-<name>` descriptor encoding. Every
machine has **one** shutdown line and **one** interrupt line shared by the whole
amplifier group, both carried on the index-0 node only.

`speaker-protection = 1` on every machine with a sense path and `0` on
j623/j624, j773g/j773s and j575c. `find-speaker-id = 1` with
`valid-speaker-ids = {0, 3}` on the machines listed with speaker-ID pins: two
GPIOs are sampled as inputs and combined as `id = pin0 | (pin1 << 1)`; if the
resulting 2-bit value is not in `valid-speaker-ids` a default identifier is used
instead. [Confirmed] The identifier selects **which speaker assembly is
fitted**; see §9 for what it selects.
