## 8.4 Scaling: raw sample to volts and to amperes

### 8.4.1 The formulae

With `s` the signed 16-bit received sample:

```
V_out(t)  =  (s_V / 32768) × VS_FULLSCALE     VS_FULLSCALE = 14.00  V  (peak, differential)
I_coil(t) =  (s_I / 32768) × IS_FULLSCALE     IS_FULLSCALE =  3.75  A
P(t)      =  V_out(t) × I_coil(t)                                  W
```

☠ **Which received channel supplies `s_V` and which supplies `s_I` is
[Probable], not Confirmed** (§8.2.1). Under the mainline naming `s_V` is the
even channel (sense slot A) and `s_I` the odd (slot B); under the exchanged
naming it is the other way round. The **product** `P(t)` is identical either way
— which is why a power-based model cannot detect a mistake here — but
`V_out / I_coil`, and therefore every impedance- or excursion-based quantity, is
wrong by `(14 / 3.75)² ≈ 13.9` if the assignment is reversed. Do not build an
impedance-based model on either convention without the two-load bench check of
§8.2.1.

| Quantity | Constant | Units per LSB | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voltage sense full scale | **14.00 V peak** | 427.25 µV / LSB | Datasheet: "SPEAKER VOLTAGE SENSE / Full Scale Input Voltage 14 V_PK" |
| Current sense full scale | **3.75 A** | 114.44 µA / LSB | Datasheet: "SPEAKER CURRENT SENSE / Full Scale Input Current 3.75 A" |

[Confirmed — two fully independent sources: the TI datasheet electrical
characteristics table, and the community speaker-protection daemon, whose
per-machine configuration carries `vs_scale = 14` and `is_scale = 3.75`
identically on every machine it supports.]

### 8.4.2 What is fixed by the part and what varies per machine

**Fixed by the part, on every variant and every machine: both constants.** They
do **not** scale with the programmed analogue output level (`CHNL_0[5:1]
AMP_LEVEL`) and they do **not** scale with the digital volume (`DVC`, page 0
0x1A). The sense path is an absolute measurement of what appears across the
speaker terminals, taken at the `VSNS_P` / `VSNS_N` pins and at the internal
current-sense element, downstream of everything the digital and analogue gain
controls do. Evidence: the same two constants are used on machines whose
amplifier level differs by 4.5 dB; and the analogue level control changes the
voltage at the terminals, which the voltage sense then measures directly.
[Confirmed]

**Varies per machine: the analogue output level**, which does not enter the
scaling formulae but *does* enter any headroom or peak-power calculation built
on top of them.

| Board(s) | `speaker-config` byte 1 | Full-scale output | Full-scale output, peak | Sense present? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| j604, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j713, j715 (M4) | 0x0f | **18.5 dBV** (8.41 V RMS) | 11.89 V | yes |
| j704, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c, j813, j815 (M5) | 0x0f | **18.5 dBV** | 11.89 V | yes |
| j623, j624 (iMac 24-inch M4) | 0x12 | **20.0 dBV** (10.00 V RMS) | 14.14 V | no |
| **j773g (Mac mini M4), j773s (Mac mini M4 Pro)** | **0x0f** | **18.5 dBV** | 11.89 V | no |
| j575c (Mac Studio, t604x) | 0x14 | **21.0 dBV** (11.22 V RMS) | 15.87 V | no |
| j700 (t8140) | property absent | **fixed 12 dB gain** (see §8.10) | — | **no sense at all** |

**Per-machine delta worth flagging:** the M4 Mac mini uses 18.5 dBV where the
M2 and M3 Mac mini used 21.0 dBV — a 2.5 dB reduction in amplifier full-scale
output on an in-scope machine. The M4 iMac is unchanged from the M3 iMac at
20.0 dBV. [Confirmed — `speaker-config` byte 1 across the whole board
population.]

### 8.4.3 Range coherence — a useful sanity check

At the 18.5 dBV setting used by every in-scope machine that *has* a sense path,
amplifier clipping occurs at 11.89 V peak, which is **85 %** of the 14 V
voltage-sense full scale (1.4 dB of headroom). Into a 3.2 Ω nominal driver the
corresponding peak current is 3.72 A, which is **99 %** of the 3.75 A
current-sense full scale. The two sense ranges and the amplifier level are
matched: at this level neither sense channel clips before the amplifier does,
and the current channel uses essentially its whole range. Conversely, at the
20.0 dBV and 21.0 dBV settings used on the sense-less desktops, the
voltage-sense range would be exceeded at amplifier clip — consistent with those
machines not using the sense path. [Inferred, but the arithmetic is tight and
it is a good cross-check that the scaling constants above are right.]

A driver author should treat a sustained `|s_V|` at or near 32767 as
**clipping of the measurement**, not as a valid 14 V reading, and must not feed
a clipped sample into a power integrator.

### 8.4.4 Accuracy budget (matters for any protection threshold)

| Parameter | Current sense | Voltage sense |
|---|---|---|
| Dynamic range, unweighted, relative to 0 dBFS | 66 dB | 69 dB |
| THD+N at 1 kHz, 7.5 W output | −58 dB | −60 dB |
| Differential-mode gain | 0.98 … 1.02 (±2 %) | 0.99 … 1.01 (±1 %) |
| Gain variability after calibration at 100 mW | ±1.4 % | ±0.45 % |
| Gain error over −20 °C … +70 °C | ±1.35 % | ±0.75 % |
| Offset with the record-path DC blocker disabled | ±2 mA | ±10 mV |
| Frequency response 20 Hz … 20 kHz | ±0.1 dB | ±0.1 dB |

[Confirmed — TAS2764 datasheet electrical characteristics.] Worst-case
gain error on the instantaneous power product `V × I` is therefore of order
**±3 %** before calibration and ±2 % over temperature after it. Per-unit
correction is available: the platform carries a pointer to per-unit speaker
calibration in system configuration storage (`/product/audio` properties
`speaker-thiele-small = "syscfg/SpTS"` and `speaker-trim-gains = "syscfg/SpGa"`,
present on every in-scope board), whose Thiele–Small record is a per-driver set
of `Re`, `Le`, `Bl`, `Fs`, `Qts`, `Mms`, `Rms`, `Kms` and a reference
temperature `T`. [Probable — the field set is consistent across the in-scope
boards; the binary record layout is [Unknown], see Open questions.]

## 8.5 Hardware filtering and decimation applied before transmission

### 8.5.1 There is no decimation on the TDM sense path

One current sample and one voltage sample are produced per audio frame and
transmitted in the same frame. The sense ADCs run synchronously with the frame
clock; there is no decimation ratio for the host to account for and no rate
conversion between the amplifier and the host. **Decimation ratio = 1:1 with
respect to the frame rate.** [Confirmed — the stream is declared symmetric-rate
and the slot map allots exactly one 16-bit word per quantity per frame.]

### 8.5.2 The record-path DC blocker — the one filter in the path

The current and voltage sense ADCs share a high-pass "DC blocking" filter whose
3 dB corner is programmable:

| Register | Page | Address | Field | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DC_BLK1` | 0 | **0x05** | `[2:0] HPF_FREQ_REC` — **record-path** (sense) DC blocker corner | 1h |
| `DC_BLK0` | 0 | 0x04 | `[2:0] HPF_FREQ_PB` — forward-path (playback) DC blocker corner | 1h |

| Code | Corner at 48 / 96 kHz | Corner at 44.1 / 88.2 kHz (divide by 1.0884) |
|---|---|---|
| 0h | disabled (bypassed) | — |
| **1h** | **2 Hz** | **1.838 Hz** |
| 2h | 50 Hz | 45.94 Hz |
| 3h | 100 Hz | 91.88 Hz |
| 4h | 200 Hz | 183.8 Hz |
| 5h | 400 Hz | 367.5 Hz |
| 6h | 800 Hz | 735.0 Hz |
| 7h | reserved | — |

[Confirmed — TAS2764 datasheet `DC_BLK1` / `DC_BLK0` field tables.]

**Value programmed on every in-scope machine.** Platform firmware supplies the
property `amp-dcblocker-config`, a 4-byte array `{DC_BLK0, DC_BLK1, pad, pad}`
written to page 0 addresses 0x04 and 0x05:

| Board(s) | `amp-dcblocker-config` | `DC_BLK0` decode | `DC_BLK1` decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| j604, j614*, j616*, j713, j715, j773g, j773s, j575c, j704, j714*, j716*, j813, j815 | `01 41 00 00` | `VBAT1S_MODE`=0 (externally supplied), `IRQZ_PU`=0, **`AMP_SS`=0 (spread spectrum disabled)**, `SAR_FLT`=00 (supply-ADC filter disabled), **`HPF_FREQ_PB`=1 → 2 Hz** | `ERC_EN`=1, `EDGE_RATE`=00 (**1 V/ns**), **`TFB_EN`=0 (thermal foldback disabled)**, **`HPF_FREQ_REC`=1 → 2 Hz** |
| j623, j624 (iMac) | `01 71 00 00` | as above | `ERC_EN`=1, `EDGE_RATE`=11 (**0.25 V/ns**), `TFB_EN`=0, `HPF_FREQ_REC`=1 → 2 Hz |
| j700 (t8140) | property absent | — | — |

[Confirmed — the property is byte-identical on every in-scope `sn012776`
machine and byte-identical to the M2 and M3 machines; the field decode is from
the public datasheet and the two values differ in exactly one documented field.]

So: **the only filtering in the sense path on every in-scope machine is a 2 Hz
single-pole high-pass.** Its practical effects for a driver author:

- The DC component of the voice-coil voltage and current is removed. A
  DC-resistance measurement cannot be made from the sense stream directly;
  voice-coil resistance must be estimated from the AC `V/I` ratio at low
  frequency, and the estimate is unreliable below about 20 Hz.
- Because the corner is 2 Hz and not 0 Hz, a step in output level settles in the
  sense stream with a time constant of about 80 ms. A protection integrator with
  a shorter window will see a transient error after a large level change.
- The ±2 mA / ±10 mV offset figures quoted in §8.4.4 are specified with the
  filter *disabled*; with the filter at 2 Hz the residual offset is smaller.

Two further amplifier-internal filters exist but are **not** in the sense path
and must not be confused with it: the forward-path DC blocker `HPF_FREQ_PB`
(also 2 Hz on every in-scope machine — note this differs from the community
driver's practice of setting 800 Hz on tweeters and 2 Hz on woofers, which is a
software policy choice, not the platform's value), and the supply-ADC filter
`SAR_FLT[1:0]` in `DC_BLK0` bits [4:3] (00 = disabled, 01 = 300 kHz,
10 = 150 kHz, 11 = 50 kHz), which filters the PVDD/VBAT1S measurement only and
is **disabled** on every in-scope machine.

---

## 8.6 Configuration required to enable the sense path

### 8.6.1 Register sequence, in order

All addresses are page 0 unless stated. This is the order that must be used; the
part will come up with a non-functional sense path if the power-down bits are
changed while the device is Active.

| # | Step | Register / field | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bring the amplifier group out of hardware shutdown | shared shutdown GPIO (§8.6.4) | drive high | wait 1–2 ms before the first I²C transaction |
| 2 | Software reset | `SW_RESET` (0x01) bit 0 | 1 | wait 1–2 ms; **everything** below must then be programmed, including the analogue level, which resets to its maximum |
| 3 | Enter software shutdown | `MODE_CTRL` (0x02) `MODE[2:0]` | `010b` | the reset state already; the sense power-down bits may only be changed from here |
| 4 | Set the frame format and rate | `TDM_CFG0` (0x08), `TDM_CFG1` (0x09), `TDM_CFG2` (0x0A) | per link | `TDM_CFG2[7:6] IVMON_LEN` must be `00` for 16-bit sense |
| 5 | Set the playback receive slot | `TDM_CFG3` (0x0C) | `RX_SLOT_R<<4 \| RX_SLOT_L` | from byte 0 of that amplifier's own `speaker-config` record — record structure **[Confirmed]**, record-to-transducer binding **[Probable]** on the MacBook Pro chassis and [Confirmed] elsewhere (§8.2.3, §8.2.4). **It must match the coprocessor's serialiser transmit assignment, which the platform description does not state: on the MacBook Pro chassis read `TDM_CFG3` back and confirm the binding before any speaker is driven** — Open question 1 |
| 6 | **Set the transmit pin timing and idle behaviour** | `TDM_CFG4` (0x0D) | see §8.6.2 | must be done on **every** amplifier on the link, not only the one being enabled |
| 7 | **Set the transmit slot masks** | `SDOUT_HIZ_1…8` (page 1, 0x3D…0x44) and `SDOUT_HIZ_9` (page 1, 0x45) bit 7 `FORCE_0_EN` | from `amp-tx-zd-config`, §8.6.3 | again on every amplifier on the link |
| 8 | **Enable sense transmit A and set its slot** | amplifier register `0x0E` (`TDM_CFG5`) | `0x40 \| slot_A` | `speaker-config` **byte 2** (the lower slot, `4n`) |
| 9 | **Enable sense transmit B and set its slot** | amplifier register `0x0F` (`TDM_CFG6`) | `0x40 \| slot_B` | `speaker-config` **byte 3** (the upper slot, `4n+2`) |
| 10 | **Power up the sense ADCs** | `MODE_CTRL` (0x02) `VSNS_PD` (bit 3) = 0, `ISNS_PD` (bit 4) = 0 | clear both | **these are power-DOWN bits; both reset to 1.** Must be written while `MODE` = software shutdown |
| 11 | Set the record-path DC blocker | `DC_BLK1` (0x05) | from `amp-dcblocker-config` byte 1 | §8.5.2 |
| 12 | Set the analogue output level | `CHNL_0` (0x03) `[5:1] AMP_LEVEL` | from `speaker-config` byte 1 | resets to 0x14 = 21.0 dBV — **reduce before unmuting** |
| 13 | Set the digital volume | `DVC` (0x1A) | as required | 0x00 = 0 dB, 0xC9 = mute |
| 14 | Programme the brown-out block | 0x1D…0x34 | `bop-config`, 24 bytes | §8.7.2 |
| 15 | Programme the interrupt masks | `INT_MASK0` (0x3B) … `INT_MASK3` (0x41) | as required | |
| 16 | Start the bit clock and frame sync | — | — | must be running and at the programmed rate before leaving shutdown |
| 17 | Leave shutdown | `MODE_CTRL` `MODE` | `001b` (Mute) then `000b` (Active) | |

**The ordering constraint at step 10 is the one that bites.** `ISNS_PD` and
`VSNS_PD` reset to 1 (powered down), and changing them outside software shutdown
leaves the sense path producing garbage or silence even though every other
register reads back correctly. The upstream driver forces a trip through
software shutdown around the change for exactly this reason. When a sense block
is powered down the device transmits **null samples** (zeros) in its slots — so
"all-zero sense channels with a running stream" is the signature of a missed
step 10, not of silence. [Confirmed — datasheet §"Current and Voltage (IV)
Sense" and the upstream driver.]

**Timing.** Shutdown-GPIO assert → first I²C: 1–2 ms. Software reset →
register map usable: 1–2 ms. Mute → shutdown ramp-down: 6–7 ms, then a further
2–3 ms. Hardware reset (not fitted on these boards): low 20 ms, high 1–2 ms.

### 8.6.2 Transmit-pin behaviour on a shared line

`TDM_CFG4` (page 0, 0x0D), reset 0x13:

| Bit | Field | Meaning | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | `TX_KEEPCY` | Bus-keeper LSB driven for a full cycle (0) or half cycle (1) | 0 |
| 6 | `TX_KEEPLN` | Keeper holds for 1 LSB cycle (0) or always (1) | 0 |
| 5 | `TX_KEEPEN` | Bus-keeper enable | 0 |
| 4 | `TX_FILL` | Unused bit fields: transmit 0 (0) or Hi-Z (1) | **1** |
| 3:1 | `TX_OFFSET[2:0]` | Bit clocks from start of frame to slot 0 | 1 |
| 0 | `TX_EDGE` | Launch on rising (0) or falling (1) bit-clock edge | 1 |

The three mechanisms are distinct and a driver author must not conflate them:

- **`TX_FILL`** is the *whole-frame* control and is only usable in a
  **single-amplifier** system: with `TX_FILL = 0` the one device fills every slot
  it does not own with zeros. On a multi-amplifier link it must stay at its
  reset value 1 (Hi-Z), or the devices will fight.
- **`SDOUT_HIZ_1…9`** is the *per-slot* control and is what a multi-amplifier
  link uses (§8.6.3).
- **`TX_KEEPEN`** enables a weak bus keeper that holds the last state of the
  shared line when every device is Hi-Z. The datasheet states that **only one
  bus keeper is required per line**, so at most one device per link should have
  it set.

The exclusivity rule is absolute and applies in **both software shutdown and
Active mode**: two devices must never be programmed to transmit in the same slot.
A device in software shutdown still drives its programmed zero-drive slots.
[Confirmed — datasheet, verbatim.]

### 8.6.3 Decoding `amp-tx-zd-config` into per-amplifier, per-slot driver settings

`amp-tx-zd-config` on the primary amplifier's control node is an array of 8-byte
records, one per amplifier, in the same amplifier-index order as
`speaker-config`. Each record has the shape
`{3-byte slot mask, 0xff, 0, 0, 0, 0}`. Its length is 48 bytes on 6-amplifier
machines and 32 bytes on 4-amplifier machines. The mask is a bitmap over
**8-bit transmit slots**, bit *n* = slot *n*, a set bit meaning **"this
amplifier actively drives zeros in this slot"**.

Only the **first amplifier on each of the two links** carries a non-zero mask.
Every other amplifier's record is all zero.

| Machine class | Amp 0 mask (link 0, left) | Amp 1 mask (link 1, right) | Amps 2…N−1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6-amplifier (j604, j614*, j616*, j715, j704, j714*, j716*, j815) | `0xf0f0f0` (+`0xff` in byte 3) | `0x0f0f0f` (+`0xff`) | 0 |
| 4-amplifier (j713, j813) | `0xf0f0f0` (+`0xff`) | `0x0f0f0f` (+`0xff`) | 0 |

**These two masks are byte-for-byte the transmit-slot idle masks published
upstream for the equivalent M1 Pro / M2 machines, on the same two links.**
[Confirmed — two independent sources agree exactly, which also confirms the
left/right link split: even-indexed amplifiers on link 0, odd-indexed on
link 1.]

Concretely, on a 6-amplifier machine:

| 8-bit slot | Contents | Driven by, link 0 | Driven by, link 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–1 | Amp 0 current | **Amp 0 (its own data)** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 2–3 | Amp 0 voltage | **Amp 0** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 4–5 | Amp 1 current | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 1 (its own data)** |
| 6–7 | Amp 1 voltage | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 1** |
| 8–9 | Amp 2 current | **Amp 2** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 10–11 | Amp 2 voltage | **Amp 2** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 12–13 | Amp 3 current | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 3** |
| 14–15 | Amp 3 voltage | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 3** |
| 16–17 | Amp 4 current | **Amp 4** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 18–19 | Amp 4 voltage | **Amp 4** | Amp 1 (zeros) |
| 20–21 | Amp 5 current | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 5** |
| 22–23 | Amp 5 voltage | Amp 0 (zeros) | **Amp 5** |
| 24+ | unused tail of frame | Amp 0 (zeros, if the 0xff byte is applied) | Amp 1 (zeros) |

So each link's slot space is **exactly partitioned**: each amplifier drives its
own four slots, and the first amplifier on that link drives every other slot
with zeros. Nothing on either link is ever driven by two devices, and nothing is
ever left floating.

**What it achieves electrically.** The transmit pins of the three amplifiers on
one link are wired in parallel (the "ORed" transmit topology) into one receive
line at the SoC. Only one driver may be active in any bit period. If two
amplifiers drive the same bit period, their output stages fight for the whole
slot: the result is an indeterminate logic level, corrupted sense samples on
**both** amplifiers' channels, and measurable extra supply current. If no
amplifier drives a bit period and there is no keeper, the line floats and the
receiver samples noise, which appears as large random sense values. Because the
line carries safety-critical data, both failure modes feed the protection model
garbage — and noise on a floating line is far more likely to read as *low*
average power than as high, so the failure is silent under-protection.

The zero-drive scheme above is preferred over the bus keeper on these machines:
the keeper only holds the *previous* value, which in a 250-bit frame is a long
hold and leaves the line at whatever the last real bit was. Driving zeros is
deterministic.

**Cropping.** The per-slot mask is 64 bits wide in the part
(`SDOUT_HIZ_1…SDOUT_HIZ_8`, page 1 0x3D…0x44, little-endian byte order, one bit
per 8-bit slot), with `SDOUT_HIZ_9` (page 1, 0x45) bit 7 `FORCE_0_EN` as the
master enable: 1 = drive zeros over the masked slots, 0 = release the pin. The
mask must be cropped to `bit-clock ratio ÷ 8` slots whenever the ratio changes.
With the platform's 3-byte masks the cropping is immaterial — the used slot
space is 24 slots on a 6-amplifier machine and 16 on a 4-amplifier machine, both
within 24 bits. The fourth byte `0xff` in each record covers slots 24…31; the
published upstream masks omit it. Whether it is applied or not makes no
difference on a 6-amplifier machine (no channel beyond 11 is captured) and none
on a 4-amplifier machine either (the receive mask is `0xff`, so channels 8…11
are discarded whatever the line does there). [Confirmed]

`FORCE_0_EN` must be set on the two keeper amplifiers and clear on all the
others.

### 8.6.4 Shared GPIO lines, per in-scope machine

One shutdown line and one fault-interrupt line serve **all** amplifiers on the
machine, exactly as in the baseline.

| Board(s) | I²C bus | Amp shutdown GPIO (`function-reset`) | Amp fault interrupt GPIO | Speaker-ID straps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| j604, j623, j624, j713, j715 (t8132) | i2c3 | AP 15 | AP 14, level low | AP 4, AP 13 |
| j773g (t8132) | i2c3 | AP 15 | AP 14 | none |
| j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c (t604x) | i2c1 + i2c3 | AP 54 | AP 55, level low | AP 52, AP 53 |
| j773s, j575c (t604x) | i2c1 | AP 54 | AP 55 | none |
| j704, j813, j815 (t8142) | i2c3 | AP 151 | AP 150, level low | j704: AP 198/199; j815: AP 6/11; **j813: none** |
| j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c (t605x) | i2c1 + i2c3 | AP 107 | AP 106, level low | AP 136, AP 137 |
| **j700 (t8140)** | **none — no control bus** | **AP 105** | **none** | **none** |

[Confirmed — `function-reset` decodes as `{u32 phandle, 'GPIO', u32 pin, u32
flags}` with flags 0x00010001 on every amplifier shutdown line, and `interrupts`
as `{u32 pin, u32 type}` with type 1 = level, active low.]

Consequences for the sense path specifically:

- The shutdown line is shared, so it can only be de-asserted when **all**
  amplifiers are idle. De-asserting it loses every register on every amplifier
  including the slot map, the zero-drive masks and the sense power-down bits;
  the complete sequence of §8.6.1 must be replayed for all of them.
- The fault line is shared and level-triggered, so every amplifier must be
  polled on every interrupt. The clear sequence is: read the six latched
  interrupt registers (page 0, 0x49, 0x4A, 0x4B, 0x4F, 0x50, 0x51) on each
  asserting device, then set `INT_CLK_CFG` (page 0, 0x5C) bit 2 `IRQZ_CLR` on
  each. Reading the status registers alone leaves the line asserted.
- **The six-amplifier Pro/Max machines split the amplifiers across two I²C
  buses** (i2c1 for the even/left indices, i2c3 for the odd/right) while the
  base-die machines put all six on i2c3. The link split (§8.6.3) and the I²C
  split coincide on the Pro/Max machines but not on the base-die machines: on
  j604/j704 all six amplifiers share one I²C bus but still sit on two separate
  serial-audio links. Do not derive the link assignment from the I²C bus.
  [Confirmed]
- On the M4 iMac and both Mac mini variants, `find-speaker-id`,
  `function-speaker-id0/1` and `valid-speaker-ids` are present (iMac) or absent
  (mini). `valid-speaker-ids` is `{u32 0, u32 3}` wherever present — two strap
  GPIOs read as a 2-bit value, of which **values 0…3 are valid** (the pair is a
  low/high inclusive range). j813 (MacBook Air 13-inch M5) carries
  `speaker-protection = 1` but **no** speaker-ID straps, unlike its M4
  predecessor j713. [Confirmed]

## 8.7 Autonomous protection, per variant

### 8.7.1 TAS2764-counterpart amplifiers (`sn012776`) — t8132, t604x, t8142, t605x

The amplifier protects **itself**. It does not protect the **speaker**.

| Mechanism | Autonomous? | Threshold / behaviour | Configured on in-scope machines |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thermal shutdown (die) | **Yes** | 135 / **145** / 155 °C (min/typ/max); output shuts down | enabled (not disableable) |
| Thermal foldback (progressive gain reduction with die temperature) | Available | `DC_BLK1` bit 3 `TFB_EN` | **disabled** (`TFB_EN = 0` in `amp-dcblocker-config`) |
| Output over-current limit, PVDD path | **Yes** | **5.9 A** (output-to-output, output-to-GND, output-to-PVDD) | enabled |
| Output over-current limit, VBAT1S path | **Yes** | **2.5 A** | enabled |
| Over-current retry | Configurable | `MISC_CFG1` (0x06) bit 5 `OCE_RETRY`: 0 = latch and stay down, 1 = retry after a timer | the published upstream driver selects retry; the platform supplies no value, so the choice is the driver's |
| VBAT1S undervoltage lockout | **Yes** | asserted at **2.0 V**, released at **2.3 V** | enabled |
| Brown-out prevention (supply sag) | **Yes, and it attenuates the signal** | four threshold levels with per-level dwell time, attack step, attack rate, release rate and maximum attenuation; total limiter+BOP attenuation capped by `BOP_CFG1[6:0] DEV_MAX_ATTEN` | **enabled**, see §8.7.2 |
| Signal limiter / inter-chip limiter alignment | **Yes** | `LIM_CFG0/1` (0x1B/0x1C), `LIM_MAX_ATTN` (0x0B) maximum attenuation 1…15 dB; `ICLA_CFG0/1` (0x17/0x18) aligns the limiter gain across the devices sharing a link | the platform supplies no value, so the part stays at its reset state (`LIM_EN` = 0) |
| **Voice-coil temperature protection** | **NO** | the part has no model of the speaker | must be done by the host |
| **Excursion / displacement protection** | **NO** | — | must be done by the host |
| **Voice-coil DC-resistance tracking** | **NO** | — | must be done by the host |

**The answer to "who protects the speaker" is: the host, entirely.** The part
supplies measurements (current, voltage, die temperature, supply voltage) and
protects its own silicon; nothing in it knows the speaker's thermal mass, its
voice-coil resistance, its excursion limit or its power handling. That was true
on M1–M3 and it is unchanged here. Notably, the platform's own configuration
**disables** the one speaker-adjacent autonomous feature the part does have
(thermal foldback), which is consistent with the host model owning that job.

The thermal model itself runs **on the host side, above the kernel driver** —
no block in the audio hardware path holds a voice-coil thermal or excursion
model, and the Thiele–Small parameter set is delivered to the host (§9).
[Confirmed] A driver must
therefore expose the sense stream and the amplifier level to userspace and must
not assume anything below it is limiting.

### 8.7.2 Brown-out configuration actually programmed

`bop-config` is a 24-byte array written to page 0 addresses **0x1D…0x34**. It is
byte-identical on every in-scope `sn012776` machine and identical to the M1
Pro–M3 value:

```
01 32 02 22 83 2d 80 02 06 32 46 30 02 06 38 40 30 02 06 3e 37 30 ff e6
```

Against the part's reset values for the same 24 registers
(`40 32 02 06 2c 4c 20 02 06 32 46 20 02 06 38 40 20 02 06 3e 37 20 ff e6`)
only eight bytes differ, at 0x1D, 0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x28, 0x2D and 0x32.
Decoding the two that matter for autonomous behaviour:

| Address | Register | Value | Decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x1D | `BOP_CFG0` | 0x01 | `LIM_DHR[4:0]` = 0 → limiter maximum headroom **20 % of PVDD**; `BOP_SHDN` = 0 → **attenuate, do not mute-and-shut-down**, on reaching brown-out level 0; **`BOP_EN` = 1 → brown-out prevention ENABLED** |
| 0x1E | `BOP_CFG1` | 0x32 | `BOP_HLD_CLR` = 0; `DEV_MAX_ATTEN[6:0]` = 0x32 = **50 dB** maximum combined limiter + brown-out attenuation |

[Confirmed for the values and the two decodes; the remaining registers form four
five-byte per-level groups of `{dwell time, attack step, attack rate, release
rate, maximum attenuation, threshold, hold time}` whose per-level numeric
thresholds in volts are **[Unknown]** from the material to hand.]

The operationally important consequence: **the amplifier can silently apply up
to 50 dB of attenuation** when the supply sags, without telling the host except
through the latched limiter/brown-out interrupt bits. A host protection model
that assumes the commanded digital level is the delivered level will
over-estimate delivered power during brown-out. The sense path measures the
*actual* terminal voltage and current, so a model driven from the sense path is
immune to this; a feed-forward model driven from the playback signal is not.

Brown-out attack latency to first attenuation step is **15 µs** at a threshold
of 8.25 V. [Confirmed — datasheet protection-circuitry table.]

### 8.7.3 MAX98360A-counterpart amplifier — t8140

See §8.10. Summary: thermal shutdown at **150 °C** with **18 °C** recovery
hysteresis, Class-D current limit, short-circuit protection, undervoltage
lockout in the range **1.5 – 2.3 V**. All silicon self-protection; **no speaker
protection of any kind, and no way to observe any of it**.

---

## 8.8 The `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC` domain is the microphone PDM converter

Every in-scope SoC's power-manager device list enumerates a power domain named
**`AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`**, together with two reference-clock domains
`PDM0_AUDIO_REF` and `PDM1_AUDIO_REF`. `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`'s parent is
`AUDIO_FR`, making it a sibling of `AUDIO_P` (the serial-audio-cluster
aggregate) and of `AUDIO_LEAP_A` (the low-power audio processor aggregate) —
i.e. it is not inside either serial-audio complex.

**It is not new, and it has nothing to do with the speaker sense return.**

| Generation | PDM converter domain | Reference domains |
|---|---|---|
| t8103, t8112, t600x, t602x (M1, M2) | `AOP_PDMC_LPD` | `AOP_PDM0_REF`, `AOP_PDM1_REF` |
| t8122, t603x, t6032 (M3) | `AOP_PDMC0` | `AOP_PDM0_REF`, `AOP_PDM1_REF` |
| **t8132, t604x, t8140, t8142, t605x (M4, A18 Pro, M5)** | **`AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`** | **`PDM0_AUDIO_REF`, `PDM1_AUDIO_REF`** |

[Confirmed — exactly one PDM converter domain and exactly two PDM
reference-clock domains exist on every board of every generation from M1 to M5.
The count did not change; the names did.]

It is the **built-in microphone array's** PDM converter, not a speaker sense
converter. **[Confirmed]** The hardware facts that fix this are:

1. It is a one-for-one rename of the domain that served the microphone PDM front
   end on M1–M3, arriving together with a wholesale rename of the surrounding
   low-power-audio domains (`AOP_MCA0…3` → `AUDIO_LEAP_MCA` plus
   `AUDIO_LEAP_RX0…4` / `AUDIO_LEAP_TX0`; `AOP_AUDIO_ADMA0` → `AUDIO_LEAP_*_ADMA`).
   [Confirmed]
2. The PDM converter block's high-frequency-decimator input selector takes a
   **microphone index** as its value, on all three in-scope generations and on
   the baseline. [Confirmed]
3. The block is grouped with the secure-microphone mute/unmute hardware in the
   same register region — a privacy feature, which only makes sense for a
   microphone. [Confirmed]
4. The domain is present, identically, on machines that have **no
   sense-capable amplifier at all**: the M4 iMac, both Mac mini variants, the
   Mac Studio, and the A18 Pro notebook. [Confirmed]
5. No in-scope machine's platform description carries any PDM-related property
   on the speaker nodes, any PDM slot assignment, or any additional receive
   stream that could carry a PDM sense return.

**Conclusion, stated explicitly: the sense-path PDM controller domain exists on
every in-scope SoC, it is named for the speaker sense path, and no in-scope
machine uses it for speaker sense. The current/voltage sense return is PCM over
TDM on every in-scope machine, for every amplifier. It does not coexist with a
PDM return, and it has not been replaced by one.** [Confirmed — by the endpoint
frame descriptors (12 × 16 bit or 8 × 16 bit inbound on the speaker link), by
the slot map, and by the five points above; §3 reaches the same conclusion from
the serial audio controller's side.]

Two related facts a driver author may trip over:

- The **amplifier family used on M1 machines** (TAS2770 counterpart) has a PDM
  *input* port (`PDMD`/`PDMCK`, 3.072 MHz single-rate or 6.144 MHz double-rate,
  decimated at 64× or 128× to a 48 kHz PCM sample) whose decimated output can be
  transmitted in a TDM slot alongside the I/V sense. That is a per-amplifier
  sensor-microphone feature, used on exactly one baseline machine and on **no**
  in-scope machine. The TAS2764 counterpart used throughout the scope has no PDM
  port. [Confirmed]
- On M4 and later the platform description no longer carries the microphone PDM
  front-end configuration node or the decimator coefficient tables that the
  baseline supplied to the host (the baseline's `audio-pdm2`, `dc-2400000`,
  `hfdc-2400000` nodes are gone). The PDM front end is configured entirely by
  the coprocessor. This is a real M4 delta, but it belongs to the microphone
  path, not to this section.

---

## 8.9 The speaker-tap stream endpoint

### 8.9.1 What the platform describes

A receive-only stream endpoint `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller/audio-speaker-tap`
exists on the M5 and A18 Pro generations and **not** on the M4 generation:

| Board | Speaker tap present? | rx channels | Sample bits | Slot width | `dma-provider-rx` | `clock-domain` | Data-source FourCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g (t8132) | **no** | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| j614*, j616*, j773s, j575c (t604x) | **no** | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| **j700** (t8140) | yes | **2** | 24 | 32 | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | `main` | `ap2a` |
| **j704** (t8142) | yes | **6** | 24 | 32 | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | `main` | `ap2a` |
| **j813** (t8142) | yes | **4** | 24 | 32 | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | `main` | `ispk` |
| **j815** (t8142) | yes | **6** | 24 | 32 | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | `main` | `ispk` |
| **j714s/c, j716s/c** (t605x) | yes | **6** | 24 | 32 | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | `main` | `ispk` |

The endpoint's `identifier` is the FourCC `tap ` (stored byte-reversed in the
device tree, as all FourCCs there are); its child node carries
`compatible = "audio-data,external"` with `device-name` and `device-uid` both
`SpeakerTap`; its `data-sources` record declares a single supported sample rate
of **48 000 Hz** and a supported-channel-count bitmap whose only set bit is
`1 << (N − 1)` for the N in the table. It has **no** transmit half and no
transmit DMA provider. Its bit clock and frame length match the speaker link's.
[Confirmed — all values read directly from the platform description.]

### 8.9.2 What it carries

**It is not the current/voltage sense return.** Four reasons:

1. Its channel count equals the **playback** channel count (N), not `2 × N`.
   A sense return for 6 amplifiers needs 12 channels; the tap has 6.
2. Its samples are **24 bit in 32-bit slots**; sense samples are 16 bit in
   16-bit slots.
3. It is **absent** on the M4 machines, which unambiguously do have a working
   sense return on the speaker endpoint's receive half.
4. It is **present** on j700, whose amplifiers have no data-output pin of any
   kind — so on that machine the data cannot be coming from the amplifiers.

**It is a monitor of the speaker playback signal** — an output reference, one
channel per speaker channel, in the same order as the playback slot map of
§8.2.2/§8.2.5. On j700 that is 2 channels (left, right); on a 6-amplifier machine it is
6 channels in amplifier-index order 0…5, i.e. the same left/right,
woofer-1/tweeter/woofer-2 ordering as the playback slots. [Probable for the
channel ordering — the supported-channel bitmap and the channel count match the
playback side exactly, and no other ordering is described.]

Its purpose on the host is as a **speaker-protection telemetry input** and/or an
acoustic-echo reference: the host-side audio graph treats a single N-channel
input stream as speaker-protection data, and falls back to an "open loop"
speaker tuning when such a stream is not available. [Probable]

Where the tap is **sourced** is not fully settled:

- It could be an internal loopback inside the SoC, taken from the speaker
  transmit serialiser after the coprocessor's processing chain (crossover,
  equalisation, limiter, protection gain). This is the only possibility on
  j700. The `clock-domain = main` property — the tap is the only audio endpoint
  on any in-scope board that carries it — is consistent with a tap that must be
  explicitly tied to the main (speaker) clock domain because it has no serial
  link of its own.
- On the `sn012776` machines it could instead be the amplifiers' own processed
  audio, which the part can transmit on its data-out pin: `TDM_CFG12` (page 0,
  0x16) `AUDIO_TX` with `AUDIO_SLEN` selecting a **24-bit** slot length — a
  width that matches the tap exactly. Against this: the platform supplies no
  slot assignment for that stream, and the frame has no room for it. A
  6-amplifier frame already spends 24 eight-bit slots (192 bit clocks) on the
  sense return; six 24-bit audio streams need a further 144 bit clocks, for 336
  in a frame of 250 (or 256) bit clocks.
  **[Confirmed that it cannot share the sense frame; [Probable] that the tap is
  therefore an internal loopback on all machines.]**

### 8.9.3 On the A18 Pro machine

j700 has a speaker tap even though its amplifier family has no sense capability
whatever. Given point 4 above, on that machine the tap unambiguously carries
**the two-channel speaker playback signal as sent to the amplifiers** — the
signal after whatever processing the coprocessor applies, captured internally.
It carries **no** measurement of the speaker: no voltage, no current, no
temperature, no impedance. [Confirmed]

It is nonetheless the only speaker-related feedback that machine has, and it is
what an open-loop, feed-forward protection model would be built on.

---

## 8.10 The A18 Pro machine (j700 / t8140) — no sense path at all

This is the case where a driver author is most likely to assume a mechanism that
does not exist. Everything in this subsection is a statement of **absence** and
is [Confirmed] unless marked otherwise.

### 8.10.1 What the hardware is

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Amplifier | `audio-control,max98360` / `audio-data,max98360`; public counterpart **MAX98360A** family |
| Channels | `num-channels = 2` (one device per channel, stereo) |
| Control bus | **none.** The amplifier node is not a child of any I²C bus; it hangs directly off `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` |
| Control interface | **one GPIO**: `function-reset` = AP pin **105**, flags 0x00010001 — the `SD_MODE` shutdown pin |
| Fault interrupt | **none.** No `interrupts` property, no shared fault line |
| Registers | **none.** The part has no register map and no readback of any kind |
| Data-out pin | **none.** The part cannot transmit anything |
| Sense | **none.** No current sense, no voltage sense, no supply-voltage readback, no die-temperature readback, no status |
| `speaker-config` | **absent** |
| `amp-tx-zd-config` | **absent** |
| `amp-dcblocker-config` | **absent** |
| `bop-config` | **absent** |
| `speaker-protection` | **absent** |
| Speaker-ID straps | **absent** |
| Speaker stream endpoint | `iop-adma-stream,leap`, `dma-provider-tx = "leap-ns-adma-tx-0"`, **no `dma-provider-rx`**, transmit channel mask `0x3`, receive channel mask `0x0` |
| Link geometry | 2 channels × 32 bit, bit clock 12 288 000 Hz, 256 bit clocks per frame, 48 kHz |
| Other platform settings on the amplifier node | `samplerate-subset` = {48 000 Hz}, `mute-ramp-sleep-ms = 20`, `enable-iop-ramp-down`, `iboot-audio-volume` |

Note also that the speaker link on this machine is on the **low-power audio
processor's** DMA domain (`leap-ns-adma-tx-0`), not the base domain used by every
other in-scope machine's speaker link.

### 8.10.2 What protects those speakers

| Layer | Present? | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Amplifier die thermal shutdown | **yes** — 150 °C, 18 °C recovery hysteresis | the amplifier IC only |
| Amplifier Class-D current limit / short-circuit protection | **yes** | the amplifier IC and the wiring |
| Amplifier undervoltage lockout | **yes** — 1.5 … 2.3 V | the amplifier IC |
| Amplifier click-and-pop suppression | yes | audible artefacts |
| **Voice-coil temperature protection** | **NO** | — |
| **Excursion protection** | **NO** | — |
| **Any measurement of the speaker whatsoever** | **NO** | — |
| Host-side feed-forward model | the only remaining possibility | see below |

[Confirmed for the amplifier self-protection figures from the public MAX98360A
family datasheet.]

**The amplifier's gain is not software-settable.** In I²S and left-justified
modes the `GAIN_SLOT` pin strap selects one of −3, 3, 6, 9 or 12 dB; **in TDM
mode the gain is fixed at 12 dB** and the same pin selects the device's TDM
slot. The machine's link is a 256-bit-clock frame, consistent with an 8-slot
32-bit TDM frame, so the two devices are almost certainly strapped to different
slots at 12 dB fixed gain. [Probable — the frame geometry and the two-channel
transmit mask are from the platform description; the pin strapping itself is not
described and is **[Unknown]**.] There is consequently **no software gain
control at the amplifier at all** on this machine: every level change must be
made in the digital domain upstream.

**The only protection budget the platform supplies is a power budget.** j700 —
**and no other board in the entire 56-board population** — carries three
properties on `/product/audio`:

| Property | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `speaker-cpms-bgd_inst` | `ffffffff ffffffff` | instantaneous budget: **unlimited** |
| `speaker-cpms-bgd_100ms` | `0x00000553`, `0x0000154d` = **1363**, **5453** | 100 ms-averaged budget: 1363 and 5453 in the same unit |
| `speaker-cpms-bgd_1s` | `ffffffff ffffffff` | 1 s-averaged budget: **unlimited** |

[Confirmed that these three properties exist only on j700. [Inferred] that the
two words of the 100 ms entry are a nominal and a maximum budget and that the
unit is milliwatts, giving 1.363 W nominal and 5.453 W maximum averaged over
100 ms for the speaker system — the magnitudes are right for a two-speaker
notebook and the `ffffffff` entries clearly mean "no limit". The unit is
**[Unknown]** and this is in the Open questions.]

The presence of a system power budget and the absence of any sense path together
say what the protection strategy is on this machine: **open-loop, feed-forward,
budget-based, entirely in software above the driver**, using the playback signal
itself (available on the speaker tap, §8.9.3) as the only observable.

### 8.10.3 What a driver author must do differently — and must not do

**Must not:**

- Must **not** open a sense capture stream on this machine. There is no receive
  half on the speaker endpoint, and no amplifier can drive one.
- Must **not** attempt any I²C access to the amplifier. There is no I²C device
  and no bus child node; probing is meaningless.
- Must **not** request or register a fault interrupt. There is no line.
- Must **not** attempt to read die temperature, supply voltage, over-current
  status, limiter state, or anything else from the amplifier. No register map
  exists.
- Must **not** assume a slot-level transmit-drive or bus-keeper configuration is
  needed. The amplifier has no data-out pin, so there is nothing to arbitrate.
  `amp-tx-zd-config` is correctly absent.
- Must **not** carry over any code path that infers "this machine has speaker
  protection" from the presence of a speaker node, a speaker tap, or the
  `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC` power domain. All three are present and none of them
  implies a sense path.
- Must **not** assume the amplifier will limit its own output before the speaker
  is damaged. Its thermal shutdown is at 150 °C **die** temperature; a voice coil
  can reach its own limit (of order 130–140 °C in the baseline thermal models) in
  a fraction of a second of undamped full-scale drive while the amplifier die
  stays comfortably cool.

**Must:**

- Treat the machine as **open loop** and enforce every speaker limit in the
  digital domain, upstream of the amplifier, before enabling output.
- Derive the gate on the platform description, not on the part family: the
  correct test for "this machine has a usable sense path" is
  `speaker-protection == 1` **and** a non-zero receive channel mask on the
  speaker stream endpoint. Both are false here; both are true on every in-scope
  portable with `sn012776` amplifiers.
- Sequence the `SD_MODE` GPIO correctly: bit clock and frame sync must be
  running before `SD_MODE` is raised, with the platform's **20 ms**
  (`mute-ramp-sleep-ms`) delay between them, and `SD_MODE` must be lowered before
  the clocks stop. This is the entire power sequence; there is nothing else.
- Default to a conservative fixed output level until a feed-forward model exists,
  and treat the 100 ms power budget above as the design target rather than the
  amplifier's own limits.

Additional per-generation differences affecting this section:

- **t8132 and t604x** bind the sense DMA channel with the baseline-style
  `dma-channels` array (receive = channel index 1); **t8140, t8142 and t605x**
  bind it by the string `base-ns-adma-rx-0` in `dma-provider-rx`.
- **t8140, t8142 and t605x** add the speaker tap on `base-ns-adma-rx-1`.
- **t605x** additionally exposes a secure low-power loopback endpoint
  (`audio-secure-leap-loopback`) not present elsewhere; it is unrelated to the
  sense path.
- The sense slot map, the transmit-drive map, the brown-out preset and the DC
  blocker configuration are **byte-identical across every generation from M1 Pro
  to M5 Max** on machines that have them. There is no M4 or M5 delta in any of
  them.
