## Open questions

Numbered. Items marked **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL** must be resolved before speaker
output is enabled on the affected machines.

1. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — which amplifier does each `speaker-config` record
   describe, and does the coprocessor's serialiser assignment agree with it?**
   This is the largest open item in this section, and it is a question about the
   record-to-transducer **binding**, not about the record structure. The
   structure is **[Confirmed]**: byte 0 of each record is that record's 32-bit
   playback receive slot and bytes 2 and 3 are its sense byte-slots. The binding
   is **[Probable]** on the MacBook Pro 14/16-inch chassis, where the
   phandle-chain reading adopted in §8.2.2 and the published hardware-tested
   maps disagree (§8.2.4), and **[Confirmed]** on every other machine in scope.
   Separately, on M4 and later the always-on coprocessor owns the serialiser, so
   which frame slot carries which speaker's audio is its decision, not the
   host's; the host can only program each amplifier's receive slot (`TDM_CFG3`,
   page 0, 0x0C) to match, and the platform description does not state that
   decision. A wrong binding delivers woofer content to a tweeter, which
   destroys the tweeter in a fraction of a second and does so upstream of every
   protection mechanism: the sense channels would faithfully report the
   delivered power, merely attributed to the wrong driver, so the thermal model
   would see nothing wrong. *Resolution:* on a running machine, read `TDM_CFG3`
   back from every amplifier to recover the playback assignment directly, and
   read `TDM_CFG5`/`TDM_CFG6` back from the parts at 0x39 and 0x3a to settle the
   binding (a transmit slot of 8 at 0x3a confirms the published map; at 0x39 it
   confirms the address-ordered reading); cross-check by playing a
   single-channel tone and confirming which physical driver sounds. **Do this
   before any speaker is driven on a MacBook Pro chassis machine.**

2. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — is the sense stream actually valid before the host trusts
   it?** There is no handshake that says "the amplifiers are configured and
   transmitting". A protection model fed an all-zero stream (sense ADCs still
   powered down) or a floating-line stream (zero-drive masks not applied) will
   compute near-zero or random power and will under-protect. *Resolution:* define
   and implement a positive validity check before unmuting — for example, drive a
   known low-level tone, verify that the measured `V/I` ratio on every channel
   lands within a plausible impedance window (roughly 2–8 Ω for these drivers),
   and verify that every channel that should be silent is exactly zero rather
   than noisy. This check should be mandatory, not diagnostic.

3. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — what values belong in `MISC_CFG1[5] OCE_RETRY`,
   `LIM_CFG0/1`, `LIM_MAX_ATTN` and `ICLA_CFG0/1`?** The host programs these
   directly, but the platform description supplies no value for any of them, so
   a driver has nothing to copy and the part's reset values govern unless it
   chooses otherwise. If over-current latches rather than retries, a transient
   fault silently kills a channel; if the limiter is left active with inter-chip
   alignment, the delivered level differs from the commanded level in a way a
   feed-forward model will not see. *Resolution:* read these registers back over
   I²C on a machine running its stock configuration to recover the intended
   values.

4. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL on j700 only — what is the unit of
   `speaker-cpms-bgd_100ms`, and is 1363 / 5453 per channel or for the pair?**
   This is the only quantitative speaker limit the A18 Pro machine's platform
   supplies and the only basis for an open-loop budget. Getting the unit or the
   scope wrong by a factor of two is the difference between a working limiter and
   no limiter. *Resolution:* correlate the values against the measured electrical
   power delivered at a known level and load, or against the same property family
   on a machine where a sense path allows the delivered power to be measured
   directly (no such machine exists in scope — so measurement on j700 itself is
   required).

5. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL on j700 only — what are the actual driver parameters?**
   With no sense path, an open-loop model needs the per-driver thermal
   parameters (coil and magnet thermal resistance and time constant, temperature
   limit, nominal impedance, resistance temperature coefficient) that on other
   machines come from the protection daemon's per-machine configuration. No such
   configuration exists for this machine. *Resolution:* measure them, or refuse
   to enable speaker output above a conservative fixed level.

6. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — the per-unit Thiele–Small calibration record layout.**
   `/product/audio` points at `syscfg/SpTS` for per-unit speaker parameters and
   `syscfg/SpGa` for per-unit trim gains. The field set is known (`Re`, `Le`,
   `Bl`, `Fs`, `Qts`, `Mms`, `Rms`, `Kms`, a reference temperature, and a
   data-source identifier), but the binary record layout, units and version
   encoding are **[Unknown]**. Without `Re` and its reference temperature, a
   resistance-based voice-coil temperature estimate has a per-unit error of the
   order of the driver's unit-to-unit spread. *Resolution:* dump the record from
   system configuration storage on a machine of each chassis type and fit the
   fields against the known parameter ranges.

7. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — which of the two 16-bit words per amplifier is
   current and which is voltage.** **[Probable], not settled** (§8.2.1). What
   *is* **[Confirmed]** is the naming-independent statement: this platform
   writes `4n` into amplifier register `0x0E` and `4n+2` into `0x0F`, while the
   published upstream trees write the two exchanged. Which register carries
   voltage rests on **one family of sources sharing one convention** — the
   mainline driver headers for the counterpart part and its sibling — and the
   controller side cannot arbitrate, because the coprocessor never distinguishes
   the two channels at all (§18 §18.5.5, four independent lines). *Why it
   matters:* the product `V × I`, and therefore a power-based thermal model, is
   identical under an exchange, so a power-based model **cannot detect the
   mistake**; but any impedance- or resistance-based estimate — which is what
   the per-unit calibration is *for* — is wrong by `(14 / 3.75)² ≈ 13.9`, i.e.
   11.4 dB, in the under-protecting direction. *Resolution, and it assumes
   neither convention:* drive one amplifier into **two different known load
   resistances** and observe which of the two received channels changes; the
   current channel scales inversely with load impedance, the voltage channel
   does not. *Until then:* adopt one stack's register programming together with
   that stack's channel labels and never mix them — see the third hazard in
   §00.

8. **☠ SAFETY-CRITICAL — which capture channels carry the tweeters on the
   six-amplifier MacBook Pro chassis?** This affects j604, j614s, j614c, j616s,
   j616c, j704, j714s, j714c, j716s and j716c: ten of the fourteen in-scope
   machines with a sense path. Two readings of `speaker-config` exist (§8.2.4).
   The adopted reading — record index = phandle-chain position, i.e. ordered by
   I²C address — puts the tweeters at capture channels 8…11; the published
   hardware-tested trees for the same chassis at three earlier generations put
   them at channels 4…7. The two coincide on every other chassis. §8.2.2 adopts
   the platform reading at **[Probable]** because on M4 and later the coprocessor
   owns the deserialiser and the blob is the only per-machine slot description it
   has; but the alternative reading — that the record index is a canonical role
   order — would reconcile every source on every chassis and cannot be dismissed.
   Getting it wrong applies a woofer thermal model to a tweeter: on this chassis
   the published thermal parameters differ by a factor of 1.23 in coil thermal
   resistance and by 10 °C in temperature limit, so the error is an
   under-protection of roughly 20 % in steady-state coil temperature rise plus a
   mistimed transient — well outside the margin the protection model is designed
   to hold. Note also that on M4+ an amplifier programmed to transmit outside the
   coprocessor's deserialiser receive mask returns constant zero rather than an
   error, so a wrong choice can present as a dead channel rather than as wrong
   data. *Resolution, a five-minute measurement:* on a running six-amplifier
   MacBook Pro read the two sense-slot registers (page 0, `0x0E` and `0x0F`)
   from the parts at 0x39 and 0x3a.
   A sense slot of 8 at 0x3a confirms the published map; at 0x39 confirms the
   adopted map. Until then, apply one map consistently to both the programming
   and the interpretation, and never mix them. The four-amplifier machines and
   the 15-inch Air are **not** affected — both readings agree there — and the
   same swap on the 15-inch Air would be a factor of 3.1 in coil thermal
   resistance, which is why the agreement there matters.

9. **What `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC` is actually for, and why it is named for the sense
   path.** The evidence (§8.8) says it is the microphone PDM converter, renamed. *Why it
   matters:* if the block did have a second input path wired to an amplifier, a PDM sense
   return would exist on some configuration and this document's "PCM over TDM everywhere"
   position would be incomplete. *Resolution — the block's register space cannot be
   enumerated, because no in-scope SoC gives the host an MMIO aperture for the audio island
   (§3 §3.2); resolve it from the outside instead, in three steps that need no aperture:*
   (a) On t8132, where the power-manager entries state a control-register address in the
   validated register-block form (§2 §2.6.1), read `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`'s power-state
   register `PS_ACTUAL` field (§2 §2.6.1) in four conditions — idle, microphone capture
   only, speaker playback with sense capture only, and both — and record which condition
   raises it. Raised by microphone capture alone settles it.
   (b) Repeat on **j773g, j773s or j575c**, which have no microphones at all: if the domain
   is never raised on a machine with no microphone, the microphone reading is confirmed
   a second time and independently.
   (c) Repeat on **j623 or j624**, which have sense-capable amplifiers with the sense path
   disabled: if the domain still tracks microphone capture there, no speaker-sense role is
   left for it to have.

10. **Whether the speaker tap is an internal loopback or the amplifiers' own
    audio-out stream on `sn012776` machines.** §8.9.2 argues for internal
    loopback (it cannot share the sense frame, and it must be internal on j700),
    but this is [Probable], not confirmed. It matters because an internal tap is
    taken *before* the amplifier's analogue level and its own limiter, whereas an
    amplifier-sourced tap is taken *after* the amplifier's digital processing —
    a difference of up to 50 dB during brown-out. A protection model that used
    the tap instead of the sense return would be wrong in the first case.
    *Resolution:* capture the tap while forcing the amplifier limiter to engage
    (low supply, high level) and see whether the tap level follows.

11. **Settled — the bit clock and frame length of the speaker link.**
    **12.000 MHz with 250 bit clocks per frame**, giving 48 000 Hz exactly, on
    every `sn012776` machine in scope and whatever the amplifier count;
    12.288 MHz with 256 on j700, whose amplifier family is different.
    **[Confirmed]** on three lines — the platform's link descriptor carries both
    figures directly, the coprocessor's built-in record for this stream family
    carries frame-sync phase 0 = 1, phase 1 = 249 with divider 1, and the
    amplifier's bit-clock-to-frame-rate register has a code for 250 (§18
    §18.4.4, §18 §18.7.1, §11 §11.7.3). The published baseline's 12.288 MHz /
    256 figure belongs to a different generation's link and does not apply here.
    250 bit clocks is **31.25** eight-bit slots, so the frame does **not** end on
    an 8-bit slot boundary: the 24 sense slots occupy bit clocks 0…191 and the
    remaining 58 are idle, which is why the transmit-drive mask of §8.6.3 covers
    32 eight-bit slots and the top eight of them fall outside the frame.
    *Retained as a confirmation measurement:* count bit-clock edges per frame on
    the speaker link with a logic analyser.

12. **The per-level brown-out thresholds in volts.** `bop-config` sets four
    brown-out levels (page 0, 0x1D…0x34) and the amplifier can silently apply up
    to 50 dB of attenuation when they trip. The per-level threshold-code-to-volts
    table is **[Unknown]**. A host model that does not know at what supply
    voltage the amplifier starts attenuating cannot distinguish "the user turned
    it down" from "the battery sagged". *Resolution:* read the `BOP_TH*` code
    table from the part's datasheet register description, and confirm by sweeping
    the supply on a bench board.

13. **Whether the amplifiers' status, die-temperature, PVDD and limiter-gain
    transmit streams could be enabled alongside the sense return.** §8.3 shows
    the part can transmit five further per-frame quantities, all currently
    disabled. Enabling die temperature (8 bit, one slot per amplifier) would cost
    6 additional slots in a 6-amplifier frame and would give the host a direct
    per-amplifier temperature at frame rate instead of a polled I²C read — which on
    machines whose only thermal protection is in the host is worth a great deal.
    *Why the obvious resolution does not work:* the coprocessor owns the deserialiser's
    receive channel mask, and the property key that would carry a channel mask is one of
    the fifteen whose numeric value is not established (Section 11 §11.4.6, Open
    question 7), so "ask the coprocessor to accept a wider slot map" is not something a
    driver can do or a probe can try.
    *Resolution, which is entirely host-side and also answers question 11:* the amplifier
    transmit registers are reached over host-owned I²C and need no coprocessor cooperation.
    On a running six-amplifier machine, take **one** amplifier and set `TDM_CFG8` (0x11)
    `TEMP_TX` = 1 with `TEMP_SLOT` swept across the whole 0–63 byte-slot range, one value
    at a time, while capturing the sense return stream. Record, for each slot value,
    whether an extra byte appears in the capture and where. Three results fall out at once:
    the set of slots the deserialiser actually captures (which **is** the real frame
    length, closing question 11), whether any slot outside the sense pairs is captured at
    all, and whether a captured extra byte displaces sense data or coexists with it. Do
    this on **one** amplifier only and with the speaker muted — a transmit-slot collision
    corrupts the sense return for the whole link, and a corrupted sense return is
    indistinguishable from a quiet speaker to any protection model built on it.

14. **What `TX_KEEPEN` is set to on the in-scope machines.** The platform's
    zero-drive scheme (§8.6.3) makes the bus keeper unnecessary, and the part's
    reset value is disabled, but no platform property covers it. If a keeper were
    enabled on more than one device per link they would contend weakly.
    *Resolution:* read `TDM_CFG4` back from every amplifier.

15. **The exact per-unit speaker-ID strap semantics.** `valid-speaker-ids` is
    `{0, 3}` on every board that carries it, and two strap GPIOs are named. What
    each of the four values selects — a vendor variant, a different I²C address
    set, or a different calibration table — is **[Unknown]**, and j813 carries
    `speaker-protection = 1` with no straps at all while its M4 predecessor j713
    has them. *Resolution:* read the two GPIOs on machines of each variant and
    correlate with the calibration record retrieved for question 6.


---

# 9. Calibration and protection data

> **Read this before driving these speakers at all.**
>
> On every in-scope machine the amplifier can deliver **10–50 times more
> continuous power into the voice coil than the coil can survive**. On a
> 14-inch MacBook Pro M4 the amplifier's full-scale output is 18.5 dBV
> (11.90 V peak) into a 3.2 Ω woofer — 44 W peak — while the woofer's thermal
> model allows **1.28 W continuous**. The gap is **15.4 dB**. Nothing in the
> hardware closes that gap. The amplifier's own protection is die-temperature,
> over-current and supply brown-out only; it has **no knowledge whatsoever of
> the voice coil** and will happily cook it. The always-on coprocessor does not
> close it either — the protection and limiting maths runs on the host CPU on
> every in-scope machine (§9.9), so a driver that starts the DMA and writes
> samples is driving the speakers **completely unprotected**.
>
> Before enabling speaker output you must have established, for the specific
> machine: (1) the per-model thermal parameter set and temperature limit for
> **each** transducer and which amplifier index each belongs to (§9.4, §9.6);
> (2) the per-unit factory calibration, or an explicit decision to run without
> it on conservative defaults (§9.2); (3) the amplifier full-scale level the
> platform specifies, which is **not** the amplifier's reset value (§9.4.5);
> and (4) a running, fail-closed limiter with a hardware/driver interlock that
> mutes or hard-attenuates the output if the limiter stops. Until all four are
> in place, clamp the amplifier's digital volume to at least **−20 dBFS** and
> preferably to the mute code.
>
> The **fail-safe of last resort on every in-scope machine, including the A18
> Pro machine, is the amplifier shutdown/reset GPIO**. It is host-owned and
> host-reachable on every board (§9.9.6). It is the only speaker control a host
> driver can reach on the A18 Pro machine at all. Wire it into your error paths
> before you wire up anything else.

---

## Baseline

Measured against three things:

1. **The published speaker-protection data model** of the Asahi Linux
   protection daemon, which defines the parameter set (`tr_coil`,
   `tr_magnet`, `tau_coil`, `tau_magnet`, `t_limit`, `t_headroom`, `t_ambient`,
   `z_nominal`, `z_shunt`, `a_t_20c`, `a_t_35c`, `is_scale`, `vs_scale`) and a
   two-stage (coil, magnet) lumped thermal model driven by the product of the
   amplifier's voltage- and current-sense returns.
2. **The M1–M3 platform hardware description**, which on every board from M1
   onward carries `/product/audio` with `speaker-thiele-small` and
   `speaker-trim-gains` pointing into the factory configuration store, plus
   `acoustic-id`, and carries `speaker-protection`, `speaker-config`,
   `find-speaker-id`, `valid-speaker-ids` and `function-speaker-idN` on the
   primary amplifier node.
3. **The public counterpart amplifier parts** — TAS2764 (Apple variant
   SN012776) and MAX98360A — for what the silicon itself will and will not do
   without host help.

## Summary of differences

| Topic | M1–M3 | t8132 / t604x (M4) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 / t605x (M5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where per-unit calibration is stored | Factory configuration region of the SPI-NOR, keys `SpTS` / `SpGa`, surfaced through the platform description | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
| Delivery mechanism (placeholder → filled by boot firmware) | unchanged | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
| Per-model constants | Operating-system-side tuning set selected by `acoustic-id` | unchanged mechanism, new IDs | unchanged mechanism, new ID | unchanged mechanism, new IDs |
| Closed-loop (sense-driven) protection | present on machines with `speaker-protection = 1` | present, **woofer limit lowered to 130 °C on 14-inch MacBook Pro** | **absent — no sense return exists** | present, parameters identical to M4 on every corresponding chassis |
| Open-loop (no-sense) protection | present on machines with `speaker-protection = 0` | present (iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio) | present, in a new feed-forward form | present |
| Excursion/displacement control | modelled, disabled | modelled, **disabled**; **13-inch Air switches to a runtime-adaptive loudspeaker model** | **actively used** (feed-forward loudspeaker model) | modelled, **disabled**; 13-inch Air adaptive |
| Speaker-module identity strap | 2 GPIO pins, valid IDs {0, 3} | unchanged | **absent** | unchanged, **except the 13-inch Air, which drops it** |
| Where the protection maths runs | host | **host** | **host** | **host** |
| Anything uploaded to the amplifier? | no | **no** | **no** | **no** |
| Amplifier-autonomous speaker protection | none | **none** | **none** | **none** |

The single structural change at the M4 boundary is that the speaker **control**
path (serialiser, clocking, routing) moved behind the always-on coprocessor
while the **data** path stayed on host DMA. Calibration and protection are
entirely on the data-path side and did **not** move. Everything in this section
that is marked "unchanged" is unchanged because the data model never changed —
only the delivery of the audio samples did.

---

## 9.1 Where per-machine and per-unit speaker data is stored

**Per-unit speaker data is delivered to the operating system in the platform
description**, as `/product/audio` → `speaker-thiele-small` and
`speaker-trim-gains`, filled in by boot firmware from the factory configuration
store. No other delivery path carries it.

Both properties are flagged as **placeholders** (property length high bit set),
and their unresolved content is the ASCII source descriptor `syscfg/SpTS` and
`syscfg/SpGa`. They are present and identical on every board from M1 to M5, in
scope and baseline alike. No numeric speaker parameter appears anywhere in any
board description. **[Confirmed]**

The placeholder syntax is `syscfg/<4-character key>[/<size>][,<fallback
source>/<size>]` and is used consistently across the tree for every
factory-programmed per-unit quantity — serial numbers, MAC addresses, radio
calibration, accelerometer/gyroscope calibration, backlight calibration, display
temperature compensation. Speaker data uses exactly the same mechanism with keys
`SpTS` (speaker Thiele/Small) and `SpGa` (speaker trim gains). That store is a
**read-only raw region of the SPI-NOR flash**, written at manufacture; it is not
NVRAM and it is not on any filesystem. **[Confirmed]**

The placeholder flag means the boot firmware replaces the property value with
the fetched object before handing the tree to the operating system. Unresolved,
the property reads as the source descriptor string; **once resolved on a
provisioned machine, the same property carries the binary blob**. A driver reads
it as an ordinary device-tree property — it does **not** need SPI-NOR access.
**[Confirmed]**

Where the per-unit data is **not** carried:

| Delivery path | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Read-write configuration variables (NVRAM) | Not carried in NVRAM. The only audio-related NVRAM variable is the boot-chime/system audio volume (a single 16-bit value, host-written); no calibration or protection quantity is held there. **[Probable]** |
| System management controller | Not carried over the system management controller; the speaker path has no dependency on it. **[Probable]** |
| Coprocessor firmware payload | Not carried in coprocessor firmware. **[Probable]** |
| Signed firmware container | No speaker calibration container is distributed as a signed firmware object; the factory store is a plain NOR region, not a signed image object. **[Probable]** |
| Host-side per-board constant table | No per-unit speaker electromechanical or thermal constants are delivered this way. **[Probable]** |
| File written at manufacturing on the data volume | No per-unit speaker data file exists on the system volume; the per-model tuning sets shipped there are identical for every unit of a model and are part of the operating-system image, not manufacturing output. **[Probable]** |
| Sealed factory-data records (the platform's tamper-evident restore data) | Not sealed. The sealed-record tag list covers every in-scope model and contains 45 tags — radio calibration, camera calibration, biometric calibration, board and serial identifiers, certificates — and **there is no audio or speaker tag in it**. Unlike camera and biometric calibration, speaker calibration is deliberately not sealed, so a replacement speaker module does not require a sealed-record update. **[Confirmed]** |

**Per-model constants are a separate matter.** They are not carried by the
platform description; only the `acoustic-id` selector is (§9.4.2). An
independent driver must supply or derive its own per-model constants.
**[Unknown]** what a complete per-model set contains.

### 9.1.1 The complete set of audio keys in the factory configuration store

| Key | Meaning | Surfaced in the platform description as | Present on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SpTS` | Speaker Thiele/Small — the per-unit factory speaker calibration block | `/product/audio` → `speaker-thiele-small` | 55/56 boards, all in-scope |
| `SpGa` | Speaker trim gains — per-transducer gain trim | `/product/audio` → `speaker-trim-gains` | 55/56 boards, all in-scope |
| `MiGa` | Microphone trim gains (same format as `SpGa`) | `/product/audio` → `mic-trim-gains` | 43/56 boards |
| `SpEQ` | Speaker equalisation calibration | **not** surfaced in the platform description | [Probable] — the key is defined but is not surfaced in any platform description |
| `WFEQ` | A further equalisation calibration object | **not** surfaced in the platform description | [Probable] |

[Confirmed] for `SpTS`, `SpGa`, `MiGa` (present byte-identically in every board
description); [Probable] for `SpEQ` and `WFEQ`, which are defined but are not
surfaced in any platform description, so they cannot be reached from the device
tree.

**Two calibration objects exist, not one.** `SpTS` is the one reachable from the
device tree with no additional machinery, and the one whose envelope is
established here (§9.2.1). `SpEQ` is the richer object but is not mirrored into
the platform description at all — it is held in the factory store and reachable
only through that store's generic 4-character-key interface, and it carries the
machine's acoustic identifier alongside the per-transducer calibration.
**[Probable]**

**On the acoustic identifier:** it does **not** have to be read from the
factory store. Every board description carries `acoustic-id` on
`/product/audio` as a plain u32 (table in §9.4.2), and those values agree with
the published per-model identifiers for every baseline machine. **The platform
description is the authoritative, machine-readable source of the model
identity; use it.** [Confirmed — present on every board of every generation.]

**Note the absence of a fallback clause.** Compare `serial-number`, whose
descriptor is `syscfg/SrNm/0x20,zeroes/0x20` — if the key is missing the
property is filled with zeros. `speaker-thiele-small` and `speaker-trim-gains`
have **no size and no fallback source**. A machine whose factory store lacks
the key therefore yields a property that is **absent or empty**, not a
zero-filled one. A driver must treat "no calibration present" as a distinct,
expected case and fall back to the per-model nominal values — never to zeros.
[Inferred from the descriptor syntax; **the behaviour on a key-missing machine
is [Unknown]** and is Open question 3.]

---

## 9.2 Format of the per-unit calibration data

### 9.2.1 Speaker calibration block (`SpTS`)

The block is a counted array with a 4-byte header. All fields little-endian.

| Offset | Size | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | u8 | `record_count` | Number of per-transducer records |
| 0x01 | u8 | `record_size` | Size of one record in bytes |
| 0x02 | u16 | `version` | Block format version |
| 0x04 | `record_count × record_size` | records | One record per transducer |
| 0x04 + N·S | — | trailer | Present in the object but outside the block the host consumes; contents **[Unknown]**, a checksum is the obvious candidate |

[Confirmed — the header field roles and the total-length rule
`4 + record_count × record_size`. An object whose length is not exactly that
expression is not a valid block.]

**Defined block-format versions** are 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7. [Confirmed]

| `version` | Block length | `record_size` |
|---|---|---|
| 0, 1 | not defined | — |
| 2 | fixed **12 bytes**, a single record | 8 (default), `record_count` = 1 |
| 3 | `4 + count × size` | 8 (default) |
| 4 | **not defined** | — |
| 5, 6, 7 | `4 + count × size` | taken from header byte 1 |
| ≥ 8 | not defined | — |

That version 4 is undefined while 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are defined is a real,
reproducible property of the format and is a useful integrity check for a
driver: any other version value must be treated as "no calibration".

The header triple `{version, record_size, record_count}` is carried verbatim as
a descriptor alongside the raw block, so the records must be parsed using the
*runtime* `record_size` rather than a compiled-in constant. **A driver must do
the same.**

### 9.2.2 Contents of one record

The **field set and its units are established**; the **byte-level layout is
not**.

Protection takes **two separate calibration inputs**: a *per-model
transducer-parameter set* (the nominal Thiele/Small numbers of §9.4.4, the same
for every unit of a model) and a *per-unit transducer-calibration override*. The
per-unit override is applied on top of the per-model set: **the per-unit object
overrides individual fields of the per-model set; it is not a complete parameter
set in its own right.** [Confirmed]

Fields carried by the per-unit calibration, with the units the consumer states
for each:

| Field | Symbol | Unit | Per-unit? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Voice-coil DC resistance | Re / DCR | **Ω** | **yes — the primary factory measurement** | Bracketed at runtime by the per-model acceptance window (§9.4.3) |
| Calibration temperature | Tcal | **°C** | **yes** | The ambient at which DCR was measured; bracketed by the per-model 10–50 °C window |
| Voice-coil inductance | Le | H | yes | |
| Force factor | Bl | **N/A** (= T·m) | yes | |
| Suspension stiffness | Kms | **N/m** | yes | |
| Moving mass | Mms | **g** | yes | **Note the unit: grams here, kilograms in the per-model set (§9.4.4). A factor of 1000.** |
| Mechanical resistance | Rms | **kg/s** | yes | |
| Free-air resonance | Fs | **Hz** | yes | |
| Total Q | Qts | — | yes | |
| Crest factor | — | — | yes | |
| Capacitive displacement-sensor offset / minimum / maximum | Coffset, Cmin, Cmax | **pF** | yes | Present in the schema; **no in-scope machine has a capacitive displacement sensor**, so these are expected to be absent or inert here [Probable] |
| Data-source identifier | — | — | — | Identifies which measurement produced the record |
| Format version | — | — | — | |

[Confirmed for the field set and the units. The parameters fall into three
groups: *speaker calibration* (DCR in Ω, calibration temperature in °C, Q, Fs in
Hz), *displacement calibration* (Kms in N/m, Le, Bl in N/A, Mms in g, Rms in
kg/s) and *capacitive-sensor calibration* (three capacitances in pF).]

This is corroborated independently by the per-model closed-loop parameter set,
which declares exactly the machinery needed to consume a per-unit DCR and
calibration temperature and nothing else: an acceptance window for the
resistance (3.0–5.5 Ω, or a per-channel window such as 3.375–5.670 Ω), an
acceptance window for the calibration temperature (10–50 °C on every in-scope
model), two temperature coefficients of resistance (at 20 °C and 35 °C,
≈0.0033–0.0038 K⁻¹, i.e. copper-clad-aluminium wire), and a scale factor
applied to the calibrated resistance (1.0 everywhere in scope).

**What a driver must take from this.** The one field it cannot do without, if
it wants a closed-loop coil-temperature estimate, is the pair
**(DCR in ohms, calibration temperature in °C)**. Everything else in the record
either refines the excursion model (which is disabled on every in-scope machine
except the A18 Pro one) or duplicates a per-model constant. A driver that reads
only DCR and Tcal, validates them against the per-model windows, and rejects
the record if either is out of range, has everything it needs.

☠ **Still [Unknown], and this is a parsing blocker: the byte offsets, widths
and scaling of each field inside the record**, the meaning of the record's
remaining bytes, and whether the optional fields are present at all on these
machines. See Open question 2.

**Stated plainly: a driver cannot parse this record from this document.** The
envelope is fully specified (§9.2.1) — a driver can locate the block, validate
its version, and walk it into `record_count` records of `record_size` bytes
each — but nothing here says which bytes inside one record are DCR and which are
the calibration temperature, how wide they are, or what scaling applies. No
in-scope board supplies the bytes either: `speaker-thiele-small` is a
placeholder property on every board description available, resolved by boot
firmware only on a provisioned machine (§9.1), so the layout cannot be recovered
by comparing board descriptions. It has to be read from a live provisioned
machine. **[Unknown]**

**What a driver must do until it is.** Two options, and the second is the one to
implement:

1. **Do not consume the record.** Fall back to the per-model nominal DCR and a
   fixed assumed ambient, and run the coil-temperature estimate open-loop with a
   conservative margin — or, safer, run no closed-loop thermal model at all and
   rely on the per-model continuous-power limit. This is correct but gives up the
   only per-unit measurement in the system.
2. **Identify the two fields empirically from the per-model acceptance windows,
   at run time, and refuse the record if the identification is not unique.**
   The per-model set brackets DCR to a narrow window — 3.0–5.5 Ω, or a
   per-channel window as tight as 3.375–5.670 Ω — and the calibration temperature
   to 10–50 °C on every in-scope model (§9.4.3). Those windows are narrow enough
   that, for a given candidate field width and scaling, at most one field of a
   record normally falls inside each. A driver can therefore scan the record for
   fields that fall inside both windows, require exactly one candidate for each
   quantity across **all** records in the block simultaneously (the same offset
   must work for every transducer), and treat any ambiguous or empty result as
   "no calibration present" and fall back to (1). **[Inferred]** — this follows
   from the windows and the record structure, not from an observed layout, and it
   is a mitigation, not a specification. It must be validated against a real
   record before it is trusted, and a driver must log the offsets it chose so
   that the layout can be recorded once and the scan retired.

**Neither option may be skipped by guessing an offset.** A wrong DCR is a wrong
coil-resistance baseline, and since coil temperature is estimated from the ratio
of measured to calibrated resistance, a wrong baseline scales the temperature
estimate by a constant factor in whichever direction the error lies — including,
half the time, the under-protecting direction. ☠
### 9.2.3 Trim-gain block (`SpGa`, and `MiGa`)

Fully established [Confirmed]. Header, then a packed array of signed 16-bit
values, then a 4-byte trailer:

| Offset | Size | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | u8 | `entry_count` | Number of gain entries |
| 0x01 | u8 | `entry_size` | Bytes per entry; **must be 2** for version 1 |
| 0x02 | u16 | `version` | **must be 1**; any other value is rejected |
| 0x04 | `entry_count × 2` | entries | `int16` little-endian, one per transducer |
| 0x04 + 2·N | 4 | trailer | Contents **[Unknown]** |

Total object length is validated as **`entry_count × entry_size + 8`** — i.e.
4-byte header plus payload plus 4-byte trailer.

**Units and scaling** [Confirmed]:

```
trim_gain_dB = entry / 10          /* entry is a signed 16-bit value */
```

Resolution **0.1 dB**; sign preserved (negative = attenuation). The value is
converted to a 32.32 fixed-point decibel quantity before use. The index into
the array is selected by a per-device transducer selector, not by a fixed
convention — the mapping from transducer to index is supplied by the machine's
configuration and is **[Unknown]** from platform data alone.

`MiGa` uses the same header, the same version-1 gate and the same 0.1 dB
scaling; it is the microphone-array equivalent.

### 9.2.4 What is per-unit and what is per-model

This is the distinction that decides what may be shipped in a driver.

| Quantity | Per-unit or per-model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Voice-coil DC resistance of each transducer | **per-unit** | factory store, `SpTS` |
| Temperature at which that resistance was measured | **per-unit** | factory store, `SpTS` |
| Per-transducer gain trim (0.1 dB steps) | **per-unit** | factory store, `SpGa` |
| Equalisation calibration | **per-unit** [Probable] | factory store, `SpEQ` / `WFEQ` |
| Thermal resistances, time constants, temperature limits, headroom | **per-model** | OS tuning set, selected by `acoustic-id` |
| Nominal/reference blocked resistance, resistance acceptance window | **per-model** | OS tuning set |
| Temperature coefficients of resistance at 20 °C and 35 °C | **per-model** | OS tuning set |
| Sense full-scale constants (14 V, 3.75 A) | **per-model** (constant across the whole population) | OS tuning set; also published by the protection daemon |
| Thiele/Small parameters (Bl, Mms, Kms, Rms, port parameters) | **per-model** | OS tuning set |
| Excursion limit | **per-model** | OS tuning set |
| Amplifier analogue full-scale level | **per-model** | platform description, `speaker-config` byte 1 |
| Sense slot assignment | **per-model** | platform description, `speaker-config` bytes 2 and 3; record structure [Confirmed] |
| Playback (receive) slot assignment | **per-model** | platform description, `speaker-config` byte 0; record structure [Confirmed], record-to-transducer **binding [Probable]** on the MacBook Pro chassis and [Confirmed] elsewhere — **confirm by `TDM_CFG3` readback before driving speakers on that chassis** (§8 §8.2.3) |
| Amplifier index → transducer identity | **per-model** | platform description, `speakerN` phandle chain |
| Speaker module variant identity | **per-unit (strapped in the module)** | GPIO pins, §9.6 |

**Consequence for a driver.** Every parameter needed to run the thermal model
except the voice-coil resistance is per-model and may be compiled in. The
voice-coil resistance and its measurement temperature are per-unit and **must
be read from the machine** if the model is to be run closed-loop. A driver that
runs the model on the per-model nominal resistance alone is running open-loop
with respect to unit-to-unit spread; that is what the protection daemon
baseline does today, and it is safe only because the daemon's power estimate
comes from the measured `V × I` product rather than from an assumed impedance.
**Do not use the per-model nominal resistance to convert a voltage into a
power or a temperature.**

---

## 9.3 Is the data uploaded to any device?

**No. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.** [Confirmed]

- **To the amplifier.** The SN012776 / TAS2764-class part has no coefficient
  memory, no thermal model and no parameter interface. Its entire host-writable
  state is the register map: level, digital volume, slot assignment, sense
  enables, high-pass corner, over-current retry, brown-out preset and interrupt
  masks. There is nowhere to put a Thiele/Small parameter. The MAX98360A-class
  part on the A18 Pro machine has **no control interface at all** — one
  shutdown/enable pin and nothing else.
- **To the always-on coprocessor.** No speaker-parameter or calibration object
  is exchanged with it; the messages that are exchanged concern stream setup,
  formats, clocking and power. **[Probable]**
- **To the low-power audio processor.** Its filter function is
  coefficient-driven (windowed-FIR blocks with a coefficient cache) and the
  coefficients come from the host. It is used for the microphone path on all
  machines and, on the A18 Pro machine only, for the speaker transport. There
  is no speaker-parameter object in its interface.

Instead, the calibration block is **carried as a property on the audio device**
and is read from there by the host-side protection model, which converts the
values into floating-point model parameters. The point in bring-up at which it
must be consumed is **before the first unmute**, not at stream start.

For an independent driver this means: the kernel's only obligations are
(a) read the calibration property out of the platform description, (b) publish
it to whatever runs the protection model, and (c) refuse to unmute until that
consumer is alive and has acknowledged it.

---

## 9.4 Speaker parameters, per model

Four parameter sets exist. Which one a machine uses is determined by whether it
has a sense return (`speaker-protection` in the platform description) and by
which tuning set its `acoustic-id` selects.

| Machine class | `speaker-protection` | Sense channels | Protection model |
|---|---|---|---|
| MacBook Pro 14/16-inch, MacBook Air 15-inch | 1 | 2 × N | **closed-loop**, sense-driven, two-stage thermal (`spp3` in the published protection-daemon nomenclature) |
| MacBook Air 13-inch | 1 | 2 × N | **closed-loop**, a different system-identification processor (not the `spp3` one) |
| iMac 24-inch, Mac mini, Mac Studio | 0 | none | **open-loop**, feed-forward thermal only (`atsp` in the published nomenclature) |
| MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) | absent | none | **open-loop**, feed-forward loudspeaker model with explicit Thiele/Small parameters, plus a neural-net stage |

### 9.4.1 Amplifier index → transducer identity

This mapping is **not** the same on all six-amplifier machines and getting it
wrong means applying a tweeter's thermal parameters to a woofer, or the
reverse. It is established from two independent sources that agree exactly:
the platform description's `speakerN` phandle chain on the primary amplifier
node (which also gives each amplifier's I²C address), and the per-model
protection parameter set's channel names.

| Layout | Machines | Amplifier index 0 … N−1 | I²C addresses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Six-amplifier, MacBook Pro** | j604, j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c (M4); j704, j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c (M5) | L woofer 1, **R woofer 1**, L woofer 2, R woofer 2, L tweeter, R tweeter | 0x38, 0x3b, 0x39, 0x3c, 0x3a, 0x3d |
| **Six-amplifier, MacBook Air 15-inch** | j715 (M4), j815 (M5) | L woofer 1, R woofer 1, **L tweeter, R tweeter**, L woofer 2, R woofer 2 | 0x38, 0x3b, 0x39, 0x3c, 0x3a, 0x3d |
| **Four-amplifier** | j713 (M4), j813 (M5), j623, j624 (M4 iMac) | L woofer, R woofer, L tweeter, R tweeter | 0x38, 0x3b, 0x39, 0x3c |
| **Single amplifier** | j773g, j773s, j575c | mono full-range | 0x38 |

[Confirmed — the phandle chain and the parameter-set channel names agree on
every board tested, including the M1 Pro and M2 baseline boards.]

Two consequences:

- The **I²C address order is not the amplifier index order**. Amplifier index 1
  is at address 0x3b, index 2 at 0x39. This is identical on M1 Pro through
  M5 Max.
- On the MacBook Pro layout the tweeters are at indices **4 and 5**; on the
  MacBook Air 15-inch layout they are at indices **2 and 3**, with the same
  `speaker-config` blob and the same I²C addresses. The blob does not
  distinguish them; only the node names and the `speakerN` chain do.

This refines rather than contradicts the established cross-section finding that
`speaker-config` and `amp-tx-zd-config` are byte-identical across all
six-amplifier machines — they are, and that is precisely why the identity of
the transducer at each index has to come from the phandle chain instead.

The sense channel pair for amplifier index *i* is capture channels
**(2i, 2i+1)**, consistent with the sense slot bytes `4i` and `4i+2` in the
`speaker-config` record for that index.

### 9.4.2 Closed-loop thermal model — per-transducer parameters

Model form (identical to the published protection-daemon model):

```
P(t)        = V(t) × I(t)                                      [W]
T_magnet   → t_ambient + P × tr_magnet,  first order, τ = tau_magnet
T_coil     → T_magnet  + P × tr_coil,    first order, τ = tau_coil
```

Gain reduction is applied when the estimated temperature approaches `t_limit`;
exceeding `t_limit + t_headroom` is a hard fault.

Units: `tr_*` in **°C/W**, `tau_*` in **s**, temperatures in **°C**,
`z_nominal` (reference blocked resistance) in **Ω**, `z_shunt` (series
resistance between the sense point and the coil) in **Ω**.

**Global parameters, identical on every in-scope closed-loop machine**
[Confirmed across 8 acoustic IDs]:

| Parameter | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Assumed ambient temperature | **50.0** | °C |
| Gain attack time | 4.6 | s |
| Gain release time | 20.0 | s |
| Look-ahead delay | 2.0 | ms |
| Fallback ("safe") temperature limit | 100 | °C |
| Fallback limit offset | −15.0 | °C |
| Fallback limit minimum hold time | 10 | minutes [Probable — unit inferred from the field's name and magnitude] |
| Displacement peak attack / decay | 0.0001 / 0.01 | s |
| Displacement control | **disabled** | — |
| Peak-current-budget control | **disabled** | — |
| Parameter-set version | 9 | — |

Note the assumed ambient of **50 °C**, not room temperature. The model assumes
the enclosure interior is already hot. A driver must use the same figure; using
25 °C would under-estimate coil temperature by 25 °C.

**Per-transducer parameters.** `acoustic-id` values map to machines as follows;
values are identical between the M4 and M5 member of each chassis pair

`z_shunt` is **0** on this machine (no series shunt modelled). Temperature
coefficients: woofers 0.003520824409191097 / 0.003281469966695325 K⁻¹;
tweeters 0.00347479622796732 / 0.00336649262905687 K⁻¹.

**This is the machine where the index→transducer mapping matters most.** The
tweeters sit at amplifier indices 2 and 3 and their thermal resistance is
**three times** the woofers'. Applying woofer parameters to index 2 or 3 would
allow roughly 3.2× the safe power into a tweeter.

**MacBook Air 13-inch — `acoustic-id` 37 (M4) and 42 (M5)**

These two machines use a **fundamentally different protection architecture**
from every other in-scope machine, and it is the one place in the range where
the *source* of the per-unit data changes.

Instead of a fixed thermal model seeded by factory calibration, they pair a
**runtime loudspeaker-model manager** with an **online system-identification
stage** that continuously measures the transducer's electrical impedance from
the sense return and updates the model in place. The model-update logic is
gated on **percentage change thresholds in coil resistance and in suspension
stiffness**, it maintains a per-channel tuning selection, and it can be told to
bypass identification and to enable or disable closed-loop temperature
estimation independently. The learned model is **cached in per-machine mutable
storage on the data volume**, not in the factory store. [Confirmed for the
mechanism and its parameter set; the numeric contents of the cache are
**[Unknown]**.]

Two consequences for a driver:

- On these two machines the per-unit factory calibration is **not the
  authoritative source of coil resistance at runtime** — the measured,
  continuously-updated value is. The factory record is a seed at most; the
  graph description for the M5 member of the pair leaves its per-unit
  calibration input **unconnected**. [Probable]
- A driver that implements only the fixed two-stage thermal model of §9.4.2 on
  these machines is implementing a *different*, simpler model than the
  reference. That is acceptable — the published open-source protection daemon
  does exactly that on the M2 and M3 members of the same chassis — **provided
  it is seeded conservatively**, because it will not adapt to a transducer
  whose resistance has drifted.

Recoverable numeric parameters for the identification stage:
sense full scales 3.75 A / 14 V (unchanged); reference blocked resistance
**4.04 Ω**, acceptance window **3.0–6.4 Ω**; a single temperature coefficient
**0.0037836 K⁻¹**; an assumed ambient of **50 °C**; a resistance-derived
temperature estimate. Per-transducer thermal resistances and time constants in
this processor's parameter vector are **[Unknown]** — the vector is not
self-describing. The M2-generation equivalent of this chassis publishes woofer
`tr_coil` 32.1 / `tr_magnet` 20 °C/W, `tau` 4.7 / 66.5 s, `z_nominal` 4 Ω and
tweeter `tr_coil` 104.9 / `tr_magnet` 129.5 °C/W, `tau` 3.9 / 70 s,
`z_nominal` 3.72 Ω, all at `t_limit` 140 °C, and the Thiele/Small set for this
chassis is **byte-identical from M2 through M5** (§9.4.4), so those figures are
the best available starting point [Probable].

### 9.4.3 Closed-loop measurement parameters (common)

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voltage-sense full scale | **14.0** | V | 16-bit signed sample ±32768 maps to ±14 V |
| Current-sense full scale | **3.75** | A | 16-bit signed sample ±32768 maps to ±3.75 A |
| Calibrated-resistance scale | 1.0 | — | multiplier applied to the per-unit resistance |
| Calibration-temperature window | 10 – 50 | °C | valid range for the per-unit measurement temperature |
| Temperature-sense window | 0.18 | s | integration window for the resistance estimate |
| Temperature-sense smoothing | 1.0 | s | first-order smoothing of the estimate |
| Limit-error decay time | 30.0 | s | |
| Limit adjustment cap | 60.0 | °C | maximum correction the closed loop may apply to the limit |
| Pilot-tone frequency | **43.0664** | Hz | sub-audible tone injected to measure coil resistance |
| Pilot amplitude, high / low | −30 / −40 | dBFS | |
| Pilot upper / lower engage thresholds | 90 / 80 | (arb.) | units **[Unknown]** |
| Pilot enable threshold | 0.03 | (arb.) | units **[Unknown]** |
| Pilot decay time (both stages) | 0.03 | s | |
| Voltage / current power thresholds | 1e-3 / 1e-5 | (arb.) | below these the estimate is not updated |

The **43.07 Hz pilot tone** is a hardware-visible fact worth stating plainly: a
correctly-operating machine injects a continuous low-level tone below the
speaker's usable band in order to measure voice-coil resistance, and therefore
voice-coil temperature, independently of programme material. An independent
driver is not obliged to do this — the published protection daemon does not —
but it is how the reference implementation converts the per-unit resistance
calibration into a live temperature.

### 9.4.5 Excursion and displacement limits

| Parameter | Unit | Values seen in scope |
|---|---|---|
| Excursion limit | mm | 0.2 and 0.4 (closed-loop machines), 0.45 on baseline Air 13-inch |
| Moving mass (displacement model) | kg | 1.85e-4, 2.35e-4, 2.55e-4 |
| Suspension stiffness (displacement model) | N/m | 2290, 3000, 3200, 4400 |
| Mechanical damping (displacement model) | N·s/m | 0.26, 0.28, 0.32, 0.33 |
| Displacement quality factor | — | 1.3, 1.9451, 2.0609, 2.1435 |
| Shape factor | — | 0.76 |
| Bandwidth factor | — | 1.0 |
| Displacement protection type | enum | 0 on every in-scope machine |

**Two warnings.**

1. On **every** in-scope closed-loop machine the displacement control is
   **explicitly disabled** in the parameter set. Excursion is not being
   protected on these machines; the thermal model is the only active limiter.
2. The displacement parameters as shipped are **not internally consistent** —
   on several models the woofer and the tweeter on the same side carry
   identical mass, stiffness and damping, which is physically impossible. They
   appear to be placeholders left in a disabled block. **Do not use them.** The
   Thiele/Small set of §9.4.4 is the one that is internally consistent
   (resonances of 416–533 Hz, force factors and masses that agree with the
   measured resistances).

The A18 Pro machine is the exception: its feed-forward loudspeaker model is
**active** and is the only excursion protection on that machine (§9.8.2).

### 9.4.6 Maximum-level constraints

The platform description states the amplifier's analogue full-scale level
directly, as the **second byte of each `speaker-config` record**:

```
full_scale_level_dBV = 11.0 + 0.5 × code
full_scale_peak_V    = √2 × 10^(level_dBV / 20)
```

This is independently confirmed three ways: the level codes match the published
per-model amplifier-gain limits in the upstream machine-level sound-card
driver on every baseline board; the code-to-decibel law is the published
TAS2764/TAS2770 register scaling; and the per-model tuning set's
amplifier-full-scale field carries **exactly** the corresponding peak voltage
on every machine tested.

| Machine | Code | Level dBV | Full scale V RMS | Full scale V peak | Tuning-set value V peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| j604, j713, j715, j614s/c, j616s/c, j704, j813, j815, j714s/c, j716s/c | 0x0f | **18.5** | 8.414 | 11.899 | **11.885** |
| **j773g, j773s** (Mac mini M4 / M4 Pro) | 0x0f | **18.5** | 8.414 | 11.899 | **11.900** |
| j623, j624 (iMac 24-inch M4) | 0x12 | **20.0** | 10.000 | 14.142 | **14.000** |
| j575c (Mac Studio) | 0x14 | **21.0** | 11.220 | 15.867 | **15.870** |
| j700 (MacBook Neo) | n/a — no control interface | — | 5.19 | **7.34** | **7.34** |

**The M4 Mac mini's amplifier level dropped from 21.0 dBV on the M2/M3 Mac mini
to 18.5 dBV.** That is a real, safety-relevant per-machine change; a driver
carrying over an M2-era level for this chassis would over-drive by 2.5 dB. ☠

**Do not rely on the amplifier's reset state.** The SN012776/TAS2764 comes out
of reset with its level field at maximum — **21.0 dBV** — and its digital
volume at 0 dB. On a 14-inch MacBook Pro that is 2.5 dB above the platform's
intended level *before* any content is applied. The level must be programmed
down from the platform value before the first unmute, and it must be
reprogrammed after every software reset or shutdown-pin cycle, because those
restore defaults.

Derived peak electrical power at full scale, into the per-model nominal
impedance, alongside the thermal model's continuous limit:

| Machine | Nominal Ω | Peak power W | Continuous safe W | Gap dB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MacBook Pro 14-inch M4/M5 (woofer) | 3.2 | 44.2 | 1.28 | **15.4** |
| MacBook Pro 16-inch M4/M5 (woofer) | 2.7 | 52.4 | 1.744 | **14.8** |
| MacBook Air 15-inch M4/M5 (tweeter) | 3.76 | 37.7 | 0.421 | **19.5** |
| iMac 24-inch M4 (tweeter) | 5.5 | 35.6 | 0.574 | **17.9** |
| Mac mini M4 | 4.6 | 30.8 | 0.90 | **15.3** |
| Mac Studio | 4.6 | 54.8 | 0.94 | **17.7** |

The "gap" column is the amount of gain reduction a protection model has to be
capable of applying, and equally the amount by which an unprotected driver can
over-drive the coil.

## 9.5 The sense return

Established in detail in the parts of this specification dealing with the
amplifier and the serial-audio path; summarised here only where it bears on
calibration.

- The sense return is **S16, interleaved, 2 channels per amplifier**, at the
  playback frame rate (48 kHz nominal), on the capture side of the same stream
  endpoint as playback. The receive channel mask in the platform description is
  exactly `2 × N` bits wide: 0xfff on every six-amplifier machine, 0xff on the
  four-amplifier Airs, **0x000 on every machine whose `speaker-protection` is
  0**, and **0x000 on the A18 Pro machine**.
- Scaling to physical units, per sample `s` in −32768 … +32767:

  ```
  V = (s_V / 32768) × 14.0     volts
  I = (s_I / 32768) × 3.75     amperes
  P = V × I                    watts
  ```

  These two constants are **the same on every machine in the population**,
  M1 through M5, and do **not** depend on the programmed amplifier level.
- The amplifier family is capable of transmitting more than current and
  voltage — the sense channel set defined per speaker is *voltage*, *current*,
  *power-supply voltage*, *boost voltage*, a *flags* word, a *PDM monitor* and
  a *keepalive* channel. **[Probable]** **Only current and voltage
  are configured on any in-scope machine**: each `speaker-config` record
  assigns exactly two 8-bit slot units per amplifier, and the receive channel
  count is exactly `2 × N`. The richer telemetry types exist in the part but
  are unused here. [Confirmed]
- There is a separate, capture-only **speaker tap** stream on the M5 and A18
  Pro machines (absent on M4), carrying one channel per amplifier in the
  machine's main clock domain. It is a monitor of the speaker signal, not a
  sense return, and it is **not** part of the protection loop
  [Probable — it carries N channels, not 2N, and the protection input is the
  2N-channel sense stream].

---

## 9.6 Speaker-module identification

A two-pin GPIO strap on the speaker module assembly, read by the host at probe.

**Mechanism** [Confirmed]:

1. The primary amplifier node carries `find-speaker-id = 1`. If absent or 0,
   no identification is performed.
2. The node carries `function-speaker-id0` and `function-speaker-id1`, each of
   the standard shape `u32 phandle | 4-byte tag ("GPIO") | u32 pin | u32 flags`,
   with flags `0x00000100` (input) on every board.
3. Each pin is read; **bit 0 of the read value** is taken.
4. The identity is assembled **LSB-first**: `id = bit(pin0) | bit(pin1) << 1`.
   The read defaults to 0xFFFF if a pin cannot be read.
5. The node carries `valid-speaker-ids`, an array of u32 values. The assembled
   identity is compared against **every element**; if it matches none, the
   identity becomes the default **0xFFFF**.
6. The resulting identity is published to the rest of the stack as a 32-bit
   value.

**How many variants a machine can report.** Exactly **two**.
`valid-speaker-ids` is `{0x00000000, 0x00000003}` — a list of two allowed
values, not a range — on **all 33 boards that carry it**, M1 Pro through
M5 Max, without exception. Two pins give four raw encodings; only both-low
(id 0) and both-high (id 3) are accepted. Encodings 1 and 2 are invalid and
map to the default. That is a deliberate complementary-strap arrangement:
a broken, unseated or unpopulated connector reads as an invalid code rather
than silently as a valid one.

**Per-board pin assignments** (GPIO pin numbers, id0 / id1):

| Board | Machine | id0 pin | id1 pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| j604 | MacBook Pro 14-inch M4 | 4 | 13 |
| j623, j624 | iMac 24-inch M4 | 4 | 13 |
| j713 | MacBook Air 13-inch M4 | 4 | 13 |
| j715 | MacBook Air 15-inch M4 | 4 | 13 |
| j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c | MacBook Pro 14/16-inch M4 Pro/Max | 52 | 53 |
| j704 | MacBook Pro 14-inch M5 | 198 | 199 |
| j815 | MacBook Air 15-inch M5 | 6 | 11 |
| j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c | MacBook Pro 14/16-inch M5 Pro/Max | 136 | 137 |
| **j813** | **MacBook Air 13-inch M5** | **— absent —** | **— absent —** |
| j773g, j773s, j575c, j700 | Mac mini, Mac Studio, MacBook Neo | — absent — | — absent — |

**Does the identity select the calibration or the protection data?**

- It selects **tuning, gain and equalisation**, not thermal protection
  parameters. [Confirmed] The per-model tuning set ships, for most machines,
  a default tuning set plus one variant per valid identity. Diffing the
  identity-0 and identity-3 variants for a 14-inch MacBook Pro M4 shows the
  **only** differences are one analysis-filter preset and **two output gain
  stages, which differ by 13.30 dB** — identity 0 runs 13.30 dB below
  identity 3. The protection processor's parameter set is shared between the
  two variants and is byte-identical.
- **A 13.30 dB difference in output gain between the two module variants is
  itself a protection-relevant quantity.** A driver that reads the identity
  wrongly, or ignores it and picks the louder variant on a machine fitted with
  the quieter module, will over-drive by 13.3 dB. ☠
- Therefore: **a driver on a machine that carries the strap must read the
  identity before choosing its output gain**, and must treat a non-matching
  code as "use the quieter default", not as "use the default variant".
  The shipped default graph is byte-identical to the **identity-0** variant on
  every machine tested that has a difference at all — i.e. the safe default is
  the quiet one.

**Machines where the identity is not available.**

- **j813 (MacBook Air 13-inch M5) silently drops the strap its M4 predecessor
  j713 carries.** It has no `find-speaker-id`, no `function-speaker-idN` and no
  `valid-speaker-ids`, while retaining `speaker-protection = 1` and a full
  eight-channel sense return. Its per-model tuning set correspondingly ships
  **no identity variants at all** — a single graph, no identity-0/identity-3
  split. The implication for a driver is clean and reassuring: **on j813 there
  is exactly one speaker module variant, the identity is not needed, and a
  driver must not attempt to read one.** [Confirmed — the absence is
  consistent across the platform description and the per-model tuning set.]
- j713 (MacBook Air 13-inch M4) is the converse and is the odd case: it
  **carries the strap** but its tuning set ships **no identity variants**.
  The identity is read and published but nothing consumes it on that machine.
  A driver should read it (to detect an invalid strap as a fault indication)
  but must not expect it to select anything. [Confirmed]
- j773g, j773s and j575c carry no strap, and although their tuning sets do
  contain nominal identity-0 and identity-3 variants those variants are
  **byte-identical to each other and to the default**, so the question is moot.
  [Confirmed]
- j700 (MacBook Neo) carries no strap and no variants.

---

### 9.7.1 Open-loop parameter sets (no-sense machines)

For the machines with no sense return the entire model is feed-forward: coil
temperature is estimated from the *known* output signal and the *nominal*
impedance, with no measurement of any kind. The parameter block is a flat
vector, one group per distinct transducer, of the form
`{full-scale V peak, nominal Ω, tr_coil °C/W, tau_coil s, tr_magnet °C/W,
tau_magnet s, t_ambient °C, t_limit °C, f_low Hz, f_high Hz, t_headroom °C}`.
[Confirmed — the mapping is established by exact agreement with the published
protection-daemon parameters for the equivalent baseline machine, on every
field.]

| Machine | Transducer | Full scale V pk | Nominal Ω | tr_coil °C/W | tau_coil s | tr_magnet °C/W | tau_magnet s | t_ambient °C | t_limit °C | t_headroom °C | Band Hz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| j623/j624 iMac M4 | woofer | 14.0 | 7.0 | 20 | 10.0 | 28 | 391 | 50 | **120** | 20 | 100 – 13 000 |
| j623/j624 iMac M4 | tweeter | 14.0 | 5.5 | 46 | 1.3 | 76 | 115 | 50 | **120** | 40 | 100 – 13 000 |
| j773g/j773s Mac mini M4 | mono | **11.90** | 4.6 | 40 | 3.4 | 60 | 210 | 50 | 140 | 40 | 1 000 – 20 000 |
| j575c Mac Studio | mono | 15.87 | 4.6 | 40 | 3.7 | 60 | 250 | **46** | 140 | 40 | 1 000 – 20 000 |

The Mac Studio numbers are identical to the published M1 Mac mini parameters
except for the amplifier full scale — i.e. the same transducer, unchanged. The
M4 Mac mini differs in `tau_magnet` (210 s vs 250 s), in ambient assumption
(50 °C vs 46 °C) and, most importantly, in full-scale level (11.90 V vs
15.87 V peak).

Because these machines have no measurement at all, **the per-unit calibration
is present in the factory store but is not used by the protection model**
[Probable]. It remains available to the gain/equalisation path.
