# 12. Capture path

## Baseline

Measured against the M1–M3 built-in-microphone path as documented upstream:
three PDM microphone elements feeding an
ADC + decimator **inside the always-on coprocessor**, delivered to the
host as decimated PCM by a host-addressable audio DMA controller, with all
control (element selection, clocking, decimator configuration, power state)
carried over a mailbox/serial-transport to the coprocessor rather than by host
MMIO. Two further capture paths existed: the headset (jack) microphone through
the analog jack codec on a receive serial link, and the speaker current/voltage
sense return merged onto a receive serialiser. On M1–M3 the platform hardware
description exposed explicit PDM and decimation-filter nodes
(`audio-pdm2`, `dc-2400000`, `dc-800000`, `hfdc-2400000`) as children of the
coprocessor audio node, each carrying its filter coefficients inline.

The transport protocol itself is Section 11 and is specified there: the mailbox
register map and message format in §11.2.1–§11.2.7, the version handshake,
endpoint map and power states in §11.2.8, the shared-memory ring endpoint
protocol in §11.4.2, the framed call header and service resolution in
§11.4.3–§11.4.5, the audio service's request framing, device identifiers,
call types and property payloads in §11.4.6, and the complete
configure-and-start sequence for the microphone capture path — including the
front-end and decimator property calls this section's hardware description
corresponds to — in §11.4.7. This section documents the **capture hardware**
— element wiring, the PDM front end and decimator, the DMA bindings, the
security gating, and the per-endpoint / per-machine inventory — and refers to
those subsections for the message layer rather than restating them.

All controller and proxy apertures below are **absolute**: the platform
description's I/O-region-relative `reg` value plus the `/arm-io` `ranges` parent
base, which is **not uniform** — `0x2_0000_0000` on t8132, t604x and t605x,
`0x2_1000_0000` on t8140 and t8142. They match §4 §4.2.4 value for value.
**[Confirmed]** Power-domain control-register addresses on the in-scope SoCs would
be derived through the group encoding that has no external ground truth; none is
quoted here, and any such address would be **[Probable]** on internal consistency
only.

## Summary of differences

| Topic | M1–M3 baseline | t8132 / t604x (M4) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 / t605x (M5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Built-in PDM element count | 3 | 3 | **2** | 3 |
| ADC + decimator location | in coprocessor | unchanged (in coprocessor) | unchanged | unchanged |
| PDM/decimator nodes in platform description | explicit, with inline coefficients | **absent** — coprocessor audio node is a service stub | absent | absent |
| Decimator coefficients | supplied to coprocessor (inline in description on M3) | **internal to coprocessor firmware** | internal | internal |
| Built-in mic-array DMA domain | non-secure coprocessor DMA | **non-secure** (`admac-leap-ns`) | **secure** (`admac-leap-s`) + isolated stream proxy | **secure** (`admac-leap-s`) + isolated stream proxy |
| Isolated / exclave capture services | none | none | present (mic array, VT, LP mic) | present (mic array, VT, LP mic, secure loopback) |
| Low-power mic I/O buffer | plain coprocessor-mapped buffer | plain (`iop-audio,io-buffer-device`) | **isolated** (`iop-audio,isolated-io-buffer-device`) | isolated |
| Speaker-tap capture endpoint | (M3 loopback only) | absent | **present** | present |
| Mic-injection endpoint (16 kHz) | absent | absent | **present** | present |
| Secure-loopback endpoint | absent | absent | absent | **present (t605x only; development-only)** |
| Second coprocessor instance | none | none | present (`aop2`) | present (`aop2`, with own firmware) |

The headline capture-path change is one of **ownership**: on M4 the built-in
microphone array is still a plain host-DMA capture stream (as on M1–M3, only
re-parented under `iop-audio-controller`); on A18 Pro and every M5-class machine
the same array is moved into a **secure DMA domain behind an isolated execution
environment**, and a normal-world driver can no longer read it directly.

## 12.1 Endpoint model and how a capture endpoint is described

Every capture and playback stream on the in-scope SoCs is a child of
`/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` (`compatible = "iop-audio,controller"`, no `reg`).
Each child endpoint carries:

- `identifier` — a FourCC naming the stream to the coprocessor audio service
  (stored byte-reversed in the description). Capture-relevant values:
  `hpai` (built-in mic array — "high-power audio input"),
  `lpai` (low-power mic / voice-trigger input),
  ` nic` (codec / headset-jack input, reads `cin`),
  `blil` (internal loopback), `kbpl` (serial-cluster loopback, reads `lpbk`),
  ` pat` (speaker tap, reads `tap`), `lpij` (mic-injection, reads `jipl`).
- `compatible` — `iop-adma-stream,leap` (endpoint on the low-power audio
  processor's serial cluster) or `iop-adma-stream,mca` (endpoint on a base-domain
  serial cluster).
- `device_type` — `iop-audio-ns` (non-secure) or `iop-audio-s` (**secure**).
- The DMA-channel binding, in one of two forms:
  - **M4 form** (`dma-channels`, 128-byte blob + `dma-parent` phandle): four
    8-word records `[channel, port, 0, buf_hi, buf_lo, 0,0,0]`, giving the
    receive/transmit channel index and a per-channel buffer byte allocation.
    Record 0/1 are the transmit pair, 2/3 the receive pair; a record of all-ones
    (`0xffffffff…`) marks that direction unused. Port `0x21`/`0x22` are the two
    coprocessor DMA slave ports.
  - **A18 Pro / M5 form** (`dma-provider-tx` / `dma-provider-rx` strings naming
    a channel node, e.g. `leap-s-adma-rx-0`, `base-ns-adma-rx-2`).
- A single data child node whose `reg` (nine u32) is the stream format
  descriptor (§12.5) and whose `data-sources` blob carries the format-tag FourCC and
  the list of supported sample rates.

[Confirmed — consistent on every board from M1 to M5.]

**How the endpoint is configured once it is attached.** A capture endpoint of
this kind is a **serial-audio stream endpoint** and takes the same property
vocabulary as a playback one: key `701` carries its receive slot mask, receive
slot and sample widths, frame geometry and clocking in one 109-byte record, key
`703` the master-clock enable, key `702` a reset, and keys `401`/`402` the two
upper state codes its power ladder uses. **Section 18 §18.2 and §18.3** give
that vocabulary; §18 §18.6.1 gives the ordered start sequence, which for a
capture stream differs from §11 §11.4.7 only in the direction mask carried by
the two key-`202` transitions. The pulse-density front end (`pdm0`) keeps its
own separate keys `200` and `212` (§11 §11.4.6) — it is not a serial-audio
endpoint. [Confirmed]

## 12.2 PDM microphone count and wiring

**Element count per machine** — established from the mic-array endpoint's
`input-data-selectors` property (a list of per-element FourCCs), corroborated by
the receive slot mask in the format descriptor and by `/product/audio`
`supportedChannels`:

| Machines | `input-data-selectors` | RX slots | `supportedChannels` | Elements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| t8132, t604x, t8142, t605x (all) | `imi1 imi2 imi3` | 0x7 (3) | 7 | **3** [Confirmed] |
| t8140 (j700, MacBook Neo) | `imi1 imi2` | 0x3 (2) | 3 | **2** [Confirmed] |

`default-input-data-selectors` equals `input-data-selectors` on every board.
The number of selectors is the microphone count and is the one microphone-array
difference on the A18 Pro machine.

**Element type**: PDM (pulse-density-modulation) digital microphones, omni,
no hardware beamforming — three (or two) elements presented as independent
channels. Unchanged from M1–M3. [Confirmed]

**Clock / data pin arrangement**: not exposed in the platform hardware
description on any in-scope board — the PDM bit clock and data lines terminate at
the PDM front end inside the coprocessor complex and are not routed to
host-visible pins. **[Unknown — pin/pad assignment]**; a probing experiment is
required (Open question 7).

**Per-element power-enable line**: present only on the A18 Pro machine (j700).
Its mic-array data node carries `function-input_power_enable` whose target is the
system power-management microcontroller, invoked through the `pcIO` power-switch
key with a rail/index argument (arg1 `0x00190000`). No other in-scope board
carries a per-element microphone power-enable in its description; on those the
element supply is managed by the coprocessor and is **[Unknown]** to the host.
[Confirmed for j700; Inferred for the rest.]

## 12.3 ADC and decimator hardware

**Location — unchanged from M1–M3.** The PDM bitstream is converted and
decimated inside the always-on coprocessor complex; the host never sees
PDM, only decimated PCM delivered by DMA. [Confirmed]

**Platform-description structure — changed.** On M1–M3 the coprocessor audio
node exposed explicit `audio-pdm2` and decimation-filter child nodes
(`dc-2400000`, `dc-800000`, `hfdc-2400000`), each carrying its decimation
`ratios`, `latency`, `filterLengths`, and the filter `coefficients` inline. On
every in-scope SoC the corresponding node
(`/arm-io/aop/iop-aop-nub/aop-audio`) is reduced to a **service stub**
(`compatible = "iop-audio,aop-service"`) with **no PDM node, no decimator node
and no coefficient array**. The PDM/decimator configuration therefore moved out
of the platform description entirely. [Confirmed — the M4/M5/A18 descriptions
carry no such child nodes; the M1–M3 descriptions do.]

**Where the configuration went — it is fixed inside the coprocessor, and a host
driver cannot read it out.** The high-frequency-decimator configuration is
unchanged in value from the M3 generation, which carried it inline in its
platform description: latency 36, decimation `ratios = 10, 5, 3`,
`filterLengths = 0x00D94960` — three per-stage filter lengths decoding as
**96 / 73 / 217 taps** (sum 386) — followed by a coefficient table of exactly
**386 × 64-bit signed words (3088 bytes)**. On every in-scope SoC that same
configuration is **resident in the coprocessor and is no longer host-supplied**.

Three consequences, all of which matter to a driver author:

1. **The platform description no longer exposes these values.** A driver must not
   look for `dc-*`, `hfdc-*`, `ratios`, `latency`, `filterLengths` or
   `coefficients` nodes under the coprocessor audio node on t8132, t604x, t8140,
   t8142 or t605x — they are absent, and their absence is not a fault.
2. **A host driver cannot read them out at run time either.** There is no call in
   the interface of §11 or §18 that returns a decimator coefficient table or a
   filter length, and no host MMIO aperture for the decimator block. The values
   above are the specification of what the hardware does; they are not something
   a driver can query and act on.
3. **A host driver does not need them to capture.** The decimation chain is
   fixed, its total ratio is 150, and the only quantities a driver needs from it
   are the resulting native rate (16 000 Hz) and the group delay implied by the
   filter lengths. Nothing in the capture path requires programming a coefficient.
   They are documented here so that a driver can predict the latency of the
   capture path and so that the chain's arithmetic is checkable.

[Confirmed — the configuration is identical in value to the M3 generation's,
which is published in that generation's platform description, and the M4, A18 Pro
and M5 platform descriptions carry no decimator configuration at all.]

**Supported / native rate.** PDM clock 2 400 000 Hz; PDM-controller reference
clock 24 000 000 Hz; decimation chain 10 × 5 × 3 = 150 ⇒ native decimated rate
**16 000 Hz**. The high-power mic-array stream is presented to the host at
48 000 Hz (§12.6); where the 16 kHz native rate is up-converted is **[Unknown]**
(Open question 4). The M1–M3 "standard" decimator variants (`dc-2400000`,
`dc-800000`; 32-bit coefficients; ratios 15·5·2 and 5·5·2, also giving 16 kHz)
are **absent** in scope — only the high-frequency (64-bit coefficient)
decimator configuration is used. [Confirmed]

**Coefficient supply.** Internal to the coprocessor firmware; the host neither
supplies coefficients nor needs the coefficient-bearing description nodes that
M1–M3 had. This is a change from the M1–M3 model in which coefficients were
delivered to the coprocessor as part of configuration. [Confirmed]

**Decimator front-end register model** (functional names; the block is
programmed by the coprocessor, not by the host, and is documented here as the
hardware a tracing observer will see the coprocessor touch):

| Functional block | Register (function) |
|---|---|
| PDM converter | configuration (per-channel enable mask, start/stop, 16-vs-24-bit channel width); FIFO control (RX flush); FIFO bit-shift (RX shift when not 24-bit); RX config (auto-restart, FIFO enable); RX FIFO watermarks (low/high); IRQ mask (RX high-water, overflow, underflow); status (RX running); software reset; a serial-cluster sync/select register |
| Decimator | three-stage rate register (stage-1/2/3 ratios + total rate); three filter-length fields; input polarity/phase select; **16-bit vs 24-bit PCM output-mode select**; forced clock-gating (coefficient/register/data/ALU); status-clear; coefficient memory |

The **16-bit / 24-bit PCM output mode** select is the one new decimator mode
relative to the M1–M3 front end (M1–M2 delivered 2 bytes/sample, M3 delivered
3 bytes/sample as a fixed per-generation choice; the in-scope front end can
select either at run time). [Probable — the mode bit exists in the decimator's
register map; its host-visible effect is **[Inferred]**.]

**The domain named for the sense path *is* the microphone front end.** The power
device list on every in-scope SoC carries an `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC` domain plus
`PDM0_AUDIO_REF` / `PDM1_AUDIO_REF` reference-clock domains, and the audio island's
global configuration carries matching `SENSE_PDMC_*` clock-enable and input-control
fields (§3 §3.6.8). The same misleading name is applied to both. Despite it, this is the
**microphone** PDM converter domain, a one-for-one rename of the baseline
generation's (§8 §8.8): its decimator input selector takes a microphone index, it
is grouped with the secure-microphone mute hardware, and it is present identically
on machines whose amplifiers have no sense capability at all. It is **not** a
speaker-sense converter, and the speaker sense return is PCM over TDM everywhere.
It is unused for sense on every in-scope machine and forms no part of the sense
path; the capture path documented here is the one it belongs to. [Confirmed]

## 12.4 Gating hardware in the capture data path (load-bearing)

There are three distinct gates, and they differ by generation. The stream behind
the isolation boundary is the **built-in digital microphone array**, not the
headset microphone.

**Headset-microphone capture is normal-world on every in-scope machine
(t8132, t604x, t8140, t8142, t605x). A normal-world driver can capture from the
headset microphone on all of them.** See D.3. The remainder of this section
concerns the built-in array.

### 12.4.1 The built-in microphone array is secured on A18 Pro and M5, not on M4

The built-in PDM mic-array endpoint (`identifier = hpai`, data node
`audio-hp-mic` / `audio-hp`, `device-uid = "Digital Mic"`) is bound differently
per generation:

| SoC | Endpoint `device_type` | DMA binding | Reachable by normal-world host DMA? |
|---|---|---|---|
| t8132, t604x (M4) | `iop-audio-ns` (non-secure) | `admac-leap-ns`, RX channel index 1 (odd ⇒ receive), 128-byte `dma-channels` blob | **Yes** — directly, as on M1–M3 |
| t8140 (A18 Pro) | `iop-audio-s` (**secure**) | `dma-provider-rx = leap-s-adma-rx-0` on `admac-leap-s` | **No** — see §12.4.2 |
| t8142, t605x (M5) | `iop-audio-s` (**secure**) | `dma-provider-rx = leap-s-adma-rx-0` on `admac-leap-s` | **No** — see §12.4.2 |

This is the central capture-path delta. On M4 the array is an ordinary
non-secure host-DMA capture stream. On A18 Pro and every M5-class machine it is
placed on the **secure** low-power DMA instance (`admac-leap-s`).

**The isolation mechanism, precisely:** on A18 Pro / M5 the secure DMA
controller node `admac-leap-s` deliberately carries an **empty `iommu-parent`
property** (`iommu-parent = <>`), and the secure *base* controller
`admac-base-s` is **not instantiated at all** (only its DART mapper stub exists).
A DMA controller with no IOMMU parent cannot be given a normal-world address
space; its buffers are instead mapped only by the isolated DART mapper
(`audio-shared-dart-proxy`, §12.4.2) into the isolated world. That empty
`iommu-parent` is the concrete hardware/firmware mechanism that puts the built-in
array out of normal-world reach. [Confirmed — empty on `admac-leap-s` and absent
`admac-base-s` on j700, j704, j813, j714s, j716c; the non-secure `admac-leap-ns`
and `admac-base-ns` on the same boards carry real IOMMU parents.]

### 12.4.2 What "secure" means for a normal-world driver

The secure mic-array stream is fronted by three cooperating description nodes:

1. **An isolated stream proxy** (`compatible = "iisaudio,isolated-stream-proxy"`,
   `device_type = "iis-ec-proxy"`; on t8140 the node is `audio-hp-mic-proxy`).
   The mic-array endpoint points at it through `isolated-audio-service-input`
   (a phandle). It carries a `physical-descriptions` blob (§12.6) and names an
   isolated-world audio service; it is marked `exclave-assigned`.
2. **An isolated DMA-channel proxy** (`compatible = "admac-ec-proxy"`,
   `device_type = "admac-proxy"`; e.g. `admac-hp-mic-ec-proxy` on t605x,
   `admac-leap-s-rx-0-proxy` on t8140). It carries its own controller aperture
   (0x34000, a *separate* window from the normal `admac-leap-s` aperture:
   e.g. t605x proxy aperture at `0x4_D320_0000` vs the controller at
   `0x2_9320_0000`, both absolute), a `use-case` FourCC (`hpai`), a
   `dma-channel` index, and a
   `function-iommu_handler` pointing at the shared isolated DART mapper. It is
   `exclave-assigned`.
3. **A shared isolated DART mapper** (`audio-shared-dart-proxy`,
   `exclave-assigned`) whose `usecase-dart-map` lists which stream FourCCs it
   maps (`hpai`, and on t605x `blls`, plus the LP-mic buffer `xpda`), and whose
   `iommu-parent` is the **secure** base/leap DART mapper pair
   (`mapper-admac-base-s` = stream ID 9, `mapper-admac-leap-s` = stream ID 11).

Consequences for a normal-world driver:

- The secure DMA channel's ring is programmed through the proxy aperture, and its
  buffer is IOMMU-mapped by the isolated DART mapper into the isolated world, not
  into the normal-world DART domain. A normal-world driver **cannot** set up a
  descriptor ring against `admac-leap-s` and read microphone frames out of
  physical memory the way it can on M4. [Confirmed — the secure channel is bound
  to the proxy/exclave path and the mapping is owned by the isolated DART
  mapper.]
- To capture the built-in array on A18 Pro / M5 a normal-world driver must
  instead **request the isolated audio service to run the stream** and receive
  decimated frames through the isolated I/O-buffer interface (a client-read
  operation against a service-owned buffer), rather than by owning the DMA.
  Opening the isolated buffer requires privilege the isolated environment
  grants; whether that restriction is enforced in hardware or only by host
  policy is **[Unknown]**. [Confirmed that the path exists and that opening the
  buffer is privileged.] The **normal-world** transport a driver would use to
  make the request is fully specified (§11.2, §11.4); what is not established
  is the isolated environment's own wire protocol and the request that crosses
  into it — §11 Open question 15 and Open question 1 of this section.
- **Net conclusion (load-bearing): on M4-class machines a normal-world driver can
  capture the built-in microphone array directly by host DMA; on A18 Pro and all
  M5-class machines it cannot capture the built-in array directly at all.** What
  blocks it is concrete: the secure DMA controller has no IOMMU parent (so no
  normal-world address space can be attached to it) and its buffer is mapped only
  by the isolated DART mapper into the isolated world; the only route to the
  built-in array on those SoCs is to ask the isolated audio service to run the
  stream and read frames from the service-owned buffer. [Confirmed]

### 12.4.3 The analog headset-jack microphone is never secured

Distinct from the built-in array, the **headset / jack microphone** arrives
through the analog jack codec (`audio-data,cs42l84-input`, endpoint
`audio-codec-input`, `identifier = cin`). It is `iop-audio-ns` (non-secure) on
**every** in-scope machine and binds to a base-domain non-secure DMA channel
(`base-ns-adma-rx-2` on the string-form boards; RX channel index 5 on the M4
blob-form boards). A normal-world driver **can** capture the headset-jack
microphone directly by host DMA on all in-scope machines. [Confirmed]

(The node literally named `audio-hp-mic` is the built-in "Digital Mic" array,
not the headphone jack — "hp" reads as high-power audio input, `hpai`. The jack
microphone is `audio-codec-input`. The secure-DMA binding in §12.4.1 applies to the
built-in array; the jack mic is never on a secure instance.)

### 12.4.4 Hardware microphone-disable and no host serialiser MMIO

Two further gates sit in front of the data path:

- The serialiser-to-DMA-channel mapping block contains a **hardware
  microphone-disable control** (§3; register field given there). This is a
  concrete privacy mechanism in
  the routing hardware — when asserted it prevents microphone samples from
  reaching the DMA channel independently of any software state. Its exact
  register field is documented in §3; a capture driver cannot re-enable
  microphone flow while it is asserted. [Probable]
- The serial audio controller that clocks and routes the capture streams has **no
  host MMIO aperture** on any in-scope SoC (its former nodes are gone; the NCO is
  absent or has no `reg`). Only the audio DMA controller is host-addressable.
  Control of capture routing is therefore only reachable through the coprocessor
  service. [Confirmed]

**The mute/unmute ramp belongs to this path, and only to this path.** A register
write inside the low-power complex, with mute and unmute ramp-time increments
and hold-off delays, accompanies a microphone-disable assertion. It is driven by
**microphone-status notification** and by no audio stream, so it is part of the
microphone privacy mechanism and not a speaker control (§18 §18.6.3).
[Confirmed] A capture driver should expect a microphone-disable
assertion to be accompanied by a ramp rather than an instantaneous cut; the
units and configured values of the four ramp parameters are **[Unknown]**
(§14 Open question 4).

## 12.5 Format descriptor (`reg`) decoding, per capture endpoint

The data-node `reg` is nine u32; the load-bearing fields decode as
`[fmt/cluster, sub, bit_clock_Hz, (flags<<16)|bclk_per_frame,
(flags<<16)|frame_rate_kHz, tx_slot_mask, rx_slot_mask,
(rx_bits<<24)|(tx_bits<<16)|(rx_ch<<8)|tx_ch, tail]`. Capture endpoints
(non-zero RX):

| Endpoint (machine class) | bit clock | frame | RX slots | RX ch × width | Native rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-hp-mic` array, 3-mic (M4/M5) | 12.000 MHz | 250 bclk/frame | 0x7 | 3 × 32-bit | 48 kHz |
| `audio-hp-mic` array, 2-mic (A18 Pro) | 12.000 MHz | 250 bclk/frame | 0x3 | 2 × 32-bit | 48 kHz |
| `audio-codec-input` (headset jack) | codec-master | 64 bclk/frame | 0x1 | 1 × 32-bit | 48/44.1/88.2/96 kHz |
| `audio-speaker-tap` (A18 Pro/M5) | 12.288/12.0 MHz | 250–256 | 0x3f/0xf/0x3 | up to 6 × 24-bit | 48 kHz |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | 12.000 MHz | 250 | 0x3 | 2 × 16-bit | 48 kHz |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback` | 12.000 MHz | 250 | 0x3 | 2 × 32-bit | 48 kHz |
| `audio-secure-leap-loopback` (t605x) | 12.000 MHz | 250 | 0x3 | 2 × 32-bit | 48 kHz |

The mic-array slot mask (`0x7` = 3 slots, `0x3` = 2 slots) tracks element count.
The receive width in the on-wire serial slot is 32-bit; the host-visible sample
format is 32-bit float little-endian (§12.6). [Confirmed for slot/width/rate;
float-LE is Probable, carried from the M1–M3 host presentation.]

The nine-u32 (36-byte) format descriptor is **structurally unchanged from M1
through M5** — the same field layout carried the same meanings on the M1–M3
serial-audio data nodes; only the parent node (`alcN` → `iop-audio-controller`
child) and the DMA-binding form changed. [Confirmed — cross-section finding,
corroborated here by identical descriptor bytes for the mic array across
generations.]

## 12.6 Channel layout presented to the host

Two sources describe host presentation: the `physical-descriptions` blobs on the
isolated stream / buffer proxies, and the `use-case-*-format` tables in
`/product/audio`.

**`physical-descriptions`** — six u32
`[region_size, sample_rate_Hz, format_tag='lpcm', format_code, bytes_per_frame,
packet_size]`. The packet size is solved exactly:
**`packet_size = header + 64 × bytes_per_frame`**, i.e. 64 audio frames per
transported packet plus a fixed header — **32 bytes** for the isolated stream
proxies, **24 bytes** for the isolated low-power-mic buffer. Verified across all
four data points below:

| Node | rate | tag | code | bytes/frame | packet = header + 64×bpf |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| built-in mic-array stream proxy (3-mic) | 48 000 Hz | `lpcm` | 9 | 12 (3 ch × 4 B) | 32 + 768 = 800 |
| built-in mic-array stream proxy (2-mic, j700) | 48 000 Hz | `lpcm` | 9 | 8 (2 ch × 4 B) | 32 + 512 = 544 |
| low-power mic buffer (isolated) | 16 000 Hz | `lpcm` | 20 | 8–12 | 24 + 512…768 = 536…792 |
| secure-loopback stream proxy (t605x) | 48 000 Hz | `lpcm` | 9 | 8 | 32 + 512 = 544 |

Format tag is linear PCM. `bytes_per_frame` = channel-count × 4, so the on-buffer
sample is 4 bytes (32-bit) and the channel count is exactly the element count
(3, or 2 on the A18 Pro). The leading `region_size` (15840 for the mic stream
proxies, 64000 for the LP buffer) is the shared-region size; its precise basis is
**[Unknown]**. [Confirmed for the packet formula, rate, tag and per-frame width.]

**`use-case-*-format`** (present only on A18 Pro / M5; each record
`[FourCC, rate_Hz, channels, bytes_per_sample, 0…]`):

- `use-case-dsp-in-format`: `mtkd` = 48 000 Hz, N ch, 4 bytes/sample;
  `hist` = 16 000 Hz, N ch, 4 bytes/sample — where N = 3 on the 3-mic machines
  and 2 on the A18 Pro 2-mic machine.
- `use-case-client-format`: `hist`, `siri`, `lpts` = 16 000 Hz, 2 ch, 4
  bytes/sample.

So the coprocessor DSP input is the full element count at 48 kHz (32-bit /
4-byte samples), while the client-facing history / Siri / low-power-trigger-store
formats are 16 kHz, 2-channel, 32-bit. Sample format is 32-bit, little-endian
(the stream descriptors assert the big-endian format flag is **not** set);
interleaved; device-buffer-backed. [Confirmed for rate/channels/width per the
tables; float vs integer is Probable from the M1–M3 presentation.]

**Buffer format**: on M4 the low-power mic buffer is a plain coprocessor-mapped
region, `io-buffer-size = 0x000B_B800` (768 000 bytes), IOMMU-mapped through the
non-secure base mapper. On A18 Pro / M5 it is an **isolated** buffer (§12.7).
The mic-array capture buffer per-channel byte allocation on the M4 blob form is
`0x120` (288 bytes) per receive slot pair.

## 12.7 The low-power microphone path

Two nodes: `lp-mic-device` (`identifier = lpai`, i.e. the voice-trigger /
always-listening input) and `lp-mic-io-buffer-device` (`identifier = adpx`),
plus the `siri-listening-device` client-manager node (`identifier = lai`).

**What makes it low-power**: it runs off the same PDM front end but at the
native 16 kHz decimated rate (`use-case` `hist`/`lpts` = 16 000 Hz, 2 ch,
4 bytes) with a small dedicated buffer, so the array can be sampled and buffered
by the coprocessor while the host application processors are asleep. It is the
`lpai` device from the M1–M3 baseline (voice-trigger channel 1), unchanged in
role. [Confirmed]

**Buffer description** (`physical-descriptions` on `lp-mic-io-buffer-device`):
`[0x0000_FA00, 0x0000_3E80, 'lpcm', 0x14, e, f]` = 16 000 Hz, linear PCM, format
code 20, leading counter 64000. On M4 the same device is instead a plain
`iop-audio,io-buffer-device` carrying `io-buffer-size = 0x000B_B800`
(768 000 bytes) and `iommu-parent = mapper-admac-base-ns` (non-secure). On A18
Pro / M5 the device is `iop-audio,isolated-io-buffer-device`, `exclave-assigned`,
named to an isolated low-power-mic audio service, with an isolated power provider
(the shared DART mapper proxy); its buffer is mapped by the isolated DART mapper.
[Confirmed]

**Can the host use it directly?**

- On M4: yes — the LP buffer is a normal-world coprocessor-mapped region behind
  the non-secure base DART; a driver can map and read it. [Confirmed]
- On A18 Pro / M5: no — it is an isolated buffer behind the isolated DART mapper;
  the host must go through the isolated LP-mic audio service. [Confirmed]

## 12.8 The voice-trigger path

Hardware: the voice-trigger controller is a **separate** node
`/arm-io/iop-voicetrigger-controller` (`compatible = "iop-audio,controller"`,
`iop-audio-service-name` = the coprocessor voice-trigger service) with one child
`audio-vt-device` (`identifier = mctv`). It shares the same PDM front end and the
`lpai` low-power input; it is a second coprocessor service, not a second front
end.

Separability: it is fully separable from the rest of the capture path. It is its
own controller node with its own coprocessor service, distinct from
`iop-audio-controller`. **A capture driver can ignore it** — nothing in the
built-in-array or headset-jack capture path depends on the voice-trigger node,
and the built-in Mac mini (j773g) omits it entirely while still exposing the
speaker/codec streams. [Confirmed]

Per-generation form: on M4 the child is a plain `iop-audio,vt-device`
(`device_type = iop-nub`). On A18 Pro / M5 it is
`iop-audio,isolated-vt-device`, `exclave-assigned`, named to an isolated
voice-trigger audio service — i.e. the voice-trigger path is also moved into the
isolated world on the later generations, consistent with the mic-array move.
[Confirmed]

## 12.9 Capture endpoint inventory (per machine)

Direction / DMA binding / domain / payload. Bindings shown in string form
(A18 Pro / M5); the M4 boards express the same routing through the 128-byte
`dma-channels` blob and `dma-parent` (mic array → `admac-leap-ns` RX ch 1;
codec-input → `admac-*` RX ch 5; loopbacks → RX ch 6/7 and 8/9; speaker
TX ch 0/1).

### Built-in-array machines (t8132, t604x, t8142, t605x)

| Endpoint | id | Dir | Cluster | DMA channel | Domain | Carries |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-hp-mic` (built-in array) | `hpai` | capture | leap | M4: `leap-ns` RX1 · A18/M5: `leap-s-adma-rx-0` | M4 non-secure / A18·M5 **secure** | 3 (or 2) PDM elements, 48 kHz, 32-bit |
| `audio-codec-input` (headset jack) | `cin` | capture | mca | `base-ns-adma-rx-2` (M4: RX5) | non-secure | jack mic via analog codec, up to 96 kHz |
| `audio-speaker-tap` | `tap` | capture | mca | `base-ns-adma-rx-1` | non-secure | tap of speaker feed (`clock-domain = main`); A18/M5 only |
| `audio-mca-loopback` | `lpbk` | capture+play | mca | `base-ns-adma-rx-3` / `-tx-3` | non-secure | base-cluster loopback, 2×16-bit |
| `audio-leap-internal-loopback` | `lilb` | capture+play | leap | `leap-ns-adma-rx-4` / `-tx-4` | non-secure | low-power-cluster loopback, 2×32-bit |
| `audio-secure-leap-loopback` | `sllb` | capture+play | leap | `leap-s-adma-rx-5` / `leap-ns-adma-tx-5` | **secure** | secure loopback; **t605x only, development-only** |
| `audio-speaker` | `spkr` | playback | mca/leap | `base-ns-adma-tx-0` (+rx-0) | non-secure | speaker feed (playback; listed for completeness) |
| `audio-codec-output` | `cout` | playback | mca | `base-ns-adma-tx-2` | non-secure | jack/codec playback |
| `lp-mic-device` | `lpai` | capture (LP) | — | via isolated/plain LP buffer | M4 non-secure / A18·M5 secure | 16 kHz low-power / voice-trigger input |
| `lp-mic-io-buffer-device` | `adpx` | buffer | — | base DART (M4) / isolated DART (A18·M5) | ditto | LP mic sample buffer |
| `lp-mic-injection-device` | `lpij` | play (inject) | mca | `base-ns-adma-tx-5` | non-secure | 16 kHz mic-stream injection; A18/M5 only |
| `siri-listening-device` | `lai` | client mgr | — | — | — | always-listening client manager |
| voice-trigger `audio-vt-device` | `mctv` | capture (VT) | — | shares `lpai` front end | M4 non-secure / A18·M5 isolated | wake-word |

### A18 Pro (j700) differences

- Built-in array has **2** elements, `leap-s-adma-rx-0`, max 2 channels — secure.
- **No** `audio-codec-input` / `audio-codec-output` codec streams on the
  `iop-audio-controller` in the same shape — the jack codec on this machine is
  `cs42l83` and the speaker part is `max98360` (no control bus); the base-domain
  codec input/output pair present on the other machines is reduced. It does carry
  `audio-hp-mic`, `audio-mca-loopback`, `audio-leap-internal-loopback`,
  `audio-speaker` (two speaker entries), `audio-speaker-tap`, LP-mic,
  mic-injection and Siri nodes.
- Has the mic-array per-element power-enable line (§12.2) that no other board has.
- No `audio-secure-leap-loopback` (that endpoint is t605x-only).

### Second coprocessor instance

A18 Pro, M5 and M5 Pro/Max carry a second always-on coprocessor
(`/arm-io/aop2`, with its own firmware on M5). It is **not on the audio path**:
no capture endpoint and no audio service references its IOMMU stream, and no
audio function is attributed to it. [Confirmed]

### Mac mini / Mac Studio (j773g, j773s, j575c)

- **No built-in microphone array at all** — no `audio-hp` / `audio-hp-mic`,
  no `lp-mic-device`, no voice-trigger controller (j773g). These desktops expose
  only `audio-speaker`, `audio-codec-output`, `audio-codec-input` (jack) and
  `audio-mca-loopback`. Headset-jack capture is the only microphone capture path.
  [Confirmed]

## 12.10 DMA and IOMMU facts for capture

- Audio DMA controller instances (all aperture 0x34000, host-addressable):
  `admac-base-ns` and `admac-leap-ns` on M4; on A18 Pro / M5 add `admac-base-s`
  and `admac-leap-s` (secure). Per-channel declared limits appear on the M5-form
  channel nodes: mic array `leap-s-adma-rx-0` = up to 3 ch, 32-bit, 48 kHz;
  headset `base-ns-adma-rx-2` = 1 ch, 32-bit, 96 kHz; speaker-tap
  `base-ns-adma-rx-1` = 6 ch, 32-bit; mic-injection `base-ns-adma-tx-5` = 3 ch,
  32-bit, 16 kHz. [Confirmed]
- The low-power serial cluster has 5 receive links and 1 transmit link
  (`AUDIO_LEAP_RX0..RX4`, `AUDIO_LEAP_TX0`), parented on the aggregate audio
  domain (`AUDIO_LEAP_C ← AUDIO_LEAP_A ← AUDIO_FR ← AUDIO_A`), sharing the
  controller register region and cross-connect; link and DMA-channel numbering is
  unchanged from the M3 generation. [Probable — cross-section finding; the
  RX0–RX4/TX0 domain set is confirmed here in the power device list.]
- IOMMU stream IDs on the coprocessor DART: non-secure base = 8, secure base = 9,
  non-secure leap = 10, secure leap = 11. The secure mic-array buffer is mapped
  through stream ID 11 by the isolated DART mapper. [Confirmed]
- The secure DMA proxy apertures are separate 0x34000 windows distinct from the
  controller apertures (e.g. t605x proxy at `0x4_D320_0000`, absolute, against the
  controller at `0x2_9320_0000`). The addresses themselves are **[Confirmed]** —
  byte-exact `reg` values plus the `/arm-io` parent base, agreeing with §4 §4.2.4.
  That these are the windows the isolated world drives, and that the normal-world
  controller aperture does not reach the secure channel's live state, is
  **[Probable]** on internal consistency.

## Per-SoC / per-machine differences

| Property | t8132 (M4) | t604x (M4 Pro/Max) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 (M5) | t605x (M5 Pro/Max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Built-in PDM elements | 3 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| Mic-array DMA domain | non-secure | non-secure | **secure** | **secure** | **secure** |
| Isolated stream/buffer proxies | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Speaker-tap capture endpoint | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Mic-injection endpoint | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Secure-loopback endpoint | no | no | no | no | **yes (dev-only)** |
| Per-element mic power-enable | no | no | **yes** | no | no |
| Headset-jack codec | cs42l84 | cs42l84 | **cs42l83** | cs42l84 | cs42l84 |
| LP-mic buffer | plain | plain | isolated | isolated | isolated |
| Voice-trigger node | plain | plain | isolated | isolated | isolated |
| Second coprocessor `aop2` | no | no | yes | yes (own fw) | yes (own fw) |
| Desktop variant w/o built-in mics | j773g (mini) | j773s (mini), j575c (Studio) | — | — | — |

Chassis A/B confirmations across the boundary: j613/j615 (M3) → j713/j715 (M4)
keep 3 mics and gain nothing secure; j504 (M3) → j604 (M4) likewise; the secure
gate first appears with A18 Pro (j700) and is universal from M5 onward.

## Open questions

1. **Isolated audio-service capture opcodes (A18 Pro / M5).** The exact
   request/grant sequence a normal-world driver issues to make the isolated
   service run the secure mic-array stream and deliver frames through the
   service-owned buffer is not established here. The carrier is no longer the
   gap: the normal-world transport, its framing and the audio service's own
   wrapped-call layout are specified in §11.2 and §11.4, and the capture
   configure-and-start sequence for a non-isolated array is given in §11.4.7.
   What is missing is the isolated environment's wire protocol (§11 Open
   question 15) and which call, if any, a normal-world caller may use to ask it
   to run the stream. *Matters because it is the only way to capture the
   built-in array on these machines.* Resolve by tracing the mailbox exchange
   and the isolated-buffer read calls during a capture from the built-in array,
   and by testing whether the privilege restriction is enforced in hardware or
   only by host policy.

2. **Whether the secure DMA channel is ever visible to normal-world MMIO.** The
   proxy aperture and the controller aperture are separate windows; it is not
   proven that the normal-world controller aperture cannot observe or perturb the
   secure channel. *Matters because it bounds what a driver could do without the
   service.* Resolve by attempting normal-world reads of the `admac-leap-s`
   channel registers on an M5 machine and checking for faults or zeroes.

3. **The hardware microphone-disable control's register field and scope.**
   Identified in the routing block but its exact bit, its default state, and
   whether it gates the headset-jack path as well as the array are unestablished
   here. *Matters because it is the concrete privacy hardware.* Resolve by
   toggling the field under trace and observing which capture streams stop.

4. **Native-rate vs presented-rate conversion.** The decimator produces 16 kHz;
   the high-power array is presented at 48 kHz. Where the 3× up-conversion (or
   re-decimation to a different chain) happens — coprocessor DSP vs a second
   decimator pass — is unknown. *Matters for exact sample timing and for driving
   the stream at native rate.* Resolve by tracing the decimator rate register and
   the DMA delivery rate simultaneously.

5. **16-bit vs 24-bit PCM output mode selection.** The decimator has a
   16/24-bit mode bit; which mode each in-scope machine actually uses, and
   whether the host can request it, is not established (the format descriptors say
   32-bit slot width but the decimator emits 16- or 24-bit). Resolve by capturing
   raw bytes and inspecting the low-order bits, and by tracing the mode register.

6. **`physical-descriptions` counter fields.** The leading size field and the
   last two fields (`e`, `f`) of each blob are only partially interpreted.
   *Matters for buffer sizing.* Resolve by correlating them against the actual
   ring/period sizes the DMA engine is programmed with under trace.

7. **PDM element pin/pad routing and physical placement.** No in-scope
   description exposes the PDM clock/data pins or the physical element positions;
   beamforming needs the geometry. Resolve by board-level probing of the PDM pads
   and by acoustic characterisation of element order.

8. **Mic-injection endpoint semantics — narrowed.** The 16 kHz
   `lp-mic-injection-device` (`lpij`, `base-ns-adma-tx-5`, terminal-type `injm`)
   lets a stream be injected into the low-power mic path. **Its link is now
   specified:** the coprocessor's built-in record for the injection family binds
   `mck5`/`ckg5`/`syn5`/`ms05`, runs from the oscillator at 3.072 MHz with
   divider 1, a 192-bit-clock frame and therefore a 16 kHz frame rate, with a
   32-bit slot width and a slot mask of `0x07` on t8142 and t605x and `0x03` on
   t8140 — i.e. three injected channels on the M5 generation and two on the
   A18 Pro machine, matching each machine's microphone element count (§18
   §18.7.1). **[Confirmed]** **Residual:** whether it is usable by a
   normal-world driver (it is non-secure) and what it feeds — voice-trigger
   test, echo reference — is still **[Unknown]**. Resolve by driving it and
   observing where the injected samples surface.


---

# 13. Digital display audio

## Baseline

The closest documented equivalent is the M1–M3 display-audio transmit block, described
upstream in the Asahi device trees as `apple,dpaudio` — one instance per display pipe,
a single `0x4000` MMIO aperture, transmit-only, fed by one channel of the general-purpose
I/O coprocessor's DMA engine (`dmas = <&sio 0x64>`, `dma-names = "tx"`), gated and reset by
a dedicated power domain `dpa<N>` whose parent is the aggregate audio power domain
`audio_p`, and linked by a device-tree `port`/`endpoint` pair to the display coprocessor.
No public driver binds to it and its register map is not publicly documented.
On t8103/t8112 the two instances sit at the top of the serial audio controller's second
(switch) region — `0x2_3833_0000` and `0x2_3833_4000` on t8112, i.e. switch base
`+0x30000` and `+0x34000`. **[Confirmed]** (upstream/Asahi device trees; mainline Linux
`t8103-pmgr.dtsi`, `t8112-pmgr.dtsi`, `t8122-pmgr.dtsi`, `t6030-pmgr.dtsi` all place
`dpa0…dpaN` under `ps_audio_p`.)

The Apple-supplied platform description calls the same objects `/arm-io/dp-audio<N>`.
On M1–M3 those nodes carry **no `reg`**: the aperture quoted above is not in the platform
description at all. They carry `dma-parent`, `dma-channels`, `power-gates`, `clock-gates`
and `function-device_reset_dpa`, and nothing else. **[Confirmed]**

Addresses below are absolute. Platform-supplied addresses are I/O-region-relative; the
offsets applied are **`0x2_0000_0000`** for t8132, t6041 (M4 Pro/Max) and t6050, and
**`0x2_1000_0000`** for t8140 and t8142. Each was read from the `ranges` property of
`/arm-io` on a board of that SoC. **[Confirmed]**

---

## Summary of differences

| Aspect | M1–M3 baseline | t8132 (M4) | t6041 (M4 Pro/Max) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 (M5) | t6050 (M5 Pro/Max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dp-audio<N>` nodes | 1 per pipe, no `reg` | **unchanged** (3) | **unchanged** (5) | **unchanged** (2) | **unchanged** (3) | **unchanged** (5) |
| Data-path DMA engine | I/O-coprocessor DMA (`sio-dma`) | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **changed** — per-pipe host audio DMA controller | **changed** — per-pipe host audio DMA controller |
| Host MMIO for the data path | none | none | none | none | **new** — `0x24000` per pipe | **new** — `0x24000` per pipe |
| Host interrupt for display audio | none | none | none | none | **new** — 2 per pipe | **new** — 2 per pipe |
| IOMMU for display audio | I/O-coprocessor IOMMU | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **new** per-pipe isochronous IOMMU, SID 30 | **new** per-pipe isochronous IOMMU, SID 30 |
| Display-audio power domain | `DPA0…N`, parent `AUDIO_P` | **changed** — parent is now `DPA_P` → `SIO` | **changed** — same | **changed** — same | **absent** — replaced by `DISP_ADMA`/`DISPEXT<n>_ADMA`, parent = that pipe's `DISP*_SYS` | **absent** — same replacement |
| Latency-escalation block | absent | absent | absent | absent | **new** — one `ced-ssw` per pipe | **new** — one `ced-ssw` per pipe |
| Memory-QoS escalation vote | n/a | virtual domain `AUDIO-LLT-V` | `AUDIO-LLT-V` | `AUDIO-LLT-V` | `AUDIO-LLT-V` | **changed** — platform function `function-vote_crit_llt_mode` |
| Stream format/rate control | display coprocessor | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |

**The headline answer to "must an audio-subsystem driver touch display audio?":**

- On **t8132, t6041 and t8140** — **no**. Display audio never enters the audio subsystem.
  It is a display-controller function fed by the general-purpose I/O coprocessor's DMA
  engine. An audio-subsystem driver can ignore it entirely. **[Confirmed]**
- On **t8142 and t6050** — **yes, partially**. The data path is now a host-programmed
  instance of the *same audio DMA controller IP* documented in section 4, one per display
  pipe, with host MMIO, host interrupts and its own IOMMU stream. Everything above the
  DMA (rate, channel allocation, IEC 60958/61937 framing, InfoFrames) is still
  display-coprocessor territory. **[Confirmed]**

---

## 13.1 Where display audio lives, per generation

The power-domain parentage is the cleanest statement of ownership, because every
generation describes it and the parentage changes exactly when the block moves.

| Generation | Display-audio domain | Parent chain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| t8103, t8112, t8122, t600x, t602x, t603x | `dpa0…dpaN` | → `audio_p` | block sits in the **audio complex** |
| t8132, t6041, t8140 | `DPA0…DPAN` | → `DPA_P` → `SIO` | block moved into the **I/O-coprocessor complex** |
| t8142, t6050 | `DISP_ADMA`, `DISPEXT<n>_ADMA` | → `DISP_SYS` / `DISPEXT<n>_SYS` | block moved into the **display pipe** |

The M1–M3 row is **[Confirmed]** from mainline Linux. The M4/A18-Pro row is
**[Confirmed]** (`DPA_P`'s parent field resolves to `SIO` on t8132, t6041 and t8140, and
`DPA_P` is the sole parent of every `DPA<N>`). The M5 row is **[Confirmed]**
(`DPA_P` and `DPA<N>` no longer exist on t8142/t6050; each `DISP*_ADMA` domain's parent
is the corresponding pipe's `*_SYS` domain).

Corollary, **[Inferred]**: the display-audio transmit block's own register aperture — the
`0x4000` window that on t8112 sits inside the serial audio controller's switch region —
is no longer in the audio complex on any in-scope SoC. The platform description gives it
no `reg` on any generation, so its address on M4 and later is **[Unknown]**; the power
parentage places it in the I/O-coprocessor neighbourhood on M4/A18 Pro and in the display
pipe neighbourhood on M5.

### Power-manager control registers for the display-audio domains

One 32-bit control register per domain, 8 bytes apart. The decode of the power-manager
device list used here (48-byte entries; flags at byte 0, first/second parent domain ids as
u16 at bytes 4–5 and 6–7, device id as u16 at bytes 26–27, name at bytes 32–47, slot index
at byte 10, register-group index at byte 11; address = the group's base plus its offset
plus slot × 8) was validated by reproducing mainline Linux's published t8103 offsets
exactly: `sio` `0x1c8`, `audio_p` `0x228`, `sio_adma` `0x230`, `mca0` `0x2b8`,
`mca1` `0x2c0`, `mca2` `0x2c8`, `dpa0` `0x2e8`, `dpa1` `0x2f0`, together with their parent
lists. **[Confirmed]** for SoCs whose device list uses the same register-group table form
as t8103 (t8132); **[Probable]** for t6041, t8140, t8142 and t6050, which use the
alternative group/offset encoding for which no public cross-check exists — all computed
addresses there are 8-byte aligned, unique, inside the referenced window, and contiguous
in the same pattern.

| SoC | Domain | Device id | Control register | Parent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| t8132 | `DPA_P` | 0x49 | `0x3_8070_02e0` | `SIO` |
| t8132 | `DPA0` / `DPA1` / `DPA2` | 0x6f / 0x70 / 0x7b | `0x3_8070_0410` / `0x…0418` / `0x…0470` | `DPA_P` |
| t8132 | `DPA3` / `DPA4` (no node) | 0x82 / 0x85 | `0x3_8070_04a8` / `0x…04c0` | `DPA_P` |
| t6041 | `DPA_P` | 0xb7 | `0x5_0228_01a8` | `SIO` |
| t6041 | `DPA0…DPA4` | 0xc8…0xcc | `0x5_0228_0230` + 8·n | `DPA_P` |
| t8140 | `DPA_P` | 0x4a | `0x3_0070_0300` | `SIO` |
| t8140 | `DPA0` / `DPA1` | 0x5c / 0x5d | `0x3_0070_0390` / `0x…0398` | `DPA_P` |
| t8142 | `DISP_ADMA` | 0xc4 | `0x3_8071_0068` | `DISP_SYS` |
| t8142 | `DISPEXT0_ADMA` | 0x70 | `0x3_8070_0420` | `DISPEXT0_SYS` |
| t8142 | `DISPEXT1_ADMA` | 0x62 | `0x3_8070_03b0` | `DISPEXT1_SYS` |
| t6050 | `DISP_ADMA` | 0x9a | `0x2_8090_01a0` | `DISP_SYS` |
| t6050 | `DISPEXT0_ADMA` | 0x44 | `0x2_8060_0270` | `DISPEXT0_SYS` |
| t6050 | `DISPEXT1_ADMA` | 0x51 | `0x2_8060_02d8` | `DISPEXT1_SYS` |
| t6050 | `DISPEXT2_ADMA` | 0x4b | `0x2_8060_02a8` | `DISPEXT2_SYS` |
| t6050 | `DISPEXT3_ADMA` | 0x4e | `0x2_8060_02c0` | `DISPEXT3_SYS` |

Every one of these domains carries flags byte `0x00` — a real, host-writable power-state
register, unlike the audio-complex aggregate domains which carry `0x10`. **[Confirmed]**

t8132 is the one SoC in scope where the silicon carries **more** display-audio domains
(five) than the package describes display pipes (three). t8122 shows the same pattern in
mainline Linux (five `dpa` domains, two pipes on the boards in scope there).
**[Confirmed]**

---

## 13.2 The display-audio nodes

One `/arm-io/dp-audio<N>` node per display pipe, on every board of every generation, with
no exceptions and no per-board variation within an SoC. **[Confirmed]**

| SoC | Boards | Display pipes | `dp-audio` nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| t8132 | j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g | `disp0`, `dispext0`, `dispext1` | 3 |
| t6041 | j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j773s, j575c | `disp0`, `dispext0…3` | 5 |
| t8140 | j700 | `disp0`, `dispext0` | 2 |
| t8142 | j704, j813, j815 | `disp0`, `dispext0`, `dispext1` | 3 |
| t6050 | j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c | `disp0`, `dispext0…3` | 5 |

Node contents, all generations:

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `device_type` | `dp-audio<N>` |
| *(no `reg`)* | no host MMIO aperture is described for the transmit block itself |
| *(no `interrupts`)* | the node itself raises no host interrupt |
| `dma-parent` | phandle of the DMA controller that feeds it |
| `dma-channels` | 8 × u32; word 0 = channel number, words 1–5 = channel configuration |
| `power-gates`, `clock-gates` | both carry the same single power-manager device id |
| `function-device_reset_dpa` | `<pmgr-phandle, 'ARST', device-id>` — block reset through the power manager, on the same device id |

`function-device_reset_dpa` is the only reset path described for the block; there is no
separate reset register. The tag reads `ARST`. **[Confirmed]** (present identically on
every board from M1 to M5.)

### `dma-channels` decode

The five configuration words map one-to-one onto the channel-configuration block the
I/O-coprocessor DMA engine takes over its shared-memory mailbox, as documented by the
published general-purpose I/O coprocessor driver: `{datashape, timeout, fifo, threshold,
limit}`. **[Probable]**

| SoC group | ch | datashape | timeout | fifo | threshold | limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t8103, t8112, t8122, t600x, t602x | 0x64 + 2n | 2 | 0 | `0x800` | `0x800` | 0 |
| t6030, t6031 | 0x64 + 2n | 2 | 0 | `0x800` | `0x600` | 0 |
| **t8132** | 0x64 + 2n | 2 | 0 | `0x800` | `0x800` | 0 |
| **t6041** | 0x64 + 2n | 2 | 0 | `0x800` | `0x600` | 0 |
| **t8140** | 0x64 + 2n | 2 | 0 | `0x800` | `0x800` | 0 |
| **t8142, t6050** | **0** | 2 | 0 | **`0x1000`** | `0x800` | 0 |

Two facts fall out:

1. `datashape = 2` on every generation. In the published mapping this is a **4-byte
   (32-bit) DMA word**. Display audio moves 32-bit words in memory on every SoC in scope.
   **[Confirmed]**
2. The channel numbers on M1–M4 and A18 Pro are 0x64, 0x66, 0x68, 0x6a, 0x6c — strictly
   **even**. In the published channel-numbering convention for that engine, even channels
   are memory-to-device. Display audio is **transmit-only**; there is no display-audio
   capture path on any SoC in scope. **[Confirmed]**
3. On M5 the channel number is 0, because each pipe now has a whole DMA controller
   instance to itself, and the FIFO allocation doubled from `0x800` to `0x1000` bytes.
   **[Confirmed]**

---

## 13.3 t8132 / t6041 / t8140 — coprocessor-driven data path (unchanged from baseline)

`dma-parent` on every `dp-audio<N>` node resolves to `/arm-io/sio/iop-sio-nub/sio-dma`
(`compatible = "sio-dma-controller"`, `device_type = "sio-dma"`). That node has **no
`reg`**: it is a service of the general-purpose I/O coprocessor, not a host-addressable
engine. Transfers are set up by messages to the coprocessor (a start/setup/configure/
issue/terminate sequence over its mailbox endpoint, with the per-channel configuration
block placed in shared memory), as documented by the published general-purpose I/O
coprocessor driver. **[Confirmed]**

Consequences for a driver author:

- There is **no audio-subsystem work to do**. The audio DMA controller instances
  (`admac-base-ns`, `admac-leap-ns`, `admac-leap-s`), the serial audio clusters and the
  numerically controlled oscillator are not involved in display audio at all on these
  SoCs. **[Confirmed]**
- The buffer lives in the I/O coprocessor's IOMMU address space, not the audio IOMMU's.
  **[Confirmed]**
- Start and stop are coprocessor mailbox transactions, not register writes.
  **[Confirmed]**
- Powering the block means raising `DPA<N>` (and therefore `DPA_P` and `SIO`), and
  releasing reset through the power manager using the `ARST` function on the same
  device id. **[Confirmed]**

Other consumers of the same engine on these SoCs: `spi2` (channel 24) on all of them, plus
`uart4` (69) and `uart5` (71) on t8140. **[Confirmed]** — worth knowing because the
coprocessor must be booted for display audio even on a machine with no other user.

On t8142 and t6050 the `sio-dma` node still exists and `spi2` still uses channel 24, but
**no `dp-audio` node references it any more**. **[Confirmed]**

---

## 13.4 t8142 / t6050 — per-display audio DMA controller instances (the structural change)

### 13.4.1 What appeared

On t8142 and t6050 only, the platform description gained, per display pipe:

| Node | `device_type` | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/arm-io/admac-disp0`, `/arm-io/admac-dispext<n>` | `admac` | the audio DMA controller instance that feeds that pipe |
| `/arm-io/admac-disp0-ced-ssw`, `…-dispext<n>-ced-ssw` | `ced-ssw` | latency-escalation detector + register-snapshot block for that instance |
| `/arm-io/dart-disp0-isoc`, `…-dispext<n>-isoc` | `dart` | isochronous IOMMU for that pipe, carrying the display-audio stream |
| `…/mapper-disp0-dpa`, `…/mapper-dispext<n>-dpa` | `dart-mapper` | the display-audio IOMMU stream within it |

**None of these exist on t8132, t6041 or t8140.** The A18 Pro (t8140) is on the *old* side
of this boundary despite being an H17-generation part: its `dp-audio0`/`dp-audio1` nodes
point at `sio-dma` exactly as on M4, it has `DPA_P`/`DPA0`/`DPA1`, and it has no
`admac-disp*`, no `*-ced-ssw` and no isochronous display IOMMU. **[Confirmed]** on every
in-scope board.

### 13.4.2 The second DMA controller type

Both types are instances of the audio DMA controller documented in **section 4**; they are
distinguished by `compatible` and by the presence of an `admac-evolution` property.

| | Main audio DMA instances | Display-audio DMA instances |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes | `admac-base-ns`, `admac-leap-ns`, `admac-leap-s` | `admac-disp0`, `admac-dispext<n>` |
| `compatible`, t8142 | `admac-evolution,t8142` | `admac,t8142` |
| `compatible`, t6050 | `admac-evolution,t6050` | `admac,t6050`, `admac,t605x` |
| `admac-evolution` property | present, `= <1>` | **absent** |
| Aperture 0 size | `0x34000` | **`0x24000`** |
| Aperture 1 | 8 bytes, shared | 8 bytes, **same address**, shared |
| Channel count properties | `#dma-channels-tx`, `#dma-channels-rx` | `#dma-channels-tx` only |
| Channels | 13 tx + 13 rx (base), 9 + 9 (low-power) | **1 tx, 0 rx** |
| `self-actuated` | absent | **present** (empty property) |
| Channel-buffer SRAM (`channel-buffer-allocation`) | `0x1e00` bytes | `0x1900` bytes (6400) |
| `channel-buffer-alloc-base-tx/rx` | `0x100` | `0` (tx and rx) |
| `channels-offset` | 0 | 0 |
| `role` (FourCC) | `BANS`, `LENS`, `LESS` | see below |

**Why a separate type exists:** on the M5 generation the main audio DMA controller moved to
a newer revision of the IP (flagged both by the `admac-evolution` compatible prefix and by
the `admac-evolution` property, and by splitting the single `#dma-channels` count into
separate transmit and receive counts), while the display-audio instances stayed on the
**earlier revision**, cut down to a single transmit channel. The evolution flag is not new
on M5: t8140 already carries `admac-evolution = <1>` on its three main instances while
keeping the plain `admac,t8140` compatible string. t8132 and t6041 carry neither.
**[Confirmed]**

So the "second type" is not a new engine — it is the *classic* audio DMA controller,
retained for display audio while the audio-complex instances moved forward.

`role` values (FourCC, stored byte-reversed in the platform description):

| SoC | `disp0` | `dispext0` | `dispext1` | `dispext2` | `dispext3` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t8142 | `DAI0` | `DAX0` | `DAX1` | — | — |
| t6050 | `DAI0` | `DX00` | `DX10` | `DX20` | `DX30` |

`role` is how the escalation-detector node binds to its controller: the `ced-ssw` node's
`dma-controllers` property carries the same FourCC (or, for the always-on instance, a list
of four). **[Confirmed]**

### 13.4.3 Register map delta versus section 4

The display instances use the audio DMA controller register map given in **section 4**;
only the following differ. Do not re-derive the common map here.

| Item | Value | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Aperture 0 length | `0x24000` (vs `0x34000`) | **[Confirmed]** |
| Missing region | the top `0x10000` of the standard aperture is not mapped | **[Confirmed]** |
| Cause of the shortfall | consistent with the absence of the receive-side descriptor/report windows: the standard aperture's tail is a set of `0x4000` pages and the display instance has four fewer | **[Inferred]** |
| Populated channels | transmit channel 0 only; no receive channels exist | **[Confirmed]** |
| Channel-buffer SRAM | 6400 bytes total, allocation base 0 for both directions | **[Confirmed]** |
| Per-channel FIFO sizing (from the consumer node) | carve-out `0x1000` bytes, threshold `0x800` | **[Probable]** |
| Interrupt output used | `irq-destination-index = 0` | **[Confirmed]** |
| Interrupt destination list | `irq-destinations` = four FourCCs, `AIC `, `ACPU`, and two further identifiers not decoded; index 0 = the host interrupt controller | **[Confirmed]** for index 0, **[Unknown]** for entries 2 and 3 |
| Aperture 1 (8 bytes) | shared with every other audio DMA controller instance on the SoC: `0x3_882a_8000` on t8142, `0x2_8832_8000` on t6050 | **[Confirmed]** |
| Function of aperture 1 | a global register block for the whole audio DMA complex; contents **[Unknown]** (section 4) | **[Inferred]** |

The shared 8-byte aperture is a real cross-domain dependency: a display-audio driver on M5
must map a register pair that lives in the **audio complex**, even though everything else
about the instance lives in the display pipe. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.4.4 `self-actuated`

The empty `self-actuated` property appears only on the display-audio instances, and only
where the instance has **exactly one channel in total** (transmit + receive = 1); the
platform description is rejected otherwise. Its effect is that the controller raises its own
power/clock domain when a transfer starts and drops it when the transfer stops, resetting
the shared channel-buffer allocator at stop, rather than being held up by an external
consumer for the lifetime of the link. It does **not** mean the hardware starts transfers
by itself. **[Probable]**

Practical reading for a driver: the display-audio DMA instance is powered only while its
stream runs, and its channel-buffer allocation must be re-established on every start.

### 13.4.5 Addresses, interrupts, IOMMU — t8142

Interrupt numbers are host interrupt-controller inputs (`interrupt-parent` = `/arm-io/aic`,
`compatible = "aic,3"`, `#interrupt-cells = <1>`). Identical on j704, j813 and j815.
**[Confirmed]**

| Pipe | DMA aperture 0 | DMA IRQ | IOMMU aperture | IOMMU IRQ | SID | Escalation apertures | Escalation IRQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disp0` | `0x2_8614_0000` +`0x24000` | 822 | `0x2_8618_0000` +`0x20000` | 823 | 30 | `0x2_862f_4000` +`0x4000`, `0x2_861a_0000` +`0x4000` | 824 |
| `dispext0` | `0x5_0614_0000` +`0x24000` | 894 | `0x5_0618_0000` +`0x20000` | 895 | 30 | `0x5_062f_4000`, `0x5_061a_0000` | 896 |
| `dispext1` | `0x3_aa14_0000` +`0x24000` | 969 | `0x3_aa18_0000` +`0x20000` | 970 | 30 | `0x3_aa2f_4000`, `0x3_aa1a_0000` | 971 |

### 13.4.6 Addresses, interrupts, IOMMU — t6050

Identical on j714s, j714c, j716s and j716c. **[Confirmed]**

| Pipe | DMA aperture 0 | DMA IRQ | IOMMU aperture | IOMMU IRQ | SID | Escalation apertures | Escalation IRQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disp0` | `0x4_8a14_0000` +`0x24000` | 1012 | `0x4_8a18_0000` +`0x20000` | 1013 | 30 | `0x4_8a2f_4000`, `0x4_8a1a_0000` | 1014 |
| `dispext0` | `0x2_b214_0000` +`0x24000` | 1092 | `0x2_b218_0000` +`0x20000` | 1093 | 30 | `0x2_b22f_4000`, `0x2_b21a_0000` | 1094 |
| `dispext1` | `0x3_9214_0000` +`0x24000` | 1164 | `0x3_9218_0000` +`0x20000` | 1165 | 30 | `0x3_922f_4000`, `0x3_921a_0000` | 1166 |
| `dispext2` | `0x3_0214_0000` +`0x24000` | 1236 | `0x3_0218_0000` +`0x20000` | 1237 | 30 | `0x3_022f_4000`, `0x3_021a_0000` | 1238 |
| `dispext3` | `0x3_0614_0000` +`0x24000` | 1308 | `0x3_0618_0000` +`0x20000` | 1309 | 30 | `0x3_062f_4000`, `0x3_061a_0000` | 1310 |

Each triple (DMA, IOMMU, escalation) is contiguous in the interrupt map, and each sits in
the same `0x100_0000`-aligned neighbourhood as its display pipe's second and third register
windows. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.4.7 IOMMU

The display-audio stream is not behind the audio IOMMU on M5. Each pipe gets a new
isochronous IOMMU whose highest stream is the display-audio stream.

| Property | Value | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| `compatible` | `dart,t8110` — the same generation of IOMMU as elsewhere on these SoCs | **[Confirmed]** |
| Aperture | `0x20000` | **[Confirmed]** |
| `sid-count` | 31 | **[Confirmed]** |
| Display-audio stream id (`mapper-*-dpa` `reg`) | **30** — the last stream | **[Confirmed]** |
| `page-size` | `0x4000` (16 KiB) | **[Confirmed]** |
| `vm-base` | `0x100_0000_0000` | **[Confirmed]** |
| `vm-size` | `0x10_0000_0000` (64 GiB) | **[Confirmed]** |
| `dart-options` | `0x25` | **[Confirmed]**, meaning **[Unknown]** |
| `allow-subpage-mapping` | present on the display-audio mapper | **[Confirmed]** |
| `flush-by-dva` | 0 | **[Confirmed]** |
| `avoid-tlbi-in-map` | present | **[Confirmed]** |

`allow-subpage-mapping` matters: the audio ring buffer need not be 16 KiB aligned or sized.
**[Probable]**

### 13.4.8 Ordering and independence

The display-audio DMA instance is **not** usable independently of the display controller.
The ordering constraints that the platform description makes unavoidable:

1. Its power domain's parent is the display pipe's `*_SYS` domain. The pipe must be powered
   before the DMA instance can be. **[Confirmed]**
2. Its `reg` windows and its IOMMU lie inside the display pipe's address neighbourhood,
   which is not accessible with the pipe unpowered. **[Confirmed]**
3. It has a single transmit channel and no receive channel; there is nothing to do with it
   except stream into the pipe's audio packetiser. **[Confirmed]**
4. Its block reset is a power-manager `ARST` on the same device id, so resetting the audio
   block and power-cycling it are the same operation. **[Confirmed]**
5. Rate, channel allocation and IEC framing are configured on the display side before
   samples mean anything. **[Inferred]**

Conversely the DMA instance is independent of the **audio** complex apart from the shared
8-byte global aperture (§13.4.3) — starting display audio does not require the serial audio
clusters, the oscillator, or the always-on coprocessor. **[Probable]**

Sensible bring-up order: power the display pipe → power and de-reset the display-audio
domain → program the pipe's audio format through the display coprocessor → map the buffer
through the pipe's isochronous IOMMU on stream 30 → program and start the DMA channel.
Stop in reverse. **[Inferred]**
