## 13.5 The latency-escalation / snapshot blocks (`ced-ssw`)

### 13.5.1 What they are

A `ced-ssw` block is a memory-traffic **escalation detector** paired with a **register
snapshot** facility. It watches the DMA controller it is bound to and, when the controller's
buffer occupancy crosses a programmed trigger threshold, escalates the controller's memory
traffic into a *critical low-latency* class for a programmed duration, so the fabric
prioritises the refill ahead of bulk traffic. On escalation it latches a fixed set of
registers into a snapshot window for post-hoc diagnosis. It is a general SoC facility, not
an audio-specific one (§13.5.5). **[Probable]**

The block type is `compatible = "admacled,<soc>"`, `device_type = "ced-ssw"`. It first
appears in the platform description on **t8142 and t6050**; it does not exist on t8132,
t6041 or t8140. **[Confirmed]**

Each SoC also has one instance covering the audio complex, `/arm-io/admac-aop-ced-ssw`,
which is bound to **four** controllers at once (`dma-controllers` = `BASS`, `BANS`, `LESS`,
`LENS`) and has `#ssw-register-count = 157`; the per-display instances are bound to one
controller and have `#ssw-register-count = 4`. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.5.2 Node properties

| Property | Display instances | Always-on instance |
|---|---|---|
| `compatible` | `admacled,t8142` / `admacled,t6050` | same |
| `identity` | `DISP-I-ISOC` (internal pipe), `DISP-E0-ISOC` … `DISP-E3-ISOC` | `ADMAC-A` |
| `reg` | two `0x4000` windows, far apart | two adjacent `0x4000` windows |
| `interrupts` | one, on the host interrupt controller | one |
| `#dma-controllers` / `dma-controllers` | 1 / the controller's `role` FourCC | 4 / `BASS BANS LESS LENS` |
| `#dma-channels-tx` / `#dma-channels-rx` | 1 / 0 | `13 13 9 9` / `14 13 9 9` |
| `#ssw-register-count` | 4 | 157 |

The controller side carries the reciprocal link: each `admac-disp*` node has a
`ced-ssw-service` string whose tail is the same identity (`DISP-I-ISOC`, `DISP-E0-ISOC`, …),
and each main audio DMA instance on M5 carries one naming the `ADMAC-A` identity.
**[Confirmed]**

Aperture order: `reg` entry **0** is the escalation-detector register window, `reg` entry
**1** is the snapshot window. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.5.3 Escalation-detector register window (aperture 0, `0x4000`)

Offsets are from the start of `reg` entry 0. Names are functional and coined here.

| Offset | Name | Access | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | `CED_RUN` | W | bit 0 | Written 1 **last** in the bring-up sequence; starts detection. |
| `0x0c` | `CED_INIT` | W | bit 0 | Written 1 **first**; initialises/clears the block. |
| `0x10` | `CED_IRQ_ENABLE` | RW | bits [7:0] | Written `0xff`; up to 8 interrupt sources. |
| `0x20` | `CED_TRIG_THRESHOLD` | RW | u32 | Occupancy/latency trigger threshold. Must be non-zero. Units **[Unknown]**. |
| `0x28` | `CED_ESC_DURATION` | RW | u32 | How long the escalated traffic class is held. Must be non-zero. Units **[Unknown]**. |
| `0x2c` | `CED_ABS_LTR` | RW | u32 | Absolute latency-tolerance value asserted while escalated. Must be non-zero. Units **[Unknown]**. |
| `0x34` | `CED_MODE` | RW | bit 0 set, bit 1 cleared | Mode select; the two bits are programmed independently. |
| `0x3c` | `CED_ARM` | RW | bits 0 and 1 set | Arms detection; both bits are set, in order. |
| `0x5c` | `CED_IRQ_STATUS` | RW | bit 2 | Interrupt acknowledge — bit 2 is written back to clear the escalation interrupt. |

Bring-up order, exactly as the sequence is constructed:
`CED_INIT ← 1` → `CED_TRIG_THRESHOLD` → `CED_ESC_DURATION` → `CED_ABS_LTR` →
`CED_MODE` bit 0 set → `CED_MODE` bit 1 cleared → `CED_ARM` bit 0 set → `CED_ARM` bit 1 set
→ `CED_IRQ_ENABLE ← 0xff` → `CED_RUN ← 1` → `SSW_RELEASE ← 0xffffffff`. **[Probable]**

All three parameter registers must be programmed non-zero before the block will be enabled;
a zero in any of them aborts the sequence. **[Confirmed]**

Reset values and the units of the three parameters are **[Unknown]**; the platform
description supplies no default values for them on any in-scope board (§13.5.6).

☠ **The block therefore cannot be configured from this document**, because all
three parameters must be non-zero and none of them has a unit. The raw defaults
recorded for the audio instance (`CED_ABS_LTR` and `CED_ESC_DURATION` `0x7f`,
`CED_TRIG_THRESHOLD` `0x1c20` — §4 §4.10.4) are dimensionless as written and must
not be transcribed into these registers as if they were not. Candidate units are
interconnect clock cycles, ticks of the DMA controller's 54-bit local counter and
ticks of the always-on global timebase (§4 §4.1.3), which differ by the integer
scalers of §4 open question 9.

**What a driver must do meanwhile: do not run the bring-up sequence.** The block
is absent on t8132, t604x and t8140 and display audio works there without it, so
it is demonstrably not required for correctness; on t8142 and t6050 it improves
behaviour under memory-bandwidth load (open question 6). Leaving it uninitialised
leaves it inert, which is the same state those three SoCs are in permanently. A
wrong threshold either never escalates — no worse than inert — or escalates
permanently, which holds the **whole memory system** in its critical low-latency
mode for as long as audio runs. That is a system-wide cost paid for an audio
optimisation, and it is the reason to leave the block alone until open question 3
is answered.

### 13.5.4 Snapshot register window (aperture 1, `0x4000`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | `SSW_STATE0` | R | First of two status words captured into each snapshot record. |
| `0x04` | `SSW_STATE1` | R | Second status word. |
| `0x08` | `SSW_RELEASE` | W | Written `0xffffffff` at enable to arm; written `1` after a snapshot has been read out, to release the capture and re-arm. |
| `0x0c` + 4·n | `SSW_CAPTURE[n]` | R | Captured register n, for n = 0 … (`#ssw-register-count` − 1). 4 words on a display instance, 157 on the always-on instance. |

On an escalation interrupt the sequence is: read `SSW_STATE0`, `SSW_STATE1` and
`SSW_CAPTURE[0…n-1]`, then acknowledge with `CED_IRQ_STATUS` bit 2, then `SSW_RELEASE ← 1`.
**[Probable]**

The snapshot also carries, per record, which transmit and receive channels of the bound
controller were active at the moment of escalation (up to four of each are reported).
**[Probable]**

### 13.5.5 The SoC-wide escalation-detector registry (t6050 only)

t6050 carries a root-level `/ced-ssw` node with two child tables, `ced_tunable_mask` and
`ced_disable_mask`, each a flat list of named u32 bit indices. They enumerate **every**
escalation detector in the SoC, per die:

`pmgr_ced`, `isp_ced`, `scodec_ced`, `aop_audio_ced`, `disp0_audio_ced`,
`dispext0_audio_ced` … `dispext3_audio_ced`, `disp0_ced`, `dispext0_ced` …
`dispext3_ced` — each with a `_die0` and a `_die1` variant, 28 entries in total.

`ced_disable_mask` assigns one consecutive index per instance (0…27); `ced_tunable_mask`
assigns indices in steps of two (0, 2, 4 … 54), i.e. **two bits per instance**.
**[Confirmed]**

This establishes that the escalation detector is a general SoC block: the display pipes have
one for their own (non-audio) fetch traffic as well as one for display audio, and the image
signal processor and the sensor codec have their own. It also shows the t6050 family
provisioning two dies' worth of instances; the four M5 Pro/Max board descriptions in scope
instantiate die-0 instances only. **[Confirmed]** The tables are byte-identical across
j714s/j714c/j716s/j716c. **[Confirmed]**

t8142 has no equivalent root node. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.5.6 Tunable tables

The block accepts two optional device-tree tunable tables, `ced-tunables` and
`ssw-tunables`, on the `ced-ssw` node. Each is an array of **24-byte** records:

| Offset in record | Width | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | u32 | register offset within the corresponding aperture |
| `0x04` | u32 | access width in bytes — must be 4 |
| `0x08` | u32 | value |
| `0x0c` | u32 | unused by the write path |
| `0x10` | u32 | mask |
| `0x14` | u32 | unused by the write path |

The value written is `value & mask`, as a 32-bit store at the given offset —
`ced-tunables` applies to aperture 0, `ssw-tunables` to aperture 1. When either table is
present it **replaces** the parameter-register sequence of §13.5.3 entirely. **[Probable]**

**No in-scope board carries either property.** On every t8142 and t6050 board the
`ced-ssw` nodes have only the properties listed in §13.5.2. **[Confirmed]** The mechanism
exists but is unused on shipping hardware, which is why the fixed sequence in §13.5.3 is
the one that matters.

### 13.5.7 Does a driver have to configure it?

**No, not to move samples.** The escalation detector is a separate device with its own
aperture and interrupt; the DMA controller will transmit with the detector untouched. What
is lost by skipping it is (a) the memory-latency escalation that protects the display-audio
FIFO under memory pressure, making underruns more likely on a loaded system, and (b) the
diagnostic snapshot. **[Inferred]**

It is worth configuring on M5 for robustness, but it is not on the critical path, and the
three parameter values a driver would need are not supplied by platform firmware
(§13.5.6) — they must be chosen empirically.

### 13.5.8 The memory-QoS vote — a second, separate mechanism

Distinct from the escalation detector, each audio DMA controller instance also asserts a
**critical low-latency traffic** vote while it is running. The mechanism changed within the
M5 generation:

| SoC | Mechanism | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| t8132, t6041, t8140, t8142 | `clock-gates` on the DMA node points at a virtual power-manager domain named `AUDIO-LLT-V` | id 0x156 (t8132), 0x1ec (t6041), 0x12b (t8140), 0x164 (t8142); flags `0x10`, no real control register |
| **t6050** | `function-vote_crit_llt_mode` on the DMA node | `<pmgr-phandle, 'VCLM', 0, 0>`; the `AUDIO-LLT-V` domain **no longer exists** on this SoC |

On t8142 the display-audio DMA instances carry `clock-gates` = `AUDIO-LLT-V`, exactly like
the main audio instances; on t6050 they carry `function-vote_crit_llt_mode` and **no**
`clock-gates` or `power-gates` at all — the display-audio node's own `power-gates` is the
only power reference. **[Confirmed]**

A driver must assert this vote around an active display-audio stream on both M5 SoCs, by
the SoC-appropriate mechanism. **[Probable]**

---

## 13.6 Host-visible stream interface

### 13.6.1 What is and is not host-visible

| Function | Where it is programmed | All in-scope SoCs |
|---|---|---|
| Sample transport from memory | DMA (coprocessor mailbox on M4/A18 Pro; host MMIO on M5) | §13.3 / §13.4 |
| Sample rate, sample size, channel count, channel allocation | display coprocessor, over its own message endpoint | not host MMIO |
| IEC 60958 / IEC 61937 framing, audio InfoFrame, clock regeneration | display pipe hardware under coprocessor control | not host MMIO |
| Sink capability discovery | EDID, read by the display coprocessor | not host MMIO |

There is **no host-visible register that sets the display-audio sample rate or channel
count on any SoC in scope.** The negotiated maxima and minima for linear PCM (channel
count, sample rate, sample size) are properties handed up from the display coprocessor per
connected sink, not SoC constants. **[Confirmed]**

#### The display-coprocessor side — what is established, and what is not

This subsection previously stopped at "not host MMIO". That is the correct
answer to "which register do I write", but it is not the whole answer to "what
must exist", so the boundary is drawn here explicitly.

**Established — the complete host-reachable control surface for display audio on
t8132, t604x and t8140.** It is three things and nothing else:

| Control | Mechanism | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Power and clock gating of the display-audio transmit block | raise `DPA<N>` (and therefore `DPA_P` and `SIO`) through the power manager; one 32-bit control register per domain, addresses in §13.1 | §13.1 |
| Reset release of the same block | the `ARST` platform function carried on the `dp-audio<N>` node as `function-device_reset_dpa`, whose argument is that domain's power-manager device index — the same index `power-gates` and `clock-gates` name | §13.3 |
| Sample transport from memory | one channel of the general-purpose I/O coprocessor's DMA service, named by `dma-parent` and `dma-channels` on the `dp-audio<N>` node (channel `0x64`, 2 channels) — a message sequence to that coprocessor, not a register write | §13.3 |

**[Confirmed]** — these three are the only audio-related properties the
`dp-audio<N>` nodes carry on any in-scope board, and the nodes carry no `reg`.

**Not established — the display coprocessor's own audio control vocabulary.**
Everything between "the DMA channel is running" and "the sink receives audio"
crosses the display coprocessor's message endpoint, and **no part of that
vocabulary is established**: not the message endpoint's opcodes, not a property
key, not a payload layout, not the sequence, and not the enable. Specifically
**[Unknown]** for t8132, t604x and t8140:

| Function | Status |
|---|---|
| Sample-rate selection | **[Unknown]** — no opcode, key or payload established |
| Sample-size selection and the packing of 16/20/24-bit samples | **[Unknown]** — see also §13.6.4 and open question 10 |
| Channel count and **channel allocation** (the CEA-861 speaker-placement code) | **[Unknown]** |
| Audio InfoFrame contents and when it is re-sent | **[Unknown]** |
| IEC 60958 channel-status and validity/user bits | **[Unknown]** — whether they are generated in the transmit block or supplied is not established |
| Audio clock regeneration (the HDMI N/CTS pair, or the DisplayPort maud/naud pair) | **[Unknown]** |
| The audio **enable** itself — the handshake that starts and stops the sink-side stream | **[Unknown]** |
| Sink capability discovery | read from EDID **by the display coprocessor**; the host does not read EDID for this purpose and the negotiated result is handed up per sink, not per SoC. **[Confirmed]** |

**Nothing in the platform description describes any of it.** The `dp-audio<N>`
nodes carry no `port`/`endpoint` link to a display node on any in-scope board,
no message-endpoint identifier, and no audio-shaped property; the display nodes
carry no audio-shaped property either. A driver author must not expect to find
this vocabulary by decoding the platform description. See open questions 16, 17
and 18.

**What this means for an audio-subsystem driver.** On t8132, t604x and t8140 it
means nothing at all: display audio is not an audio-subsystem function on those
SoCs (§13.1), and the vocabulary above belongs to whatever drives the display
coprocessor. On t8142 and t6050 the audio-subsystem driver owns the DMA half and
**still** does not own any of the functions in the table above — the split is the
same, only the data path moved. An M5-generation driver that programs the DMA
correctly and gets silence has not necessarily made a mistake: the sink-side
stream may simply never have been enabled.

### 13.6.2 Rates

The supported linear-PCM rate set for the display-audio path is the standard
CEA-861/HDMI and DisplayPort set:

**32 000, 44 100, 48 000, 88 200, 96 000, 176 400, 192 000 Hz** — seven rates.
**[Confirmed]**

Which subset is usable on a given link is a function of the sink's EDID and the available
link bandwidth, not of the SoC. **[Confirmed]**

### 13.6.3 Channels

Channel count is per-sink. The transport imposes no limit that the platform description
discloses: the DMA channel is a byte stream of 32-bit words and the packetiser downstream
performs the channel mapping and speaker allocation. The maximum for HDMI linear PCM is 8
channels by the standard; the SoC-imposed maximum is **[Unknown]** (open question 12).
A channel-allocation code (the CEA-861 speaker-allocation value) and a channel layout are
supplied to the display side per stream — **over the display coprocessor's own message
endpoint, whose vocabulary is [Unknown]** (§13.6.1, open question 16). **[Probable]**

**What a driver must do meanwhile.** Treat **2 channels** as the only count it can
rely on: it is the count every `dp-audio<N>` node's `dma-channels` record declares
on every in-scope board, it is within every sink's capability, and it needs no
speaker-allocation code beyond the trivial one. Anything above two depends on both
the unknown SoC maximum and the unknown allocation vocabulary, so a driver must not
offer it until entries 12 and 16 are answered. **[Inferred]**

### 13.6.4 Formats and sample width

| Layer | Width | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Memory / DMA word | **32 bits** (`datashape = 2` on every generation) | **[Confirmed]** |
| Wire sub-frame | IEC 60958 sub-frame; 16/20/24-bit sample sizes per the standard; which one is selected is negotiated per sink | **[Probable]** |
| Exact packing of 16/20/24-bit samples into the 32-bit DMA word | — | **[Unknown]** |

☠ **The packing is [Unknown] and there is no safe default.** The candidates are
left-justified (sample in the high bits, as the speaker link's 24-in-32 playback
slot uses — §1 §1.4.4) and right-justified (sample in the low bits). Getting it
wrong produces not silence but **full-scale noise**: a right-justified 24-bit
sample read as left-justified is the true sample scaled by 2⁻⁸ with the low byte
of the next value in its high bits, and the reverse is the true sample multiplied
by 256 with wraparound. Nor is it established whether the IEC 60958
validity/user/channel-status bits occupy part of the 32-bit word or are generated
downstream, which changes how many bits are available for the sample. Open
question 10.

**What a driver must do meanwhile.** Use the **32-bit sample width** path only.
`datashape = 2` (32-bit memory words) is **[Confirmed]** on every generation, and
a 32-bit source sample fills the word with no packing decision to get wrong,
whichever justification the hardware uses for narrower widths and whatever the
status bits occupy. Convert narrower material to 32 bits in software rather than
programming a narrower wire width. This costs memory bandwidth and nothing else.

Both linear PCM and **IEC 61937 compressed passthrough** are carried. The compressed
formats the display path recognises include AC-3, Enhanced AC-3, MPEG-1/2 audio, MP3, AAC,
and the DTS/MAT family. From the DMA's point of view all of these are the same: opaque
32-bit words at the negotiated frame rate. **[Probable]**

### 13.6.5 Starting and stopping a stream

**t8132 / t6041 / t8140** — the host does not touch a register. The sequence is: raise the
`DPA<N>` power domain and release its `ARST` reset through the power manager; configure the
display side; then configure, issue and later terminate the coprocessor DMA channel
(0x64 + 2n) by mailbox transaction. **[Confirmed]** for the power/reset half,
**[Probable]** for the transaction sequence.

**t8142 / t6050** — the host programs the DMA directly, using the audio DMA controller
interface of section 4 restricted to transmit channel 0:

1. Raise `DISP*_ADMA` (parent `DISP*_SYS` must already be up) and release its `ARST` reset.
2. Assert the critical low-latency traffic vote (§13.5.8).
3. Map the ring buffer through the pipe's isochronous IOMMU on stream 30.
4. Program the channel's buffer carve-out and FIFO thresholds (`0x1000` / `0x800`, §13.2)
   and its bus width for 32-bit words.
5. Queue descriptors and start the channel via the controller's transmit-start register.
6. Service the controller's interrupt on the host interrupt controller line in §13.4.5/6,
   using interrupt destination index 0.
7. Stop via the transmit-stop register; the instance then drops its own power domain
   (§13.4.4) and the channel-buffer allocation is released.

**[Probable]** — the register names and semantics are those of section 4; the per-instance
parameters are **[Confirmed]** from the platform description.

The `self-actuated` behaviour means the controller is *not* continuously powered: it cannot
be left armed across a stream gap without re-establishing the channel-buffer allocation.
**[Probable]**

---

## Per-SoC / per-machine differences

**Within an SoC there is no per-board variation at all.** Every display-audio-related node,
address, interrupt number, channel number, power-domain id and configuration word is
byte-identical across all boards of a given SoC, on every in-scope board
(t8132: j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g; t6041: j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j773s,
j575c; t8140: j700; t8142: j704, j813, j815; t6050: j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c).
**[Confirmed]**

Between SoCs:

- **t8132 (M4, MacBook Pro 14 M4, both iMac 24 M4, both MacBook Air M4, Mac mini M4).**
  Three pipes, three `dp-audio` nodes, coprocessor DMA channels 100/102/104, FIFO
  `0x800`/threshold `0x800`. Silicon carries five `DPA` domains; two are unused. No audio
  subsystem involvement.
- **t6041 (M4 Pro/Max, MacBook Pro 14/16 M4 Pro and Max, Mac mini M4 Pro, Mac Studio
  2025).** Five pipes, five `dp-audio` nodes, channels 100–108, FIFO `0x800`/threshold
  `0x600` — the reduced threshold is inherited from t6030/t6031, not new. No audio
  subsystem involvement.
- **t8140 (A18 Pro, MacBook Neo).** Two pipes only — the smallest display configuration in
  scope. Channels 100/102, FIFO `0x800`/threshold `0x800`. Despite being an H17-generation
  part with `admac-evolution` already set on its main audio DMA instances, it is on the
  **M4 side** of the display-audio boundary in every respect: `sio-dma` parentage,
  `DPA_P`→`SIO` power tree, no per-display DMA, no escalation detector, no isochronous
  display IOMMU. This is the single most important absence in this section.
- **t8142 (M5, MacBook Pro 14 M5, MacBook Air 13/15 M5).** Three pipes; three per-pipe
  audio DMA controller instances, three escalation detectors, three isochronous IOMMUs.
  Roles `DAI0`/`DAX0`/`DAX1`. Memory-QoS vote via the `AUDIO-LLT-V` virtual domain.
- **t6050 (M5 Pro/Max, MacBook Pro 14/16 M5 Pro and Max).** Five pipes with the same
  per-pipe structure. Roles `DAI0`/`DX00`/`DX10`/`DX20`/`DX30`. Memory-QoS vote via
  `function-vote_crit_llt_mode` instead; `AUDIO-LLT-V` does not exist. Carries the SoC-wide
  escalation-detector registry at `/ced-ssw`, provisioned for two dies although the boards
  in scope use one.

---

## Open questions

1. **Address and register map of the display-audio transmit block itself on M4 and later.**
   The platform description gives `dp-audio<N>` no `reg` on any generation; the baseline
   `0x4000` aperture is known only for t8103/t8112 from the Asahi trees, and the power
   parentage shows the block has moved twice since. *Needed for:* deciding whether a driver
   can influence anything about the transmit block directly, or must go through the display
   coprocessor for everything. *Resolve by:* hypervisor-level MMIO tracing of a display
   audio start on an M4 and an M5 machine, watching for accesses in the I/O-coprocessor and
   display-pipe register neighbourhoods respectively, and correlating with the `DPA<N>` /
   `DISP*_ADMA` power-domain register being raised.

2. **The top `0x10000` of the standard audio DMA controller aperture.** The display
   instances map `0x24000` where the main instances map `0x34000`. The hypothesis that the
   missing region is the receive-side descriptor/report window set is an inference.
   *Needed for:* knowing whether any transmit-side register a driver needs lives above
   `0x24000`. *Resolve by:* probing the two apertures for decode (read-back of a written
   pattern) page by page on an M5 machine, on both a `0x34000` and a `0x24000` instance.

3. **Units and sane values for the three escalation-detector parameters** (`CED_TRIG_THRESHOLD`,
   `CED_ESC_DURATION`, `CED_ABS_LTR`). No in-scope board supplies `ced-tunables`, so there
   are no platform-supplied defaults. *Needed for:* configuring the block at all; wrong
   values either never escalate or escalate permanently. *Resolve by:* reading the
   registers back after a stock boot with display audio active on an M5 machine, on both a
   display instance and the always-on-complex instance, and correlating the duration value
   against a measured escalation window using a memory-pressure generator.

4. **`CED_MODE` and `CED_ARM` bit semantics.** Bit 0 of `CED_MODE` is set and bit 1 cleared;
   both bits of `CED_ARM` are set. The meaning of the cleared bit and of the two arm bits is
   not established, and there may be further mode bits. *Resolve by:* reading both registers
   back on a stock boot and toggling individual bits with a stream running while watching
   the escalation interrupt rate.

5. **The four snapshot capture registers on a display instance.** `#ssw-register-count = 4`
   says how many words are latched but not which controller registers they mirror.
   *Needed for:* using the snapshot as an underrun diagnostic. *Resolve by:* forcing an
   underrun on an M5 machine and comparing the four captured words against a full read of
   the DMA controller's own status registers taken immediately afterwards.

6. **Whether the escalation detector must be enabled for glitch-free display audio under
   load.** Currently assessed as optional-but-recommended, by inference. *Resolve by:*
   running display audio with the detector disabled and with it enabled under a heavy
   memory-bandwidth load on an M5 machine, and counting underruns.

7. **Meaning of `irq-destinations` entries 2 and 3.** Entry 0 is the host interrupt
   controller and entry 1 the always-on coprocessor; the remaining two FourCCs are not
   identified. All in-scope display instances use index 0. *Needed for:* nothing on the
   host path, but it bears on whether the display coprocessor can take the DMA interrupt
   instead. *Resolve by:* setting a non-zero destination index on a spare channel and
   observing which agent is notified.

8. **`dart-options = 0x25` on the isochronous IOMMUs.** The option bits are not decoded.
   *Needed for:* correct IOMMU setup, in particular whether bypass or a special translation
   mode is implied. *Resolve by:* comparing the value against other IOMMU instances of the
   same generation whose behaviour is already characterised, and by probing the IOMMU
   configuration registers directly.

9. **Function of the shared 8-byte second aperture** (`0x3_882a_8000` on t8142,
   `0x2_8832_8000` on t6050) that every audio DMA controller instance maps, display
   instances included. *Needed for:* knowing whether a display-audio driver must write it,
   and whether two drivers racing on it need a lock. *Resolve by:* tracing writes to it
   during independent start/stop of a display-audio stream and a speaker stream on an M5
   machine. Cross-reference section 4.

10. **Packing of 16/20/24-bit samples into the 32-bit DMA word**, and whether the
    packetiser expects samples left- or right-justified, and whether the IEC 60958
    validity/user/channel-status bits are carried in the DMA word or generated downstream.
    *Needed for:* getting anything other than silence or noise out of the link.
    *Resolve by:* streaming a known ramp on an M5 machine and capturing the wire with a
    DisplayPort/HDMI analyser.

11. **Whether IEC 61937 compressed passthrough uses the same DMA word format** as linear
    PCM, or requires a different `datashape`. The platform description supplies a single
    fixed channel configuration per pipe, which suggests the former. *Resolve by:* starting
    a compressed passthrough stream and comparing the programmed channel configuration
    against a linear-PCM stream.

12. **Maximum channel count the display-audio packetiser supports**, as opposed to the
    per-sink negotiated maximum. *Resolve by:* attaching a sink advertising 8-channel
    linear PCM and confirming an 8-channel stream is accepted on each of M4, A18 Pro and M5.

13. **Why t8140 was left on the old display-audio architecture** while sharing the
    `admac-evolution` main audio DMA revision with t8142/t6050 — i.e. whether the
    per-display DMA is genuinely absent from the silicon or merely undescribed.
    *Needed for:* nothing immediately, but a driver should not probe for it speculatively.
    *Resolve by:* probing the address offsets within the t8140 display pipes that
    correspond to the t8142 `admac-disp*` and `ced-ssw` windows, for bus decode.

14. **Whether the two unused `DPA` domains on t8132** (`DPA3`, `DPA4`, ids 0x82 and 0x85)
    correspond to real display-audio blocks on a larger package of the same die.
    *Resolve by:* raising those domains on an M4 machine and checking whether the power
    state acknowledges.

15. **What the second die's escalation-detector entries in the t6050 `/ced-ssw` registry
    imply** for a two-die M5 part not represented among the four in-scope boards — in
    particular whether a die-1 display pipe would bring a sixth through tenth display-audio
    DMA instance. *Resolve by:* re-examining the platform description of any future
    two-die M5 machine.

16. **The display coprocessor's audio control vocabulary: the message endpoint, the
    opcodes or property keys, and the payload layouts** for sample rate, sample size,
    channel count, channel allocation, audio InfoFrame, IEC 60958 channel status and
    audio clock regeneration (§13.6.1). **[Unknown]** on t8132, t604x and t8140, and
    equally on t8142 and t6050 — moving the data path did not move any of this.
    *Needed for:* getting audio out of a display link at all. Programming the DMA is
    necessary and demonstrably not sufficient; a driver that does only that will see a
    running channel and a silent sink and will have no way to tell which side is wrong.
    *Resolve by:* tracing the display coprocessor's mailbox traffic across a display-audio
    start and stop on one M4 machine and one M5 machine, isolating the messages that
    appear only when audio is enabled, and correlating their payloads against a rate and
    channel-count change made one at a time. Cross-check against the audio InfoFrame and
    the channel-status block captured on the wire with a DisplayPort/HDMI analyser, which
    gives the field values the payload must have produced.

17. **The audio enable handshake — what starts the sink-side stream, and in what order
    relative to the DMA channel.** **[Unknown]** (§13.6.1). *Needed for:* start and stop
    ordering on M5, where the host owns the DMA and something else owns the enable, so
    the two must be sequenced across an interface this document does not specify.
    Starting the DMA first risks an underrun before the first sample is consumed;
    starting the enable first risks the sink seeing invalid frames. *Resolve by:* on an
    M5 machine, trace the display coprocessor's mailbox and the `admac-disp0` channel
    registers together across a start, and record which happens first and what the gap
    is; repeat across a stop.

18. **Whether the host can influence any of the functions in §13.6.1's second table at
    all, or whether the display coprocessor owns them absolutely.** **[Unknown]**.
    *Needed for:* knowing whether an independent driver can offer rate or channel-layout
    selection to userspace on a display link, or must accept whatever the display stack
    negotiates. *Resolve by:* after answering entry 16, attempt a rate change on an
    active display-audio stream from the host side and observe whether it is accepted,
    refused, or accepted and ignored.

# 14. Power management and sequencing

## Baseline

Measured against the M1–M3 arrangement, in which every audio block is host power-managed:

- The serial audio controller's common domain, its per-cluster domains and the audio DMA
  domain are real host-addressable power-manager devices, children of the host serial-I/O
  domain. The serial controller and the DMA controller **share one reset**, declared on
  both nodes.
- The serial controller has no suspend/resume behaviour at all — it relies on
  reference-counting the cluster domains, and reprograms every register on every stream
  start, so nothing is saved or restored.
- The audio DMA controller likewise has no system-level suspend/resume; ring state is torn
  down per stream.
- The speaker amplifier (TAS2764/TAS2770 family, Apple variant SN012776) loses its entire
  register file whenever the shared shutdown line is asserted, and the whole file is
  replayed on resume.
- The jack codec (CS42L42 family) is powered off at system sleep by platform policy and is
  re-reset and reprogrammed on wake.
- The always-on coprocessor is taken to a sleep state — never to the unrecoverable off
  state — and the whole boot handshake is re-run on resume.
- Pop/click suppression is entirely in the amplifier's mute ramp: mute, wait 6–7 ms, shut
  the DAC down, wait a further 2–3 ms.

Public counterparts for the third-party parts: TAS2764/TAS2770 (SN012776), MAX98360A
(t8140 amplifier), CS42L42/CS42L83 and CS42L84 (jack codecs).

## Summary of differences

| Item | M1–M3 | t8132 (M4) | t604x (M4 Pro/Max) | t8140 (A18 Pro) | t8142 (M5) | t605x (M5 Pro/Max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who powers the serial controller, clocks and clusters | host | **coprocessor** | coprocessor | coprocessor | coprocessor | coprocessor |
| Audio power domains host-addressable | yes | **no** (all virtual) | no | no | no | no |
| Audio DMA controller has a host power gate | yes (two real domains) | **no** (`power-gates` absent) | no | no | no | no |
| Host can power-cycle the DMA domain to clear a latched fault | yes | **no** | no | no | no | no |
| Host performs the serialiser reset dance before each DMA start | yes | **no** — coprocessor-owned | no | no | no | no |
| Audio IOMMU sleeps at system sleep | yes (no flag) | **no** — `no-sleep` | **no** | **no** | **no** | **no** |
| Coprocessor declared never-shut-down | no | **yes** (`no-shutdown = 1`) | **no** | yes | yes | yes |
| Coprocessor declared a wake claimant | no | **yes** (`claim-wake`) | **no** | yes | yes | yes |
| Second coprocessor instance with its own power state | no | no | no | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** |
| Audio controller names a hibernation-surviving power provider | no | no | no | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** |
| Per-endpoint power provider is the DMA controller node | n/a | **yes** (`external-power-provider` + `function-admac_powerswitch`) | yes | replaced by named channels | replaced | replaced |
| Jack codec powered off at sleep | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Jack codec reset line domain | always-on nub | always-on nub | always-on nub | **application processor** | always-on nub | **application processor** |
| Amplifier register state lost on shutdown assertion | yes | yes | yes | **n/a — no registers** | yes | yes |
| Platform-carried mute-ramp delay | none | none | none | **20 ms** | none | none |
| Coprocessor-performed ramp-down flag | none | none | none | **`enable-iop-ramp-down`** | none | none |
| Audio domains performance-managed | n/a | **6 of them** | no | no | no | no |

---

## 14.1 The ownership boundary, and why it dominates this section

On every in-scope SoC the audio power tree is rooted inside the always-on coprocessor
island and **every audio power domain carries the "no host power-state register" flag**
(§2.6). The host therefore has:

- **no** power domain for the serial audio controller or any of its six base clusters;
- **no** power domain for the low-power serial audio cluster or the low-power audio
  processor;
- **no** power domain for any of the four audio DMA apertures — the `admac-*` nodes carry
  no `power-gates` property at all, and their `clock-gates` names only a virtual
  latency-tolerance vote (on t605x not even that, only `function-vote_crit_llt_mode`);
- **no** reset line bound to any audio node.

What the host does own, and must therefore sequence itself:

| Host-owned | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The audio DMA controllers' registers and per-channel state | `reg` present, aperture 0x34000, host interrupt lines (§4, §5.2) |
| The I2C controllers on which the amplifiers and jack codec sit | real power-manager devices, flags `0x00`, `clock-gates` + `function-device_reset` (§6.1) |
| The amplifier shutdown line, the jack codec reset line, the speaker-ID pins | `function-reset`, `function-speaker-id0/1` (§6.5, §6.8) |
| The amplifier and jack codec register files | I2C (§6.2); absent on t8140, which has no amplifier control bus |
| The coprocessor mailbox and the audio service on it | §11 |

**Consequence for this section.** A host driver cannot express "power down the audio
block"; it can only stop its own DMA, release the codecs, and let the coprocessor decide.
Every sequence below is therefore split into *host-side steps* and *requests to the
coprocessor*, and the two must interleave in a fixed order. **[Confirmed]** for the
ownership facts; **[Inferred]** for the split.

---

## 14.2 Suspend and resume requirements, per block

### 14.2.1 Audio DMA controllers

Instances, per SoC (host-visible nodes only):

| SoC | `admac-base-ns` | `admac-base-s` | `admac-leap-ns` | `admac-leap-s` | Per-display |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t8132 | yes | no node (IOMMU mapper only) | yes | no node | none |
| t604x | yes | no node | yes | no node | none |
| t8140 | yes | no node | yes | **yes** | none |
| t8142 | yes | no node | yes | **yes** | `admac-disp0`, `admac-dispext0/1` |
| t605x | yes | no node | yes | **yes** | `admac-disp0`, `admac-dispext0…3` |

**[Confirmed]** from the platform description on every in-scope board.

**Suspend requirement, every instance.** Every channel must be brought to rest before the
instance is left: stop the channel through the global `TX_STOP` / `RX_STOP` bit for that
channel, then pulse the channel's `RESET_RINGS` control (write 1, write 0). A channel that
is merely idle must still be stopped before it is deactivated. **[Confirmed]** — the
stop-before-deactivate rule is enforced by the controller's own channel state machine,
which admits a distinct *stop-before-deactivate* transition out of the idle state.

**The per-channel state ladder** the hardware exposes is:

```
uninitialised → ready → initialising → idle → (configure) → first transfer
             → transferring → complete → stopping → idle → sleep
sleep → initialising  (on resume)
sleep → (configure)   (permitted, but only after re-initialisation)
```

and each channel carries a two-valued power state, **suspended** and **available**.
**[Probable]** — the ladder and the two-state model are consistent across all in-scope SoC
variants of the controller.

Read from the ladder: **a channel that has been through *sleep* re-enters at
*initialising*, not at *idle*.** Its configuration is therefore not retained across a
system sleep and must be re-established — see §14.3.2 for the exact register set.

**Resume requirement.** Before power is re-gated to a channel, that channel must be
observed in the *suspended* power state; it is then moved to *available*, re-initialised,
its FIFO depth re-read from the controller (the transmit- and receive-side staging-memory
size registers are read, not assumed), its carveout re-allocated, and its rings reset.
**[Probable]**

**Two host-side hazards new to this generation:**

1. **The descriptor repeat flag's latching misbehaviour, documented in the baseline as
   surviving everything short of a full power-domain reset, is no longer host-recoverable**
   — the host has no power gate for any audio DMA domain on any in-scope SoC. A host
   driver that sets the repeat flag and then needs to clear the latch must ask the
   coprocessor to cycle the domain. **[Inferred]** — the premise is **[Confirmed]** from
   the baseline and the absence of `power-gates` is **[Confirmed]**.
2. **The whole-block reset is gone from the host's reach.** On M1–M3 the serial audio
   controller and the audio DMA controller shared one reset line, asserted once at probe.
   No in-scope board binds a reset to any audio node. Per-channel `RESET_RINGS` is the only
   reset a host driver can perform. **[Confirmed]** — no such property is declared on
   any in-scope board.

**Latency-tolerance vote.** Each `admac-*` node declares a latency-tolerance vote —
as a virtual clock-gate entry on t8132, t604x, t8140 and t8142, and as
`function-vote_crit_llt_mode` (tag `VCLM`, two zero arguments) on t605x and on the
per-display instances of t8142/t605x. The vote is asserted around active transfer and
released when the controller goes idle; it is not a power gate and gates nothing on its
own. A driver that leaves the vote asserted will hold the memory fabric out of its
low-latency-tolerant state indefinitely. **[Confirmed]** that the vote exists and is
per-instance; **[Probable]** for the assert/release discipline.

**Per-display instances (t8142, t605x).** These feed the display-audio serialisers and are
powered and sequenced with their display pipes, not with the audio island. They must be
quiesced before their display pipe is torn down. **[Inferred]** — cross-reference §5.3 for
their interrupt structure and §1.15 for their endpoint mapping. **[Unknown]** whether they
retain channel configuration across a display-pipe power transition.

**Secure apertures.** `admac-base-s` has no node on any in-scope board; `admac-leap-s` has
a node on t8140, t8142 and t605x but carries an empty IOMMU parent and is reached through a
separate proxy aperture. A host driver neither suspends nor resumes the secure instances —
it cannot address them. **[Confirmed]**

### 14.2.2 Serial audio controller (six base clusters + one low-power cluster)

**No host suspend or resume action exists or is possible.** No aperture is described, no
power domain is host-addressable, and no reset is bound. The block's entire state is
managed by the coprocessor, which reprograms it on its own schedule including at power
transitions (§3.5). **[Confirmed]**

What a host driver must nevertheless know:

- **All cluster state is volatile.** Each cluster's master-clock cell (`AUDIO_MCA0_M` …
  `AUDIO_MCA5_M`) and the low-power cluster cell (`AUDIO_LEAP_MCA`) is an independent
  power-manager device; none carries the *critical* flag on any in-scope SoC, so none is
  declared unpowerable-down. When a cell drops, the cluster behind it loses its clock
  generator, frame-sync generator, serialiser configuration and routing. **[Confirmed]**
  for the flags; **[Inferred]** for the consequence.
- The block's configuration registers carry **defined power-on-reset values that are
  explicitly rewritten at bring-up** — the frame-generator divider, the frame-generator
  source multiplexer and pulse multiplexer, the transmit and receive serial-agent
  configuration, the transmit and receive DMA-agent configuration, the FIFO packer
  configuration and the timestamp mode select all have a known reset value that the
  coprocessor-side control path restores before use. These registers are therefore lost
  on a domain transition, not retained. **[Probable]**
- The frame-sync generator and each serialiser have **self-clearing reset bits that are
  polled to zero**; the clock generator has a reset with a paired reset-pending bit that
  must also be polled clear. **[Probable]** — cross-reference §3.6.4.

### 14.2.3 Clock generator

- **t8132, t604x, t8142, t605x**: the numerically controlled oscillator node is absent
  entirely. **t8140**: the node exists with `compatible` and `clock-ids` but no `reg`.
  Either way there is no host aperture and therefore no host suspend/resume action.
  **[Confirmed]** (§2.1).
- Each cluster master-clock cell has its own **source-select multiplexer register in the
  always-on clock generator, with a defined power-on-reset source**, and each stage of the
  clock-generator chain (pre-divider, divider, clock configuration, final clock) carries a
  **pending bit that must be polled to zero before the next stage is written**.
  **[Probable]** This is the M1–M3 "poll every clock-cell stage" rule made explicit per
  stage; a driver that ever drives these directly during bring-up must honour it.
- **Requirement inherited from the baseline and still load-bearing:** the reference clock
  must be running before a cluster domain is attached — on the baseline parts the cluster
  domains are marked externally clocked and cannot complete a state transition with the
  reference absent. The M4-and-later domains are literally named as master-clock cells, so
  the dependency is explicit. **[Probable]**

### 14.2.4 IOMMU

The audio path's IOMMU (`dart-aop`, `compatible = "dart,t8110"`) carries, on every in-scope
board and on **no** M1–M3 board:

| Property | Value | Present on |
|---|---|---|
| `no-sleep` | valueless flag | t8132, t604x, t8140, t8142, t605x |
| `manual-availability` | `1` | t8132, t8140, t8142, t605x (**absent on t604x**) |
| `avoid-tlbi-in-map` | valueless flag | t8142, t605x only |
| `sid-count` | 16 / 16 / 18 / 17 / 17 | t8132 / t604x / t8140 / t8142 / t605x |

**[Confirmed]** — checked on j604, j713, j773g, j614s, j616c, j575c, j700, j704, j813,
j815, j714s, j716c, against j504, j514s, j613.

Read for sequencing:

- **`no-sleep` means the audio IOMMU is not taken down at system sleep.** Its page tables
  and stream configuration survive, and a host driver must **not** rebuild them on resume.
  This is required for the low-power microphone and voice-trigger paths, which keep
  transferring into memory while the application processor is asleep. **[Inferred]**, from
  the flag plus the wake-source structure of §5.7. It is a genuine delta: no M1–M3 board
  declares it.
- **`manual-availability` means the IOMMU's availability is asserted explicitly rather than
  following a power domain.** Its absence on t604x is a real per-SoC difference and a
  driver must not assume the property is present. **[Confirmed]** for presence/absence;
  **[Probable]** for the reading.
- Mappings for all four DMA apertures are children of this one instance
  (`mapper-admac-base-ns`, `-base-s`, `-leap-ns`, `-leap-s`), plus a coprocessor mapper and
  a secure-world mapper. All audio DMA shares one fault line (§5.6.3). **[Confirmed]**
- **Ordering:** the IOMMU mapping for a DMA aperture must exist before any descriptor is
  submitted on that aperture, and must not be torn down while a channel is running. A
  running channel whose mapping disappears raises the shared IOMMU fault, which does not
  identify the offending instance. **[Inferred]**

### 14.2.5 Always-on coprocessor, and the second instance

The coprocessor node itself has **empty `clock-gates`, empty `power-gates` and empty
`clock-ids`** on every SoC from M1 to M5 — it is not host power-managed. **[Confirmed]**
Its own power states and their relation to the audio domains are §14.8.

Per-board declarations that bear directly on suspend/resume:

| Board set | `no-shutdown` | `claim-wake` | `sleep-on-hibernate` | `watchdog-enable` | Second instance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1–M3 baselines (j504, j514s, j516c, j613) | — | — | yes | yes | — |
| t8132 (j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g) | **1** | **yes** | yes | yes | — |
| t604x (j614s, j614c, j616s, j616c, j773s, j575c) | **—** | **—** | yes | yes | — |
| t8140 (j700) | 1 | yes | yes | yes | **yes**, with `aot-power = 1` |
| t8142 (j704, j813, j815) | 1 | yes | yes | yes | **yes** |
| t605x (j714s, j714c, j716s, j716c) | 1 | yes | yes | yes | **yes** |

**[Confirmed]** on every in-scope board and on four baseline boards.

Decoded:

- **`no-shutdown = 1`** declares that this coprocessor must never be taken to its off
  state. The baseline already establishes that the off state is unrecoverable — the part
  never wakes again. On t8132, t8140, t8142 and t605x the platform description now says so
  explicitly. **t604x does not carry the declaration**, which does not make the off state
  safe there; it only means the description is silent. Treat off as forbidden on every
  in-scope SoC. **[Confirmed]** for the property; **[Probable]** for the universality.
- **`claim-wake`** declares that this coprocessor participates in wake, i.e. it holds the
  wake reason and the host must interrogate it rather than assume. Consistent with §5.7,
  where the only audio-capable wake sources are this coprocessor's mailboxes.
  **[Inferred]**
- **`sleep-on-hibernate`** (present on every board, baseline included) declares that on
  hibernate the coprocessor goes to a sleep state rather than off — unchanged.
  **[Confirmed]**
- **`aot-power = 1`** on the t8140 second instance is unique to that machine and marks the
  second instance as belonging to the always-on-timer power group. **[Probable]**
  **[Unknown]** what it changes in ordering.
- The coprocessor node on every in-scope SoC except t8140 carries a
  **`function-pll_off_mode`** property (phandle into the power manager, four-character tag
  reading `PLLM`, arguments `1, 0`) — a declared PLL-off mode for the island. **t8140 has
  no such property.** **[Confirmed]** for presence; **[Probable]** that it selects the
  island PLL's behaviour when the island is idle. **[Unknown]** what argument `1` selects.

**Second instance.** On t8140, t8142 and t605x there is a second coprocessor with its own
mailboxes, its own wake-source entries (§5.7) and — on t8142 and t605x — its own firmware
image. It declares the same `no-shutdown` / `claim-wake` / `sleep-on-hibernate` set. It is
**[Unknown]** whether any audio stream endpoint is served by the second instance; the
audio controller node names a service on the first. A driver must not assume the second
instance is irrelevant to audio, because on t8142 and t605x it is the instance that carries
an `idle-ctrl-check` declaration. **[Confirmed]** for the declarations; **[Unknown]** for
the audio relevance.

### 14.2.6 I2C controllers

Unchanged from the baseline as a block (`compatible = "i2c,t8101"`), and — uniquely among
the blocks in this section — **still fully host power-managed**:

- `clock-gates` names a **real** power-manager device with flags `0x00` (not virtual, not
  critical, not on-at-boot); on j604 the amplifier bus `i2c3` names device 65 (`I2C3`), on
  j714s the amplifier bus `i2c1` names device 191. **[Confirmed]**
- `function-device_reset` on the controller node targets the power manager with a
  four-character tag reading `ARST` and the controller's own device index as the argument —
  i.e. the controller is reset through its power-manager device, not through a GPIO.
  **[Confirmed]**

**Suspend:** no outstanding transaction; then the clock gate may be released. **Resume:**
re-gate, reset through the power-manager reset, and reapply the controller's timing
tunables (`filter-tunable`, `trigger-level-tunable`, `tbuf-tunable`) and bus speed before
the first transaction — all controller state is lost with the gate. **[Probable]** —
cross-reference §6.1.5 for the tunable encodings.

**Ordering rule that is easy to get wrong:** the I2C controller carrying the amplifiers
must be up *before* the shared shutdown line is deasserted, and must still be up when it is
asserted, because the amplifiers must be reprogrammed after every deassertion and there is
no other way to reach them. **[Confirmed]**

### 14.2.7 Speaker amplifier

**On t8132, t604x, t8142 and t605x** (Apple variant of the TAS2764 family, 1, 4 or 6
devices per machine across one or two buses): behaviour is **unchanged from the M1–M3
baseline**. Suspend is a software shutdown, the shared line asserted, then a wait; resume
is the line deasserted, a wait, and a full replay of the register file. Exact sequences and
delays are in §14.4.4, §14.4.5 and §14.6; the exhaustive restore list is §14.3.3.

**On t8140 (j700)** the part is a MAX98360-family digital-input Class-D amplifier with **no
control interface of any kind**. There is nothing to suspend and nothing to restore. The
only power control is the enable line (application-processor GPIO pin 0x69 = 105, flags
`0x00010001`), and its sequencing is dominated by the 20 ms ramp requirement of §14.6.3.
**[Confirmed]**

### 14.2.8 Jack codec

**Every in-scope board carries `PowerOffAtSleep = 1` on the jack codec control node** —
`/arm-io/i2c1/audio-codec-output` on t8132 and t8142, `/arm-io/i2c2/audio-codec-output` on
t604x and t605x, `/arm-io/i2c0/audio-codec-output` on t8140. The property is a single u32
with value 1. **[Confirmed]** — checked on j604, j713, j623, j773g, j614s, j616c, j575c,
j773s, j700, j704, j813, j815, j714s, j716c.

Decoded: **the codec is to be fully powered down at system sleep, not merely idled.** Its
register file is therefore lost at every system sleep, on every machine in scope, and must
be replayed in full on wake — including the whole jack-detection configuration, without
which the jack state read after wake is meaningless. Unchanged from the baseline, where the
same property carries the same value on every board. **[Confirmed]**

The codec's own device states are: *reset pin pulled down*, *after reset*, *sleep*, and
*system shutdown* — four distinct states, with a separate wake-from-sleep path and a
separate power-down-for-sleep path. **[Probable]**

Two per-machine differences that change the sequence:

- **The reset line's power domain moved on two machines.** On t8132, t604x and t8142 the
  jack codec reset is on the always-on nub pin controller (pins 0x11, 0x3a, 0x12
  respectively); on **t8140 (pin 0x67 = 103) and t605x (pin 0x8b = 139) it is on the
  application-processor pin controller**. **[Confirmed]** Consequence: on those two SoCs
  the reset line's pin state is re-established by the platform's pin restore on wake rather
  than retained, and the host must not assume the codec was held in reset across the
  transition. On the other three the nub controller declares `no-resume-restore = 1`,
  i.e. it retains its pin state and is not restored. **[Inferred]**
- **t8140 uses a CS42L83 rather than a CS42L84**, with a different register map, a link
  master clock of 24 MHz divided by 4 to a 6 MHz bit clock, and a 48 kHz-only rate set
  (§2 §2.3.2, §2.4). Its power-down-for-sleep and
  wake-from-a-powered-off-state paths are distinct from the CS42L84's. **[Probable]**

### 14.2.9 GPIO pin state across a transition

| Controller | `no-resume-restore` | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `/arm-io/gpio0` (application processor) | — | pin state is **re-established on wake**; the description enumerates exceptions in `no-restore-gpio-pins` |
| `/arm-io/nub-gpio(0)` | `1` | retains state; not restored |
| `/arm-io/aop-gpio(0)` | `1` | retains state; not restored |
| `/arm-io/smc-gpio(0)` | `1` | retains state; not restored |

**No audio pin appears in any board's `no-restore-gpio-pins` list.** The lists are:
j604 `{0x88, 0x89, 0x0a}`; j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g, j773s, j575c — empty;
j614s/j614c/j616s/j616c `{0xbf, 0xc0, 0xbe}`; j700 `{0x86, 0x31, 0x32, 0x33}`;
j704 `{0x88, 0x89, 0xa3, 0x4e, 0xcb}`; j813, j815 `{0x4e, 0xcb}`;
j714s/j714c/j716s/j716c `{0x06, 0x07, 0x05, 0x8d, 0x70}`. None of these is an amplifier
shutdown pin (0x0f / 0x36 / 0x97 / 0x6b / 0x69), an amplifier interrupt pin, a speaker-ID
pin, a jack reset pin or a jack interrupt pin. **[Confirmed]**

Read: the amplifier shutdown line's **pin configuration** is restored on wake, but the
**amplifier's register file is not** — the two are independent, and restoring the pin does
not restore the part. A driver must reprogram the amplifiers on wake regardless of what the
pin reads. **[Inferred]**

---

## 14.3 Register state lost across a power-domain transition

### 14.3.1 What the platform description proves, and what it does not

The power-manager device entry's flag byte is the only retention-relevant evidence the
description carries. On every in-scope board the audio flag values are:

| Flag byte | Meaning | Audio domains carrying it |
|---|---|---|
| `0x10` | virtual: no host power-state register | every audio domain on every in-scope SoC |
| `0x30` | virtual + performance-managed | on **t8132 only**: `AUDIO_A`, `AUDIO_BASE_S_A`, `AUDIO_BASE_NS_A`, `AUDIO_LEAP_A`, `AUDIO_LEAP_S_A`, `AUDIO_LEAP_NS_A` |
| `0x11` | virtual + on-at-boot | the alias `AUDIO-P-V`, on t604x and t8140 only |
| `0x08` | **critical — must not be powered down** | **none** |
| `0x02` | notify the power-management processor | **none** |

**[Confirmed]**

Three conclusions follow:

1. **No audio domain is declared unpowerable-down on any in-scope SoC.** The *critical*
   flag appears in the tree (the host serial-I/O domain carries it on t8132 and t605x) but
   on nothing in the audio island. Therefore **no audio block's registers may be assumed
   retained across any transition**, and every one of them must be treated as volatile.
   **[Confirmed]** for the flags; **[Inferred]** for the conclusion.
2. **The parent chain gives the loss granularity.** Dropping a parent necessarily drops
   every child, so losing `AUDIO_P` loses all six cluster master-clock cells and the
   low-power cluster cell; losing `AUDIO_FR` additionally loses the low-power audio
   processor subtree and the microphone PDM converter domain (`AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`,
   misleadingly named — §8 §8.8); losing `AUDIO_A` loses everything
   including the DMA aggregates. The tree is in §2.6.4 and §3.3.1. **[Confirmed]**
3. **The on-at-boot alias tells you the starting condition, not the retention.**
   `AUDIO-P-V` with flags `0x11` on t604x and t8140 says the base peripheral domain is
   already up when the host starts. t8132 and t8142 omit the alias and t605x carries
   `AUDIO_P_V` without the on-at-boot bit; that does not mean the domain is off, only that
   the description does not assert it. **[Confirmed]** / **[Unknown]**

Corroborating evidence from the hardware itself: the serial audio complex's configuration
registers have **named power-on-reset values** which the coprocessor-side control path restores at bring-up
(§14.2.2). A register with a restored reset value is a register that was lost.

### 14.3.2 SoC blocks — what must be re-established

| Block | State lost | What must be rewritten |
|---|---|---|
| Audio DMA controller, per channel | all | bus width (word size + words-per-frame), staging-memory carveout base and size, FIFO threshold and limit, the four per-channel interrupt masks, then ring reset; descriptors must be re-submitted from an empty ring |
| Audio DMA controller, global | **[Unknown]** for most of the aperture | the two generation-gated global words the baseline records being written before the first channel configuration are **[Unknown]** on these parts; the interrupt-output state registers are write-1-to-clear and come up clear |
| Audio DMA controller, read-only | n/a | transmit- and receive-side staging-memory size registers are read back after re-initialisation rather than cached |
| Serial audio cluster (each of six) | all | clock generator source and divisor; frame-sync generator source, edge, pulse length and both phase counts; per-serialiser slot masks, widths, polarity, data delay and configuration word; DMA-agent channel count and mode; routing/cross-connect selection — all coprocessor-performed |
| Low-power serial cluster and its stream domains | all | as above, plus the per-stream receive/transmit domain must be raised before its agent is configured |
| Sense PDM converter | all | software reset polled clear, then clock enable with its change-pending bit polled clear, plus the high-frequency-data input control (§2.6.3, §3.10) |
| Clock generator | all | per-cell source multiplexer restored to its defined reset source; every divider stage's pending bit polled clear |
| IOMMU | **none at system sleep** (`no-sleep`) | nothing; page tables and stream configuration survive |
| I2C controller | all | bus speed, filter/trigger-level/tbuf tunables, then reset through the power manager |
| Application-processor GPIO pin configuration | all | restored by the platform for every audio pin (§14.2.9) |
| Always-on / nub / system-controller GPIO pin configuration | none | retained (`no-resume-restore`) |

**[Probable]** throughout, except the IOMMU row (**[Confirmed]** from the flag) and the DMA
rows (**[Confirmed]** from the baseline register map plus the channel state ladder).

### 14.3.3 Speaker amplifier — exhaustive restore list

Applies to t8132, t604x, t8142 and t605x. **Every register below is lost whenever the
shared shutdown line is asserted, whenever the software-reset bit is written, and whenever
the part's supply is removed.** The public counterpart specifies the register file as
undefined after a shutdown-pin low period. **[Confirmed]**

The list is exhaustive in the sense that it covers every writable address the public map
and the public Apple-variant deviation set establish. Anything not listed is **[Unknown]**
and must be treated as lost.

**Page 0x00 — the main page.** Restore in this order; the page and book selectors must be
re-established first because they too are volatile.

| Offset | Name | Why it must be restored | Danger if missed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x7F / 0x00 | `BOOK` / `PAGE` | every other access depends on them | writes land in the wrong page — arbitrary |
| 0x02 | `MODE_CTRL` | power mode, sense power-down bits, brown-out source select | part stays in shutdown, or sense is dead |
| 0x03 | `CHNL_0` | Y-bridge mode and **analogue output level** — resets to its **maximum, 21 dBV** | ☠ full-scale output into a driver rated for less |
| 0x04 | `DC_BLK0` | playback DC blocker corner, ADC filter, spread spectrum, interrupt-pin pull-up | DC into the driver; wrong interrupt-pin electrical behaviour |
| 0x05 | `DC_BLK1` | **sense-path DC blocker**, edge rate, thermal-foldback enable | sense telemetry offset; foldback disabled |
| 0x06 | `MISC_CFG1` | over-current / over-temperature retry enables, post-filter feedback, safe mode | fault behaviour changes silently |
| 0x07 | `MISC_CFG2` | shutdown-pin mode and timeout, volume ramp rate, global-address enable | shutdown timing and ramp change |
| 0x08–0x0A | `TDM_CFG0`–`TDM_CFG2` | sample-rate code, auto-rate, frame start, receive justification/offset/edge, receive word and slot length, **sense transmit width** | ☠ wrong slot alignment drives the wrong amplifier |
| 0x0B | `LIM_MAX_ATTN` | limiter maximum attenuation, 1 dB per code | limiter ineffective |
| 0x0C | `TDM_CFG3` | receive slot assignment | ☠ channel swap |
| 0x0D | `TDM_CFG4` | transmit pin keeper/fill/offset/edge — the bus-keeper configuration | bus contention on the shared transmit line |
| 0x0E–0x0F | `TDM_CFG5`, `TDM_CFG6` | voltage- and current-sense transmit enable and slot; **both enabled at reset**, at slots 2 and 0 | ☠ every amplifier drives slot 0/2 simultaneously — sense data destroyed |
| 0x10–0x14 | `TDM_CFG7`–`TDM_CFG11` | supply-rail, die-temperature, second-rail, status-byte and gain-reduction transmit slots | telemetry lands in the wrong slot |
| 0x15 | `ICC_CNFG2` | inter-chip pin mode | contention on the inter-chip line |
| 0x16 | `TDM_CFG12` | playback loop-back slot | echo reference lost |
| 0x17–0x18 | `ICLA_CFG0`, `ICLA_CFG1` | inter-chip limiter/brown-out alignment and its slot-enable bitmap | uncoordinated gain across the array |
| 0x19 | `DG_0` | diagnostic generator | benign if left at reset |
| 0x1A | `DVC` | digital volume | ☠ level jumps |
| 0x1B–0x1C | `LIM_CFG0`, `LIM_CFG1` | limiter enable, attack, release, hold | ☠ excursion limiting lost |
| 0x1D–0x34 | `BOP_CFG0`–`BOP_CFG24` | 24-byte brown-out prevention table — supplied per machine as `bop-config` | brown-out response wrong |
| 0x35 | noise-gate configuration | a fixed value published for this part variant | idle behaviour and a reserved bit |
| 0x38 | `DIN_PD` | per-pin weak pull-downs | floating inputs |
| 0x39–0x3A | `IO_DRV0`, `IO_DRV1` | output drive strength on data, clock, interrupt and inter-chip pins; **reset is 8 mA on every pin** | over-driven bus, reflections |
| 0x3B–0x3D, 0x40–0x41 | `INT_MASK0`, `INT_MASK1`, `INT_MASK4`, `INT_MASK2`, `INT_MASK3` | interrupt masks (1 = masked) | ☠ faults silently unreported on a shared line |
| 0x5C | `INT_CLK_CFG` | clock-halt enable and timer, interrupt-pin mode, latch-clear | clock-loss behaviour changes |
| 0x5D | `MISC_CFG3` | interrupt polarity, Y-bridge/bypass shift | wired-OR line polarity wrong |
| 0x60 | `CLOCK_CFG` | manual bit-clock-to-frame-sync ratio | ☠ clock-error fault at start |
| 0x63 | `IDLE_IND` | idle-channel current optimisation | idle current |
| 0x65 | `MISC_CFG4` | load-diagnostic clock source and sense averaging window (5 / 10 / 50 / 100 ms) | telemetry rate wrong |
| 0x67 | `TG_CFG0` | idle-channel hysteresis timer | chatter |
| 0x6A | `LV_EN_CFG` | Class-D / low-voltage-signalling delays | transient behaviour |
| 0x6B | rail-converter mode | a fixed value published for this part variant | rail measurement wrong |
| 0x6B–0x70 | `NG_CFG2`–`NG_CFG7` | extended noise gate | idle behaviour |
| 0x71 | `PVDD_UVLO` | under-voltage threshold, ≈0.219 V per code from 2.2 V | under-voltage trip point wrong |
| 0x76 | DAC modulator reset control | a fixed value published for this part variant | modulator state |

**Page 0x01.** Slot ownership on the shared transmit line: `SDOUT_HIZ_1` … `SDOUT_HIZ_8`
(offsets 0x3D–0x44, a per-slot bitmap over slots 0–63) and `SDOUT_HIZ_9` (0x45, whose top
bit selects "unused slots high-impedance" versus "unused slots driven to zero"). Also the
modulation select at 0x19 and the thermal-detector enable at 0x47, plus the two further
values published for this part variant at 0x33 and 0x37. **☠ Losing the transmit-slot ownership map means
every amplifier on the link drives every slot; on a six-amplifier link that is six drivers
into one wire.** **[Confirmed]** — the ownership map must be programmed on *every* device
on the line before any of them is taken out of shutdown with the sense path enabled.

**Page 0x04.** The 32-bit coefficient block, MSB first across four addresses each:
diagnostic DC level (0x08), limiter maximum, minimum, inflection point and tracking slope
(0x0C, 0x10, 0x14, 0x18), thermal-foldback hold, release rate, slope, temperature threshold
and maximum attenuation (0x1C, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x2C), and the load-diagnostic thresholds
and efficiency coefficients (0x40, 0x44, 0x48). **☠ These are the excursion- and
thermal-protection coefficients; losing them removes the part's autonomous protection.**

**Page 0x06.** A twelve-write, order-sensitive sequence, published for this part variant
and required on it (offsets 0x14–0x19, 0x16 a second time, 0x1B–0x1F, with 0x1A skipped).
Not in the public register map of the counterpart part; restore it in the published
order. **[Confirmed]** that it exists and is order-sensitive;
**[Unknown]** what it does.

**Page 0xFD and the hidden sub-page behind it.** A second-level selector at offset 0x0D
opens a sub-page; the variant writes 0x6C and 0x6D inside it and closes it again. If the
shutdown-sequencing behaviour is in use, the hidden-page bit at 0x64 must additionally be
set before and cleared after **every** transition into shutdown. **[Confirmed]** for the
shape; **[Unknown]** for the semantics.

**Platform-supplied blocks that must be re-applied with the rest.** From the amplifier node
in the platform description (§1.8): `bop-config` (24 bytes, page 0 from 0x1D),
`amp-dcblocker-config`, `amp-tx-zd-config` (the transmit zero-drive / bus-keeper table),
`speaker-config` (the per-device slot map), and the per-unit calibration selected by the
speaker-ID pins. **The speaker-ID pins must be re-sampled after the shutdown line is
released if the calibration set is not cached**, because the pins are on the
application-processor pin controller and are only meaningful once the amplifiers are
enabled. **[Probable]**

**Order within the restore.** Page/book first; then everything except the power mode; then
the transmit-slot ownership map on every device; then the sense enables; then the power
mode last. Raising the power mode before the slot map is programmed on all devices is the
single most damaging ordering error available here. **[Confirmed]**

### 14.3.4 Jack codec — exhaustive restore list

Applies to t8132, t604x, t8142, t605x (CS42L84). **Everything is lost** on a hardware reset,
on a software reset, and at system sleep (`PowerOffAtSleep = 1`). The part has a flat 16-bit
register address space with no paging.

| Group | Registers | Why it must be restored |
|---|---|---|
| Silicon trim / patch | a revision-dependent table of thirteen register/value pairs, plus a small high-capacitance variant set and a trim-data register | applied immediately after reset; without it the analogue blocks are untrimmed. **[Probable]** |
| Global | `FRZ_CTL` (0x0006) | volume updates must be bracketed by its engage bit to be atomic |
| Block enables | `MSM_BLOCK_EN1` (0x1800, carries a **global enable**), `MSM_BLOCK_EN2` (0x1801: serial port, internal bus, DAC, ADC), `MSM_BLOCK_EN3` (0x1802: tip/ring sense, DC impedance detect) | nothing works until these are set, and the global enable gates all of them |
| Clocking | `CCM_CTL1` (0x0600: clock source, band), `CCM_SAMP_RATE` (0x0601), `CCM_CTL3` (0x0602: reference pre-divider, PLL reference source), `CCM_CTL4` (0x0603: reference-clock enable), `CCM_ASP_CLK_CTRL` (0x0608: bit-clock select, inversion, frame-sync alignment, provider/consumer) | ☠ a wrong clock source silently mutes or produces pitch error |
| PLL | `PLL_CTL1` (0x0800: mode, enable), `PLL_DIV_FRAC0/1/2` (0x0804–0x0806), `PLL_DIV_INT` (0x0807), `PLL_DIVOUT` (0x0808) | PLL will not lock |
| Serial port framing | `ASP_CTL` (0x5000: TDM mode, bit-clock enable, frame-sync enable, two-frame-sync modes), `ASP_FSYNC_CTL2/3` (0x5010, 0x5011: 12-bit frame period), `ASP_DATA_CTL` (0x5018: transmit high-impedance delay and enable, per-slot high-impedance enable, frame-start phase and delay) | ☠ wrong framing drives data into the wrong slot |
| Serial port channels | `ASP_RX_EN` (0x5020), `ASP_TX_EN` (0x5024), and the slot-start / edge / width triplets at 0x5028–0x502A, 0x502C–0x502E, 0x5068–0x506A, 0x506C–0x506E | channel swap or silence |
| Routing | `BUS_ASP_TX_SRC` (0x4000), `BUS_DAC_SRC` (0x4001) | capture and playback paths disconnected |
| DAC and headphone | `DAC_CTL1` (0x3000: unmute), `DAC_CTL2` (0x3001), `DAC_CHA_VOL_LSB/MSB` (0x3004/0x3005), `DAC_CHB_VOL_LSB/MSB` (0x3006/0x3007), `HP_VOL_CTL` (0x3020: **soft-ramp** and **zero-cross** policy), plus the headphone load select / capacitive-load / high-voltage-enable control, the output pull-down control, the full-scale compensation control and the charge-pump reference trim | ☠ a lost volume setting is a full-scale headphone output into someone's ears; a lost ramp/zero-cross policy is an audible click on every gain change |
| Output clamps | the headphone clamp override control, the headphone force control, and the ground noise-suppression clamp disable (`HS_CLAMP_DISABLE`, 0x1813) | pops on transitions |
| Supply filter | the FILT+ charge/discharge control (clamped / unclamped) | pop at power-down; incorrect charge at power-up |
| ADC | `ADC_CTL1` (0x2000: pre-amplifier gain 0/10/20 dB, PGA gain −12.0…0.0 dB in 0.5 dB steps), `ADC_CTL2`, `ADC_CTL4` (0x2003: wind-noise and high-pass filters) | capture level and filtering |
| Pad electrical | the serial-data-out and I2C data slew-rate controls | bus integrity |
| Jack detection | `TIP_SENSE_CTL` (0x1283) and `RING_SENSE_CTL` (0x1282) polarity and rise/fall debounce, `TIP_SENSE_CTL2` (0x1473), `MISC_DET_CTL` (0x1474: detect mode, bias control, level-detect power-down), `MIC_DET_CTL1` (0x1475: presence threshold), `MIC_DET_CTL4` (0x1477: latch-to-supply-domain), `HS_DET_CTL2` (0x1811), `HS_SWITCH_CTL` (0x1812: the eight-switch analogue matrix), the headset-bias sense/clamp autocontrol with its tip-sense enable, and the DC-impedance-detect control and force registers | **the jack state read before the detection block is reconfigured is meaningless**; a wrong switch matrix can bias the wrong contact |
| Interrupts | `TSRS_PLUG_INT_MASK` (0x0418) and the headset-detect interrupt masks | plug events lost, or a level-triggered line left asserted |

**[Confirmed]** for the registers in the public map; **[Probable]** for the additional
groups (trim table, global enable, FILT+ control, clamp/force controls, full-scale
compensation, charge-pump trim, pad slew, DC-impedance block), which are established as
existing but whose exact addresses are **[Unknown]** publicly.

**One ordering rule inside the restore, inherited from the family and still load-bearing:**
the register that latches the analogue controls into the always-powered supply domain must
be written **first**, before the rest of the replay, or the sticky registers in that domain
do not latch. **[Probable]**

On t8140 the part is a CS42L83, whose register map is the public CS42L42 map; the same
principle applies with that map's register set, including the soft-ramp rate register
(0x100A), the slow-start enable (0x100B), the three power-control registers (0x1101–0x1103)
and the full jack-detection group on pages 0x11 and 0x1B. **[Probable]**
