## 14.4 Ordering constraints

### 14.4.1 What the clocking and serialiser hardware require

Bringing a stream up or down touches six things, in three configure/enable pairs:

| Stage | What it touches |
|---|---|
| configure master clock | the cluster's master-clock source multiplexer and divider |
| configure sync clocks | the frame-sync generator: source, edge, pulse length, phase counts |
| enable master clock | the cluster master-clock gate |
| enable sync clocks | the frame-sync generator output |
| configure data | serialiser slot masks, widths, polarity, data delay; DMA-agent channel count and mode |
| start data | the serialiser enable |

The ordering relations the hardware forces, each with its reason:

| # | Constraint | Hardware reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Configure the master clock before opening its gate | A clock generator must be configured before its gate is opened, or the first edges are at the wrong rate |
| 2 | Configure the frame-sync generator before enabling its output | The same: an unconfigured generator emits a frame pulse at the wrong length and phase, and the first frame of a stream is already carrying data |
| 3 | Master clock running before the frame-sync output is enabled | The frame-sync generator divides the master clock; with the master gate shut it has no edges to divide and emits no frame |
| 4 | Frame-sync generator running before any serialiser is enabled — this step can never be skipped | A serialiser has no other frame reference; enabled without one it latches indeterminate data and drives the link at arbitrary slot boundaries |
| 5 | Serialiser slot geometry configured before the serialiser is enabled | An enabled serialiser with the wrong slot mask drives slots another device on the same link owns, which is a contention on a shared pin |
| 6 | At teardown, remove the frame clock before the master clock | The inverse of 4: a serialiser clocked without a frame reference latches indeterminate data |

**[Inferred]** for the reasons; **[Probable]** for the constraints themselves.

A full bring-up that satisfies all six is:

```
1. configure master clock
2. configure sync clocks
3. enable master clock
4. enable sync clocks
5. configure data
6. start data
```

and the matching teardown:

```
1. stop data
2. deconfigure data
3. disable sync clocks
4. disable master clock
5. deconfigure sync clocks
6. deconfigure master clock
```

Two orderings in those two listings do **not** follow from the constraints above,
and whether the hardware requires them is **[Unknown]**: that *both* configure
stages precede *either* enable stage, and that on teardown the deconfigure
stages trail after both gates are shut. See Open question 17.

Around these stages the power-manager domains for the stream are raised before the
first stage and lowered after the last: each of the stream's power-manager cells is
raised by writing its target level and polling the actual-level field until it matches
(§2.6.1). **[Probable]** — cross-reference §2.6.1 for the register and §2.6.4 for the
tree.

### 14.4.2 Stream start

Host steps are marked **H**, coprocessor requests **C**.

| # | Step | Hardware reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **H** Ensure the I2C controller for the amplifier bus (and, on Pro/Max dies, both buses) is clocked and reset | the amplifiers are unreachable otherwise, and they must be programmed before clocks start |
| 2 | **H** Deassert the shared shutdown line if it is asserted; wait **≥ 1 ms** | the parts do not acknowledge their I2C addresses while asserted; the counterpart's published flow waits 1000–2000 µs at exactly this point |
| 3 | **H** Software-reset each amplifier; wait **1–2 ms** | known starting state |
| 4 | **H** Restore the full amplifier register file (§14.3.3) **except** the power mode, with the transmit-slot ownership map programmed on **every** device on the link before any sense enable | ☠ contention on the shared transmit line |
| 5 | **H** Unmask amplifier interrupt sources, then unmask the shared line at the pin controller | a device that faults before its mask is set will assert a line nobody is listening on |
| 6 | **C** Request the stream endpoint's power-on | the endpoint's power providers must be satisfied first — see §14.8.3 |
| 7 | **C** The coprocessor-side control path raises the stream's power-manager cells, then runs stages 1–4 of §14.4.1: configure master clock, configure sync clocks, enable master clock, enable sync clocks | the bit and frame clocks must be running before any codec is unmuted |
| 8 | **H** Configure the DMA channel: bus width, staging carveout, FIFO threshold and limit, interrupt masks; reset the rings | channel state was not retained (§14.3.2) |
| 9 | **C** The coprocessor-side control path runs stages 5–6: configure data, start data | the serialiser must be armed before data flows |
| 10 | **H** Submit descriptors and start the channel (`TX_START` / `RX_START`) | |
| 11 | **H** Take the amplifiers out of shutdown: power mode → active-with-mute, then active-without-mute | the DAC is powered by the with-mute state; clearing mute after it is what avoids the click |
| 12 | **H** (jack path) With the bit clock already running: enable the codec's reference clock, start and lock its PLL if used, switch its clock source, then unmute | the clock-source switch logic requires the PLL to be running; the part must not be unmuted before its clock is stable |

Two constraints that are **not** negotiable:

- **The bit clock must be running before any amplifier leaves shutdown** and must keep
  running for as long as any amplifier is out of shutdown. See §14.5.2.
- **Nothing may unmute before the transmit-slot ownership map is programmed on every device
  on the link.** **[Confirmed]**

Confidence: **[Probable]** for the interleave as a whole; **[Confirmed]** for steps 2, 4,
5, 11 and for the ordering relations of §14.4.1.

### 14.4.3 Stream stop

| # | Step | Hardware reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **H** (jack path) Mute the codec DAC | mute before the clock goes away |
| 2 | **H** Mute the amplifiers: power mode → active-with-mute; **wait 6–7 ms** for the output ramp | the ramp is the pop suppression; the clocks must still be running throughout it |
| 3 | **H** Amplifiers → software shutdown; **wait a further 2–3 ms** | the DAC is shut down after the ramp has completed |
| 4 | **H** Stop the DMA channel (`TX_STOP` / `RX_STOP`), then pulse the channel's ring reset | a channel must be stopped before it is deactivated |
| 5 | **C** Request the stream's stop; the coprocessor-side control path runs the teardown sequence of §14.4.1 | data stops before clocks; sync clocks before master clock |
| 6 | **H** (jack path) Disconnect the codec's PLL **before** stopping it: switch the clock source back to the internal oscillator, wait **150–300 µs**, clear the PLL enable, then clear the reference-clock enable | doing this in the wrong order is an explicit hazard on this family |
| 7 | **C** Request the endpoint's idle state; the coprocessor-side control path drops the stream's power cells | |
| 8 | **H** Release the latency-tolerance vote | |

**The shared shutdown line is *not* asserted at stop.** It is shared by every amplifier in
the machine, so asserting it stops audio on links that are still running. It is a
system-sleep and recovery operation only. **[Confirmed]** — unchanged from the baseline.

**Port-clock release rule, inherited:** a port's clock source is released only when *both*
directions on that port have stopped. On these SoCs the release is performed by the control
path, not the host, but a host that stops only the playback direction of a link that also
carries sense capture must expect the clocks to keep running. **[Probable]**

Confidence: **[Confirmed]** for steps 2, 3 and 6 and their delays; **[Probable]** for the
interleave.

### 14.4.4 System suspend

| # | Step | Hardware reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **H** Stop every audio stream by §14.4.3 | nothing may be mid-transfer |
| 2 | **H** Mask the amplifier and jack interrupt lines at the pin controller | the pins are on the application-processor controller and are not wake-capable (§5.5.4); an unmasked level-triggered line can block entry |
| 3 | **H** Amplifiers: write software shutdown | ramp already completed at step 1 |
| 4 | **H** **Assert the shared shutdown line**; allow **≥ 6 ms** before anything else touches the amplifier rails | the counterpart's published suspend flow waits 6–7 ms here |
| 5 | **H** Mark every amplifier's cached register image invalid | all register state is now lost (§14.3.3) |
| 6 | **H** Jack codec: restore the interrupt masks and the presence-threshold register to their power-on values, mute both analogue outputs and the mixer, disable the receive path and the serial-port clock, clear the headset-detect control, assert the global power-down, wait for the power-down to complete, engage the supply-filter discharge, then assert the reset line | `PowerOffAtSleep = 1` requires a full power-down, and the supply-filter discharge is the pop suppression for it |
| 7 | **H** Bring every DMA channel to the suspended power state | the controller's state ladder requires *idle → sleep*, and resume re-enters at *initialising* |
| 8 | **C** Tell the coprocessor the host is entering sleep | the coprocessor keeps running; see §14.8 |
| 9 | **H** Release the I2C controller clock gates | nothing left on those buses needs servicing |

**Never** take the coprocessor to its off state as part of this (§14.8.1). **[Confirmed]**

The audio IOMMU is **not** touched: it carries `no-sleep` and must stay up so the
coprocessor can keep transferring for the low-power microphone and voice-trigger paths.
**[Confirmed]** for the flag; **[Inferred]** for the instruction.

Confidence: **[Probable]** overall; **[Confirmed]** for steps 4, 5, 6 and the IOMMU rule.

### 14.4.5 System resume

| # | Step | Hardware reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **H** Re-gate and reset the I2C controllers; reapply bus speed and timing tunables | all controller state was lost with the gate |
| 2 | **H** (t8140 only) Ask the system-management controller to re-enable the microphone-array supply (line index 0x19) if capture is wanted | §6.9; the supply is not a GPIO |
| 3 | **H** Release the jack codec reset; wait **3 ms** for its internal boot | the part does not answer on I2C before this |
| 4 | **H** Write the codec's supply-domain latch control first, then replay the whole register file of §14.3.4, ending with the jack-detection configuration | the sticky registers in the always-powered domain do not latch otherwise; the jack state is not trustworthy until detection is reconfigured |
| 5 | **H** Deassert the shared shutdown line; wait **≥ 1 ms** | amplifiers answer on I2C only after this |
| 6 | **H** Software-reset each amplifier, wait **1–2 ms**, replay the entire register file (§14.3.3), then restore the power mode last | reset gives a known state; the analogue level register comes back at its maximum and must be corrected before the part is unmuted |
| 7 | **H** Re-sample the speaker-ID pins if the calibration set is not cached, and select the matching calibration | the pins are only meaningful with the amplifiers enabled |
| 8 | **H** Re-initialise every DMA channel from the *initialising* state: re-read the staging-memory sizes, re-allocate carveouts, reprogram bus width, FIFO and masks, reset rings | the channel does not return to *idle* directly out of *sleep* |
| 9 | **C** Re-establish the audio service session and re-open any endpoint that was open | the coprocessor's endpoint state is not the host's to assume |
| 10 | **H** Unmask the jack and amplifier interrupt lines, then read and clear each amplifier's latched status | events that occurred across the transition are latched; a level-triggered shared line stays asserted until every device is cleared |

**Known resume defect carried over from the baseline:** after system resume the
current/voltage sense capture stream can come back broken in a way that is only cleared by
tearing the capture path down and reopening it rather than by the normal resume path. What
hardware state is not restored is **[Unknown]**. Because the sense stream is what keeps the
speakers safe, a driver must verify sense data is live after resume before allowing
playback above a conservative limit. **☠ [Confirmed]** that the defect exists on the
baseline; **[Unknown]** whether it persists on M4 and later.

Confidence: **[Probable]** overall; **[Confirmed]** for steps 3, 5, 6 and their delays.

### 14.4.6 Interleaving with the coprocessor — what the host may and may not do

| Host action | Safe while the coprocessor owns the link? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Program amplifier or jack-codec registers over I2C | **yes** — but see below | those buses are host-owned on every in-scope board (§6.3) |
| Start or stop a host DMA channel | **yes** | the DMA controllers are host-owned |
| Change the amplifier's power mode or mute | **yes**, provided the bit clock is running | §14.5.2 |
| Change the amplifier's slot map or sample-rate code while the link is running | **no** | the part faults on a ratio or frame-rate change while out of shutdown |
| Write any serial-audio, clock-generator or frame-sync register | **no** | there is no arbitration primitive of any kind; the coprocessor reprograms these on its own schedule, including at power transitions (§3.5) |
| Write any audio power-state register | **no** | every audio domain is flagged as having no host power-state register; on t604x, t8142 and t605x no address exists at all |
| Assert the shared shutdown line while a coprocessor-owned link is running | **no** | it silences every amplifier in the machine and destroys their register state |

**[Confirmed]** for the two "no" rows about power and arbitration; **[Probable]** for the
rest.

**The request/response shape the host must use.** The coprocessor-side control path exposes, per endpoint, a
power-state request carrying a target state and a direction, and a readable current state;
transitions are asynchronous and the request may complete later. Endpoints additionally
have an explicit idle request distinct from a power-off. A host driver must therefore treat
every stop and suspend step that crosses the boundary as a request-and-wait, not a
register write. **[Probable]** — cross-reference §11 for the transport.

### 14.4.7 Power-domain ordering

Unchanged in principle from §2.6.4 and reproduced here only as the dependency that governs
the order of everything above: `AUDIO_A` → `AUDIO_FR` → {`AUDIO_P` → {DMA aggregates,
`AUDIO_LEAP_MCA`, `AUDIO_MCA0_M`…`AUDIO_MCA5_M`}, `AUDIO_LEAP_A` → `AUDIO_LEAP_C` → {its
DMA aggregates, `AUDIO_LEAP_RX0`…`RX4`, `AUDIO_LEAP_TX0`}, `AUDIO_SENSE_PDMC`}, with
`PDM0_AUDIO_REF` and `PDM1_AUDIO_REF` as independent roots. Power-down is the exact
reverse. The island root's parent is `AOP_FILTER` on t8132, t604x, t8140 and t605x, and
**`AOP_DART` on t8142** — a driver that walks the chain must not assume the root name.
**[Confirmed]**

## 14.5 Runtime idle behaviour

### 14.5.1 What may be gated while a stream is open but silent

| Item | May be gated? | Note |
|---|---|---|
| DMA channel | **yes** | stop and restart is supported; the channel's configuration must survive or be rewritten (§14.5.4) |
| Serialiser data enable | **yes** | stopping the serialiser leaves the port clocks running if another direction or cluster drives them |
| Frame-sync generator output | **no**, while any amplifier on the link is out of shutdown | §14.5.2 |
| Cluster master clock (`AUDIO_MCAn_M`) | **no**, while the cluster drives any active port | the cell gates the clock the whole cluster derives from |
| `AUDIO_P`, `AUDIO_FR`, `AUDIO_A` | **no**, while any link is up | ancestors of everything |
| Jack-codec bit clock | **no**, while the codec's clock source is the link bit clock | every in-scope board sets `internal-mclk-src = 1`; stopping the bit clock unlocks the codec |
| Latency-tolerance vote | **yes** | release it when no channel is transferring |
| Audio IOMMU | **no** | `no-sleep`; other consumers depend on it |

**[Inferred]** except where a cross-referenced section makes it **[Confirmed]**.

The serialiser's transmit configuration word carries a **"disable output when idle"** bit,
and the two slot masks — "slots this unit fills" and "slots this unit owns" — are
programmed independently. A link can therefore be silent without releasing the bus. **Muting
is a data-domain operation and never requires stopping a clock.** **[Confirmed]** (§2.7.1).

### 14.5.2 The amplifier's clock-loss fault — the hazard that governs idle

The Apple-variant amplifier's public counterpart raises a **TDM clock error** on any of
three conditions: an invalid bit-clock-to-frame-sync ratio, the frame rate changing on the
fly, or the ratio changing on the fly. The autonomous response is a software shutdown after
the clock-halt timer expires, and optionally a full power-down if the clock-error
power-enable bit is set. The detector can be disabled, and the latched flag is **masked at
reset**, so a driver that has not unmasked it will see the part shut itself down with no
interrupt. **[Confirmed]** — public datasheet plus the fault table of the baseline.

Therefore:

- **Do not stop the bit clock while any amplifier on that link is out of software
  shutdown.** Mute in the data domain instead.
- **Do not re-rate the link while any amplifier on it is out of shutdown.** Mute, wait the
  ramp, shut down, re-rate, reprogram the sample-rate code, then bring the parts back up.
- The clock-halt timer (2 / 4 / 6 / 23.8 ms range on the shutdown-pin timeout field; the
  clock-halt timer is a separate three-bit field) sets how long a clock dropout is
  tolerated before the part shuts itself down. Its value on these machines is
  **[Unknown]**.
- The part also reports the **detected** ratio and rate in a read-only clock-configuration
  register — a cheap way to verify the link before unmuting. **[Confirmed]**

The coprocessor-side control path independently validates the bit-clock-to-frame-sync ratio and refuses an
unsupported one, so a request that would produce a clock error is rejected before it
reaches the hardware. **[Confirmed]** (§2.7.1).

**On t8140** the amplifier has no clock-error fault to raise, but its digital input going
idle puts it into standby and toggling brings it out — so clock changes there are an
audible-transient problem rather than a fault problem. **[Probable]**

### 14.5.3 The jack codec while idle

- The codec's only clock source on every in-scope board is the link bit clock
  (`internal-mclk-src = 1`). Stopping it unlocks the part; the recovery is a reference-clock
  re-enable, a PLL re-lock (polled every **250 µs** for up to **1250 µs**) and a
  **150 µs** glitchless source switch. **[Confirmed]**
- The block enables are independent, so the DAC or ADC may be powered down while the serial
  port and internal bus stay enabled. **[Probable]**
- **A constraint inherited from the family:** the PLL must not be started with both the ADC
  and the headphone blocks powered down, or the supply filter does not charge correctly. At
  least one of them must be up before the PLL is enabled. **[Confirmed]**
- Jack detection continues to work with the audio path idle, provided the detection block
  and the tip/ring sense block remain enabled.

### 14.5.4 DMA channel state that must be preserved while idle

A channel that is stopped but still allocated must keep:

| State | Why |
|---|---|
| Staging-memory carveout base and size | carveouts must remain non-overlapping across all channels of the same direction; releasing one and reallocating it while another channel is live corrupts that channel |
| Bus width (word size and words-per-frame) | must match the link's frame geometry when restarted |
| FIFO threshold and limit | restart behaviour depends on them |
| Per-channel interrupt masks | an unmasked ring error on restart is the only signal of a stale ring |
| Overflow/underflow counters | the only accounting handle available; cleared only by the explicit counter-clear control |

Ring contents are **not** preserved: a stop-and-ring-reset leaves an empty ring and
re-submission starts from empty. **[Confirmed]** — baseline register semantics.

The **descriptor repeat flag** must be used with care: its latching misbehaviour is cleared
only by a full power-domain reset, and on these SoCs the host has no such reset (§14.2.1).
**☠ [Confirmed]** for the premise; **[Inferred]** for the consequence.

### 14.5.5 Coprocessor-side idle levels

The low-power capture path retains the baseline's three-level model: an idle level, an
intermediate level in which the DMA block is powered but not capturing, and a capturing
level. The intermediate level exists precisely so the DMA engine can be programmed before
capture starts. **[Probable]** — unchanged. Per-endpoint the coprocessor-side control path exposes an
explicit idle request distinct from power-off, and the always-listening client-manager
device (`compatible = "iop-audio,client-manager-device"`, node `siri-listening-device`)
carries its own power state with policies for powering down when its last client closes and
for powering down ahead of system sleep. **[Probable]**

A hardware-triggered microphone disable exists in the audio reference-clock domain's global
block, with separate address/data pairs for the disable and enable actions, separate
hardware-trigger enables for each, and a software-control override. It is independent of
host power state and is not affected by host suspend. **[Probable]** — cross-reference
§12.

## 14.6 Pop and click suppression

### 14.6.1 The mechanisms available, per part

| Part | Mechanisms |
|---|---|
| Apple-variant TAS2764 amplifier | output mute ramp (fixed duration, ≈6–7 ms), digital-volume ramp rate (`MISC_CFG2[3:2]`, four settings), spread-spectrum/edge-rate controls affecting switching transients, the shutdown-pin mode (immediate versus timed) |
| MAX98360 amplifier (t8140) | a volume ramp inside the part on enable and disable (13 ms on the C/D variants), plus a coprocessor-performed digital ramp-down |
| CS42L84 jack codec | headphone volume update policy — **soft ramp** and **zero-cross** — a freeze bracket for atomic multi-register volume updates, output clamp override and force controls, an output pull-down, and a supply-filter discharge control |
| CS42L83 jack codec (t8140) | the same family mechanisms: soft-ramp rate register, slow-start enable, analogue headphone mutes, supply-filter discharge |
| Coprocessor-side control path | a mute/unmute ramp engine, §14.6.4 |

### 14.6.2 Delay table

Every value below is a hardware requirement, not a software convenience. Units are as
written.

| Event | Sequence | Delay | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amplifier out of hardware shutdown, before first I2C | deassert line | **≥ 1 ms** (counterpart's published flow: 1000–2000 µs) | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier software reset | write the reset bit | **1–2 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier shutdown-line cycle, to force a clean state | assert, hold, deassert | **≥ 10 ms** asserted on these machines; the counterpart's published flow uses **20 ms**. Use 20 ms | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier un-mute | power mode → active-with-mute (powers the DAC), then active-without-mute | none between them | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier mute | power mode → active-with-mute | **wait 6–7 ms** for the output ramp | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier DAC shutdown after mute | power mode → software shutdown | **wait a further 2–3 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier suspend | software shutdown, line asserted, rails off | **wait 6–7 ms** after | **[Confirmed]** |
| Amplifier shutdown-pin timeout field | `MISC_CFG2[5:4]` | **2 / 4 / 6 / 23.8 ms**, reset = 6 ms | **[Confirmed]** |
| **t8140 amplifier: ramp settle before the enable line may drop** | ramp/silence the stream first | **20 ms** (`mute-ramp-sleep-ms = 0x14`) | **[Confirmed]** |
| t8140 amplifier turn-on, A/B variants | enable line high | ≈**1 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| t8140 amplifier volume ramp, C/D variants | enable and disable | **13 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec reset pulse | assert, hold, release | **10–500 µs** low | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec after reset release | internal boot | **3 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec clock-source switch | glitchless switch | **150 µs** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec PLL lock | poll / timeout | **250 µs** / **1250 µs** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec PLL disconnect before stop | source back to internal oscillator, then wait | **150–300 µs** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec headphone / ADC enable settle | after the block powers up | **20 ms** | **[Confirmed]** (CS42L42 family) |
| Jack codec global power-down | fixed wait, then poll | **65 ms** fixed, then poll every **1 ms** up to **235 ms** | **[Confirmed]** (CS42L42 family) |
| Jack codec headset-type detection dwell | two dwell periods | **50 ms** each (CS42L84) / **100 ms** per comparator step (CS42L83) | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec headset-bias ramp to stable | per ramp setting | ≈**0.01 / 14 / 36 / 65 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Jack codec button-detect debounce | initial / per event | **100 ms** / **10 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Tip-sense debounce (CS42L84) | rise / fall | **250 ms** / **125 ms** at the settings these machines use | **[Probable]** |
| Ring-sense debounce (CS42L84) | rise | up to **1.0 s** at the settings these machines use | **[Probable]** |
| Microphone array turn-on / settle (t8140) | platform parameters | **20 ms** / **50 ms** | **[Confirmed]** |
| Serialiser reset self-clear | assert, wait, verify | **25 µs** (upstream) or **50 µs** (Asahi variant); observed clear ≈**1 µs** | **[Confirmed]** on the baseline; **[Unknown]** on M4+ — the host never performs it |
| Pre-DMA-start settle after frame-sync source reprogramming | before starting the channel | **100 µs** | **[Confirmed]** on the baseline; **[Unknown]** on M4+ |
| Power-manager state-change poll | target written, actual polled | no absolute time published; poll to a bounded iteration count | **[Confirmed]** |

### 14.6.3 The t8140 machine, decoded

`/arm-io/iop-audio-controller/audio-speaker` on j700 carries exactly four power-relevant
properties, and no other in-scope board carries any of them:

| Property | Raw | Decode |
|---|---|---|
| `mute-ramp-sleep-ms` | `0x14000000` (u32 = 20) | **20 ms**: the time the host must wait after the stream has been silenced or ramped, before the amplifier enable line may be dropped |
| `enable-iop-ramp-down` | zero-length (a flag) | the **digital ramp-down is performed by the coprocessor-side stream**, not by the host and not by the amplifier. Its presence is what makes the 20 ms wait a wait on the coprocessor rather than on the part |
| `function-reset` | phandle → application-processor pin controller, tag `GPIO`, pin `0x69` (105), flags `0x00010001` | the amplifier's **enable** line, host-driven output, logical 1 = enabled |
| `num-channels` | `2` | two amplifier channels gated by that one line |

**[Confirmed]** — byte-exact on j700 and absent on every other in-scope board.

The resulting sequences:

**Power-up:** drive the enable line high → wait **≥ 20 ms** (covers the ≈1 ms A/B turn-on
and the 13 ms C/D ramp with margin) → unmute the stream. **[Probable]**

**Power-down:** request the coprocessor ramp-down (or silence the stream) → wait **20 ms**
→ drive the enable line low. **[Confirmed]**

**Mute / unmute:** entirely a data-domain operation on the coprocessor side; the enable line
is not used for muting, because dropping it costs the full 20 ms each way.
**[Inferred]**

### 14.6.4 The coprocessor-side control path's mute/unmute ramp engine

Beyond the per-part mechanisms, the coprocessor-side stream carries a programmable
mute/unmute ramp with **four parameters**, each a 32-bit value written into a parameter
block at a configured offset:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Mute hold-off delay | delay between the mute request and the start of the ramp |
| Mute ramp time increment | per-step increment governing the ramp-down rate |
| Unmute hold-off delay | delay between the unmute request and the start of the ramp |
| Unmute ramp time increment | per-step increment governing the ramp-up rate |

**[Probable]** that the engine exists with exactly these four parameters. **[Unknown]**
their units, their scaling, and the values configured on any in-scope machine. This is the
mechanism `enable-iop-ramp-down` turns on for the t8140 speaker path; whether it is also
used, unconditionally, on the machines with the Apple-variant amplifier is **[Unknown]** —
none of those boards carries the flag, so either the ramp is unconditional there or the
part's own 6–7 ms ramp is relied upon instead.

### 14.6.5 Jack insertion and removal

Insertion and removal are the only pop/click events the host does not initiate, so the
suppression must already be configured before they happen.

**On insertion:**

1. The tip-sense debounce elapses (**250 ms** at the setting these machines use) and the
   plug interrupt is raised. Ring-sense events are masked until a tip insertion has been
   processed, so that ring transitions are only considered when they can be meaningful.
   **[Probable]**
2. The analogue switch matrix and the headset bias are configured **before** the bias is
   applied, so that the bias is never applied to a contact that is about to be reassigned.
   **[Probable]**
3. The headset bias ramps at the configured rate (≈0.01 / 14 / 36 / 65 ms).
4. Headset-type detection runs — two dwell periods of **50 ms** on CS42L84, **100 ms** per
   comparator step on CS42L83. On the in-scope CS42L84 machines a DC impedance detection
   block is additionally enabled (`enable-dcid = 1` on every in-scope jack codec node) and
   its measurement must complete before the output is configured. **[Confirmed]** for the
   property; **[Probable]** for the sequencing.
5. Only then: set the volume to a safe value, set the ramp/zero-cross policy, unmute.
   **☠ Unmuting before the volume is restored is a full-scale headphone output.**

**On removal:**

1. The unplug interrupt is raised after the fall debounce (**125 ms**).
2. Mute the DAC in the data domain first.
3. Engage the output clamps / pull-down before removing the bias, and discharge the supply
   filter, so that the contact does not see a step. **[Probable]**
4. Re-arm the detection block and mask the ring-sense events again.

**Ring-sense polarity.** Every in-scope board carries `enable-ringsense = 1` **and**
`ringsense-inverted = 1`, and every board carries `mic-config = {0x0001, 0xffff, 0xffff}`
and `bits-per-sample-subset = 24`. A driver that gets the ring-sense inversion wrong will
see plug and unplug exchanged and will bias the wrong contact. **[Confirmed]** — identical
on every jack-codec-bearing in-scope board.

---

## 14.7 The shared shutdown line in power sequencing

**What it is.** One host-driven output on the application-processor pin controller, going
to the shutdown pin of **every** amplifier in the machine, including amplifiers on a
different I2C bus. Pin numbers: t8132 `0x0f` (15), t604x `0x36` (54), t8142 `0x97` (151),
t605x `0x6b` (107), t8140 `0x69` (105 — there it is an enable line for a part with no
registers). Flags `0x00010001` on every board; logical 1 = amplifier operating.
**[Confirmed]** (§6.5).

**When it may be asserted:**

| Situation | Assert? |
|---|---|
| System suspend, after every amplifier has been muted, ramped and software-shut-down | **yes** — this is its intended use |
| Recovery from an amplifier that is unresponsive or has latched a fault that survives a software reset | **yes**, but it is machine-wide: stop every link first |
| Driver shutdown / unload | yes, with the same preconditions |
| Stream stop | **no** — other links may still be running |
| Runtime idle | **no** — unchanged from the baseline, which never deasserts it at runtime for exactly this reason |
| While any link on any bus is streaming | **no** |

**[Confirmed]** for the first and last rows; **[Probable]** for the rest.

**What is lost when it is asserted.** The complete register file of **every** amplifier in
the machine — the public counterpart specifies the register file as undefined after a
shutdown-pin low period. That includes, and this is the part that matters:

- the analogue output level, which returns to its **maximum (21 dBV)**; **☠**
- the digital volume;
- the limiter and brown-out configuration and the page-4 protection coefficients; **☠**
- **the transmit-slot ownership map on page 1 and the sense transmit enables and slots,
  which return to enabled at slots 0 and 2 on every device** — i.e. after an assertion,
  every amplifier on the link is configured to drive the same two slots; **☠**
- the interrupt masks;
- the sample-rate code and the frame configuration;
- the pin drive strengths;
- every Apple-variant deviation write on pages 0, 1, 4, 6 and 0xFD.

**[Confirmed]**

**What must be reprogrammed afterwards.** Everything in §14.3.3, on **every** amplifier in
the machine, in the order given there — page/book, then all configuration, then the
transmit-slot ownership map on every device, then the sense enables, then the power mode.
Plus: re-sample the speaker-ID pins if the calibration selection was not cached, and
re-read each part's latched status registers and issue the latch-clear so the shared
interrupt line starts from a clean state.

**Hold and settle times.** Assert for **≥ 10 ms** (use **20 ms** to match the counterpart's
published flow) when cycling it deliberately; after deassertion wait **≥ 1 ms** before the
first I2C transaction; after the software reset that should follow, a further **1–2 ms**;
after asserting it at suspend, **≥ 6 ms** before rails are touched. **[Confirmed]**

**There is no second reset.** The public counterpart has a hardware reset pin distinct from
the shutdown pin, but no in-scope board declares a second GPIO for the amplifiers. The
shutdown line plus the software-reset register are the whole toolkit. **[Confirmed]**

**Boot-firmware interaction.** Every in-scope board — and every baseline board — carries
`iboot-audio-volume` (a valueless flag) on amplifier index 0, meaning boot firmware plays
audio through the speakers before the host driver runs. **At handoff the shutdown line may
already be deasserted and the amplifiers may already be configured and running by another
agent.** A host driver must not assume a cold part: read the identity register, and either
adopt the existing configuration or cycle the line deliberately and reprogram from scratch.
**[Confirmed]** for the property; **[Inferred]** for the consequence.

---

## 14.8 The coprocessor's own power states and their relation to the audio domains

### 14.8.1 The states

The management interface carries a power-state value in both directions, with an
acknowledgement. The state set is unchanged from the baseline:

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `0x0000` | off | powered off; **cannot be restarted** |
| `0x0001` | sleep | sleeping, restartable |
| `0x0010` | quiesced | running, no communication |
| `0x0020` | on | normal operation |
| `0x0201` | idle | sleeping, state retained |
| `0x0220` | init | initial state after the processor is released |

The running check compares only the low byte against `0x20`. **[Confirmed]** — baseline;
**[Unknown]** whether the upper bits of `0x201` and `0x220` mean anything, and **[Unknown]**
whether the value set is unchanged on M4-and-later firmware.

**The `0x0000` state is a one-way door and every in-scope SoC except t604x now says so in
the platform description** (`no-shutdown = 1`, §14.2.5). Never use it.

Transition sequences, unchanged from the baseline: shutdown is host → quiesced then
coprocessor → sleep; idle is host → idle, coprocessor → idle; quiesce is host → quiesced,
coprocessor → quiesced followed by re-initialisation; wake from idle or quiesced is
coprocessor → init followed by the whole boot handshake. Each wait is bounded at 1000 ms.
**[Confirmed]** on the baseline; **[Probable]** on M4 and later.

### 14.8.2 Relation to the audio power domains

- **The audio power tree is rooted inside the coprocessor island on every in-scope SoC.**
  `AUDIO_A`'s parent is `AOP_FILTER` (t8132, t604x, t8140, t605x) or **`AOP_DART`**
  (t8142). On M1–M3 the equivalent domain's parent was the host serial-I/O domain.
  **[Confirmed]**
- **Consequence 1:** audio can run with the application processor asleep. The low-power
  microphone and voice-trigger paths depend on exactly this.
- **Consequence 2:** the host cannot power the audio block down by releasing its own
  domains, because it holds none. Releasing the last stream is a *request*, and whether the
  island actually drops is the coprocessor's decision.
- **Consequence 3:** on **t8142** the audio island's root is the coprocessor's **IOMMU**
  domain. Taking that IOMMU down there takes the entire audio island with it — which is
  consistent with the IOMMU's `no-sleep` flag and makes that flag load-bearing rather than
  an optimisation. **[Inferred]**
- **Consequence 4:** the coprocessor drives the audio power-manager devices itself,
  addressing each cluster master-clock cell and the low-power cluster cell by index,
  writing a target level and polling the actual level until it matches. A host that writes
  the same registers — possible on t8132, t8140 and t8142, where the addresses are
  derivable — races that loop. **[Probable]**
- **Performance states.** On **t8132 only**, six audio domains are performance-managed. The
  island's internal clock frequency therefore changes under the coprocessor's control on
  that SoC and a driver must not assume a fixed internal rate. On t604x, t8140, t8142 and
  t605x no audio domain is performance-managed. **[Confirmed]**

### 14.8.3 The named external power providers

Three distinct power-dependency declarations appear on the audio controller and its
children, and they mean different things:

| Declaration | Where | Value | Present on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `external-power-provider` (phandle) + `function-admac_powerswitch` (tag `CSPa`) | each stream endpoint under `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` | phandle of that endpoint's DMA controller node — `admac-base-ns` for base-domain links, `admac-leap-ns` for low-power links | **t8132, t604x** |
| `external-named-power-provider` (string) | `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller` | `HibernationAppUntrusted` | **t8140, t8142, t605x** |
| `external-named-power-provider` (string) | `/arm-io/iop-audio-controller/lp-mic-io-buffer-device` | `SharedDARTMapperProxy` | **t8140, t8142, t605x** |

**[Confirmed]** — present or absent exactly as tabulated on every in-scope board.

**Decoded, and what each means for ordering:**

1. **Per-endpoint provider = the DMA controller (t8132, t604x).** The stream endpoint's
   power is supplied by its own DMA controller node, and a switch function ties the two
   together. Ordering: **the DMA controller must be up before the stream endpoint can be
   opened, and it is the last thing released when the endpoint closes.** On t8140, t8142
   and t605x these per-endpoint properties are replaced by `dma-provider-tx` /
   `dma-provider-rx` string references to named channel nodes, but the dependency is the
   same — the named channel's controller must be up first. **[Confirmed]** for the
   properties; **[Inferred]** for the ordering.
2. **`HibernationAppUntrusted` on the controller (t8140, t8142, t605x).** The provider is
   named, not referenced by phandle. Ordering consequences: **the audio controller cannot
   come up until the named provider is present**, and it must be released before a
   hibernation image is taken. Functionally it
   declares that the audio path has a defined power relationship across the host's
   hibernate transition rather than simply disappearing. **[Inferred]** A driver on those
   three SoCs must wait on a named provider rather than on a power domain, and must expect
   the audio subsystem to be live across host suspend/resume without re-initialisation.
   **[Probable]** On t8132 and t604x no such relationship is declared and the audio path
   has no hibernate contract.
3. **`SharedDARTMapperProxy` on the low-power microphone I/O buffer device (t8140, t8142,
   t605x).** The provider is named rather than referenced by phandle. Ordering:
   **the IOMMU mapping service must be established before the buffer device is powered, and
   the buffer device must be down before the mapper is released.** Together with the
   IOMMU's own `no-sleep` flag this says the low-power capture buffer's mapping is intended
   to survive host sleep. **[Inferred]**

**Every declared external power provider must be up before the audio controller can be
used**; a driver must satisfy all of them before opening a stream. A driver that does not
will see audio come up before its DMA or its IOMMU mapping is ready. **[Probable]**

---

## 14.9 System sleep behaviour

### 14.9.1 Wake sources

Established in §5.7 and not repeated: **the only audio-capable wake path on every in-scope
SoC is a mailbox message from an always-on coprocessor.** There is no wake source
corresponding to the audio DMA controller, the serial audio controller, the display-audio
path, or any application-processor GPIO pin, and the amplifier and jack-codec interrupt
pins are all on the application-processor pin controller, which declares no wake events on
any board of any generation. Headphone insertion cannot wake the machine through the
codec's own interrupt pin.

What this section adds: the coprocessor nubs on t8132, t8140, t8142 and t605x carry
`claim-wake`, i.e. they are declared wake claimants and hold the wake reason. **t604x does
not carry it**, which — with t604x also lacking `no-shutdown` — makes that SoC the outlier
in this area and the one where a driver should verify behaviour rather than assume.
**[Confirmed]** for the properties.

### 14.9.2 Is the codec powered off at sleep?

**Yes, explicitly, on every in-scope machine.** `PowerOffAtSleep = 1` on the jack codec
control node, on all fourteen boards that have a jack codec, on every SoC in scope, with
the identical single-u32 encoding. **[Confirmed]** (§14.2.8).

The amplifiers have no equivalent property; their power-down at sleep is expressed
structurally instead, by the shared shutdown line (§14.7). On t8140 the amplifier's enable
line serves the same purpose with no register state to lose.

### 14.9.3 What survives, and what must be re-established on wake

| Survives | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The coprocessor's firmware state | it goes to a sleep state, never off |
| The audio IOMMU's page tables and stream configuration | `no-sleep` on every in-scope board |
| Always-on / nub / system-controller GPIO pin state | `no-resume-restore = 1` on those controllers |
| Low-power microphone and voice-trigger capability | the wake path depends on it |

| Must be re-established | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Application-processor GPIO pin configuration for every audio pin | restored by the platform; no audio pin is in any board's `no-restore-gpio-pins` exception list |
| Every I2C controller's speed, tunables and reset state | real host power gate, released at suspend |
| The entire jack codec register file including jack detection | `PowerOffAtSleep = 1` |
| The entire amplifier register file on every amplifier | shutdown line asserted at suspend |
| Every DMA channel's configuration, carveout and rings | the channel re-enters at *initialising* out of *sleep* |
| The audio service session and every open endpoint | the coprocessor's endpoint state is not the host's to assume |
| The speaker calibration selection, if not cached | the identification pins are only meaningful with the amplifiers enabled |
| Interrupt masks on both codec and amplifier, and a latch-clear pass on every amplifier | latched events across the transition hold a level-triggered shared line asserted |

**[Confirmed]** for the IOMMU and GPIO rows and for the codec row; **[Probable]** for the
rest.

**Verify before trusting.** Two things must be checked positively after wake rather than
assumed: that the sense capture stream is producing live data (§14.4.5, the baseline resume
defect), and that each amplifier's detected clock ratio and rate match what was programmed
(read the part's clock-configuration status register) before anything is unmuted.
**☠ [Inferred]**

## Per-SoC / per-machine differences

| Aspect | t8132 (j604, j623, j624, j713, j715, j773g) | t604x (j614s/c, j616s/c, j773s, j575c) | t8140 (j700) | t8142 (j704, j813, j815) | t605x (j714s/c, j716s/c) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Audio-domain control registers derivable by the host | yes | **no** | yes | **no** | **no** |
| Audio domains performance-managed | **6** | none | none | none | none |
| On-at-boot alias for the peripheral domain | absent | `AUDIO-P-V` (`0x11`) | `AUDIO-P-V` (`0x11`) | absent | `AUDIO_P_V`, no on-at-boot bit |
| Audio island root | `AOP_FILTER` | `AOP_FILTER` | `AOP_FILTER` | **`AOP_DART`** | `AOP_FILTER` |
| Coprocessor `no-shutdown` / `claim-wake` | **yes / yes** | **no / no** | yes / yes | yes / yes | yes / yes |
| Coprocessor `function-pll_off_mode` | present | present | **absent** | present | present |
| Second coprocessor instance | no | no | **yes**, with `aot-power = 1` | **yes** | **yes** |
| Audio IOMMU `manual-availability` | yes | **no** | yes | yes | yes |
| Audio IOMMU `avoid-tlbi-in-map` | no | no | no | **yes** | **yes** |
| Audio IOMMU stream count | 16 | 16 | **18** | 17 | 17 |
| Host-visible DMA instances | base-ns, leap-ns | base-ns, leap-ns | base-ns, leap-ns, **leap-s** | + **leap-s**, + 3 display | + **leap-s**, + 5 display |
| Latency-tolerance vote form | virtual clock-gate entry | same | same | same | **`function-vote_crit_llt_mode`** |
| Controller names a hibernation-surviving provider | no | no | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** |
| Per-endpoint provider is the DMA node | **yes** | **yes** | replaced by named channels | replaced | replaced |
| Amplifier family | SN012776 (TAS2764 variant) | same | **MAX98360, no control bus** | same as t8132 | same as t8132 |
| Amplifier count per machine | 6 (j604, j715), 4 (j623, j624, j713), 1 (j773g) | 6 (j614s/c, j616s/c), 1 (j773s, j575c) | 2 channels on one line | 6 (j704, j815), 4 (j813) | 6 |
| Amplifier buses | one (i2c3) | **two** (i2c1 + i2c3) | none | one (i2c3) | **two** (i2c1 + i2c3) |
| Amplifier register state to restore | full file, §14.3.3 | full file | **none — no registers** | full file | full file |
| Shared shutdown/enable pin | gpio0 15 | gpio0 54 | gpio0 105 | gpio0 151 | gpio0 107 |
| Platform mute-ramp delay | none | none | **20 ms** | none | none |
| Coprocessor ramp-down flag | none | none | **present** | none | none |
| Jack codec | CS42L84 | CS42L84 | **CS42L83** | CS42L84 | CS42L84 |
| Jack codec reset controller | nub (retained) | nub (retained) | **AP (restored)** | nub (retained) | **AP (restored)** |
| Jack codec `PowerOffAtSleep` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Extra supply to sequence | none | none | **microphone array, via the system-management controller, line 0x19** | none | none |
| Sense capture to re-verify after wake | 6 amps: yes; j623/j624/j773g: none | 6 amps: yes; j773s/j575c: none | **none** | j704/j815 yes, j813 yes (8 ch) | yes |

Machines with **no** sense return (j623, j624, j773g, j773s, j575c, j700) have no
post-resume sense verification to perform and no sense slot programming to restore — but
also no telemetry, so their excursion and thermal limits must come from a fixed per-machine
table and must be applied before the first unmute. **☠ [Confirmed]**

**j700 is the structural outlier of this section.** Its only speaker power control is one
GPIO. There is no register file, no interrupt, no sense path, no speaker identification and
no per-unit calibration. Everything that protects the drivers on the other machines is
absent, and the only sequencing obligations are the **20 ms** ramp wait in both directions
and keeping the digital input coherent so the part does not bounce in and out of standby.
**[Confirmed]**

## Open questions

1. **Does the host's write to an audio power-state register on t8132, t8140 or t8142 have
   any effect while the coprocessor owns the island?** *Why it matters:* it is the
   difference between a host driver being able to force the audio island up for bring-up
   and tracing, and being able only to ask. *How to resolve:* with the island idle, read
   the control register of `AUDIO_MCA0_M` (t8132: `0x3_8828_40e8`; t8140:
   `0x3_0828_4100`), write a different target level, and poll the actual-level field;
   repeat with an audio stream running and check whether the coprocessor overwrites it.

2. **What is the settling time of a cluster master-clock cell, and of the audio island root
   domain?** *Why it matters:* every start sequence has an unquantified wait in it, and the
   baseline's 25/50/100 µs figures are for a different ownership model. *How to resolve:*
   on t8132 or t8140, instrument the actual-level field of the cell's control register and
   measure the target-to-actual latency; separately, measure the interval between a stream
   power-on request and the first valid frame on the link with a logic analyser on the
   frame-sync pin.

3. **Do the baseline's serialiser-reset self-clear (25–50 µs) and pre-DMA-start settle
   (100 µs) still apply, and does the host ever have to perform either?** *Why it matters:*
   if the coprocessor performs them the host's start path is shorter, but a bring-up driver
   that programs the block directly still needs the numbers. *How to resolve:* trace the
   coprocessor's register writes to a cluster during a stream start and measure the
   intervals between the reset write, the read-back, and the DMA start.

4. **What are the units and the configured values of the four mute/unmute ramp parameters?**
   *Why it matters:* they set how long a mute takes to become silent, which a driver must
   know before it drops a clock or asserts the shutdown line. *How to resolve:* capture the
   speaker link's serial data during a mute request on a machine with an SN012776 amplifier
   and measure the ramp duration and step count directly; repeat on j700 and compare with
   the declared 20 ms.

5. **Is the coprocessor's mute/unmute ramp engine used on the machines that do not carry
   `enable-iop-ramp-down`?** *Why it matters:* if it is not, the only pop suppression on
   those machines is the amplifier's own 6–7 ms ramp, and the host owns the timing; if it
   is, the host must not also ramp. *How to resolve:* as in (4) — look for a digital ramp in
   the transmitted data on a t8132 or t605x speaker link during a mute.

6. **What is the amplifier's clock-halt timer value on these machines, and is the
   clock-error power-enable bit set?** *Why it matters:* it bounds how long a bit-clock
   dropout can be before the part shuts itself down or powers down entirely, which
   determines whether a brief re-rate is survivable. *How to resolve:* read `INT_CLK_CFG`
   (page 0, 0x5C) from a live amplifier after platform initialisation.

7. **Does the post-resume sense-stream defect observed on M1–M3 persist on M4 and later, and
   what state is not restored?** *Why it matters:* the sense stream is the speaker-protection
   input; a driver that trusts a silently dead sense stream will allow unlimited excursion.
   **☠** *How to resolve:* suspend and resume a six-amplifier machine with the sense capture
   open, and compare the received sense slots before and after without reopening the path;
   if broken, bisect by re-writing individual amplifier registers and individual DMA channel
   registers until it recovers.

8. **What exactly does the named hibernation power provider gate on t8140, t8142 and t605x,
   and how long does it take to become available?** *Why it matters:* it is a hard
   precondition for the audio controller coming up on three of the five in-scope SoCs, and
   its absence would look like an audio probe failure with no audio-specific cause. *How to
   resolve:* instrument the audio controller's transition to on and correlate its timing
   with the host's hibernate-infrastructure availability across a cold boot, a resume from
   suspend, and a resume from hibernate.

9. **Is the low-power microphone I/O buffer device's IOMMU mapping actually retained across
   host sleep, as the combination of `no-sleep` and the shared-mapper provider implies?**
   *Why it matters:* if it is, the host must not tear it down; if it is not, the host must
   rebuild it before the first capture after wake. *How to resolve:* read back the audio
   IOMMU's translation table entries for the low-power stream before and after a
   suspend/resume cycle.

10. **Does the second coprocessor instance participate in the audio path at all, and does it
    have its own audio power dependencies?** *Why it matters:* on t8140, t8142 and t605x it
    has its own wake sources and its own `no-shutdown` declaration, and on t8142/t605x it
    carries an idle-control declaration; if it serves any audio endpoint, suspend/resume
    must interleave with two coprocessors rather than one. *How to resolve:* enumerate the
    services announced on the second instance's mailbox and check for an audio service
    name; independently, check whether any audio stream stalls when the second instance is
    quiesced.

11. **What does `aot-power = 1` on the t8140 second coprocessor instance change?** *Why it
    matters:* it is unique to that machine and sits on the instance that shares the audio
    island. *How to resolve:* compare that instance's power-domain behaviour against the
    t8142/t605x second instance, which lacks the property, across an idle transition.

12. **Which per-machine values do the amplifier idle-behaviour selectors take?** Two
    per-machine switches exist that select between leaving the amplifier enabled and silent
    versus soft-shutting it down on mute, and an "enable idle channel" operation exists on
    the coprocessor-side control path. Their values are not in the platform description on any in-scope
    board. *Why it matters:* the two choices have different pop behaviour and different idle
    current, and the soft-shutdown choice interacts with the clock-loss fault. *How to
    resolve:* observe whether the amplifier's power-mode register changes when playback goes
    silent but the stream stays open, on one machine of each SoC.

13. **What are the addresses of the CS42L84 registers that are established as existing but
    not publicly located** — the global enable, the supply-filter charge/discharge control,
    the headphone clamp override and force controls, the full-scale compensation control,
    the charge-pump reference trim, the pad slew-rate control, and the revision-dependent
    trim table? *Why it matters:* they are on the pop-suppression and restore paths and
    cannot be replayed without addresses. **☠** for the full-scale-related ones. *How to
    resolve:* trace the I2C traffic to the codec across a reset, a power-down for sleep and
    a wake, and diff the write sets.

14. **Is the audio IOMMU's `no-sleep` behaviour conditional on any audio path being open?**
    *Why it matters:* if the IOMMU can in fact be powered down when no low-power capture is
    active, then its page tables are not unconditionally retained and a driver must check
    rather than assume. *How to resolve:* read a translation table entry after a
    suspend/resume cycle performed with no audio open at all, and compare with one performed
    with the voice-trigger path armed.

15. **Do the per-display DMA instances on t8142 and t605x retain channel configuration
    across a display-pipe power transition?** *Why it matters:* display audio is torn down
    and re-established far more often than speaker audio, and a wrong assumption produces
    intermittent silence on hotplug. *How to resolve:* read back a display-audio channel's
    bus-width, carveout and FIFO registers after the associated display pipe has been
    powered down and back up.

16. **What is the coprocessor's power-state value set on M4-and-later firmware, and does the
    quiesce/sleep/idle transition table still hold?** *Why it matters:* the entire
    system-sleep interleave depends on it, and taking the part to the off state is
    unrecoverable. **☠** *How to resolve:* observe the management-endpoint traffic across a
    suspend and a resume on one machine per SoC and compare the values against the baseline
    table of §14.8.1.

17. **Which of the clock/serialiser stage orderings of §14.4.1 are hardware requirements?**
    The six constraints tabulated there each have a hardware reason; two further orderings
    — that both configure stages precede either enable stage, and that on teardown the
    deconfigure stages trail after both gates are shut — have none, and are **[Unknown]**.
    *Why it matters:* a driver that must observe them pays extra round trips to the
    coprocessor on every stream start, and one that ignores a real requirement gets a
    glitched first frame. *How to resolve:* with the serial-audio register region reachable,
    reconfigure a running generator with its gate open and watch the bit and frame clocks on
    a scope; and interleave configure and enable across the two generators, checking the
    first frame of the resulting stream for a phase or rate error.


---

# 15. Initialization state machine

## Baseline

On M1 through M3 the bring-up order is the conventional one for a host-owned
audio subsystem: raise the power domains and clocks, bring the control bus up,
probe and identify the codecs, configure the serial audio controller and the DMA
engine, configure the codecs to match, load protection data, release the
amplifiers.

That order is no longer available. On every SoC in scope the host cannot power
the audio complex, cannot generate the bit, frame or master clocks, and cannot
configure the serialisers or the slot geometry — those capabilities belong to
the always-on coprocessor (Section 11.6). What the host retains is the control
bus to the discrete parts, the shutdown and identification GPIO lines, the DMA
controllers, and the IOMMU.

The consequence is structural rather than incremental: bring-up splits into two
independent chains that must rendezvous before any audio can flow.

- A **host chain** that can run entirely without the coprocessor: control bus,
  codec probing, identification, calibration selection, IOMMU mappings, DMA
  channel programming.
- A **coprocessor chain** that the host can only request, not perform: audio
  power domains, clocking, serialiser and routing configuration, stream
  lifecycle.

Neither chain can complete the bring-up alone, and the rendezvous point is
fixed by hardware: the discrete parts must be programmed to the slot geometry
and sample rate that the coprocessor has already chosen, and the amplifiers must
not leave shutdown until the clocks that chain produces are actually running.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Summary of differences

| Aspect | M1–M3 | Every SoC in scope |
|---|---|---|
| Who raises the audio power domains | host | coprocessor only |
| Who generates the bit/frame/master clocks | host | coprocessor only |
| Who configures serialisers and slot routing | host | coprocessor only |
| Who owns the codec/amplifier control bus | host | host, unchanged |
| Who owns the DMA controllers and IOMMU | host | host, unchanged |
| Codec probing may begin before audio clocks exist | yes | yes, unchanged |
| Slot geometry chosen by | host | coprocessor; host must match it |
| Bring-up shape | one linear chain | two chains with a mandatory rendezvous |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 15.1 State diagram

```
                     ┌──────────────────────────┐
                     │  S0  COLD                │
                     │  no audio state assumed  │
                     └────────────┬─────────────┘
                                  │
                  ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
                  │                                │
                  ▼                                ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   │ S1  CONTROL BUS READY    │    │ S5  COPROCESSOR RUNNING      │
   │ I2C + GPIO usable,       │    │ firmware resident, core      │
   │ codec supplies up        │    │ released, transport up       │
   └────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                │                                 │
                ▼                                 ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   │ S2  PARTS IDENTIFIED     │    │ S6  AUDIO SERVICE OPEN       │
   │ amps + jack codec        │    │ service located by name,     │
   │ answer; revisions read   │    │ device identifiers attached  │
   └────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                │                                 │
                ▼                                 ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   │ S3  MACHINE IDENTIFIED   │    │ S7  STREAM CONFIGURED        │
   │ speaker-ID straps read,  │    │ rate, format, slot geometry  │
   │ calibration selected     │    │ set; audio domains powered   │
   └────────────┬─────────────┘    │ CLOCKS NOW RUNNING           │
                │                  └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                ▼                                 │
   ┌──────────────────────────┐                   │
   │ S4  TRANSPORT MAPPED     │                   │
   │ IOMMU mappings for the   │                   │
   │ audio DMA instances      │                   │
   └────────────┬─────────────┘                   │
                │                                 │
                └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                │  RENDEZVOUS
                                ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                 │ S8  PARTS MATCHED            │
                 │ amps + codec programmed to   │
                 │ the negotiated geometry;     │
                 │ protection limits loaded;    │
                 │ still muted, still shut down │
                 └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                 │ S9  DMA ARMED                │
                 │ channel programmed, buffers  │
                 │ mapped, interrupts unmasked  │
                 └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                 │ S10 OUTPUT ENABLED           │
                 │ amps released from shutdown, │
                 │ ramp elapsed, still muted    │
                 └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                 │ S10a SENSE VALIDATED         │
                 │ each sense channel inside    │
                 │ its impedance window,        │
```
